Second Session.
First, from within the assembly at the site of enlightenment (*bodhimaṇḍa*), there is the section on "Exalting the Fruit and Encouraging Joy to Generate Faith.
This is followed by the section on the "Seven Locations and Nine Assemblies of the Dharma-realm," which separately enumerates the ten branches of Dharma practice.
With all reverence, we pay homage to the inexhaustible Triple Gem.
First, as for the extensive cultivation of offerings:
each person among this assembly shall kneel on their right knee, solemnly holding incense and flowers, and make offerings according to the Dharma. May this ocean of offerings...
Clouds [of offerings] pervade the entirety of the Dharma-realm and the realm of empty space, making offerings to all Buddha-fields of the ten directions and the three periods of time.
Within each and every atom, there are Buddhas as numerous as the atoms in all worlds;
at the site of each Buddha, they are surrounded by oceans of various bodhisattvas. By the power of the practices and vows of Samantabhadra, I give rise to profound faith and understanding.
Manifesting direct knowledge and vision, they made offerings with all manner of sublime and excellent articles of worship, namely:
clouds of flowers, clouds of garlands, clouds of celestial music, clouds of celestial parasols, clouds of celestial garments, and various kinds of celestial incense and unguents.
Incense, powdered incense, and clouds such as these, each as vast in measure as Sumeru, the King of Mountains;
various lamps are lit—butter lamps, oil lamps, and lamps of various fragrant oils—with each lamp-wick as large as Mount Sumeru and each lamp-oil as deep as the waters of the great ocean.
With such articles of offering, they constantly perform offerings, even unto this extent.

This supreme offering is vast; it shall only be exhausted when the realm of space is exhausted, the realm of sentient beings is exhausted, the karma of sentient beings is exhausted, and the afflictions of sentient beings are exhausted.
Yet, because the realm of space and even the afflictions can never be exhausted, this offering of mine is likewise inexhaustible.
It continues from moment to moment without interruption, such that my actions of body, speech, and mind are never-ceasing.
Without weariness, they constantly offer such various articles of worship to the ocean-like assemblies of Buddhas,
Bodhisattvas, and holy sages, arranged in the infinite layers of Indra’s net. May these clouds of incense and flowers be received by them as luminous pedestals,
vast as boundless realms, immeasurable and inexhaustible, performing the work of the Buddha.
Next, I offer this cloud of offerings—
supremely excellent, consisting of jewel-studded mandalas, the intrinsic nature of precious gems,
vast oceans, and mountains of the seven treasures— arising before the Buddhas and all others. I present them as an offering.
Oṃ sarvatathāgatādhiṣṭhānaparigrahe svāhā. The *Ratnakūṭa-sūtra* states:
"There is a dhāraṇī named 'The Mantra of Immeasurable Varieties,' which can accomplish all things and possesses great power."
Yes. The *dhāraṇī* says:
Oṃ siddhara siddhara medini siddhara mā hvala huṃ. Next, perform the seal and mantra of the Vast Amogha-maṇi (the method for the seal is the same as in the first session).
Oṃ amoghapāśa mahāvidyārāja tathāgatamaitrīkaruṇā-sarvasattvānugrahāya hūṃ.
Next, perform the general offering of the dhāraṇī.
Namaḥ ratnatrayāya namaḥ arhadbhyo 'rhatsiddhebhyaḥ sarvabuddhānāṃ mūrdhnādhiṣṭhitamokṣasiddhisamaya tathāgatāliṅgita svāliṅgita siddhasamyak-sambuddha oṃ mañjuśrī.
Majjimahe majjimahe ḍaṃkamañjimahe mīlaya majjimahe maṇe jjaṭa mañjiri mahe maṇe maṇe daṃbaśaṅkarāmanaye mañjiri sa.
*Kṣemakṣema ākarṇa-miśraṇa-damana-kīla svāhā*. If there is anyone who contemplates this dhāraṇī even once,
they will immediately accomplish the ten stages of worship and making offerings.
To all the Buddhas throughout world-systems as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, at the abode of each and every Buddha, [I offer] various exquisite flowers,
various exquisite nets, various burning incenses, various powdered incenses, various exquisite lamps,
various exquisite ointments, various garments, various foods and drinks, various necklaces, various exquisite seats, and various bedding. Various...
With music, various banners, pennants, flags, parasols, and all other offerings, they shall achieve success in every way.
All karmic obstructions shall be completely purified, and all roots of goodness shall be fully perfected.
They shall behold the faces of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, who will bring peace and comfort to their hearts. [This applies to] devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, and so forth.

The kinnaras and mahoragas, as well as the Lord of Secrets Vajrapāṇi, the Four Great Heavenly Kings, and others, will constantly follow, protect, and assist them, shielding them by concealing their presence. At the end of life, they shall immediately attain rebirth in the world of Ultimate Bliss.
Even if one does not seek to practice this dhāraṇī, merely recollecting it once will cause all such merits to be fully accomplished.
Having made offerings, take refuge with a sincere heart and pay homage to the Honored One, Vairocana Buddha.
Second, the praise of the Tathāgata:
A Praise of the Buddha in a Single Brahma-Voice.
The Tathāgata’s great wisdom is rare and without equal; All the worlds cannot fathom it through thought.
Ordinary beings observe falsely, Grasping at signs in an improper manner.
The Buddha is free from all signs; He cannot be seen by them, For his mind is eternally quiescent.
Pure as space, they completely adorn all worlds; they manifest before all sentient beings—

within every single atom of all lands throughout the ten directions and the three periods of time across the entire dharma-realm and the realm of empty space— to praise the Buddha with two direct words.
Within each and every atom, there are Buddhas as numerous as the atoms in all worlds, and at the site of each Buddha, there is an ocean-like assembly of Bodhisattvas surrounding them.
With profound and supreme resolve, I shall perceive and behold them all directly;
with a subtle tongue-root surpassing that of the goddess Sarasvatī, from each and every tongue-root, I shall produce inexhaustible sounds.
Oceans! From each and every sound, there issue forth oceans of all speech, extolling and praising the oceans of all the virtues of all Tathāgatas.
This continues uninterrupted until the end of the future, pervading the entire Dharma-realm without exception.

Thus, until the realm of space is exhausted, the realm of sentient beings is exhausted, the karma of sentient beings is exhausted, and the afflictions of sentient beings are exhausted, I shall continue my praise.
They would indeed come to an end; yet, because the realm of empty space and even the afflictions have no end, this praise of mine has no exhaustion.
It continues from moment to moment without interruption, and my actions of body, speech, and mind never grow weary or fatigued.
Having offered praise, one takes refuge with a sincere heart and pays homage to the Honored One, Vairocana Buddha. Third,

one pays respectful homage to all Buddhas throughout the entire Dharma-realm and the realm of empty space, in all Buddha-fields of the ten directions and the three periods of time, as numerous as the atoms of a microdust.
To all the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones: by the power of the practices and vows of Samantabhadra, I believe and understand with a profound mind as if they were before my very eyes.
With every pure action of body, speech, and mind, I constantly practice prostration and reverence.

At the presence of each and every Buddha, I manifest bodies as numerous as the atoms within unspeakably unspeakable numbers of Buddha-fields; from each and every body, I universally prostrate to unspeakably unspeakable...
One might say that even if there were Buddhas as numerous as the atoms within a Buddha-field, and even if the realm of space were to be exhausted, my prostrations would not end;
for since the realm of space is inexhaustible, these prostrations of mine are without end.

Likewise, until the realm of sentient beings is exhausted, until the karma of sentient beings is exhausted, and until the afflictions of sentient beings are exhausted, my prostrations will continue; yet the realm of sentient beings and so forth...

Because afflictions are inexhaustible, this prostration of mine is without end; it continues from moment to moment without interruption, and my physical, verbal, and mental actions are never weary or exhausted.

from all ten directions, we take refuge. May our sins be extinguished and our pure faith increase; may we be born in the Flower Treasury Ocean and the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss.

Homage to the Tathāgata Vairocana of the Ten Unobstructed Bodies and to the ocean-like assembly at all sites of enlightenment.
Homage to the Dharma-gate of the "Chapter on the Sublime Array of World Rulers" within the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Great Vaipulya*.
Throughout the ten directions, we take refuge; may our transgressions be extinguished, our pure faith increase, and may we be reborn in the Flower Treasury Ocean.
The *Sukhāvatīvyūha Sūtra*, Chapter One, "The World-Ruler’s Sublime Adornment," states:
Thus have I heard. At one time the Buddha was dwelling in [the land] manifested as the reflection of all adornments.

May I, together with all sentient beings, be reborn in the Flower Treasury Ocean within the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss, and subsequently within the Bodhi-maṇḍala of the Dharma-realm, amidst the assembly at the Sea-gathering beneath the Bodhi tree.
As the *Sūtra on the Assembly at the Sea* states: "That Bodhi tree is lofty, eminent, and extraordinary... (omitted)... it expounds various dharmas without end or limit."
(Chorus: May we, together with all sentient beings, be reborn in the Flower Treasury Ocean, within the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss.

Namo to the Flower Treasury World-Ocean! From the Bodhi-mandala of the Dharma of Aranya in the Kingdom of Magadha, from amidst the Tree of Awakening Wisdom, may the vast ocean-like assembly of all Bodhisattvas appear simultaneously, as numerous as clouds.
(All together: We take refuge in all directions; Sins are extinguished and pure faith increases.

May we be born within the Flower Treasury Ocean, In the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss, And within the palace at the Bodhimanda of the Dharma-realm, Amidst the ocean-like assembly that has emerged there.
The Sūtra says: "The palaces and towers where the Tathāgata dwells... in a single thought-moment, they entirely encompass the Dharma-realm.

throughout the ten directions, we all take refuge; may our transgressions be extinguished, our pure faith increase, and we be reborn in the Flower Treasury Ocean and the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss.

with a sincere heart take refuge and pay obeisance to the Honored One, Vairocana Buddha.
Fourth, the confession of karmic obstructions:
I now reflect upon myself that throughout the beginningless kalpas of the past, due to greed, hatred, and delusion, I have given rise to actions of body, speech, and mind.
I have committed immeasurable and boundless evil karmas. If these evil karmas possessed a physical form or characteristics, even the entirety of the realm of empty space could not contain them.
Now, with my three karmas completely purified, I pervade every atom and dust-mote world throughout the entire Dharma-realm.
Before all the Buddhas and the assembly of Bodhisattvas, I sincerely repent and vow never to commit such acts again. May I always abide in pure precepts.

All my merits shall endure until the realm of empty space is exhausted, the realm of sentient beings is exhausted, the karma of sentient beings is exhausted, and the afflictions of sentient beings are exhausted—only then shall my repentance be finished;
yet the realm of empty space, and even the afflictions of sentient beings, can never be exhausted.
Therefore, this confession of mine is inexhaustible; it continues from moment to moment without interruption, and my actions of body, speech, and mind never grow weary or exhausted.
Having finished the confession, I take refuge with a sincere heart and prostrate to the Honored One, Vairocana Buddha.
Fifth, regarding the merit of sympathetic joy:
throughout the entire realm of phenomena and the realm of empty space, in all Buddha-fields of the ten directions and three periods of time,

as numerous as the atoms within them, there are all the Tathāgatas who, from their first aspiration for omniscience, have diligently cultivated a mass of merit, not sparing even their own bodies or lives.

For as many eons as there are atoms in unspeakably unspeakable numbers of Buddha-fields, in each and every eon, he relinquished as many heads, eyes, hands, and feet as there are atoms in unspeakably unspeakable numbers of Buddha-fields—performing all such difficult practices and ascetic austerities.
He brought to perfection the various gates of the *pāramitās* and realized the various stages of bodhisattva wisdom. He attained...
I rejoice in all roots of goodness regarding the unsurpassed enlightenment and parinirvāṇa of all Buddhas, as well as the distribution of their relics.
Furthermore, I rejoice in every merit belonging to all types of beings within the six destinies and four modes of birth across all worlds in the ten directions, down to even a single speck of dust.
I also rejoice in all the śrāvakas of the ten directions and the three periods of time, and...
I rejoice in all the merits of the Pratyekabuddhas, both those in training and those beyond training.
I rejoice in all the immeasurable difficult and ascetic practices cultivated by all Bodhisattvas who aspire to seek unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment, as well as their vast merits.
Thus, until the end of the realm of space, the end of the realm of sentient beings, the end of the karma of sentient beings, and the end of the afflictions of sentient beings...
My afflictions are exhausted; this rejoicing of mine is inexhaustible. It continues from moment to moment without interruption, and my actions of body, speech, and mind never grow weary or fatigued.
Having rejoiced, one should with a sincere heart take refuge and pay homage to the Honored One, Vairocana Buddha.
Sixth, for the request to turn the wheel of Dharma:
throughout the entire realm of phenomena and the realm of empty space, within all Buddha-lands of the ten directions and three periods of time, as numerous as the atoms of dust—
Within each [of these], there are as many vast buddha-fields as there are atoms in unspeakably unspeakable numbers of buddha-fields.

In each of these fields, moment after moment, there are as many Buddhas attaining perfect enlightenment as there are atoms in unspeakably unspeakable numbers of buddha-fields, surrounded by oceans of assemblies of bodhisattvas; and I, with my entire body...
Through various skillful means of body, speech, and mind, I earnestly entreat [the Buddhas] to turn the sublime Wheel of Dharma.

Thus, until the realm of space is exhausted, the realm of sentient beings is exhausted, the karma of sentient beings is exhausted, and the afflictions of sentient beings are exhausted, I shall constantly entreat all Buddhas to turn the True Wheel of Dharma without end.
Moment after moment, in continuous succession without interruption, [I shall do so with my] body and speech...
With a mental activity free from weariness,
having requested [the turning of the wheel], one should take refuge with a sincere heart and pay homage to the Honored One, Vairocana Buddha.
This is the seventh request for the Buddha to remain in the world.
I universally entreat all the Buddhas, Tathāgatas, who are about to manifest their parinirvāṇa throughout the entire Dharma-realm and space-realm,
in all ten directions and across the three periods of time— within Buddha-fields as numerous as the atoms of all such realms—
as well as all Bodhisattvas, Śrāvakas, Pratyekabuddhas, those in training and those beyond training, and even all spiritual friends: I pray that you do not enter nirvāṇa.
For as many eons as there are atoms in all buddha-fields, for the sake of benefiting and bringing happiness to all sentient beings—
until the realm of space is exhausted, the realm of sentient beings is exhausted, the karma of sentient beings is exhausted, and the afflictions of sentient beings are exhausted—
this exhortation of mine shall never come to an end. It shall continue from moment to moment without interruption, with no cessation in the actions of my body, speech, and mind.
Having become weary and having made the request, one takes refuge with a sincere heart and pays homage to the Honored One, Vairocana Buddha. This is the eighth [practice]:
Constantly Following the Buddha’s Example.
Thus, in this Sahā world, from the time he first resolved his mind, the Tathāgata Vairocana practiced with diligence without ever retreating.

He offered up unspeakably unspeakable numbers of his own bodies and lives as alms; he flayed his skin to serve as paper, split his bones to serve as pens, and drew blood to serve as ink, copying the sūtras in quantities as vast as Mount Sumeru. For the sake of honoring the Dharma, he did not spare his own body.
Life, let alone the royal throne, cities, towns, villages, palaces, gardens, groves, and all possessions, as well as various other difficult ascetic practices,
up to attaining great enlightenment beneath the tree, manifesting various supernatural powers, arising in various transformations,
appearing in various Buddha-bodies, dwelling in various assemblies, and even abiding in such various [conditions].

I shall follow and learn from all such [manifestations], including the assembly of various congregations, the perfect voice like the roar of a great thundercloud that matures sentient beings according to their inclinations and desires,
and even the manifestation of entering into nirvana— just as the World-Honored One Vairocana does now,
so too throughout all Buddha-lands in the ten directions and the three periods of time, as far as the limits of the Dharma-realm and the realm of empty space.
There is within the realm of dust; all Tathāgatas are likewise so. In every thought-moment, I follow and learn from them.

Thus, until the exhaustion of the realm of space, the exhaustion of the realm of sentient beings, the exhaustion of the karma of sentient beings, and the exhaustion of the afflictions of sentient beings, my following and learning shall never come to an end.
Moment after moment they continue in succession without interruption; there is no [cessation] in the actions of my body, speech, and mind.
Having become weary from following and studying [the teachings], one should take refuge with a sincere heart and pay homage to the Honored One, Vairocana Buddha.
Ninth: Constantly Accord with Sentient Beings.
This refers to all sentient beings of every variety throughout the entire Dharma-realm, the realm of empty space, and the oceans of lands in the ten directions.
These include those born from eggs, born from wombs, born from moisture, and born by transformation; those who dwell and subsist depending upon earth, water, fire, or wind;
and those who dwell and subsist depending upon space or various plants and trees—every kind of living being, even down to a single...
To all the devas, nāgas, the eight classes of beings, humans, non-humans, and suchlike categories, I shall accord with them in every way, performing various services and various offerings.
I shall do so without distinction, as if honoring my parents, as if serving my teachers and elders, or even Arhats and Tathāgatas.
For those suffering from illness, I shall act as a skilled physician; for those who have lost their way...
He shows them the correct path; he provides illumination in the midst of the dark night; and for those who are impoverished, he causes them to find hidden treasures.
In this way, the Bodhisattva equally benefits all sentient beings. Why is this?
Because if a Bodhisattva can accord with sentient beings, he thereby accords with and makes offerings to all Buddhas. If he respects and serves sentient beings, [he respects and serves the Buddhas].
This constitutes honoring and serving the Tathāgatas. If one causes sentient beings to give rise to joy, one causes all Tathāgatas to rejoice. Why is this?
Because the Buddhas, the Tathāgatas, take great compassion (*mahākaruṇā*) as their very essence.
It is because of sentient beings that great compassion arises; because of great compassion that the bodhicitta is generated; and because of the bodhicitta that [enlightenment] is accomplished.

Equal and Perfect Enlightenment. Even until the realm of empty space is exhausted, the realm of sentient beings is exhausted, the karma of sentient beings is exhausted, and the afflictions of sentient beings are exhausted, this compliance of mine shall never come to an end.
Moment after moment it continues in succession without interruption; my actions of body, speech, and mind shall never grow weary or exhausted.
Having thus constantly complied, with a sincere heart take refuge and pay homage to the Honored One, Vairocana Buddha. Tenth,
universally dedicate all merits from our initial offerings,
praises, prostrations, and repentances, up to and including all acts performed in accordance with sentient beings.
I dedicate all these merits entirely to all sentient beings throughout the entire Dharma-realm and the realm of empty space.
May all sentient beings always attain peace and happiness; may they be free from all illness and suffering; may their attempts to practice unwholesome dharmas never succeed;
may all the wholesome deeds they cultivate be swiftly fulfilled; may the gates to all evil realms be closed; and may the true path to the human and celestial realms and to Nirvana be revealed.
If there are sentient beings who, because they have accumulated various evil karmas, experience all manner of most grievous fruits of suffering,
may I take them all upon myself in their stead, so that those beings may all attain liberation and ultimately achieve unsurpassed bodhi.

The dedication practiced by the bodhisattva in this manner is inexhaustible: as long as the realm of space endures, as long as the realm of sentient beings endures, as long as the karma of sentient beings endures, and as long as the afflictions of sentient beings endure, so too shall this dedication of mine never come to an end.
It continues in every thought-moment without interruption, and the actions of body, speech, and mind never grow weary or exhausted.
Having performed the dedication, take refuge with a sincere heart and pay homage to the Honored One, Vairocana Buddha.
With a sincere heart, make this aspiration:
"May we, by virtue of practicing those ten inexhaustible merits of the vows and conduct of Samantabhadra, swiftly..."
It can eliminate all physical and mental ailments of the world, as well as the various sufferings and afflictions resulting from the five deeds of immediate retribution;
even all evil karma, numbering as many as the atoms within a Buddha-field, shall be entirely eradicated.
Furthermore, it shall dispel all demonic armies, yakṣas, rākṣasas, kumbhāṇḍas, piśācas, bhūtas, and others who drink blood and devour flesh.
Malevolent spirits and ghosts will all keep far away; at times, they may even resolve to draw near and provide protection.
Therefore, if a person recites this vow while moving through the world, they will encounter no obstacles, like the moon emerging from the clouds and mists.
Praised by all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, all humans and devas should pay them homage and respect. All sentient beings...
One should make offerings to him. This son of good family has well attained a human body and has perfected all the merits of Samantabhadra.
Before long, he shall become like the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra and quickly achieve a sublime form-body endowed with the thirty-two marks of a great man.
Whether born among humans or devas, wherever he dwells, he will always reside within a superior clan. He is fully able to destroy all...
They will be able to remain far removed from all evil destinies; they will be able to subdue all non-Buddhist teachers (tīrthika);
and they will be able to liberate themselves from all afflictions (kleśa), just as a lion king overcomes the herd of beasts.
They shall be worthy of receiving the offerings of all sentient beings. Furthermore, at the time of their death, in the final moment, all their faculties (indriya) will completely...
It shall disintegrate and perish. All kinsmen and relatives will be utterly forsaken; all power and majesty will completely decline and be lost.
Ministers, high officials, the inner and outer palace precincts, elephants, horses, chariots, precious jewels, and hidden treasures—all such things as these will no longer follow him.
Only this King of Vows shall not abandon him, leading him from the front at all times, for a single *kṣaṇa*.
Therein, one immediately attains rebirth in the World of Ultimate Bliss (*Sukhāvatī*).
Upon arrival, one beholds Amitābha Buddha, as well as Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva, Maitreya Bodhisattva, and others.
These bodhisattvas possess dignified and majestic physical forms and are fully endowed with merit, surrounding [the Buddha] together. That person sees themselves born within a lotus flower.

Within that flower, he received the Buddha’s prophecy of enlightenment. Having received this prophecy, for countless hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of nayutas of kalpas, throughout unspeakably unspeakable worlds in the ten directions, he benefited sentient beings according to their inclinations through the power of his wisdom.
Before long, he shall sit at the site of enlightenment (bodhimaṇḍa), subdue the armies of Māra, and attain equal and perfect awakening (samyak-saṃbodhi).
He attains perfect enlightenment and turns the sublime wheel of Dharma, enabling sentient beings in worlds as numerous as the atoms within a Buddha-field to resolve upon Bodhicitta.
According to their faculties and natures, he teaches and brings them to maturity, continuing until the end of the ocean of future kalpas to extensively benefit all sentient beings.
Thus, even when the realm of space is exhausted, the realm of sentient beings is exhausted, and the karma of sentient beings is exhausted—

When the afflictions of sentient beings are exhausted, my making of this vow shall have no end. May it continue from thought to thought without interruption, and may my actions of body, speech, and mind never grow weary or discouraged.
Having made this vow, take refuge with a sincere heart and pay homage to the Honored One, Vairocana Buddha.
Next, perform the mudrā and mantra for repentance and the eradication of transgressions: *Oṃ sarvapa-pame-si-pratara-nātha-namadra-ya svāhā*.
(One should recite this three times:
The sins accumulated over a hundred kalpas Are all swept away in a single thought-moment; Like fire consuming dry grass, they are utterly extinguished without remainder.
All the evil karma I have created in the past, Arising from beginningless greed, hatred, and delusion, Produced through body, speech, and mind— I now repent for it all.
(Recite: May the assembly listen to the verse on impermanence from the sutra.
In all the worlds, those who are born must all return to death; though one’s lifespan may be immeasurable, it must inevitably come to an end.
What flourishes must surely decline; meeting is followed by parting; youth does not linger long.
There is no phenomenon that is permanent. Thus one awakens to impermanence.
Be heedful and do not be negligent; for the non-negligent do not die, while negligence is the cause of death.
Non-negligence is supreme; one shall become a king of the gods. Negligence is the root of birth and death, while heedfulness is the excellent path.
Therefore, abandon negligence and you shall always experience happiness.
I respectfully address the noble sages;
I look up to the Ten-Body Pervasive Illumination Buddha, all the Tathāgatas of the Flower Treasury World,
the Honored Śākyamuni, the Original Teacher of this Sahā World, and the supreme leaders such as Samantabhadra and Mañjuśrī.
The holy assemblies of the oceans of lands and their retinues, the noble beings of the Flower Treasury Assembly,
the hosts of Śakra, Brahmā, and the various classes of devas and spirits, and all those who have attained the divine eye of knowing others' minds—
may you all, without forsaking the power of your compassion, bear witness to us two people.
For the sake of practicing the dharani-door of vows, at this time we wholeheartedly prostrate and repent;
may the merit thus produced be used entirely to adorn the ocean of lands throughout the Dharma-realm.

May sentient beings aspire that celestial immortals shall not fall, that they may awaken to the realization that worldly pleasures are impermanent, and that their lands shall be pure, peaceful, and tranquil. May they recognize the True Vehicle as supreme among all classes of beings, and dwell therein forever.

May those in positions of rank and office all rejoice in the teachings of the Perfect and Sudden Vehicle. May the people enjoy eternal peace and security, and may they all cultivate the Way of Awakening and Illumination.
May the blessings and prosperity of teachers, monks, and parents flow forth boundlessly; may the donors and patrons who provide offerings perfect the myriad practices.

May those in the three miserable realms simultaneously be freed from suffering, and may the eight difficulties be entirely eliminated. May the cauldron of boiling water transform into a cool, refreshing pond, and the iron bed transform into a lotus flower.
Upon the flower-throne, the sounds of lamentation are stilled and harmonized with the voice of mindfulness of the Buddha. Every person possesses the mind to return to the source;

each attains the illumination that returns to the origin. May they constantly cultivate their present vows and future aspirations, together never retreating from the resolve for enlightenment, so that their contemplative practice may be brought to fulfillment.
To witness together in the ocean-like assembly of the Avataṃsaka Sūtra is a supreme and auspicious condition.
[These include] the Vairocana Buddha of the pure *dharmakāya*, the Rocaṇa Buddha of the perfected *saṃbhogakāya*,
the Śākyamuni Buddha of the hundreds of thousands of millions of *nirmāṇakāya* emanations, and the Bhaiṣajyaguru Vaiḍūryaprabha Buddha of the twelve supreme vows.

Jihvā-tālū-kaṇṭha-māṃsa-khara-pravāla-dala-ya-hūṃ. The world is like space; like a lotus, it is unstained by water.

Circumambulating and reciting:
Homage to the Buddhas of the ten directions of the Dharma-realm; Homage to the Dharmas of the ten directions of the Dharma-realm;

Next, within the Dharma-realm Bodhimanda, the ocean-like assembly of ordinary beings all paid homage with profound reverence to the inexhaustible Triple Gem.
Each member of this assembly knelt on one knee and, holding fragrant flowers, made offerings according to the Dharma, vowing that this ocean of offerings...
Clouds pervade the worlds of the ten directions. There are incalculable (*asaṃkhyeya*) pure jewels; seats spread with various precious substances;
incalculable jewel canopies and nets draped and hung; incalculable jewel parasols where all exquisite jewel buds reflect one another with penetrating clarity;
and incalculable clouds of jewels raining down everywhere. Incalculable jewel flowers completely fill the pure space.
Balustrades and railings formed of various jewels, pure and magnificently adorned with incalculable (*asaṃkhyeya*) jewels;

bells that constantly emanate the subtle and wondrous voices of all Buddhas, pervading the entire *dharmadhātu* with incalculable jewels; lotus flowers of various jewel-hues, blooming in radiant splendor with incalculable jewels;
and rows of trees surrounding [the area], possessing immeasurable exquisite jewels as their flowers and fruits.
There were incalculable (*asaṃkhyeya*) jewels; within them dwelt immeasurable bodhisattvas. There were incalculable jewels for the palaces;

there were incalculable jewels for the vast, lofty, and magnificent multi-storied pavilions extending far and wide; there were incalculable jewels for the battlements, adorned with great treasures in exquisite beauty;
and there were incalculable jewels for the gates and portals, draped all around with wonderful jewel necklaces.
The windows and casements were composed of inconceivable jewels, adorned with countless pure and magnificent treasures.
Shaped like *tāla* trees, they resembled half-moons and were formed from a collection of various jewels. All such features were embellished with every kind of precious gem;
they were stainless, pure, and inconceivable, none of which had not arisen from the roots of goodness of the Tathāgata, and they were fully endowed with innumerable treasuries of jewels.
With these and other such offerings, [I] constantly make offerings to the ocean-like assembly of Buddhas,
Bodhisattvas, and worthy sages within the infinitely nested Indra-nets. May they receive these clouds of incense and flowers as luminous pedestals,
vast as boundless realms, immeasurable and inexhaustible, and perform the work of Buddhas.
Having made these offerings, they paid all homage.
Next, they presented the most excellent Seven-Jeweled Mountains, vast oceans of the nature of precious lattices and jewels.
I manifest such clouds of offerings as these and present them to all the Buddhas and their equals. Oṃ sarva-tathāgata-arhat-samyak-saṃbuddha-samaya hūṃ.

With Brahma-like voice, he praises the Tathāgata’s profound wisdom, which universally enters the Dharma-realm; able to turn in accordance with the three periods of time, he serves as a guiding light for the world.
All Buddhas share the same Dharma-body—without dependence and without distinction.
In accordance with the inclinations of all sentient beings, they now behold the physical form of the Buddha;
Possessing all-encompassing wisdom and universal knowledge of all phenomena, Throughout all lands, there is nowhere they do not see him;
They speak straightforwardly in praise of the Buddha.
The Tathāgata’s pure and wondrous Dharma-body is peerless throughout all the three realms;
transcending the world, it lies beyond the path of speech, for its nature is neither existent nor non-existent.
Thus, while it has nothing upon which to rely, there is nowhere it does not abide; while there is nowhere it does not reach, there is nowhere it departs.
Like a painting in the sky or what is seen in a dream, one should contemplate the Buddha-body in this manner;
just as one sees the Buddha’s seat in this assembly, so it is in every atom.
The Buddha-body neither goes nor comes, yet all its merits are clearly manifest.
The Bodhisattva dwelling within the mother’s womb, Manifesting the ten supreme and subtle states of compassionate abiding—
From dwelling in the heavens and the initial birth, Up to the attainment of enlightenment and entry into parinirvāṇa;
Through the vast and tranquil samādhi, He is neither born nor extinguished, with no coming or going.
Adorning and purifying the buddha-lands to manifest to sentient beings— this is the liberation of the Flower Deity of this tree.
Sometimes appearing in the form of boys or girls, or as devas, nāgas, asuras,
and even mahoragas, they cause all to see according to their respective inclinations.
The forms and appearances of sentient beings are each different, And their karmic actions and voices are likewise immeasurable;
All such things he can manifest through the majestic spiritual power Of the Ocean-Seal Samādhi.
The body of reality is equal and signless, A pure Dharma-body of stainless radiance.
The Tathāgata’s body of immeasurable wisdom and tranquility universally responds to the ten directions as he expounds the Dharma.
His essence does not consist of marks; rather, it is the markless, quiescent Dharmakāya.
Yet, he is fully endowed with all physical marks, majestic deportment, and dignified bearing, so that all in the world may behold him according to their inclinations.
Within each and every pore of the Tathāgata, Buddhas as numerous as the atoms of all lands sit amidst assemblies of Bodhisattvas surrounding them, expounding the supreme conduct of Samantabhadra;
through the Buddha’s original vows, he manifests spiritual powers that illuminate every direction throughout the ten quarters.
Just as the Buddha practiced and cultivated his conduct in the past, he expounds it all within the net of light;
sometimes he becomes the sun or moon traveling through the sky, or he manifests as rivers, ponds, wells, and spring water;
again, he transforms himself into the realm of earth, and he is likewise able to become wind and fire.
You should observe a single pore of the Buddha, wherein all sentient beings are entirely contained;
yet they neither come nor go—this is what King Universal Vision has realized.
The Buddha’s body pervades all great assemblies, filling the entire Dharma-realm without end or limit.
Quiescent, devoid of intrinsic nature, and ungraspable, you appear for the sake of saving the world.
Homage to the Vairocana Buddha, the Original Honored One with Ten Unobstructed Bodies in the Flower Treasury World-Ocean within the Great Vaipulya Buddhāvataṃsaka Sūtra.
Homage to Śākyamuni Buddha, the Greatly Compassionate One who made five hundred vows to rescue sentient beings from suffering in the five turbidities.

To the Celestial King Namo, I pay homage. To the Celestial King Acintyavyūhasāgaravyavasthāpana-ekakṣaṇalokadharmaparijñāna-viśeṣajñānadhvaja, I pay homage. To the Celestial King Vidyutprabha, I pay homage. To the Celestial King Namo, I pay homage. To the Celestial King Acintyavyūhasāgaravyavasthāpana-ekakṣaṇalokadharmaparijñāna-viśeṣajñānadhvaja, I pay homage. To the Celestial King Vidyutprabha, I pay homage. To the Celestial King Namo, I pay homage. To the Celestial King Acintyavyūhasāgaravyavasthāpana-ekakṣaṇalokadharmaparijñāna-viśeṣajñānadhvaja, I pay homage. To the Celestial King Vidyutprabha, I pay homage. To the Celestial King Namo, I pay homage. To the Celestial King Acintyavyūhasāgaravyavasthāpana-ekakṣaṇalokadharmaparijñāna-viśeṣajñānadhvaja, I pay homage. To the Celestial King Vidyutprabha, I pay homage. To the Celestial King Namo, I pay homage. To the Celestial King Acintyavyūhasāgaravyavasthāpana-ekakṣaṇalokadharmaparijñāna-viśeṣajñānadhvaja, I pay homage. To the Celestial King Vidyutprabha
Homage to the Celestial King Joyful in Tranquility, who has attained the liberation door of manifesting inconceivable Buddha-fields within a single pore without obstruction.
Homage to the Celestial King Universal Wisdom Eye, who has attained the liberation door of entering the universal gateway to observe the dharma-realm.
Homage to the Celestial King Joyful Revolving Wisdom, who has attained the liberation door of constantly manifesting before all sentient beings in various forms throughout boundless eons;
homage to the One of Good Seed, who has attained the liberation door of observing all worldly realms and entering the inconceivable Dharma.
Homage to the Celestial King Radiance of Wisdom;
Homage to the Celestial King Immaculate Tranquil Light, who has attained the gate of liberation that reveals the essential Dharma for all sentient beings to transcend.
Homage to the Celestial King Vast Pure Light, who has attained the liberation door of observing all sentient beings to be transformed and causing them to enter the Buddha-dharma;
homage to those such as him who act as leaders, their number being immeasurable, and to all the celestial kings of the Broad Fruit Heaven.
All in the ten directions take refuge; Sins are extinguished and pure faith increases. May they be born within the Flower Treasury Ocean in the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss.
The Sūtra says: Furthermore, O Viśuddhamati, this is the gateway entered by the Devaputra Yaśaskāma (up to) the Devaputra Manojña-ghoṣa.
May I, together with all sentient beings, be reborn in the Flower Treasury Ocean, in the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss,
and subsequently in the Bodhimanda of the Dharma-realm, amidst the assembly of the Sudṛśa Heaven Kings.
Namo to the One of Pure Wisdom who has attained the skillful means of liberation for the sake of the path to liberation of all sentient beings.
Homage to the Celestial King Renown,
who possesses the liberation door of manifesting everywhere like a reflection of light according to the inclinations of all the hosts of devas;
and to the Celestial King Supreme Vision.
Homage to the Celestial King Silent Virtue, who has attained the great skillful means liberation door of universally adorning and purifying the realms of all Buddhas.
Homage to the Celestial King Sumeru Sound, who has attained the liberation door of following all sentient beings as they eternally circulate in the ocean of birth and death.
King Namaskāra to the Tathāgata Smṛtilabdha, [who possesses] the liberation door of taming sentient beings through conduct; Pure-Mind-Eye Heavenly King,
Namaskāra to the liberation door of what flows forth from the ocean of the Samantamukha-dhāraṇī, [named] "Delightful Universal Illumination."
The World-Ruling Lord Heavenly King, Namah, who possesses the liberation door of the treasury that enables sentient beings to encounter the Buddha and give rise to faith.

Homage to the Celestial King Sovereign Radiance, who has attained the liberation door of causing all sentient beings to hear the Dharma, to believe and rejoice, and thereby attain transcendence and liberation;
homage to the liberation door of entering the boundless and inexhaustible conduct of taming all bodhisattvas, which is like space.
To the Celestial King of the Transformation of Delighting in Contemplating the Dharma,
Homage to the Celestial King of the Banner of Transformation, who has attained the liberation door of universally compassionate wisdom that observes the immeasurable afflictions of sentient beings.
Homage to the Buddha Prabhāsa-pramukta-saṃdarśana; to the Devaputra Nakṣatra-ghoṣa-vicitra-vyūha, who liberates through the three wheels of conversion;
to all such as these who serve as leaders, their number being immeasurable; and to all the Śuddhāvāsakāyika devaputras.
All in the ten directions take refuge; Sins are extinguished and pure faith increases. May they be born in the Flower Treasury Ocean within the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss.
The Sūtra says: Furthermore, from the King of the Heaven of Delightful Light (until) the King of Supreme Light hears [this] and rejoices greatly.
May I, together with all sentient beings, be reborn in the Flower Treasury Ocean, in the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss, and subsequently in the Bodhimanda of the Dharma-realm.
To the assembly of the King of Gods of Light and Sound, Homage!
You who have attained the constant enjoyment of tranquil bliss, yet can manifest in the world to extinguish its sufferings— to this gate of liberation, I pay homage!
Homage to the Celestial King Lovely Light of Joy,
who has attained the liberation door of the ocean of correspondence with the great compassionate mind, the treasury of joy and happiness for all sentient beings,
and the pure, wondrous light.

Homage to the Celestial King Sovereign Sound, who has attained the liberation door of universally manifesting all the merit and power of sentient beings throughout boundless eons within a single thought-moment.
Homage to the one who has attained the pure realization that causes all worlds— whether forming, abiding, or decaying— to be entirely like empty space.
Homage to the Celestial King Supreme Mindfulness and Wisdom of the Gate of Liberation;
Homage to the Celestial King Lovely Pure and Wondrous Sound, who causes all noble ones to joyfully accept and believe in the Dharma of liberation.

Homage to the Celestial King Sound of Skillful Reflection, who is able to abide for as many eons as there are grains of sand in the Ganges and expound the meaning of all stages (*bhūmi*) along with the gates of skillful means and liberation.
Homage to the Array of Great Offerings at the Time All Bodhisattvas Descend from the Tuṣita Heaven to Be Born Below.
Homage to the Celestial King Adorned Sound Who Manifests the Gate of Liberation;
Homage to the Celestial King Profound Light Sound Who Has Attained the Ocean of Wisdom and Inexhaustible Supernormal Powers through Contemplation; Homage to the Celestial King Gate of Liberation.
Homage to the Celestial King Vast Renown, who has attained the liberation door of the skillful means for appearing in the world with the fulfillment of the ocean of merits of all Buddhas.
Homage to [the one] who has attained the liberation door of the treasury of profound faith and joyful love, generated through the power of the Tathāgata’s past vows.
To the Sovereign Devas of Supreme Pure Light,
Namo to these and others who serve as their leaders, and to all the Sovereign Devas of Light and Sound, infinite in number throughout the ten directions,
we take refuge. May our transgressions be extinguished, may our pure faith increase, and may we be born in the Flower Treasury Ocean.
In the *Sukhāvatīvyūha Sūtra*, it is said: "Furthermore, from the Brahmā King Śikhin... [up to] this liberation of King Samudraghoṣa:
'May I, together with all sentient beings, be reborn in the Flower Treasury Ocean within the Pure Land of Sukhāvatī.'"
Next, the Great Brahma King of the Dharma-realm Bodhimanda Assembly,

who has attained the liberation door of preaching the Dharma within the bodhimandas of the ten directions while abiding universally therein, whose conduct is pure and free from defilement or attachment;
Homage to Śikhin Brahma King.
Homage to the Brahma King Wisdom Light, who has attained the liberation door of causing all sentient beings to enter meditative concentration and abide in liberation.
Homage to the Brahma King Good Thought Wisdom Radiance, who has attained the liberation door of universally entering all inconceivable dharmas.
Homage to the Brahma King Universal Cloud Sound, who has attained the liberation door of entering the ocean of all the voices of the Buddhas.

Homage to the Brahma King Sovereign in Contemplating Words and Sounds, who has attained the liberation door of being able to recollect the skillful means by which Bodhisattvas teach and transform all sentient beings.
Homage to the Brahma King Silent Radiant Eye, who has attained the liberation door of discerning the distinct characteristics of all karmic retributions manifested in all worlds;
homage to the one who has attained the liberation door of manifesting the subduing of all classes and types of sentient beings according to their differences.
Homage to the Brahma King Samantaprabha;
Homage to the Brahma King Vicitraghoṣa, who dwells in the liberation door of the realm of the practice of quiescence characterized by the purity of all phenomena.
Homage to the Brahma King Eye Radiant with the Gate of Liberation Always Diligently Manifesting Non-attachment Toward All Existence and Non-existence, Boundless and Without Dependence;
homage to the Brahma King Ocean-like Melodious Sound that Delights the Mind through the Gate of Liberation of Constantly Contemplating and Examining the Inexhaustible Dharma.
Homage to these and others who serve as their leaders—incalculable Great Brahmā Kings from all ten directions.
We take refuge in you all; may our transgressions be extinguished and our pure faith increase, and may we be reborn within the Flower Treasury Ocean in the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss.
The Sūtra says: Furthermore, the Sovereign Heavenly King (up to) that which was realized by this Sublime Radiance Heaven.

May [I], together with all sentient beings, be reborn in the Flower Treasury Ocean within the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss, and subsequently in the Dharma-realm Bodhimanda of the Sovereign Heavenly King of Other-Transformation.
The assembly of the Sovereign Heavenly King of Other-Transformation.

First, the Sovereign Heavenly King of the Gate of Liberation called the Sovereign Treasury of Mastery Over Maturing Immeasurable Sentient Beings Through the Manifestation of Homage gathered with the various devas of the desire realm.
Homage to the Celestial King Sudarśana, Lord of the Good Eye, who attains the liberation door of observing the happiness of all sentient beings and causing them to enter the bliss of the noble realm.
Homage to the Celestial King Ratnadhvaja,
Wondrous Jewel Banner, who attains the liberation door of following the various desires and understandings of all sentient beings and causing them to give rise to practice.
The Celestial King Who Wears the Crown,
Homage to Him Who Attains Universal Gathering; the Gate of Liberation of Explaining the Meaning for the Sake of All Sentient Beings, the Celestial King of Valiant Wisdom.
Homage to the Celestial King Wondrous Sound Phrase, who has attained the liberation door of increasing one’s own practice through vast compassion by means of mindfulness of the Tathāgata;
homage to the Wondrous Light, who has attained the liberation door of manifesting the gate of great compassion that destroys all banners of pride.
To the Celestial King Dhvaja, I pay homage: you who have attained the gate of liberation that subdues all anger and malice in the world; to the Celestial King Śāntaviṣaya, I pay homage:
you who have attained the gate of liberation wherein the infinite Buddhas of the ten directions all come to attend upon one’s recollection; to the Celestial King Citracakravyūha... [I pay homage].
Homage to the Celestial King Ugradhvaja,
who universally manifests the attainment of perfect enlightenment according to the mental inclinations of sentient beings; and to the Celestial King Padmaprabhaprajñā.
Homage to the Celestial King Indramaniruciraprabha, who has attained the liberation door of the great majestic power and sovereignty that universally enters all worlds;
homage to these and other such celestial kings of the Paranirmita-vaśavartin heaven, who are innumerable and serve as their leaders.
All in the ten directions take refuge; Sins are extinguished and pure faith increases. May they be born within the Flower Treasury Ocean in the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss.
The Sutra says: Furthermore, from the Good Transformation Heavenly King (up to) what this Universal Vision King has realized.
May I, together with all sentient beings, be reborn in the Flower Treasury Ocean within the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss, and subsequently in the Bodhimanda of the Dharma-realm.
To the assembly of the Heavenly Kings of Nirmāṇarati:
Homage to the Heavenly King Skillful Transformation, who has attained the liberation door of the power to manifest the transformations of all karma.
Homage to the Celestial King Silent Sound Radiance, who has attained the liberation door of relinquishing all objects of attachment.

Homage to the Celestial King Transformation Power Radiance, who has attained the liberation door of universally extinguishing the darkness of ignorance in the minds of all sentient beings and causing their wisdom to be perfected.
Homage to the Celestial King Adorned Lord, who attained the liberation door of manifesting infinite, pleasing sounds;
homage to the Celestial King Radiant Mindfulness, who attained the liberation door of thoroughly knowing the inexhaustible marks of the merit of all Buddhas;
homage to the Celestial King Supreme Cloud, who attained the liberation door of universally knowing the sequence of the formation and destruction of all past kalpas.
To the Celestial King Sound, I pay homage to the liberation door of attaining the wisdom that awakens all sentient beings.
To the Celestial King Supreme Radiance, I pay homage to the liberation door of emitting light that swiftly fills the void realms of the ten directions. To the Celestial King Wondrous Topknot...
Homage to the Celestial King Joyful Wisdom, who has attained the liberation door of indestructible power of diligence in accomplishing all tasks.
Homage to the Celestial King Flower-Light Topknot, who has attained the liberation door of knowing the karmic retributions received by all sentient beings.
Homage to the Universal... who has attained the liberation door of manifesting the inconceivable distinctions among the forms and classes of sentient beings.

Next, within the Dharma-realm Bodhimanda, [I pay homage to] the assembly of Tuṣita Heaven Kings:
I take refuge in the Tuṣita Heaven King who has attained the liberation door of the perfect wheel of teaching for the appearance of all Buddhas in the world;
I take refuge in the Tuṣita Heaven King who has attained the liberation door of the pure radiant body that exhausts the realm of empty space; and [I pay homage to] the Heaven King Joyful Ocean Crest.
The King Homage to the Celestial King Supreme Banner of Merit, the Gate of Liberation of the Pure Vow Ocean that Eliminates the Suffering of the World.
Homage to the Celestial King Silent Light, who has attained the liberation door of manifesting bodies everywhere to preach the Dharma;

Homage to the Celestial King Suvarṇa, who has attained the liberation door of making the bodhicitta of all sentient beings firm and indestructible.

All in the ten directions take refuge; Sins are extinguished and pure faith increases. May they be born within the Flower Treasury Ocean in the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss.
