May I, together with all sentient beings, be reborn in the Flower Treasury Ocean within the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss, and subsequently in the Bodhimanda of the Dharma-realm.
[Homage to] the assembly of the Suyāma Heavenly Kings:
the gate of liberation that enables the arousal of all roots of goodness in sentient beings, causing them to forever leave behind sorrow and affliction.
To the Celestial King Vibhakti, I pay homage; to the Celestial King Samantagatipraveśa, I pay homage; to the Celestial King Prabhāsa, I pay homage;
to the one who has attained the liberation door of the great compassion wheel that extinguishes all afflictions, I pay homage; to the Banner of Inexhaustible Wisdom and Merit, I pay homage.

Homage to the Celestial King Who Has Attained Liberation through Thorough Knowledge of the Minds of All Sentient Beings of the Three Times, the Celestial King of Skillful Transformation and Majestic Dignity.

Homage to the Celestial King Mahāprabha, the Great Radiance, who has attained the dharani-door of illumination for recollecting and upholding all dharmas without forgetfulness, and the inconceivable door of liberation through skillful means regarding the self-nature of all karma. Homage to the Inconceivable... [text truncated]
To the Celestial King Discerning Wisdom, I pay homage to his liberation door of skillful means for turning the wheel of Dharma and bringing sentient beings to maturity.

To the Celestial King Navel-Wheel, I pay homage to his liberation door of attaining the vast eye that universally observes sentient beings and proceeds to tame them. To the Celestial King Radiant Flame...
Homage to King Light-Illumination, who has attained the liberation door of transcending all karmic obstructions and not following the deeds of Māra.
Homage to the Heavenly Hosts Who Attain Skillful Instruction and Cause All to Receive and Practice the Gate of Mental Purity and Liberation;
homage to the Great Renowned Heavenly King Samantadarśin, and to those of like kind who serve as their leaders, numbering immeasurably; homage to Suyāma, the Lord of all Heavenly Kings.

All beings throughout the ten directions take refuge; May their transgressions be extinguished and their pure faith increase; May they be born within the Flower Treasury Ocean, in the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss.
The Sūtra says: Furthermore, Śakrendra, King of Devas... (up to)... this is what the King of Radiance has attained.

May I, together with all sentient beings, be reborn in the Flower Treasury Ocean, within the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss, and subsequently in the Bodhimanda of the Dharma-realm, amidst the assembly of the Thirty-three Heavenly Kings.

Homage to the liberation door of Great Joy through Clearly Seeing the Arising of the Buddhas of the Three Times and Even the Formation and Destruction of All Lands, attained by Śakrendra, King of the Gods;
homage to the liberation door of Making the Buddha’s Form Body Utterly Pure, Vast, and Peerless in the World.
Homage to the Celestial King Universal Renowned Full Sound,
who has attained the liberation door of the pervasive covering of compassionate clouds. Homage to the Celestial King Compassionate Eye Jewel Topknot,
who has attained the body of various forms and majestic virtue that constantly appears before all world-protectors in the presence of the Buddhas.
Homage to the Celestial King Renowned as the Jewel-Light Banner of the Gate of Liberation;
Homage to the Celestial King Crest of Joyful Arising, who knows from what meritorious karma the cities and palaces of all sentient beings arise.
Homage to the Celestial King Enduring Right Mindfulness, who has attained the liberation door of manifesting the Buddhas’ deeds of maturing sentient beings.
Homage to the Celestial King Exalted Sound, who has attained the liberation door of knowing the signs of transformation during all kalpas of formation and destruction in every world.
Homage to the Celestial King Accomplished Mindfulness, who attained the liberation door of the bodhisattva practice of taming sentient beings through recollection of the future;
homage to the Celestial King Pure Flower Radiance, who attained the liberation door of thoroughly knowing the causes of all celestial happiness.

Homage to the Celestial King Wisdom-Sun Eye, who has attained the liberation door of revealing to all the sons of heaven the roots of goodness for their rebirth, so that they may be free from delusion and confusion.
Homage to the Celestial King Self, who has attained the liberation door of enabling all the hosts of devas to forever sever various doubts.
In the Heaven of Light,
the Heavenly Kings headed by Namah and others were present in immeasurable numbers; so too were all the heavenly kings of the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven.
All in the ten directions take refuge; Sins are extinguished and pure faith increases. May we together [attain rebirth] within the Flower Store Ocean and the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss.
The Sūtra says: Furthermore, from the Sun Devas (to) the Universal Radiance Devas.
May I, together with all sentient beings, be reborn in the Flower Treasury Ocean within the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss;
next, in the Bodhimanda of the Dharma-realm, to the assembly of the Sun Deity,
Homage to the One Who Attains Pure Light Universally Illuminating Sentient Beings of the Ten Directions, Constantly Bringing Benefit and Liberation throughout All Future Kalpas.
To the Devaputra Sun of the Gate of Liberation,
Namah! To the Devaputra Radiant Eye, who attains the gate of liberation that awakens sentient beings through bodies of every kind and causes them to enter the ocean of wisdom!
Homage to the Celestial Son Sumeru-light-Joy-Banner, who has attained the liberation door of becoming a lord for all sentient beings and causing them to diligently cultivate boundless pure merit.
Homage to the Celestial Son Pure Jewel Moon, who has attained the liberation door of deep-seated joy in the cultivation of all ascetic practices.
Homage to the Celestial Son Courageous and Non-regressive, who attained the liberation door of obtaining unimpeded light that shines universally to benefit the vital spirits of all sentient beings;
homage to the one who attained the liberation door of pure light shining universally upon the bodies of sentient beings to cause them to give rise to joy and an ocean of faith and understanding.
Homage to the Celestial Son Radiant with Wondrous Flower Garlands;
Homage to the Celestial Son Supreme Banner Light, who attains the liberation door of radiating light that universally illumines all worlds and brings to fulfillment various wondrous merits.
Homage to the Devaputra Universal Radiance Jewel-Tuft, who has attained the jewel liberation door of manifesting infinite realms and various forms and signs from the ocean of great compassion;
homage to the light that has attained the liberation door of purifying the eyes of all sentient beings so that they may see the treasury of the Dharma-realm.
To the Devaputra Eye,
who possesses the liberation door of attaining the arising of a pure, continuous mind that is never lost or destroyed, and to the Devaputra Holder of Virtue, I pay homage.
Homage to the Sun Palace Universal Movement, which illuminates the ten directions and causes all sentient beings to accomplish their karmic activities;
to the Devaputra Universal Movement Radiance,
and to all such as these who serve as leaders, their number being immeasurable— all the Sun Devas.
All in the ten directions take refuge; Sins are extinguished and pure faith increases. May they be born within the Flower Treasury Ocean in the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss.
The Sutra says: Furthermore, the Moon Deva-son... (up to) ...thus did the Liberation-Light Heaven Devas awaken.

May I, together with all sentient beings, be reborn in the Flower Treasury Ocean within the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss, and subsequently in the Bodhimanda of the Dharma-realm. To the assembly of Moon Devas:
Homage to the Moon Deva who possesses the liberation door of attaining pure light that universally illumines the dharma-realm and gathers and transforms sentient beings.
Homage to the Celestial Son Flower-King-Tuft-Light, who has attained the liberation door of observing all realms of sentient beings and causing them to universally enter the infinite Dharma;
homage to the assembly who have attained the liberation door of thoroughly knowing the various objects of focus and the turning of the ocean of minds of all sentient beings.
To the Celestial Son Sublime Pure Light,
who possesses the liberation door of bestowing inconceivable happiness upon all sentient beings and causing them to leap for great joy,
and to the Celestial Son Peaceful Mind of the World; I pay homage.

Homage to the Devaputra Tree-King Eye-Light, who has attained the liberation door of protecting the sprouts, stalks, and so forth of his work like a farmer’s field according to the seasons, thereby bringing them to fulfillment;
homage to him who has attained compassion to rescue and protect all sentient beings, causing them to clearly perceive the experiences of suffering and joy.
Homage to the Celestial Son Pure Light Appearing from the Gate of Liberation;

Homage to the Celestial Son Universal Traveling in Immutable Light, who has attained the gate of liberation of being able to hold the pure moon and manifest it universally throughout the ten directions.

Homage to the Devaputra King of Constellations Sovereign, who has attained the liberation door of realizing that all phenomena are like illusions and like space— without marks and without intrinsic nature.
Homage to the Devaputra Pure Awakened Moon, who has attained the liberation door of universally performing great karmic activities for the sake of all sentient beings.
I pay homage to the Son of the Buddha, the Devaputra Great Majestic Virtuous Radiant Light, who possesses the liberation door of universally severing all doubts;
I pay homage to these and others who are their leaders, whose number is immeasurable, as well as to all the Moon Devas.
The ten directions all take refuge, Eradicating sins and increasing pure faith; May they be born within the Flower Treasury Ocean and the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss.
Next follows the Repentance for Karmic Retribution in the Three Realms.
I only pray that the inexhaustible Jewels of the Buddha, Dharma, and Sangha, as vast as the celestial net; Vairocana Tathāgata;

the assembly of holy beings of Samantabhadra, Mañjuśrī, and the ocean-like gathering; and all mundane and supramundane deities—by virtue of your compassionate original vows, may you emit great radiance to illuminate this Dharma assembly.
May you bear witness, protect, and remember us; may you compassionately take us into your care.

I pray that for myself and the ocean of all sentient beings, from the beginningless past until this very moment, the ocean of karma—exhaustless, with its Indra-net of layered complexities, the karmic retributions of the three realms, and all afflictions—[may they be purified].
Confess and repent. The *Mahāprajñāpāramitā-śāstra* states: "The devas of the formless realm (*ārūpyadhātu*) are attached to the bliss of meditative concentration and remain unaware of it;

when their lives end, they fall into the desire realm (*kāmadhātu*) and receive the forms of birds and beasts as the retribution for their offenses. One must confess these karmic retributions. The same applies to the various devas of the form realm (*rūpadhātu*). From the pure...
In pure places, one falls back into sexual desire; repent for the retribution of these offenses committed amidst impurity.
The six heavens of the desire realm are attached to the pleasures of the five desires; yet they fall back into hell and undergo all manner of suffering; repent for the retribution of these offenses.

Within the human path, one obtains a human body by trading for it with the merit of the ten wholesome actions; yet the human body has much suffering and little joy, and when life ends, one mostly falls into the evil realms. Repent for the retribution of these offenses.

Within the realms of existence, one repents for the retribution of past offenses: seeing various animals undergoing all manner of suffering and affliction—driven by whips and staves, forced to carry heavy loads over great distances, their necks and throats pierced and torn, and scorched by glowing red-hot iron. This is due to the causal conditions of this person’s past conduct:

having bound sentient beings and subjected them to the suffering of whips and staves through such various causes and conditions, they now receive the bodies of elephants, horses, oxen, sheep, and deer.
Deer are the form of beasts; their lustful passions are heavy and their ignorance is particularly abundant.

They undergo rebirth as geese, ducks, peacocks, mandarin ducks, pigeons, doves, chickens, ducks, parrots, thrushes, and other such species. They receive hundreds and thousands of such various bird forms as a retribution for their sins;
through the confession of these sins of lustful conduct, hair and feathers grow upon their bodies, obstructing all that is smooth and delicate, while their beaks and claws become coarse and harsh.

A separate taste of contact: repentance for the retribution of offenses. Those with an excess of hatred and anger receive the bodies of venomous snakes, vipers, scorpions, mosquitoes, bees, centipedes, and other poisonous insects;

repentance for the retribution of offenses. Because of an abundance of delusion, one receives the bodies of earthworms, moths, dung beetles, crickets, ants, owls, horned owls, and the like—various foolish insects and birds; repentance for the retribution of offenses. Because of an abundance of arrogance...
I repent for the karmic retribution of receiving the bodies of lions, tigers, leopards, and other fierce beasts.

I repent for the karmic retribution of being born among donkeys, pigs, and camels due to the conditions of perverse pride. I repent for the karmic retribution resulting from stinginess, greed, jealousy, fickleness, and brevity of life.
I repent for the retribution of my sins that caused me to take the forms of monkeys, apes, bears, and brown bears.

I repent for the retribution of my sins caused by the karmic conditions of perverse greed, hatred, and jealousy, which led me to receive the bodies of wildcats, foxes, earth-tigers, and various other beasts.

I repent for the retribution of my sins caused by the karmic conditions of shamelessness, lack of remorse, and gluttony, which led me to receive the forms of birds such as magpies, crows, ospreys, and vultures. I repent for the retribution of my sins caused by the karmic condition of [disrespecting]... lightness.
Because of being arrogant toward virtuous people, one receives the bodies of chickens, dogs, jackals, and the like; repent for this retribution of sin.
Because of practicing great acts of giving with a crooked mind of anger and resentment, one receives the bodies of various dragons; repent for this retribution of sin.

Because of practicing great acts of giving while being haughty and oppressing others with suffering to afflict sentient beings, one receives the form of a garuḍa; repent for this retribution of sin. As it is said:
Due to these various fetters, afflictions, karmic causes, and conditions, they undergo the sufferings of the various animals and beasts.

Through the confession of their retributive offenses, the Bodhisattva attains the divine eye (*divyacakṣus*). Observing with it how sentient beings revolve and circulate through the five destinies (*pañcagati*), he sees those who have died among the gods.
Born among humans, they die and are born among devas; dying among devas, they are born in the hells. Dying in the hells, they are born in the heavens;
dying in the heavens, they are born among the hungry ghosts (preta). Dying among the hungry ghosts, they are again born in the heavens;
dying in the heavens, they are born among animals (tiryagyoni). Dying among animals, they are born in the heavens; dying in the heavens, they are again born in the heavens. [In the hells...]
The same applies to hungry ghosts and animals. Regarding the repentance for karmic retribution: one may die in the desire realm and be reborn in the form realm;
die in the form realm and be reborn in the desire realm; die in the desire realm and be reborn in the formless realm;
die in the formless realm and be reborn in the desire realm; or die in the desire realm and be reborn in the desire realm. The same applies to the form and formless realms.
Thus it is. Repenting of the retribution for one's offenses: dying in the Sañjīva Hell and being reborn in the Kālasūtra Hell;
dying in the Kālasūtra Hell and being reborn in the Sañjīva Hell; dying in the Sañjīva Hell and being reborn again in the Sañjīva Hell.
From the Sañjīva Hell to the Saṃghāta Hell, and even up to the Avīci Hell, it is likewise. Repenting of the retribution for one's offenses: [the hell of] the Charcoal Pit.
Dying in hell, one is reborn in the Boiling Excrement Hell; dying in the Boiling Excrement Hell, one is reborn in the Charcoal Pit Hell;
dying in the Charcoal Pit Hell, one is reborn again in the Charcoal Pit Hell.
It is the same for the Burning Forest Hell up to the Mahāpadma Hell. One is reborn therein again and again. This is the retribution of sin; [therefore,] perform repentance.
Dying among those born from eggs, one is reborn among those born from wombs; dying among those born from wombs, one is reborn among those born from eggs.
Dying among those born from eggs, one is reborn again among those born from eggs. The same applies to those born from wombs, moisture, or transformation.
Through the repentance of karmic offenses: dying in Jambudvīpa, one is reborn in Pūrvavideha; dying in Pūrvavideha, one is reborn in Jambudvīpa.
Those who die in Jambudvīpa are reborn in Jambudvīpa; it is the same for Godānīya and Uttarakuru. Regarding the repentance of karmic retribution:
those who die in the four heavenly realms are reborn in the Trāyastriṃśa heaven; those who die in the Trāyastriṃśa heaven are reborn in the four heavenly realms;
those who die in the four heavenly realms are reborn again in the four heavenly realms; and this continues from the Trāyastriṃśa heaven up to the Paranirmita-vaśavartin heaven.
The same applies to the Lord Maheśvara. Regarding the repentance for karmic retribution: one dies among the Brahmakāyika devas and is reborn among the Brahmapurohita devas;
dies among the Brahmapurohita devas and is reborn among the Brahmakāyika devas; dies among the Brahmakāyika devas and is reborn again among the Brahmakāyika devas.
[Likewise through] the Brahmapurohita, Parīttābha, Apramāṇābha, Ābhāsvara, Parīttaśubha, Apramāṇaśubha, and Śubhakṛtsna [devas].
It is the same for the pure Ānāgāmin, the merit-born, those of great fruit, and those in the spheres of infinite space, infinite consciousness, nothingness, and neither-perception-nor-non-perception.
Dying from among the gods of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, one may be reborn in the Avīci Hell.
Thus, through successive births, one wanders through the five realms of existence. One must repent of these karmic retributions of sin.
Having seen this, the Bodhisattva gives rise to a heart of great compassion, thinking: "I have been of no benefit to sentient beings;
though I grant them worldly pleasures, when such pleasure reaches its limit, it turns to suffering. I must instead benefit all beings with the eternal bliss of the Buddha-way and Nirvana.
How shall I bring about this benefit? I must apply myself with great vigor to attain true wisdom. Having attained true wisdom, I shall know the true nature of all phenomena."
Supported by the other perfections and used to benefit sentient beings, this is the bodhisattva’s perfection of diligence (*vīrya-pāramitā*).
Seeing those among the hungry ghosts (*preta*) who suffer from hunger and thirst—their eyes sunken and their hair and body-hair long—they run hither and thither.
If they wish to go toward water, the various ghosts guarding the water strike them with iron staves; even if there were no guarding ghosts, the water would naturally dry up. Or at times...
When it rains from heaven, the rain turns into charcoal. Some hungry ghosts are constantly scorched by fire, as if at the end of a kalpa when fires erupt from all the mountains.
Some hungry ghosts are emaciated and run about frantically, their hair and fur disheveled and covering their bodies.
Some hungry ghosts constantly eat excrement and urine, mucus, saliva, vomit, and the residual wash-water from cleansing; at times they go to the side of latrines.
They stand searching for impurities. There are some hungry ghosts who constantly seek the blood from the wombs of women in childbirth to drink;
their bodies resemble scorched trees and their throats are like the eye of a needle. Even if they were given water, it would not suffice for a thousand years.

There are some hungry ghosts who split open their own heads and lick the brain with their hands. There are some hungry ghosts whose forms are like black mountains, with iron chains binding their necks, striking [against them].

They beseech for mercy and take refuge in the wardens of hell. There are also hungry ghosts who, in previous lives, committed the offense of harsh speech, delighting in inflicting coarse words upon other sentient beings.
Because those beings detested them and viewed them as enemies, these offenders fell among the hungry ghosts due to such sins.
For various offenses such as these, they fall into the realm of hungry ghosts and undergo immeasurable suffering. One must repent for this retribution of their sins.
He saw the myriad forms of bitter suffering in the eight great hells. Within the Saṃjīva (Reviving) Great Hell, those undergoing punishment each fought one another;
with malicious hearts and angry contention, they grasped sharp blades and hacked and flayed one another.

They pierced each other with spears, impaled one another on iron forks, struck one another with iron clubs, beat one another with iron staves, and skewered one another with iron spikes, using sharp knives to [mutilate] one another.

They are minced like raw meat and further torn apart with iron claws; each is smeared with the blood of the others. Overwhelmed by agonizing pain, they fall into a stupor from which they have no awareness.
Then, due to the causal conditions of their past karma, a cold wind blows upon them, and the hell-wardens call out to them:
"Ho! You sinners, live again! For this reason, it is called the Reviving Hell (*Saṃjīva*). Immediately, they are restored to life and once more undergo bitter suffering. This...
Beings within this world, due to the causal conditions of their past actions, take pleasure in killing living beings.
For the sake of fields, dwellings, slaves, wives and children, kingdoms, and wealth, they slaughter one another.
Because of the retribution for such various karmas of killing, they undergo these severe punishments. One must repent for the retribution of these sins.
He saw the sinners within the Black Rope Great Hell being constantly measured with black, glowing iron cords by evil rākṣasas, hell-wardens, ghosts, and craftsmen;
they were then made to be cut with iron axes from the hell using men as tools, lengthening them until they were short.

That which is short they cause to grow long; that which is square they make round; that which is round they make square. They sever their four limbs, remove their ears and noses, and lop off their hands and feet.
With great iron saws, they dismember and cut them apart, slicing through the flesh and weighing each piece as it is cut.
Due to the causal conditions of this person’s past conduct—slandering and envying the loyal and virtuous; engaging in false speech, harsh words, double-tongued talk, and frivolous chatter;
and unjustly killing the innocent; or acting as a corrupt official who was cruel, violent, and predatory—because of such various forms of evil speech and treacherous slander.
Therefore, they undergo these punishments.
As they repent for their karmic retribution, they see the evil rākṣasas and hell-wardens within the Saṃghāta Great Hell assuming various forms:
oxen, horses, pigs, sheep, deer, gazelles, foxes, dogs, tigers, wolves, lions, six-tusked elephants, eagles, vultures, and quails. They manifest in all such diverse shapes.
Various birds and beasts with heads [of animals] come forth, swallowing, devouring, gnawing, and tearing at the offenders. Two mountains close together;
a great, glowing-hot iron wheel crushes the offenders, shattering their bodies.

They are pounded in a glowing-hot iron mortar until they are crushed like grapes being squeezed, or like oil being pressed, or like grain being trampled in a threshing floor. Piles of flesh accumulate like a mound; their heads are like mountains, and blood flows.
It becomes a pool. Hawks, vultures, tigers, and wolves each come to scramble and tear at it. This is due to the causal conditions of this person's past karma:

they killed many oxen, horses, pigs, sheep, deer, roe deer, foxes, rabbits, tigers, wolves, lions, six-legged beasts, great elephants, and various birds; they committed many acts of mutual slaughter and injury.
Because of such various birds and beasts, they receive these heads of many birds and beasts in return to come and harm the offenders.
Furthermore, due to their power and influence used to oppress others, or their bullying of the weak and vulnerable, they undergo the retribution of two mountains closing together.

Because of their stinginess, greed, anger, delusion, and fear, they adjudicate matters of light and heavy offense without correct principle; they may destroy the Right Path or distort the True Dharma.
They are crushed by burning iron wheels and pounded in hot iron mortars; they repent for their karmic retribution.
The fourth and fifth are named Raurava (Screaming) and Mahāraurava (Great Screaming).

Within these great hells, the rākṣasa hell-wardens have heads as yellow as gold and eyes from which fire issues; they wear ochre-colored robes, their bodies are firm and tough, and they run with great speed.
Like the wind, his hands and feet were large and long, and his mouth emitted a foul sound. Grasping a trident, he rained down arrows like rain, piercing and shooting at the sinners.

The sinners, driven mad with terror, struck their heads in supplication for mercy. Yet the Great General, showing only slight leniency and slight compassion, immediately led them into the Hot Iron Hell, which was a hundred *yojanas* in length and breadth; there he drove and beat them as they fled, their feet [all...]
They are scorched; fat and marrow flow out like butter being pressed. Iron clubs strike their heads until they are shattered and the brains spill forth like broken jars of curd.
Their bodies are hacked, pierced, sliced, and flayed until they are mangled and putrefied. They are then cast into iron lattice-roofed houses where black smoke billows and stifles them.
As they press against one another, they harbor mutual resentment and malice, each crying out, "Why are you crushing me? Just as they desire to escape, [the doors close].
The gates were already closed, yet he cried out with a loud voice, his sound never ceasing. This was due to the karmic causes and conditions of this person's past deeds:

all resulted from deceiving others with false scales and measures, adjudicating matters unjustly, failing to return entrusted deposits, encroaching upon the lowly and inferior, and tormenting the destitute and widowed.
They cause others to wail and weep; they destroy the walls and towers of cities and ravage human settlements; they inflict injury and plunder, leaving families filled with resentment and poison;
entire cities cry out in lamentation. At times, they employ guile and deception to lure people out and then harm them.
Due to various causes and conditions such as these, they undergo such retribution. I now repent for these karmic offenses.

Those in the Great Screaming Hell (*Mahāraurava*) are all beings of the class that dwells in burrows and is killed by smoke, confined within prisons, or else smoked to death in dark, smoky caves; or those who cast others into wells and plunder their wealth.
For various causes and conditions such as these, they undergo the retribution of the Great Screaming Hell. [I now] repent of these karmic offenses.
In the sixth and seventh hells, Tapana and Pratāpana, there are two great copper cauldrons:

one named Nanda and the other named Upananda (which in the language of Qin means "Joy" and "Great Joy"). They are filled with boiling brine. Rākṣasa demons and hell-wardens cast the sinners into them, just as a cook boils meat.
The people within the cauldrons have their feet up and their heads down, like beans being boiled until cooked.
They become putrid; their bones and joints fall apart, and their skin and flesh separate. Knowing they have rotted away, they are pried out with forks.

Due to the causal conditions of their past karma, a cold wind blows them back to life, and they are cast again into pits of burning charcoal or placed amidst boiling ashes—like fish taken from water and placed upon hot sand.
Furthermore, they are seared by pus and blood as they are cast out from the charcoal pits.
With a bed of flames, they forcibly compel him to sit; from his eyes, ears, nose, mouth, and all his pores, fire erupts everywhere.
This person, in past lives, had troubled and disturbed his parents, teachers, elders, śramaṇas, and brahmins, as well as virtuous people and fields of merit.
Affliction causes the mind to burn with fever. Because of these transgressions, one undergoes the Heat Hell (*tāpana-naraka*).

Repentance for the Retribution of Sins: Perhaps in past lives one boiled and killed silkworm cocoons; or was born to cauterize pigs and sheep; or impaled people on wooden stakes and roasted them alive;
or burned mountains, wilds, villages, Buddhist shrines (*stūpa*), monasteries (*vihāra*), and the abodes of celestial deities; or pushed sentient beings [off cliffs].
They are cast into pits of fire. Through various causes and conditions such as these, they are born in this hell. Regarding the confession of karmic retribution:
one sees the Avīci Hell, four thousand li in length and breadth, with iron walls surrounding it on all sides. Among the seven hells, its location is the deepest.
The rakṣasa jailers strike the sinners with great iron hammers, just as a blacksmith beats out iron. From...
Their heads were flayed, and even their feet were nailed to the ground with five hundred iron spikes, stretching out their bodies like stretched hides of oxen;
they were pulled and dragged against one another until they split apart at the touch of the hands. Hot iron chariots rolled over their bodies, driving them into pits of fire.
They force them to carry glowing coals out [of the hells]. They drive them into the River of Boiling Excrement;

therein dwell venomous insects with iron beaks that enter through their nostrils and emerge from the soles of their feet, or enter through the soles of their feet and emerge from their mouths. Along the path of upright swords, they drive them to run.
Their feet are shattered like minced meat in a kitchen; sharp swords, blades, and spears fly into their bodies.
Like leaves falling from a tree in the frost, they tumble down in disorder with the wind. The hands, feet, ears, noses, limbs, and joints of these sinners are all hacked, flayed, and severed.
Blood flows upon the ground, forming pools. There are two great, evil dogs: the first is named Śyāma, and the second is named Śabala-ayaḥ-mukha.

Their mouths are fierce and powerful, capable of shattering human bones and sinews; their strength exceeds that of tigers and leopards, and they are as ferocious as lions. There is also a great forest of thorns.
The sinners are driven and coerced to climb trees; as they ascend, the thorns point downward, and as they descend, the thorns point upward.
Great-bodied venomous snakes, vipers, scorpions, and malevolent insects swarm to bite them. Large birds with long beaks pierce their heads and devour their brains.
They enter the briny river, drifting up and down with the current; when they emerge, they tread upon ground of glowing red-hot iron and walk upon iron spikes.

Or they are made to sit upon an iron spit; the spit enters from below and is held with tongs. Their mouths are opened and molten copper is poured in. They swallow hot iron balls; when they enter the mouth, the mouth is scorched;
when they enter the throat, the throat is seared; when they enter the belly, the belly burns; all five viscera are consumed by fire, passing straight through until they fall to the ground.
They see only unpleasant sights, constantly smell foul odors, and perpetually touch coarse and rough textures. They encounter various pains and sufferings, becoming bewildered and exhausted;
they may become狂逸 (madly reckless) and impulsive, or hide and flee, or throw things about, or fall down and tumble over.

This person, in their past conduct, committed many great evils and the grave offenses of the five rebellious acts (*pañcānantarya*), severing all roots of goodness. They spoke of the Dharma as non-Dharma, and non-Dharma as Dharma. Truly...

Speaking what is not true, and claiming as true that which is not true; subverting causes and subverting effects; harboring malice and envy toward virtuous people—for these offenses, one enters this hell and undergoes the most severe punishment. This is the confession for the retribution of such sins.
Such are the various eight great hells, which further have sixteen minor hells as their retinues:
eight cold ice hells and eight fiery hells. Within them, the poisonous torments are beyond description or hearing. As for the eight fiery hells: the first is named the Pit of Charcoal;
the second, Boiling Excrement; the third, Burning Forest; the fourth, Sword Forest; the fifth, Path of Blades; and the sixth...
The first is named the Forest of Iron Thorns; the second is named the Salt River; the third is named Copper Stakes. These constitute the eight [hot hells]. As for the eight cold ice hells:
the first is named Arbuda; the second is named Nirarbuda; the third is named Aṭaṭa (the sound of shivering from cold).
The fourth is named Kharasvara (also suffering from a cold voice); the fifth is named Kūṭaśālmalī (also suffering from a harsh voice);

the sixth is named Utpala (the shape of this hell is likened to the blue lotus); the seventh is named Padma (red lotus, where one type of offender undergoes suffering); and the eighth is named Mahāpadma.
These are the eight. If one violates the pure precepts of the monastic way of life, causing laypeople to despise the Buddha-way;

or if one pushes sentient beings into pits of fire; or if one roasts sentient beings over fires while their lives are not yet exhausted—through various causes and conditions such as these, one falls into the Charcoal Pit Hell, where great flames and glowing coals reach the knees and burn the offenders.
Regarding the body: one should repent for the retribution of transgressions.

For instance, if a śramaṇa or brāhmaṇa touches the food of a field of merit with impure hands, or eats it first, or places impure things within it, or pours boiling excrement over another’s body, thereby destroying pure livelihood and sustaining oneself through wrong livelihood.
Due to various causes and conditions such as these, one falls into the Hell of Boiling Excrement. The boiling excrement therein is deep and vast, like the waters of the great ocean.
Within it dwell tiny insects with iron beaks that pierce the heads of the offenders to devour their brains, and break through the bones to eat the marrow.
This is the retribution for one's sins; one must repent.
If one burns grasses and trees, harming various insects, or sets fire to forests for large-scale hunting, the harm is even more extensive.

Due to such various causes and conditions, one falls into the Scorching Forest Hell (*Dāva-dahana-naraka*). There, the grasses and trees are set ablaze to burn the sinners. [This is the retribution for their sins;
now they must repent.]
If one wields swords and blades to fight, injure, or kill; or if one cuts down trees to crush people in order to avenge old grudges;

or if one secretly betrays another despite their having informed one with loyalty, faith, and sincerity—through various causes and conditions such as these, one falls into the Sword-Leaf Forest Hell (*Asipatravana-naraka*).
When the offenders of this hell enter therein, the wind blows the sword-leaves, which slice and cut off their hands, feet, ears, and noses.
They were all caused to fall [into hell]. At that time, there were vultures, eagles, and fierce dogs in the forest that came to devour their flesh.

[The text continues: "Repentance for the retribution of one's sins: whether piercing people with sharp knives, or wounding them with stakes or spears, or cutting off roads, or pulling down bridges..."
The Liang dynasty destroyed the path of the True Dharma and showed people the path of non-Dharma. Due to various causes and conditions such as these, they fell into the Hell of the Path of Blades.
In this Hell of the Path of Blades, among narrow paths on sheer precipices, sharp blades are set upright so that the offenders must pass over them from above.
This is the retribution for their sins; [herein lies] the repentance.

If one commits sexual misconduct, violating the wives of others, or out of greedy attachment craves pleasant touch—and through various causes and conditions such as these—one falls into the Iron Thorn Forest Hell (*ayaḥśālmalīvana*).
There, thorn-trees stand one *yojana* high, upon which dwell great venomous serpents who manifest in the form of beautiful women.
They call out to these sinners, saying, "Come up here and enjoy pleasure with us! The hell-wardens then drive them upward, and the thorns all...
It descends and pierces the sinner; his body is struck and harmed, penetrating the bones and reaching the marrow.

Once it reaches the top of the tree, the transformed woman reverts to her snake form, splitting open the head and entering the belly, boring through holes everywhere until the body is completely mangled and putrefied. Suddenly, he revives once more.
The body was restored to health. The transformed woman again called out to him from beneath a tree. The hell-warden shot an arrow upward at him, calling for him to descend;
the thorn likewise pierced him from above. Once he reached the ground, the transformed woman’s body turned into a venomous serpent, tearing apart the offender’s body.
He then repented for his karmic retribution.
After a long time, he emerges from the Forest of Hot Iron Thorns. Seeing from afar a river that is cool, refreshing, and pleasant, he runs toward it.
Upon entering it, it turns into boiling brine. While the sinner is within, in a mere moment, his skin and flesh fall away and only his bones remain standing in the water.
The hell-warden rākṣasas pull him out with forks and hooks and place him upon the bank. This person—
Due to the causal conditions of past actions—such as harming or killing aquatic creatures like fish and turtles; or at times pushing people and other sentient beings into water;
or throwing them into boiling water, or into ice-cold water—one undergoes this retribution because of various such evil karmic causes and conditions.
This is the confession for the retribution of these sins.
If they are in the Copper Stake Hell, the rākṣasa hell-wardens ask the sinners, "Where have you come from?
They reply, "I am distressed and do not know where I have come from; I suffer only from hunger and thirst.

If they say they are thirsty, the hell-wardens immediately drive the sinners away and force them to sit upon hot copper stakes. They pry open their mouths with iron tongs and pour molten copper into them. If they say...
They sit hungry upon copper spikes and swallow iron balls; as they enter the mouth, the mouth is scorched; as they enter the throat, the throat is seared;
as they enter the belly, the belly burns, and the five viscera are destroyed. Passing straight through, they fall to the ground. This is due to the causal conditions of this person’s past conduct:

having stolen the wealth of others to provide for their own mouths, or having feigned illness to seek out large quantities of ghee, oil, and rock honey from renunciants, or having lacked moral discipline.

Lacking meditative concentration and lacking wisdom, yet receiving many offerings from others, or using harsh speech to wound people—due to various such causes and conditions of past karma, one falls into the Copper Stake Hell. One must repent for these karmic retributions.

If a person falls into the Arbuda hell, where masses of ice accumulate and poisonous winds blow, causing the skin and hair of the sinners to crack and fall off, their flesh and sinews to be severed, and their bones to shatter and marrow to be exposed; yet they immediately become whole and firm again, suffering as before.
This is due to the causal conditions of their past karma: having stripped people during cold months, or having robbed and frozen people, mouthful by mouthful, with firewood and flames.
Or they may become evil nāgas, whose poisonous wrath and fury cause them to release great hailstorms and rain, freezing and harming people;
or they may treat with contempt and slander the Buddha, his disciples, or those who uphold the precepts; or through the four verbal karmas, they commit various grave offenses.
Due to such various causes and conditions as these, they fall into the Arbuda hell; it is the same for the Nirarbuda hell.
In Arbuda, there is a brief interval where one may momentarily find rest; in Nirarbuda, it is without interval, with no time for rest.
As for the three hells of Aṭaṭa, Hahava, and Huhuva, cold winds cause such shivering that the mouth cannot be opened;
these hells are named after the sounds of the cries they utter. In the Utpala hell, the freezing ice is so pervasive that it resembles...
The blue lotus (*utpala*) and the *padma* are like the beautiful lotuses found here in this world;
the *mahā-padma* is the dwelling place of Kokālika. When wise people hear of this, they cry out in alarm: "Alas!

Because of these dharmas of ignorance, hatred, and craving, one undergoes such suffering—emerging and re-entering [the cycle] without end or limit. Thus one should repent for the retribution of one's sins.

We were shrouded by ignorance and did not recognize the causes of transgression within the three realms. Now that we have encountered this site of enlightenment, we are finally able to awaken to this truth.
We take refuge in the Tathāgata Vairocana and the ocean-like assembly of all worthy sages.

We burn incense and scatter flowers, confessing and repenting for all our karmic retributions without daring to conceal anything. By virtue of these causes and conditions, may I and the entire dharma-realm...
May the ocean of sentient beings and the karmic retributions of the three realms all become pure.
Next, the mudrā and dhāraṇī for repentance and the eradication of sins: Oṃ sarva-pāpa-m-eṣyantu praṇamya dharāya svāhā.
(One should recite this three times:
The sins accumulated over a hundred kalpas Are all swept away in a single thought-moment; Like fire consuming dry grass, they are extinguished without remainder.
All evil karma that I have created in the past, Arising from beginningless greed, hatred, and delusion,
Produced by my body, speech, and mind— I now confess it all. Having confessed,
I take refuge with a sincere heart and pay homage to the Honored One, Vairocana Buddha.
○ (Proclamation: Listen, all you people, to these verses on impermanence from the Sūtras:
Wealth and nobility are all impermanent; Where there is meeting, there must be parting. The life of man is like a flash of lightning; Even the powerful must all die.
Impermanence destroys the mountain of jewels; The Mara of Death strips away all fullness.
The Supreme Dharma is eternally firm; one should cultivate heedfulness.
*The Ritual for the Tenfold Vows and Practices of the Sea-Seal Bodhimanda of the Avataṃsaka Sūtra, Volume Three: The Constant and Universal Rite of Prostration and Repentance.*

The Ritual for the Constant and Universal Prostration and Repentance Based on the Tenfold Vows and Practices of the Sea-Seal Samādhi at the Site of Enlightenment from the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha’s Great Vaipulya*,
Volume Four.
Compiled by the Śramaṇa Huìjué, the State-Protecting National Teacher Yíxíng of Cí’ēn Monastery on Mount Yún of Lán, during the Táng Dynasty, based upon the sūtra.
Supplemented with annotations by the Śramaṇa Pūrui of Zai Guang Temple on Mount Cang in Song;
verified by the Buddhist disciple Mu Zeng, Provincial Commissioner of Sichuan, who honors loyalty and righteousness;
and reviewed by the Śramaṇa Du Che of Ji Guang Temple on Chicken Mountain (Jishan).
Tiantai’s Practice of Teaching and Contemplation: The Monk Zhengzhi’s *Zhiding* (Cultivating Stillness), Fourth Session, Part Four:
The Assembly of the Eight Divinities, Including the Four Heavenly Kings.
With all reverence, we pay homage to the inexhaustible Triple Gem.
All these members of the assembly kneel with their right knees on the ground, solemnly holding incense and flowers to make offerings according to the Dharma.
May this ocean-like cloud of offerings pervade the worlds of the ten directions, where palaces adorned with every jewel spontaneously appear, exquisitely and magnificently ornamented.
It surpasses all the adornments of the devas. All kinds of jewel nets completely cover it on every side.
It rains down everywhere clouds of the most sublime and wondrous jewels; it rains down everywhere clouds of all manner of ornaments; it rains down everywhere clouds of all kinds of precious garments;
it rains down everywhere clouds of all kinds of sandalwood incense; it rains down everywhere clouds of all kinds of solid fragrances; it rains down everywhere clouds of all kinds of jewels.
Adorned with clouds of canopies, they universally rain down inconceivable clouds of gathered flowers and universally produce the sounds of inconceivable music.
With such various articles of offering, they constantly perform worship.
Within the infinitely layered Indra-nets, the oceans of Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and holy assemblies receive these clouds of offerings and take them as luminous platforms, vast beyond measure.
The boundaries are immeasurable and inexhaustible. May they perform the work of a Buddha.
Having made offerings, all pay homage with reverence;
next, they present jeweled lattices.
Clouds of offerings such as these— vast oceans of the intrinsic nature of precious jewels, the most excellent emergence of the seven-jeweled mountains,
and so forth— I offer to all the Buddhas and others. Oṃ sarva-tathāgata-arcana-pratīccha-mama.
*Phraṇātsamaing hūṃ*. The *Ratnakūṭa Sūtra* states:
"There is a dhāraṇī named 'Infinite Varieties of Spells,' which can accomplish all things and possesses great efficacy. The dhāraṇī says:
Oṃ smara smara me manaḥ siddharaṃ hūṃ phaṭ svāhā. Next, bind the seal of the Great Amoghapāśa Mantra (the binding of the seal is the same as before):
Oṃ amoghapāśāya mahāvidyārājñe tathātā-mayāya svāhā.
*Kiṃ-dsa-man-da-bra-sa-ra hūṃ.* In the Sanskrit language,
I praise the Buddha,
the Perfectly Awakened One, who is immeasurable, equal to the Dharma-realm and space, profound and vast, without limit or bottom.
The path of language is entirely cut off; the Tathāgata has thoroughly mastered it. In all places he practices the Dharma;
throughout the various lands of the dharma-realm, wherever he goes, he is unimpeded.
If a person can believe and accept the unimpeded omniscience and cultivate the bodhisattva practices, their mind will be immeasurable.
Speaking directly, he praised the Buddha, the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, at the time of his attainment of perfect enlightenment: regarding all meanings, there is nothing observed;
regarding the equality of phenomena, there is no doubt; it is non-dual and signless, without activity and without cessation, immeasurable and boundless, and utterly remote.
Abiding in the Middle Way beyond the two extremes, they transcend all written characters and verbal expressions.
They know the mental activities, faculties, dispositions, inclinations, afflictions, and habitual tendencies of all sentient beings. To state the essential point:

within a single thought-moment, they fully know all phenomena of the three periods of time and universally manifest according to the mental activities, faculties, dispositions, and inclinations of all sentient beings. And...

There is nothing manifested. Therefore, it is said that when the Buddhas, the Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas, attain perfect enlightenment, they obtain body, speech, and mental actions equal in measure to all sentient beings;
they obtain body, speech, and mental actions equal in measure to all dharmas, all lands, all three periods of time, all Buddhas, and all languages. Thus the Tathāgata attains perfect enlightenment.

At the time of awakening, within one's own body, one universally manifests the attainment of perfect enlightenment by all sentient beings, even unto the universal manifestation of all sentient beings entering nirvana;
all are of one and the same nature, namely: the nature of no-nature, no-birth, no-extinction, and no-self.
There is no nature of non-self; indeed, there is even no nature of attaining perfect enlightenment.
Homage to the Vairocana Buddha, the Original Honored One of the Ten Unobstructed Bodies in the Flower Treasury World-Ocean within the Great Vaipulya Buddhāvataṃsaka Sūtra.
Homage to Śākyamuni Buddha, the Greatly Compassionate One who made five hundred vows to save sentient beings from suffering in the five turbidities.
Homage to Bhaisajyaguru-vaiḍūryaprabha-rāja Buddha of the Pūrṇacandra World in the East, who made twelve supreme vows to save sentient beings from suffering in the five turbidities.
Homage to Amitābha Buddha of the Western World of Ultimate Bliss, who, through his forty-eight vows, rescues sentient beings from suffering amidst the five turbidities.

Homage to the Ocean of Perfect Teachings of the Great Vaipulya Buddhāvataṃsaka Sūtra within all the lands as numerous as atoms throughout the entirety of space across the ten directions and three periods of time.
Homage to the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Samantabhadra, who presides over the truth of conduct and vows within the Great Vaipulya Buddha-avatamsaka Sūtra;
homage to Mañjuśrī, who presides over the wisdom of faith, understanding, and realization within the Great Vaipulya Buddha-avatamsaka Sūtra.

Homage to the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva of Great Kindness and Great Compassion, the Thousand-Handed and Thousand-Eyed Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva, Savior from Suffering in the Five Turbidities.

Homage to the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Kṣitigarbha-Rāja, whose great vows are vast and profound, who rescues those suffering in the five turbidities and appears in worlds where no Buddha dwells to comfort the hearts of sentient beings, and who eternally abides in the realm of Yamarāja.
Homage to the ten [stages of] faith Bodhisattvas within all the lands as numerous as atoms throughout the entirety of space across the ten directions and three periods of time.

Homage to the Bodhisattvas dwelling in the ten practices (*daśa-caryā*), the ten dedications (*daśa-pariṇāmanā*), the ten stages (*daśa-bhūmi*), and the stage of Equal Enlightenment (*samyak-saṃbodhi*);
to the assembly of all oceans of Bodhisattvas, numbering as the atoms within the oceans of lands throughout the entire Dharma-realm;
and to the fifty-five locations for the cultivation and realization of the five stages within the final assembly of the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra*, the Great Vaipulya Scripture of the Buddha.
The Noble Sudhana,
a vessel of perfect capacity and superior faculties from the final assembly of the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra*,

who sought the Dharma through a hundred cities and perfected the bodhisattva practices within a single lifetime, serving as a model for practice and realization for the sudden teaching of the末代 (final age).

Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas pay homage to all Buddha-activities— whether in the form of the Dharma-body, the form-body, physical relics, jeweled stupas, or monasteries— within the dust-mote lands of the ten directions and three periods of time throughout the entirety of the realm of empty space,
as well as to the treasuries of the Dharma and the places where the Dharma is preached.
Homage to the assembly of all noble and holy Bodhisattvas, the ocean-like multitude;

to those who have donned the armor of great vows to seek birth in the Pure Land; to those who protect the True Dharma during the final dregs of the summer kingdom; and to the National Preceptors who guard the nation.

With a sincere heart, I take refuge and pay homage to the World-Honored One Vairocana, the Honored One of the Flower Treasury Ocean-World System in the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra*, the Great Vaipulya Scripture of the Buddha.
To all ten directions, I take refuge; may my sins be extinguished, may my pure faith increase, and may I be reborn in the Flower Treasury Ocean.
From the *Sūtra on the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss*:
"Furthermore, Dhṛtarāṣṭra, King of the Gandharvas... [up to] this liberation of the Adornment of Joy.
May I, together with all sentient beings, be reborn in the Sea of Flower Treasury, within the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss."
Next, within the Bodhimanda of the Dharma-realm, to the assembly of Gandharva Kings in the south:
Homage to the Gandharva King Dhṛtarāṣṭra, who possesses the liberation door of attaining mastery in skillful means to gather in all sentient beings.
Homage to the Gandharva King Tree Light, who has attained the liberation door of universally beholding all adornments of merit;
homage to the Gandharva King Pure Eye, who has attained the liberation door of forever severing the sorrow and suffering of all sentient beings and giving rise to the treasury of joy.
Homage to the Gandharva King Flower-Crown, who has attained the liberation door of eternally severing the delusions of wrong views in all sentient beings.
Homage to the One of Joyful Steps Who Universally Benefits, who has attained the liberation door of spreading widely like clouds to universally shade and nourish all sentient beings.
To the Gandharva King Sound, I pay homage;
he possesses the gate of liberation that manifests a vast, wondrous, and beautiful body, causing all beings to attain peace, happiness, and deliverance.
To the Gandharva King Joyfully Shaking Beautiful Eyes, I pay homage.
Homage to the Gandharva King Lion Banner of Wondrous Sound, who has attained the liberation door of the great renown spread throughout all ten directions;
homage to the one who has attained the liberation door of the pure body that manifests all great joy and radiates light, universally emitting jewels.
Homage to the Gandharva King Radiance,
who attains the liberation door of universally nourishing all trees and causing those who see them to rejoice;
and to the Gandharva King Vajra-Tree-Flower-Banner.

Homage to the Gandharva King Universal Manifestation of Adornments, who has attained the liberation door of skillfully entering the realm of all Buddhas and bestowing peace and happiness upon sentient beings;
homage to all such Gandharva Kings as these, who serve as leaders, numbering in infinite measure. All Gandharva Kings.
The ten directions all take refuge; Sins are extinguished and pure faith increases. May [beings] be born within the Flower Treasury Ocean and the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss.
As the Sūtra says: "Furthermore, this was understood by the mind of the King Vistīrṇamukha (Broad-Faced), starting from the King of Kumbhāṇḍas named Vardhana."
May I, together with all sentient beings, be reborn in the Flower Treasury Ocean and within the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss,
furthermore, inside the Bodhimanda of the Dharma-realm. To the host of Kumbhāṇḍa Kings,
namo to the Kumbhāṇḍa King named Increasing Power who has attained the liberation door of destroying all enmity and harm.
Homage to the Kumbhāṇḍa King Nāgendra, who attained the liberation door of the ocean of gates for cultivating boundless practices;
homage to the Kumbhāṇḍa King Vyūhadhvaja, who attained the liberation door of knowing the inclinations of the minds of all sentient beings.
Homage to the Kumbhāṇḍa King Beneficial Conduct, who has attained the liberation door of accomplishing all pure great lights and performing deeds;
homage to the Terrifying One,
who has attained the liberation door of revealing to all sentient beings the path of peace and fearlessness.
Homage to the Kumbhāṇḍa King Wondrous Adornment, who has attained the liberation door of exhausting the ocean of craving and desire of all sentient beings.
Homage to the Kumbhāṇḍa King Peak Wisdom, who has attained the liberation door of the light-cloud that universally manifests in all realms of existence;
homage to the Kumbhāṇḍa King Valiant Arm, who has attained the liberation door of universally emitting light to extinguish heavy obstructions like mountains.
Homage to the Kumbhāṇḍa King Anantaviśuddhapadmākṣa, who has attained the liberation door of the treasury of great compassion that reveals non-retrogression;
homage to the Kumbhāṇḍa King Vipulavaktra, who has attained the liberation door of manifesting bodies that flow through all realms of existence.
Homage to these and others who serve as their leaders, numbering in infinite measure—all the Kumbhāṇḍa kings throughout the ten directions take refuge.
May our sins be extinguished and our pure faith increase; may we be reborn within the Flower Treasury Ocean, the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss.
The Sūtra says: "Furthermore, Vairocana Dragon King... [omitted] ...the Great Dragon Anavatapta is able to realize this.

May I, together with all sentient beings, be reborn in the Flower Treasury Ocean within the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss, and further within the Dharma-realm Bodhimanda, amidst the assembly of dragon kings."
Homage to the Dragon King Virūpākṣa, who has attained the liberation door of extinguishing all the intense sufferings of the nāga realm;
homage to [the one] who has attained the liberation door of transforming his own dragon form within a single thought-moment to manifest the bodies of boundless sentient beings.
Sāgara Dragon King,
Homage to the Liberation Door of Cloud-Sound Banner Dragon King, who, within all realms of existence, speaks the ocean of the Buddha’s boundless names with a pure voice.
Homage to the Dragon King Jvālāmukha, who has attained the liberation door of establishing distinctions within the world-system of the Buddha Universal Manifestation of Boundlessness;
homage to the liberation of causing all sentient beings’ shrouds and entanglements of anger and delusion to be extinguished through the Tathāgata’s compassionate pity.
Homage to the Dragon King Gate-Flame-Eye;
Homage to the Dragon King Cloud-Banner, who has attained the liberation door of the ocean of merit and great joy for all sentient beings.
Homage to the Dragon King Takṣaka, who possesses the liberation door of attaining a voice of pure protection that eliminates all fears;
homage to the Boundless One, who possesses the liberation door of manifesting the physical bodies of all Buddhas and abiding through the succession of kalpas.
To the Dragon King Step,
I pay homage; to the Dragon King Pure Form Swift Speed, who has attained the liberation door of the ocean of great love, joy, and delight that causes all sentient beings to be born [therein].
Homage to the Dragon King Universal Practice Great Sound, who has attained the liberation door of manifesting all-pervasive, equal, pleasing, and unobstructed sounds.
Homage to the Heatless One, who has attained the liberation door of extinguishing all suffering in the world through clouds that universally cover with great compassion.
To the Nāga King Nanda and others who serve as his leaders— those who are infinite in number, all the nāga kings throughout the ten directions—
I take refuge. May my transgressions be extinguished, may my pure faith increase, and may I be reborn in the Flower Treasury Ocean.

who possesses the liberation door of rescuing and protecting evil sentient beings through boundless skillful means— homage to them!
Homage to the Yakṣa King Sovereign Sound, who has attained the liberation door of universally observing sentient beings and skillfully rescuing and protecting them;
homage to [the Yakṣa King] Adorned with Weapons, who has attained the liberation door of being able to provide sustenance and benefit to all extremely weak and afflicted sentient beings.
Homage to the Yakṣa King Sarvāryaguṇasāgaranirghoṣavikurvita-mahājñāna;
homage to the Yakṣa King Samantasarvasattvāvalokanamahākaruṇājñānavikurvita; homage to the Lord of the Flaming Eyes.
To the Yakṣa King Vajranetra, the King of the Forks, who possesses various skillful means for the liberation, benefit, and peace and happiness of all sentient beings, I pay homage.
Homage to the Yakṣa King Vīrabāhu, who has attained the liberation door of universally entering into the meaning of all dharmas;
homage to the Yakṣa King Mahāsena, who is invincible and has attained the liberation door of protecting all sentient beings so that none pass by their path in vain.
Homage to the Yakṣa King Dhanada, who possesses the liberation door of increasing the mass of merit for all sentient beings and causing them to constantly experience happiness;
homage to the Yakṣa King Baladharakūṭa,
who possesses the liberation door of the light of the wisdom and power of the Buddhas arising from compliant recollection.
The King of the Mountain Yakṣas,
Namah to these and others who serve as their leaders, numbering immeasurably— all the Yakṣa Kings throughout the ten directions take refuge.
May my transgressions be extinguished, may pure faith increase, and may I be born in the Flower Treasury Ocean.

Furthermore, the Mahoraga King Sudhi (up to: "This wondrous radiance can skillfully enter [all realms].
May I, together with all sentient beings, be reborn in the Flower Treasury Ocean within the Land of Ultimate Bliss."
Next, within the Dharma-realm Bodhimanda, among the hosts of Mahoraga kings to the south,
is the Mahoraga King Good Wisdom (Kalyāṇamati), who has attained the liberation door of using all supernatural powers and skillful means to cause sentient beings to accumulate merit.
Homage to the Mahoraga King Pure Resonance, who has attained the liberation door of causing all sentient beings to eliminate afflictions and obtain cool, refreshing joy;
homage to the one who has attained the universal liberation door of causing all sentient beings with wholesome or unwholesome thoughts and perceptions to enter the pure Dharma.
I pay homage to the Mahoraga King Gate of Supreme Wisdom Adorned Topknot;
I pay homage to the Mahoraga King Wondrous Eye Lord, who has attained the liberation gate of the equal marks of sovereign mastery over merit that is thoroughly realized and entirely unattached.
Homage to the Mahoraga King Lamp Banner, who has attained the liberation door that reveals all sentient beings and causes them to leave behind the fear of darkness;
homage to the Most Victorious Radiance, who has attained the liberation door of knowing all the virtues of the Buddhas and giving rise to joy.
Homage to the Mahoraga King Dhvaja,
who has attained valorous power as the protector and lord for all sentient beings;
and to the Mahoraga King Siṃhahanu.
Homage to the Mahoraga King Adorned with All Mysterious Sounds, who has attained the liberation door of causing all sentient beings to give rise to boundless joy and bliss through recollection;
homage to the one who has attained the liberation door of reaching the perfection of immovability regarding all objects of focus and fulfilling the ultimate shore.
Homage to the Mahoraga King Sumerumūrdhan;
homage to the Mahoraga King Lovely Light, who reveals the path of liberation and equality for all sentient beings who are unequal.
Homage to these and others who serve as their leaders, numbering in the infinite. All the Mahoraga Kings throughout the ten directions take refuge;
may their sins be extinguished and their pure faith increase, and may they be born within the Flower Treasury Ocean in the Pure Land of Sukhāvatī.

"May I, together with all sentient beings, be reborn in the Flower Treasury Ocean and within the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss, inside the Dharma-realm Bodhimanda," [followed by] the assembly of Kinnara Kings.
Homage to the Kinnara King Sunetra-prabhāsa, who has attained the liberation door of universally producing all karma of joy and bliss; homage to the Kinnara King Subhūṣita-puṣpa,
who has attained the liberation door of being able to produce unsurpassed Dharma-joy and causing all beings to receive peace and happiness.
Homage to the Kinnara King Dhvaja,
who has attained the liberation door of the treasury of vast and pure faith and understanding that fulfills all merits;
and to the Kinnara King Citravyūha.
Homage to the King of the Nāras, Joyful Roar, who has attained the liberation door of producing all delightful sounds at will so that those who hear them are freed from sorrow and fear;
and homage to the Jewel who has attained the liberation door of great compassion, establishing all sentient beings and causing them to awaken to their objects of focus.
I pay homage to the Kinnara King Tree Radiance, who has attained the liberation door of manifesting all bodies of exquisite form;

I pay homage to the Kinnara King Universal Delight to Behold, who has attained the liberation door of fully knowing the karma from which all supreme adornments arise. I pay homage to the Supreme... [liberation door].
Homage to the Kinnara King Jyotiṣprabha-vyūha;
homage to the Kinnara King Sūkṣma-puṣpa-ketu, who has attained the liberation door of skillfully observing all worldly karmic retributions.
Homage to the Kinnara King Earth-Shaking Power, who has attained the liberation door of constantly initiating all activities for the benefit of sentient beings.
Homage to the Lord of Majestic Ferocity, who has attained the liberation door of skillfully knowing the minds of all kinnaras and expertly guiding and subduing them.
The Kinnara King Namah and others were their leaders, numbering in infinite measure. All the Kinnara Kings throughout the ten directions take refuge:
may our sins be extinguished, our pure faith increase, and may we be born in the Flower Treasury Ocean.
In the *Sukhāvatīvyūha Sūtra*, it says:
"Furthermore, the Great Swift-Force Garuḍa King... [as far as] the Dragon-Sound Liberation is able to do so."
May I, together with all sentient beings, be reborn in the Flower Treasury Ocean, within the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss, and further,
within the Bodhimanda of the Dharma Realm, as part of the assembly of the Garuḍa Kings.
Homage to the One Who Has Attained the Unattached and Unobstructed Eye, the Gate of Liberation that Universally Observes the Realms of Sentient Beings, the Great Swift One.
Homage to the Garuḍa King Bala,
who has attained the liberation door of universally abiding in the Dharma-realm to teach and transform sentient beings; and to the Garuḍa King Indestructible Jewel-Crest.
Homage to the Garuḍa King Pure and Swift, who has attained the liberation door of the power of diligence that universally accomplishes the pāramitās;
homage to the [Garuḍa King] Adorned with Non-retrogressive Resolve, who has attained the liberation door of entering the realm of the Tathāgatas through the power of valor.
The Kinnara King Namode rjubuddhacaryāvipulajñānasāgaravimokṣamahāsāgarasthānasaṃdhāraṇabala.
Homage to the Garuḍa King Firm Dharma Pure Light, who has attained the liberation door of the wisdom that discerns the distinctions of infinite sentient beings;
homage to the Garuḍa King Wondrously Adorned Topknot, who has attained the liberation door of adorning the city of the Buddha-dharma.
Homage to the Garuḍa King Universal Manifestation of Swift Prowess, who has attained the liberation door of indestructible power of equality;
homage to the Universal Observer Ocean, who has attained the liberation door of manifesting forms while knowing the bodies of all sentient beings.
Homage to the Garuḍa King who has attained the liberation door of the wisdom of conduct for entering universally into the deaths and births of all sentient beings;
the Garuḍa King Dragon-Sound Great-Eye.
Homage to these and others who serve as their leaders, numbering in infinite quantities—all the Garuḍa Kings throughout the ten directions take refuge.
May my transgressions be extinguished and my pure faith increase; may I be born within the Flower Treasury Ocean in the Pure Land of Sukhāvatī.
The Sūtra says: Furthermore, Rāhu, King of the Asuras... [up to] "praised by this King of Wondrous Sound.

"May I, together with all sentient beings, be reborn in the Flower Treasury Ocean, within the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss, and further within the Bodhimanda of the Dharma-realm," [Thus spoke] the assembly of Asura Kings.
Homage to the Asura King Rāhu, who has attained the liberation door of manifesting as the Honored and Victorious Lord for great assemblies.
Homage to the Asura King Vemacitrin, who has attained the liberation door of manifesting immeasurable kalpas.
Homage to the Asura King Kuśala-māyā-vidhi, who has attained the liberation door of extinguishing all the suffering of sentient beings and causing them to be purified.
Homage to the Asura King Mahāparivāra, who has attained the liberation door of self-adornment through the cultivation of all ascetic practices.
Homage to the Asura King Bhañji, who has attained the liberation door of shaking the infinite realms of the ten directions;
homage to the Asura King Samantaprabha, who has attained the liberation door of establishing all sentient beings through various skillful means.
Homage to the Asura King Subhavyūha-dṛḍhacaryā, who attained the liberation door of the pure accumulation of indestructible roots of goodness that purify all defiled attachments;
homage to the Asura King Mahāhetu-prajñā, who attained the liberation door of the lord of great compassion’s power free from doubt.

Homage to the Asura King Manifesting Supreme Virtue, who attained the liberation door of universally causing all to see the Buddha, serving and making offerings to him, and cultivating all roots of goodness;
homage to the Asura Good Sound, who attained the liberation door of the certain and impartial practice that universally enters all realms of existence.
The Rākṣasa King Namu and others as his leaders, numbering immeasurably— all the Asura Kings throughout the ten directions take refuge.
May their transgressions be extinguished, their pure faith increase, and may they be born in the Flower Treasury Ocean.
In the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss, next is the repentance for the transgression of killing.
I take refuge in the infinite Jewels of the Buddha, Dharma, and Sangha, as vast as a celestial net; in Vairocana Tathāgata; and in Samantabhadra and Mañjuśrī.

The assembly of noble ones gathered like the ocean, and the mundane and supramundane deities, by virtue of their compassionate original vows, radiate great light that illuminates this Dharma assembly.
May they bear witness, protect, and sustain us; may they look upon us with pity and compassionately receive us. I pray that for myself and the ocean of all sentient beings, from time immemorial...
Up until this very moment, the ocean of karma remains inexhaustible, with its Indra-net of interpenetrating layers. I now openly confess and repent for all karmic offenses of killing.
Regarding the offense of killing, the *Mahāprajñāpāramitā-śāstra* states: "If it is truly a sentient being, and one knows it to be a sentient being, yet one gives rise to the intention [to kill]..."
Desiring to kill and thereby depriving one of life, the bodily karma produced at that moment is called the offense of killing.
Other acts, such as binding, confinement, and flogging, are auxiliary methods for killing. Furthermore, one incurs the offense of killing by killing another, not by killing one's own body.
To kill a sentient being while knowing it is one constitutes the sin of killing. This is not like killing someone at night, mistaking them for a tree stump;

that is intentional killing, which incurs the sin of killing, for it is not unintentional. To kill with a sense of satisfaction incurs the sin of killing. When the life-faculty (*jīvitendriya*) is severed, this is the sin of killing.
It is not merely a bodily action (*kāyakarma*) that inflicts a wound; it is the sin of killing. It is not merely a verbal instruction that constitutes the sin.
The Imperial Edict on Oral Instruction states: "This sin of killing is not merely a matter of the mind conceiving evil; such things as these are called the characteristics of the sin of killing.

Furthermore, one who kills living beings will undergo various physical and mental sufferings in both this life and future lives, whereas one who does not kill is free from these manifold difficulties—this constitutes a great benefit.
Furthermore, the practitioner reflects: 'I cherish my own life and love my own body; so too does that [other being]...'"
It is likewise so. How would this differ from my own case? For this reason, one should not kill living beings.
Furthermore, if one kills, they will be censured by virtuous people and envied by their enemies; because they have taken another's life, they will always live in fear and be loathed by others.
At the time of death, their mind will be filled with regret, and they shall fall into hell. Even if they are reborn among animals, or emerge as a human being, they will always...
Life is short. Furthermore, killing is the gravest among all transgressions. Why is this? When people face the urgency of death, they do not spare even their most precious treasures;
they prioritize nothing but the preservation of life. It is like a merchant who has entered the sea to gather jewels;

as he is about to emerge from the great ocean, his ship suddenly breaks apart and his precious treasures are lost entirely. He rejoices and, raising his hand, says: "How nearly I have lost these great treasures! The assembly...
People marveled at his words, saying, "You have lost your wealth and escaped in the nude; why do you joyfully say that you nearly lost a great treasure?
He replied, "Among all treasures, human life is foremost. People seek wealth for the sake of life, but they do not seek life for the sake of wealth.
For this reason, the Buddha taught that among the ten unwholesome paths of action, killing is the first, and it is likewise the most serious among the five precepts."
First: If a person cultivates various kinds of merit and virtue but lacks the precept against killing, it will be of no benefit. Why is this?
Although one may be born into a position of wealth and status with great power and influence, if one lacks a lifespan, who can experience such pleasure?
For this reason, it is known that among all other offenses, the offense of killing is the most grave; and among all virtues, non-killing is the foremost.
First: Among all things in the world, the cherishing of life is foremost. How is this known?

All people in the world willingly endure punishments—such as mutilation and flogging—in order to protect their lives. Furthermore, throughout the three times and the ten directions, the Buddha is the most honored.
As the Buddha told the lay follower Nandika: "There are ten kinds of offenses for killing living beings. First, the mind is constantly..."
1. Their poison will remain destructive, continuing without end from lifetime to lifetime. 2. Sentient beings will loathe them; their eyes will take no pleasure in seeing them. 3.
They will constantly harbor evil thoughts and contemplate wicked deeds. 4. Sentient beings will fear them as if they were seeing snakes or tigers. 5.

Their hearts will be filled with terror when they sleep, and they will remain uneasy even when awake. 6. They will frequently experience nightmares. 7. After the end of their lives, they will be driven by madness and terror.
One fears death. Eighth, one plants the causes and conditions for a short life. Ninth, at the breaking up of the body and the end of life, one falls into hell.
Tenth, if one emerges as a human being, one will always be short-lived. Furthermore, the practitioner contemplates that all who possess life...
Even down to the parasites within the body, all cherish their own lives. How can one, for the sake of clothing and food for oneself, kill sentient beings?
We were shrouded by ignorance and did not recognize the karmic cause of the sin of killing; now that we have encountered this site of enlightenment, we are finally able to awaken.

I know. I take refuge in the Tathāgata Vairocana and the ocean-like assembly of all worthy and holy ones. I offer incense and scatter flowers, confessing and repenting for the karmic offenses of taking life.
I dare not conceal them. By these causes and conditions, may the grave sins of killing committed by myself and the ocean of sentient beings throughout the Dharma-realm be entirely purified.
Next, the mudrā and mantra for repentance and the eradication of sins: Oṃ sarvapāpam me kṣayaṃ kuru svāhā.
(Recite three times.)
Sins accumulated over a hundred kalpas are entirely swept away in a single thought; Like fire consuming dry grass, they are extinguished without remainder.
All the evil karmas I have created in the past Arise entirely from beginningless greed, hatred, and delusion.
Whatever has arisen from my body, speech, and mind— I now confess it all.
Having confessed, with a sincere heart I take refuge and pay homage to the Honored One, Vairocana Buddha.
○ (Proclamation: Listen, all you people, to these verses on impermanence from the Sūtra:
Seeing the signs of illness and death in others, Yet failing to realize it for oneself— When the signs of decay arrive, One suffers even unto one's own distress.
With a mind clouded by negligence, One constantly delights in sensory objects.
Unaware that death follows one, One constantly fails to abandon greed and desire. Delighting in play and indulging in the pleasures of the world, one acts with negligence;
The army of Death is about to arrive, Destroying all like a lethal poison.
Exert yourself and observe with diligence, So that afflictions do not arise; Should afflictions nevertheless arise, [one must strive to subdue them].

Universally seeing the lands of the ten directions, and also seeing the Buddhas therein,

To speak directly in praise of the Buddha is like a great mountain of jewels; it brings benefit to all sentient beings. The Buddha-mountain is likewise, universally benefiting the world.

Seeing the Buddha is likewise able to eliminate all thirst and craving.

like the sea that possesses manifold jewels, those who seek them are all satisfied. The wisdom that requires no teacher is also thus.
