Just as a skilled illusionist displays various phenomena, so too is the Buddha’s wisdom: it manifests all powers of mastery.
Just as the wish-fulfilling gem Can satisfy all desires, So too is the Most Victorious One;
He fulfills all pure aspirations. Just as a bright and pure jewel Universally illuminates all things, The Buddha’s wisdom is likewise;
It universally illuminates the bodies of all living beings. Just as a jewel with eight facets...
Equally beholding all directions, the Unobstructed Lamp is likewise;

Next is the repentance for the sin of stealing.
I only pray that the inexhaustible Jewels of the Buddha, Dharma, and Sangha, as vast as the celestial net; Vairocana Tathāgata;

the assembly of holy beings in the ocean-like gathering of Samantabhadra and Mañjuśrī; and all mundane and supramundane deities—by virtue of your compassionate original vows, may you emit great radiance to illuminate this Dharma assembly.
May you bear witness, protect, and remember us; may you compassionately take us into your care.

I pray that I and the ocean of all sentient beings, from beginningless time until this very moment, shall confess and repent for all karmic offenses of theft—exhaustless as an ocean and as vast as a layered Indra-net.
Regarding theft, the *Mahāprajñāpāramitā-śāstra* states: "Knowing that it is another's property, one conceives the intent to steal;
taking the object and moving it from its original location so that it belongs to oneself—this is called stealing. To not do so is called non-stealing.

All other preparatory means, calculations, and even grasping with the hand before the object has left the ground are termed auxiliary methods of stealing. There are two kinds of property: that which belongs to others..."
There is [the offense]. Not to leak [the secret] to others. To take property belonging to another constitutes the sin of theft.

Property belonging to another is also of two kinds: first, that within a village; second, that in open space. If one takes property from these two locations with the intent to steal, one incurs the sin of theft.
If the object is in open space, one should investigate to know to whose kingdom it is near; that object must have an owner. One should not...
Take it up as explained in the Vinaya. The various forms of not stealing are called the characteristics of non-stealing.
Question: What are the benefits of non-stealing? Answer: Human life has two aspects: the internal and the external. If one seizes another's wealth and property...
This is what constitutes the taking of external life. Why is this? Life depends upon food, drink, clothing, bedding, and so forth for its sustenance;
if these are plundered or stolen, it is called the taking of external life. For this reason, a person of wisdom should not plunder or steal.
Furthermore, one should reflect for oneself: even if one plunders and seizes goods to provide for oneself and, though the body may be satisfied, one will inevitably die nonetheless.
Upon death, one enters hell. Although one’s family and relatives may share in happiness together, one alone must undergo the retribution for one’s sins, and they cannot rescue one.
Having attained this contemplation, one should refrain from stealing. Furthermore, there are two kinds of taking what is not given: first, theft; [the second is robbery].
The second is robbery (*haraṇa*). These two together are termed "taking what is not given" (*adattādāna*). Within taking what is not given, theft is the most serious.
Why? Because all people sustain themselves through wealth; yet to break into houses or leap over walls to steal it is the most impure act. Why?
Because one who lacks power and is superior [in strength] steals out of fear of death. Therefore, among acts of plundering, theft is the gravest offense. Question:
[Question: It is said that there are those who plunder, and in this world, some praise them for their prowess. Why should one let go of such plundering? [Answer:
To steal what has not been given is an unwholesome characteristic. Although there may be degrees of severity within the act of plundering, [the nature of the offense remains the same].
Both are unwholesome. It is like fine food mixed with poison and coarse food mixed with poison; though the quality of the food differs, the presence of the poison is no different.
It is also like stepping on fire in either light or darkness; though day and night differ, the burning of the foot is one and the same.

Thus, the foolish people of this world do not recognize the retribution of sin and merit across the three periods of time, nor do they possess a heart of benevolence and compassion. When they see someone using force to encroach upon others, they [encourage it] by their own strength...

To seize the wealth of others and to praise such an act as being "strength" is condemned by all Buddhas and noble sages, who are compassionate toward all beings and have fully realized that the consequences of one's actions throughout the three periods of time are inexhaustible; therefore, they do not commend it.

Thus, one should know that the sin of robbery is in every way unwholesome and is something that virtuous people and practitioners do not do. As the Buddha taught, there are ten offenses regarding taking what is not given. What are these ten?

First, the owner of the goods is constantly angry; second, there is grave suspicion (the suspicion of one who has committed a grave offense); third, acting at an improper time without due deliberation.
Fourth, associating with evil people and distancing oneself from the virtuous and good. Fifth, destroying the signs of goodness. Sixth, incurring the wrath of the authorities.
Seventh, having one's wealth and property confiscated. Eighth, planting the causes and conditions for the karma of poverty. Ninth, falling into hell after death.
Tenth, if reborn as a human, seeking wealth through toil and hardship; such wealth is shared among five parties: the king, thieves, fire, water, and ungrateful heirs.
Fire is like water; even if one does not use it for one's own dear children, it will be lost even if buried away. We repent for the retribution of our sins.
Enveloped by ignorance, we did not recognize the causal nature of the offense of theft. Now that we have encountered this site of practice, we have finally come to realize it.
We take refuge in the Tathāgata Vairocana and the ocean-like assembly of all worthy and holy ones. We burn incense and scatter flowers.

I confess and repent for the karmic offenses of stealing; I dare not conceal them. By virtue of these causes and conditions, may the grave sins of stealing committed by myself and the ocean-like assembly of sentient beings within the Dharma-realm all be purified.
Next, the mudrā and mantra for repentance and the eradication of transgressions: Oṃ sarvapāpam me kṣayaṃ kuru svāhā.
(Recite three times.)
Sins accumulated over a hundred eons are entirely swept away in a single thought; like fire consuming dry grass, they are extinguished without remainder.
All the evil karma I have created in the past arose solely from beginningless greed, hatred, and delusion.
Whatever has arisen from my body, speech, and mind, I now confess it all.
Having confessed, I take refuge with a sincere heart and pay homage to the Honored One, Vairocana Buddha.
○ (Proclamation: Listen, all you gathered, to these verses on impermanence from the Sūtra:
Desires cause one to whirl in the eddies of saṃsāra; In the midst of them, there is constant suffering and distress.
How can a foolish person give rise to love and delight for desires? They are like poisonous flowers of exquisite color, Or like touching the flames of a fierce fire.
Sensual pleasures are also like this: In the end, one undergoes great suffering and distress.
Just as adding more fuel to a fire makes its flames impossible to extinguish, And it can burn both oneself and others, So too are sensual pleasures.

*Kiṃ dsa samanta bhasara hūṃ.* In the Sanskrit language,
this praises the Buddha:
All Buddhas of the three times, Whose Dharma-body is entirely pure, Manifest according to those who are to be transformed.
Universally beholding the wondrous form-body, which is undifferentiated throughout the dharma-realm and has no point of dependence, yet within the world-systems manifests infinite bodies.
The Buddha-body is neither a transformation nor is it not a transformation; within the state of non-transformation, it manifests the forms of transformations.
He spoke directly in praise of the Buddha,
the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, the Unsurpassed King of Physicians, who, throughout immeasurable hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of kalpas,
has refined and prepared the medicinal drugs of the Dharma until they were fully perfected, and who has cultivated and mastered all skillful means and the power of great vidyā-mantras.
They have all reached the other shore. They are well able to eliminate the diseases of affliction of all sentient beings and abide for immeasurable eons.
Their bodies are pure; they are free from discursive thought and free from active exertion, yet they never cease performing any of the Buddha-works.
Sentient beings who behold them find that all their diseases of affliction are completely extinguished. This is the Tathāgata.

Next is the repentance for the offense of sexual misconduct:
I pray that the inexhaustible Buddha, Dharma, and Sangha jewels of the Indra’s Net; Vairocana Tathāgata; the assembly of holy beings of Samantabhadra, Mañjuśrī, and the ocean-like gathering;
and all mundane and supramundane deities, by virtue of your compassionate original vows, may emit great radiance to illuminate this dharma assembly.
May you bear witness and protect us with your mindful attention; may you compassionately take us into your care.

I pray that for myself and the ocean of all sentient beings, from beginningless time until this very moment, we confess and repent for all the karmic offenses of sexual misconduct—exhaustless as an ocean and as vast and intricate as a celestial net of Indra.
We have been thus from immeasurable kalpas until this very day: addicted to female beauty, we make no distinction between kin and stranger;

our lust is so rampant that we disregard whether a person is beautiful or ugly. Stained by the objects of desire, we are as if bound by ropes; chasing after emotions and forms, we are like those who are crazed or intoxicated.
The Bodhisattva rebukes sensual desire, for the sutras state: "Female beauty is the shackles of the world for ordinary beings."
One becomes attached and cannot extricate oneself. Female beauty is a grave affliction in the world; because of it, ordinary people reach their deaths.
That one cannot escape female beauty is a calamity of the world; when ordinary people encounter it, no misfortune arises that does not follow.

Once a practitioner has attained the ability to renounce it, if they look back with longing, this is like having escaped from prison only to return and think of re-entering, or like emerging from madness only to think of falling into it again.

Having attained health, they take pleasure in it; having recovered from illness, they long for the sickness itself. The wise feel pity for them, knowing that such people are mad and deluded, and that their death is imminent.
Ordinary people cherish form and are willing to become its servants, galloping after it for the rest of their lives.

One undergoes toil and hardship for its sake; even if the axe, the stake, or being hacked to pieces inch by inch, and the clash of spears and arrows should all come upon one, one would accept it with a willing heart and not regard it as a calamity.
A madman delights in his madness and does not know it to be a fault. If a practitioner can cast it aside and disregard it, this is to break the yoke and shed the shackles.
Free from evil madness and loathsome disease, one departs from all misfortunes and calamities; being both secure and auspicious, one escapes from the prison.
They shall forever be free from affliction and hardship. Such is the characteristic of women: their speech is like honey, yet their hearts are like poison.

It is as if a clear, still pool or a mirror-like lake were inhabited by a venomous dragon, or as if a golden mountain or a jeweled cave were inhabited by a malevolent beast. One should recognize this danger.
One must not associate with them. Domestic discord arises from women; they destroy homes and ruin clans. The crimes of women are truly like hidden predators:
they extinguish a person’s wisdom and clarity, much like a hunting encirclement from which few escape, or like a high net.
Flocks of birds fall into it and cannot fly away. It is like a dense net; when schools of fish cast themselves into it, their entrails are ripped out and their bellies torn open.
It is also like a dark pit; those without eyes who cast themselves into it are like moths rushing into a flame. Therefore, the wise, knowing this, keep far away from it.
One does not suffer its harm; one loathes it as foul and is not deluded by it. Failing to awaken to this Dharma, I now repent for all of it.
Furthermore, the *Mahāprajñāpāramitā-śāstra* states: "As for sexual misconduct (*kāmamithyācāra*):
if a woman is protected by her parents, brothers, sisters, husband, sons, or by the laws of the world or the Dharma-kings, to violate her is called sexual misconduct. Even if there is one who..."
Guarding: guarding by means of the Dharma. What is guarding by the Dharma? All women, whether ordained or lay, who receive the one-day precepts (upavāsa)—this is called guarding by the Dharma.
If one uses force, wealth, or seduction and deception; or if one’s own wife is observing the precepts, is pregnant, or is nursing an infant;
or if one engages in sexual intercourse by an improper path, or even makes a pact with a prostitute using a flower garland as a token—such acts constitute an offense.
This is called sexual misconduct (*kāmamithyācāra*). Refraining from such various acts is called abstaining from sexual misconduct. Question:

If one guards against a person but feels aversion toward the Dharma, or guards against the Dharma while breaking [the rules regarding] persons, this should be termed sexual misconduct. If one has one’s own wife, why would it be considered misconduct? Answer: [Because...]
Once she has received and accepted the one-day precepts (*upavāsa*), she falls within the category of the Dharma. Although she was originally a wife, she now possesses no autonomy;

at the time of receiving the precepts, she is not under the protection of her husband. Furthermore, a pregnant woman, because her body is heavy, finds her former habits distasteful, and moreover, [sexual intercourse] would harm the fetus.
When nursing an infant, if one indulges with the mother, the milk will dry up. Furthermore, because her mind is attached to lustful desire, she no longer maintains protection [over herself].

Child, when it is in a place that is not the proper way, it is not the female organ; the woman’s mind does not find pleasure in it, yet one forcibly applies oneself through what is improper—therefore, this is called sexual misconduct (*kāmamithyācāra*).
To refrain from such an act is called abstaining from sexual misconduct. Question: If the husband does not know, see, or suffer from it, what fault is there for the other? Answer:
Because it is improper (*mithyā*), and since it is named "improper," it is therefore incorrect (*asamyak*). This is so.
Therefore, there is sin. Furthermore, this involves various faults and transgressions. The affection between husband and wife consists of two bodies sharing one essence;
to seize what another loves and to shatter their fundamental heart is called being a thief. There are further grave sins:
an evil reputation and a foul name, being loathed by others, little joy and much fear—fearing execution or punishment, and fearing that the husband or bystanders might discover [the act]. Much...
To harbor false speech is what the noble ones condemn; it is the gravest of all sins. Furthermore, one who is prone to lewdness should reflect:
"My own wife and the wives of others are both women; in their physical form and emotional nature, there is no difference between them.
Why, then, do I give rise to deluded thoughts and follow such perverse intentions? One who engages in sexual misconduct ruins and loses both this life and the next."
Joy. Furthermore, by exchanging one's own position with that of another and thereby restraining the mind: if another were to violate my wife, I would feel bitter resentment;
yet if I were to violate another’s, how would they be any different? By exercising self-restraint through empathy for oneself, one should refrain from such acts.

Furthermore, as the Buddha taught, those who commit sexual misconduct will later fall into the Sword-Tree Hell (*asipattravana-naraka*), where they undergo all manner of suffering. Even if they eventually emerge to become human again, their family...
The Way is not harmonious. One constantly encounters lewd women; their depravity and cruelty, and their lustful transgressions, become a source of affliction.
They are like vipers and like great fires; if one does not avoid them with urgency, calamity will surely follow. As the Buddha has taught, there are ten offenses of sexual misconduct.
First, she will constantly be threatened with harm by her husband, the one with whom she has illicit relations. Second, the husband and wife will lack harmony and will constantly quarrel and dispute.
Third, all unwholesome qualities will increase day by day, while all wholesome qualities will diminish day by day.
Fourth, one does not protect one's person; one’s wife and children become orphaned and widowed. Fifth, one’s wealth and property diminish daily.
Sixth, various evil deeds arise, and one is constantly suspected by others. Seventh, one is not loved or delighted in by relatives and acquaintances.
Eighth, one plants the karmic causes and conditions for enmity. Ninth, when the body breaks up and life ends, one dies and enters hell. Tenth, if one emerges [from there],...
If a woman has many men as husbands, or if a man’s wife is not chaste— due to various causes and conditions such as these—
one does not commit what is called sexual misconduct.

We have been shrouded by ignorance and failed to recognize the karmic causes of sexual misconduct. Now that we have encountered this place of practice, we are finally able to awaken to this knowledge.
We take refuge in the Tathāgata Vairocana and the ocean-like assembly of all worthy sages. We burn incense and scatter flowers.
I openly confess and repent for the karmic offenses of sexual misconduct; I dare not conceal them.
By this cause and condition, may the grave sins of sexual misconduct of myself and the ocean-like assembly of sentient beings within the Dharma-realm all become purified.
Next, the mudrā and mantra for repentance and the eradication of transgressions: Oṃ sarvapāpam me kṣayaṃ kuru svāhā.
(Recite three times.)
Sins accumulated over a hundred eons are entirely swept away in a single thought; like fire consuming dry grass, they are extinguished without remainder.
All the evil karmas I have created in the past arose from beginningless greed, hatred, and delusion.
Whatever has arisen from my body, speech, and mind, I now confess it all.
Having confessed, I take refuge with a sincere heart and pay homage to the Honored One, Vairocana Buddha.
○ (Proclamation: Listen, all of you, to these verses on impermanence from the Sūtra:
Suffering is boundless, With craving as its root. Craving causes all sentient beings To be unable to escape;
The heart of craving is difficult to abandon, Sticking fast like sticky glue.
Therefore, one should sever craving and diligently seek the unsurpassed path;
for in this world, the attainment of a human body is most difficult to obtain.
When a man is able to seek his own benefit, if he does not seek it at this time, how will he ever again be able to possess such a state?
If my karmic offenses have not yet been extinguished, I fear that death may arrive before me;
what means or plan is there for escape? I only pray that you will swiftly rescue and deliver me.

The Brahma-voice praises the Tathāgata as free from discrimination, Transcending the world and surpassing all calculation. The appearance of all Teachers of the Three Realms is likewise:
Just like the pure orb of the sun, It does not coexist with the darkness of night.
And it is said that on such and such a day and night, the Dharma of all Buddhas is thus:
the kalpas of all three times do not coincide with the Tathāgata, yet he speaks of the Buddhas of the three times; such is the Dharma of the Guide—these are the direct words praising the Buddha.
The Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, appears by means of immeasurable dharmas;
he does not appear through a single condition nor through a single matter, for it is through these that the appearance of the Tathāgata is accomplished (this is the general characterization).

He raises a great cloud of Dharma and rains down a great rain of Dharma, which can extinguish the afflictions of all sentient beings (the first), and can give rise to the roots of goodness in all sentient beings (the second).
1) It can cease all the delusions of view (*dṛṣṭi-kleśa*) of all sentient beings; 2) it can accomplish the jewel-treasure of all wisdom and dharmas;

3) it can discern the mental inclinations and joys of all sentient beings; 4) it rains down the single-flavored water of the Dharma of great compassion; 5) it preaches the Dharma according to what is appropriate, with immeasurable distinctions;
6) it first gives rise to the wisdom of the various practices of bodhisattvas, and subsequently gives rise to the roots of goodness and various practices of śrāvakas.

Wisdom. Next, there is the wisdom regarding the various conditioned roots of goodness and practices of other sentient beings. This is the rain of the Dharma of a single flavor, which accords with the differences in their capacities (the seventh).

Homage to the Mountain Spirit Sovereign of Universal Illumination and High Banner, who has attained the liberation door of purifying the faculties by observing the inclinations of the hearts of all sentient beings.
Homage to Jewel-Crest Free from Dust, who has attained the liberation door of tireless and diligent vigor throughout oceans of boundless eons.

The Mountain-Ruling Spirit of the South, Namah, who possesses the liberation door of universally awakening through the light of boundless merit, and the Mountain-Ruling Spirit who illuminates the ten directions.
Homage to the Mountain Deity Great Power Radiance Lord, who has attained the gate of liberation that brings oneself to maturity and causes sentient beings to abandon delusion and attain liberation;
homage to the Mountain Deity Universal Victory of Majestic Light, who has attained the gate of liberation that uproots all suffering so that none remains.
Homage to the Mountain Deity, Sovereign of the Subtle and Secret Radiant Orb, who manifests the light of the teaching of the Dharma and reveals the liberation and merit of all Tathāgatas.
Homage to the Mountain Deity Sovereign of Universal Vision, who has attained the liberation door of causing all sentient beings to increase their roots of goodness even within dreams;
homage to the Mountain Deity Sovereign of Vajra-Firm Eyes, who has attained the liberation door of manifesting an infinite ocean of great meaning.
Homage to these and other such deities who serve as their leaders, numbering in infinite quantities. All you mountain-deity lords of the ten directions, we take refuge in you;
may our sins be extinguished, our pure faith increase, and may we be reborn in the Flower Treasury Ocean.
The Sūtra on the Land of Ultimate Bliss states:
Furthermore, the Earth-Ruling Spirit named Universal Virtue Pure Flower (up to) Universal Sustainer, having seen [this], gives rise to joy.
May they, together with all sentient beings, be reborn in the Sea of Flower Treasury within the Land of Ultimate Bliss.
Next, within the Bodhimanda of the Dharma-realm, among the host of Earth-Ruling Goddesses,

[I take refuge in] the Earth-Ruling Goddess named Universal Virtue Pure Flower, who possesses the liberation door of universally observing all sentient beings with a mind of compassion at every moment of thought.
Homage to the Earth-Ruling Spirit Firmly Adorned with Merit, who has attained the liberation door of the power of merit that universally manifests for all sentient beings;
homage to the Earth-Ruling Spirit Wondrous Flower, who has attained the liberation door of universally entering all dharmas and giving rise to the adornments of all Buddha-fields.
Homage to the Earth-Ruling Spirit Adorned with Trees,
who possesses the liberation door of attaining various samādhis to cause sentient beings to eliminate hindrances and defilements;
and to the Earth-Ruling Spirit Universally Scattering All Jewels.
Homage to the Earth Deity Pure-Eye Observer of Time, who has attained the liberation door of causing all sentient beings to always sport in joy and liberation;
homage to the Golden Splendor, who has attained the liberation door of manifesting all pure bodies to subdue sentient beings.
To the Earth-Ruling Spirit named Eye-Master,

who has attained the liberation door of the ocean-like majestic power that knows all the merits of the Buddhas, I pay homage. To the Earth-Ruling Spirit named Fragrant Hair Emitting Light, I pay homage.
Homage to the Earth-Ruling Spirit Joyful Sound, who has attained the liberation door of universally encompassing the ocean of the voices and sounds of all sentient beings;
homage to the Earth-Ruling Spirit Whirl of Exquisite Flowers, who has attained the liberation door of the stainless nature that fills the Buddha-fields.
Homage to the Earth-Ruling Goddess Vajra-Universal-Sustainer, who has attained the liberation door of the universal manifestation sustained by the Dharma-wheel of all Buddhas;
homage to all such Earth-Ruling Goddesses, headed by these, whose number is immeasurable.
All in the ten directions take refuge; Sins are extinguished and pure faith increases. May they be born within the Flower Treasury Sea and the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss.
The Sūtra says: Furthermore, the City-Ruling Spirit Jewel Peak Radiance... (up to) ...such is the entry of Jewel Peak.

May I, together with all sentient beings, be reborn in the Flower Treasury Ocean, in the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss, and subsequently in the Bodhimanda of the Dharma-realm. To the host of City-Ruling Goddesses:
Homage to the City-Ruling Goddess Jewel Peak Radiance, who has attained the liberation door of benefiting sentient beings through skillful means.

Homage to the City-Ruling Goddess Sublime Adornment Palace, who knows how to discern the faculties of sentient beings and possesses the gate of liberation through teaching, maturing, and liberating them;
homage to the Pure One, who possesses the gate of liberation that brings constant joy and causes all sentient beings to receive all manner of merit and virtue.
Homage to the City-Ruling Spirit Nandaratna, who attains the liberation door of the treasury of great compassion that rescues from all fears;
homage to the City-Ruling Spirit Viśokaviśuddha, who attains the liberation door of universally clear and great wisdom; homage to the City-Ruling Spirit Puṣpadīptāgninetra.
Homage to the City-Ruling Spirit Flame-Banner Radiance-Manifestation, who has attained the liberation door of manifesting universal skillful means;

homage to the City-Ruling Spirit Abundant Merit and Majestic Light, who has attained the liberation door of universally observing all sentient beings and causing them to cultivate a vast ocean of merit.
Homage to the City-Ruling Spirit Pure Radiant Body, who has attained the liberation door of awakening all ignorant and dark sentient beings;
homage to the one who has attained the liberation door of universally observing the sovereign power of the Tathāgata throughout the world to tame sentient beings.
Homage to the City-Ruling Goddess Fragrant Topknot Adornment;
Homage to the City-Ruling Goddess Jewel Peak Radiant Eye, who possesses the liberation door of being able to shatter the mountains of obstacles for all sentient beings with great radiance.
Homage to these and others who serve as their leaders, numbering in infinite quantities—all you City-Ruling Goddesses, throughout the ten directions, we take refuge in you.
May our sins be extinguished and our pure faith increase; may we be reborn within the Flower Treasury Ocean, in the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss.
The Sūtra says: Furthermore, the Dharma-assembly of the Maṇḍala-guardian Śuddhālaṃkāraketu (extending to): "This goddess Subhāprabhā is able to hear and receive [this teaching].
May she, together with all sentient beings, be reborn in the Flower Treasury Ocean and within the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss.
Next, the assembly of Maṇḍala-guardians presiding over the Bodhimanda of the Dharma-realm.
Homage to the Dharma-protector of the site of enlightenment named Vastly Adorned with the Power of Vows, who has attained the liberation door of making offerings to the Buddhas who appear;
homage to the Dharma-protector of the site of enlightenment named Banner of Pure Adornment,
who has attained the liberation door of manifesting before all sentient beings and accomplishing the vast practice of bodhi.
The Dharma-door of causing all sentient beings to see the Buddha within their dreams according to the inclinations of their hearts, and preaching the Dharma for them,
[practiced by] the Dharma-arena deity Jewel-Light Banner; and the Dharma-arena deity Thunder-Sound Banner-Mark.

Homage to the Dharma-protector of the Bodhimanda named Wondrous Eye Raining Flowers, who has attained the liberation door of being able to rain down all manner of difficult-to-renounce precious ornaments;

homage to the Dharma-protector of the Bodhimanda named Vast Transformation and Maturation of Sentient Beings through Manifesting Sublime Adornments, who has attained the liberation door of being able to manifest sublime adornments to bring sentient beings to maturity.
Homage to the Ritual Site Deity Pure Flame Form,
who possesses the liberation door of causing right mindfulness to arise by preaching the Dharma according to the faculties [of beings]; and to the Ritual Site Deity Flower Garland Hanging Topknot.
Homage to the Spirit of the Ritual Site named Vajra-Adorned Rain of Jewels, who possesses the liberation door of being able to universally rain down the Dharma of boundless joy through eloquence;
homage to the Spirit of the Ritual Site named Courageous Fragrant Eye, who possesses the liberation door of attaining the vast praise of the merits of all Buddhas.
Homage to the Vajra-Colored Cloud Altar-Attendant Deity of the Liberation Door of Adorning the Site of Enlightenment with Trees Displaying Infinite Physical Forms;
homage to the Lotus of the Liberation Door of Remaining Tranquil and Immovable beneath the Bodhi Tree while Pervading the Ten Directions.
The Flower Radiance Altar Spirit,
who pays homage to the liberation door of the Tathāgata’s manifestation of various powers; the Radiant Illumination Altar Spirit,
who pays homage to those such as these as their leaders, numbering in infinite quantities— all these altar spirits.
The ten directions all take refuge, Sin is extinguished and pure faith increases. May they be born within the Flower Treasury Ocean, in the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss.
The Sūtra says: Furthermore, the foot-attendant spirit named Jewel Seal (up to: having seen this, his heart gave rise to great joy.
May I, together with all sentient beings, be reborn in the Flower Treasury Ocean, in the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss,
and subsequently in the Bodhimanda of the Dharma-realm. To the host of foot-traveling deities,
namo to those who attain the liberation door of universally raining down various jewels and giving rise to vast joy, the jewel-seal hand and foot-travelers.

The Lotus-Radiant Foot-Traveling Spirit, Namah, possesses the liberation door of manifesting the body of a Buddha seated upon a lotus throne of all radiant colors, causing those who see it to rejoice and attain liberation.
Homage to the goddess Cāritramati-sarva-tathāgata-parṣan-maṇḍala-vyūha-ekacitta-kṣaṇa-pratiṣṭhita-vimokṣa-parama-vara-keśa-śekhara-pāda;
homage to the goddess Sarva-kuśala-dharma-saṃgraha-samanta-sattva-vinaya-padavikṣepa-vimokṣa.
The Footstep-Attendant Spirit named Wondrous Jewel Star Banner, who beholds the footprints and enters the liberation door of manifesting various lotus-net radiances within every thought-moment,
universally raining down all manner of jewels and producing sublime sounds.
Homage to the footstep-following spirit Delightful Exquisite Sound, who has attained the liberation door of giving birth to an ocean of boundless joy;
homage to the footstep-following spirit Sandalwood Tree Radiance, who has attained the liberation door of universally awakening all assemblies at sites of enlightenment with fragrant winds.
Homage to the goddess Lotus-Light-Foot-Stride, who has attained the liberation door of emitting light from every pore to proclaim the subtle and wondrous sound of the Dharma;
homage to the goddess Subtle, who has attained the liberation door of her body universally emitting various nets of light that shine everywhere.

The footstep-traveling spirit Radiant Light pays homage to the liberation door of "Causing all sentient beings to attain awakening and give rise to an ocean of roots of goodness"; the footstep-traveling spirit Accumulating Exquisite Flowers pays homage...
Homage to these and others who serve as their leaders, numbering in infinite quantities—all you foot-traveling spirits, throughout the ten directions, we take refuge in you.
May our transgressions be extinguished and our pure faith increase; may we be born within the Flower Treasury Ocean in the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss.
The Sūtra says: "Furthermore, from the realm of the Pure Joy Body-Host Spirits (up to) the realm observed by the Immovable Light Spirit.
May [I], together with all sentient beings, be reborn in the Ocean of Flower Treasury, within the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss, and subsequently within the Bodhimanda of the Dharma-realm.
[This is the assembly of the Body-Host Spirits]."
Homage to the Body-Assembly Spirits of the Ocean of Past Vows of the Buddha Smṛtilabdha, who possess the liberation door of the sphere of pure joy;
homage to the Body-Assembly Spirits of the Radiance Illumining the Ten Directions, who possess the liberation door of light universally illuminating boundless worlds.

Homage to the Sea-Sound Subduing Body Host Deity, who has attained the liberation door of obtaining a great voice that universally awakens all sentient beings, causing them to rejoice, be subdued, and attain liberation;
homage to the Pure Flower Adorned Topknot Body Host Deity, who has attained the liberation door of a body like space that dwells pervasively everywhere.
Homage to the deity of the multitude of bodies with immeasurable dignified postures, who has attained the liberation door of manifesting to all sentient beings the realm of all Buddhas.
Homage to the deity of supreme light, who has attained the liberation door of causing all hungry and destitute sentient beings to have their physical strength and vitality fully satisfied.
Homage to the host of deities who adorn the body,
who have attained the liberation door of removing all afflictions and stains from sentient beings; and to the host of deities whose bodies are clouds of pure light and fragrance.
Homage to the Spirit Who Guards and Sustains the Multitude of Bodies, who has attained the liberation door of overturning the demonic karma of ignorance in all sentient beings;
homage to the Spirit Who Has Attained the Liberation Door of Manifesting Adorned Marks Throughout All the Palaces of Worldly Rulers.
Homage to the Devas of the Universal Manifestation of Transformation Bodies,
who have attained the liberation door of universally gathering all sentient beings and causing them all to give rise to pure roots of goodness;
and to the Devas of the Immovable Radiant Body.
Homage to these and others who serve as their leaders, numbering in infinite quantities. To all the deities of the body, throughout the ten directions, I take refuge;
may my transgressions be extinguished and my pure faith increase, and may I be reborn in the Flower Treasury Sea and the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss.
The Sūtra says: Furthermore, the Vajrapāṇi deity Miśrakavarṇa-Nārāyaṇa (and so forth), manifesting the sphere of the Buddha’s conduct, vows:
"May I, together with all sentient beings, be reborn in the Flower Treasury Ocean, within the Pure Land of Sukhāvatī, and subsequently in the Dharma-realm Bodhimanda.
[This concludes] the assembly of Vajrapāṇi deities within the Dharma-realm Bodhimanda.
Homage to the Vajrapāṇi deity Sunetra, who possesses a body of wondrous color and infinite manifested forms through the liberation door of manifesting boundless physical appearances;
homage to the one who attains the liberation door of each and every hair on the Buddha’s body appearing like a solar disc, manifesting clouds of various kinds of radiance.
Homage to the Vajra-holder Sun-disc Swift Banner;
to the Vajra-holder Sumeru-flower Radiance, who possesses the liberation door of the great supernormal power of manifesting immeasurable bodies.
Homage to the Vajra-wielding Spirit Pure Cloud Sound, who has attained the liberation door of obtaining infinite voices that accord with the species [of beings].
Homage to the Vajra-wielding Spirit Wondrous Arm Lord of Heaven, who has attained the liberation door of manifesting as the lord of all worlds to awaken sentient beings.
Homage to the Vajra-holding Spirit Lovely Radiance, who has attained the liberation door of universally revealing all the distinct categories of the Buddha-dharma without exception;
homage to the Great Tree Spirit, who has attained the liberation door of gathering all tree spirits by means of delightful ornaments.
To the Vajra-holding deity Thunderous Sound,
I pay homage; to the Vajra-holding deity Lion King Radiance, who has attained the gate of liberation that fully possesses the vast accumulation of merit and adornments of the Tathāgata, I pay homage.

Homage to the Vajra-wielding Spirit *Guhyajvālāśrīnetra*, who possesses the liberation door of manifesting a majestic body to those sentient beings in perilous and evil states who seek universal observation;
and homage to the Lotus [Spirit], who possesses the liberation door of the *maṇi* crest that universally rains down all ornaments of the Bodhisattvas.
To the Vajrapāṇi deity Maṇicūḍa and all such others who serve as leaders— numbering immeasurably— to all these Vajrapāṇi deities throughout the ten directions,
I take refuge. May my transgressions be extinguished, may my pure faith increase, and may I be born in the Flower Treasury Ocean.
In the *Sukhāvatīvyūha Sūtra*, it is said:
"Furthermore, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva... [omitting intermediate text] ...bestows the dharmas equal to those of the Tathāgata.
May he, together with all sentient beings, be reborn in the Flower Treasury Ocean within the Pure Land of Sukhāvatī."
Homage to the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Samantabhadra, who enters the inconceivable realm and possesses various gates of liberation;

I take refuge in him throughout the ten directions. May my sins be extinguished, may my pure faith increase, and may I be reborn in the ocean of the Flower Treasury and the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss.
The Sūtra says: "Furthermore, the Bodhisattvas Pure Virtue and Wondrous Light... [until] all sufferings and difficulties are utterly extinguished.

May I, together with all sentient beings, be reborn in the Flower Treasury Ocean, within the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss, and subsequently at the Bodhimanda of the Dharma-realm, upon the Tathāgata’s lion throne, amidst all the bodhisattvas."

The oceanic assembly pays homage to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Pure Virtue Sublime Light, who possesses the liberation door of the adornment of the site of enlightenment through the assembly of Bodhisattvas who can travel everywhere throughout the ten directions.

Homage to the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Universal Attainment of the Light of the Supreme Lamp, who possesses the liberation door of manifesting infinite perfect enlightenment within a single thought-moment and teaching and ripening inconceivable realms of sentient beings;
homage to the liberation door of attaining the cultivation of the bodhisattva’s adornment of merit that gives birth to all buddha-lands.
To the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Universal Radiance Lion Banner at the Gate,

I pay homage; to the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Universal Jewel Flame Sublime Light, who has attained the liberation door of non-deluded understanding of the Buddha’s sphere of supernatural powers, I pay homage.

Homage to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Universal Sound Merit-Ocean Banner, who has attained the liberation door of manifesting the adornments of all Buddha-lands within a single assembly at a site of enlightenment;
homage to the Bodhisattva who has attained the liberation door of following the Tathāgata to observe the profound and vast treasury of the Dharma-realm.
Homage to the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Jñānālokaketurāja,
who has attained the liberation door of the treasury of offerings that serves and attends all Buddhas;
and to the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Samantabodhimanoharasvara.

Homage to the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Universal Purity and Inexhaustible Merit and Majestic Light, who has attained the liberation door of the vast empowerment that gives rise to all miraculous transformations;
homage to the one who has attained the liberation door of the boundless practices of a bodhisattva that universally enters into the conduct of all worlds.
Homage to the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Universal Jewel Topknot Flower Banner,
who has attained the liberation door of manifesting the realms of all Buddhas within the signless dharma-realm;
homage to the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Universal Mark Supreme Light.
Homage to all such Bodhisattvas as these, who are their leaders, numbering immeasurably. To all Bodhisattvas throughout the ten directions, I take refuge.
May my transgressions be extinguished and my pure faith increase; may I be born within the Flower Treasury Ocean in the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss.
The Sūtra says: "Furthermore, Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Ocean-Light-Moon Great Radiance... [until] all lands are clearly manifest.

May I, together with all sentient beings, be reborn in the Flower Treasury Ocean, within the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss, and subsequently at the Dharma-realm Bodhimanda, upon the Tathāgata’s lion throne, amidst all the bodhisattvas."

The assembly in the ocean paid homage to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Samudrareṇu-prabhāsa-śrī, who possesses the ocean-like gate of skillful means and liberation for attaining birth in the various stages and perfections of a bodhisattva,
for teaching and transforming sentient beings, and for adorning and purifying all buddha-fields.

I pay homage to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Cloud-Sound-Ocean-Light-Stainless-Treasury, who possesses the liberation door of universally entering all various distinct locations within the dharma-realm in every moment of thought.
Homage to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Ratnaśikhin, who attained the wisdom-born liberation door of manifesting pure great merit before all sentient beings throughout inconceivable eons;
homage to those who attained the various adornments when first approaching the site of enlightenment to behold all Bodhisattvas in the ten directions.
Homage to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Sovereign King of the Merit of the Gate of Liberation of Pure Light;

Homage to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Lotus Topknot of Excellent Valor, who has attained the ocean of understanding the faculties and inclinations of all sentient beings and universally manifests all Buddha-dharmas through the gate of liberation.
Homage to the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Universal Wisdom Cloud Sun Banner, who has attained the liberation door of eternally abiding for immeasurable eons through the Tathāgata’s accomplished wisdom;
homage to the Great Vīrya Vajra, who has attained the liberation door of the power of the seal of universal entry into all boundless dharmas.
Homage to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Nābhi;
homage to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Gandhārciḥketu, who has attained the liberation door of manifesting all Buddhas of the present,
from the initial cultivation of the bodhisattva path until the perfection of the mass of wisdom.
Homage to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Great Radiant Virtue with Profound and Beautiful Voice, who has attained the liberation door of the ocean of all great vows of Vairocana’s secure abiding;
homage to the Bodhisattva Great Merit Light, who has attained the liberation door of manifesting the Tathāgata’s profound realm pervading the entire Dharma-realm.
To the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Jñānajanman and all such as he who serve as the leaders— bodhisattvas whose number is immeasurable—
I, from all directions, take refuge. May my sins be extinguished, may my pure faith increase, and may I be born in the Flower Treasury Ocean.
The Sutra on the Land of Ultimate Bliss states:
At that time, the Tathāgata, upon his lion throne... (up to) ...by the power of the Buddha, was able to proclaim [this teaching].
I vow to go together with all sentient beings to be reborn in the Flower Treasury Ocean, within the Land of Ultimate Bliss.
Next, from the wheel-base terraces, steps, and all the windows of the Tathāgata’s lion throne within the Dharma-realm Bodhimanda,
there emerged an ocean-like assembly of beings who bowed toward the multitude of exquisite jewel-flower wheel-terraces of the Tathāgata’s lion throne in the Dharma-realm Bodhimanda.
In all such ornaments as the foundations, steps, and windows— within these Buddha-land-microdust numbers of assemblies of all Bodhisattvas—
I pay homage to the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Sāgaramati-vikrīḍita-abhijña-rāja (The King of Oceanic Wisdom, Sovereign of Spiritual Powers).
Homage to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Thunderous Sound Universally Resounding;
homage to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Crest of Multitudinous Jewel Radiance;
homage to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Great Wisdom Sun of Valiant Intelligence.
Homage to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Inconceivable Merit Jewel Wisdom Seal;
homage to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Hundred-Eyed Lotus Topknot;
homage to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Golden Flame Perfect Radiance.
Homage to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Universal Sound of the Dharma Realm;
homage to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Cloud Sound Pure Moon;
homage to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Banner of Good Courageous Light.
Homage to the ocean-like assembly of all Bodhisattvas who appear simultaneously, as numerous as the atoms within unspeakably unspeakable Buddha-fields;
with a sincere heart, we take refuge and pay homage to the Honored One of the Flower Treasury World-Ocean in the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra*.

To Vairocana Buddha, throughout the ten directions, I take refuge; may my transgressions be extinguished and my pure faith increase. May I be born within the Lotus Treasury Ocean, in the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss.
Next is the Assembly of the World-Ruling Lord of the Array of the Flower Treasury World-Ocean.

The *Sūtra on the Manifestation of Auspicious Omens in Heaven and Earth* states: "At that time, in the Flower Treasury Arrayed World-Ocean... (up to)... throughout the world-oceans, it was likewise in every respect."
May we, together with all sentient beings, be reborn in the Flower Treasury Ocean; in the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss,
within the assembly at the site of enlightenment in the Sahā world, may clouds of offerings rain down, and may all lords of the world each enter the gate of the Tathāgata’s liberation.
Homage to all the world-rulers within every land throughout the Flower Treasury Adorned World-Ocean;
homage to all such lands within the Flower Treasury worlds, as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many Buddha-fields.
All these Lords of the World likewise take refuge with a sincere heart;
they pay homage to the World-Samudra of the Flower Treasury within the Avataṃsaka Sūtra,
to the Honored One Vairocana Buddha.
All in the ten directions take refuge; Sins are extinguished and pure faith increases. May they be born in the Flower Treasury Ocean and the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss.
Next is the repentance for the sin of false speech.
I only pray that the inexhaustible Jewels of the Buddha, Dharma, and Sangha, as vast as the celestial net; Vairocana Tathāgata;

the assembly of holy beings of Samantabhadra, Mañjuśrī, and the ocean-like gathering; and all mundane and supramundane deities—by virtue of your compassionate original vows, may you emit great radiance to illuminate this dharma assembly.
May you bear witness and protect us with your mindfulness; may you compassionately accept us.

I vow that for myself and the ocean of all sentient beings, from beginningless time until this very moment, we confess and repent for all karmic offenses of false speech—exhaustless as an ocean and as vast as a layered net of Indra—within the infinite realms of existence.

As for the offense of lying, its sprout is light but its root is heavy, and the harm it causes is extreme. It is an offense of the karmic paths (*karmapatha*), a violation of the precepts, a breach of the bodhisattva vows, and an infraction of the *pārājika* rules.
Whether by nature (*svabhāva*) or by prohibition (*pratikṣepa*), it is in every case classified as a grave offense. The *Mahāprajñāpāramitā-śāstra* states:
"Lying is when, with an impure mind desiring to deceive another, one conceals the truth and utters a divergent discourse, thereby giving rise to verbal karma. This is [the definition].

This is called false speech (*mṛṣāvāda*). The offense of false speech arises from the mutual understanding of the characteristics of vocal sounds. If there is no such mutual understanding, even if one speaks what is untrue, there is no offense of false speech.
This false speech consists of: knowing and saying one does not know; not knowing and saying one knows; seeing and saying one does not see; not seeing and saying one sees;
hearing and saying one does not hear; or not hearing and saying one hears. This is called false speech. If one does not act [upon these], [there is no offense].
This is called non-false speech. A person who speaks falsely first deceives themselves and then deceives others;
they take the real for the unreal and the unreal for the real, thus inverting truth and falsehood. Such a person does not receive wholesome dharmas, just as water cannot enter an overturned jar.
The mind of one who speaks falsely is devoid of shame and remorse, which blocks the gates to the heavenly realms and nirvana. One should observe and understand this.
This is a transgression; therefore, one does not engage in it. Question: If lying has such a fault, for what reason do people lie?
Answer: There are those who are foolish and lacking in wisdom; when they encounter misfortune or hardship, they lie in an attempt to escape it.

They do not realize that their actions will be exposed, leading them to incur guilt in this life, nor do they realize that there is a great retribution for their sin in future lives. Furthermore, there are those who, although they know the sin of lying, are driven by stinginess...
Because of an abundance of greed, hatred, and delusion, one utters false speech. Furthermore, there are those who, though not driven by greed or hatred, falsely testify to another's crimes;
believing in their hearts that it is truly so, they fall into hell after death. As the Buddha taught, there are ten offenses for lying.
What are these ten? First, the breath is constantly foul-smelling. Second, benevolent deities abandon them, while non-human spirits find an opportunity to harm them. Third...
1. Although one speaks the truth, people do not believe or accept it. 2. One never participates in the deliberations of wise men. 3.
One is constantly slandered, and an evil reputation spreads throughout the world. 4. One is not respected by others;
though one issues instructions, they are not trusted or followed. 5. One is constantly beset by much sorrow and anxiety. 6. One plants the karmic causes for slander.
Conditioned by these nine factors, upon the dissolution of the body at the end of life, one will fall into hell. Tenth, if one emerges as a human being, one will constantly be subjected to slander.
To refrain from such various acts is non-false speech; it is called the virtuous restraint of speech.

We have been shrouded by ignorance and failed to recognize the causal nature of the offense of false speech. Now that we have encountered this site of enlightenment, we have finally awakened to this truth.
We take refuge in the Tathāgata Vairocana and the ocean-like assembly of all worthy and holy ones. We burn incense and scatter flowers.

Regarding the retribution for the sin of lying, I confess and reveal it openly, not daring to conceal it. By these causes and conditions, may the heavy sins of lying committed by myself and the ocean of sentient beings throughout the Dharma-realm all become purified.
Next, the mudrā and mantra for repentance to extinguish transgressions: Oṃ sarvapāpam me kṣayaṃ kuru svāhā.
(Recite three times.)
Sins accumulated over a hundred kalpas are entirely swept away in a single thought; like fire consuming dry grass, they are extinguished without remainder.
All the evil karma I have created in the past arose from beginningless greed, hatred, and delusion.
Whatever has arisen from my body, speech, and mind, I now confess it all.
Having confessed, I take refuge with a sincere heart and pay homage to the Honored One, Vairocana Buddha.
○ (Proclamation: Listen, all you people, to these verses on impermanence from the Sūtras:

Even the Unsurpassed World-Honored Ones, The Pratyekabuddhas, and the assembly of Śrāvakas— Since they still abandon their impermanent bodies, How much more so for ordinary persons? Parents, wives, and children, Brothers, and kinsmen as well.
Beholding with my own eyes the separation of birth and death, how could I not grieve and lament?
Therefore, I exhort all people to listen attentively to the true Dharma. Together, abandon the realm of impermanence and enter the gate of the Deathless.
The Buddha’s teaching is like nectar; it removes the fever of suffering and brings cooling peace. You should listen with a single-minded focus.

Innumerable fragrances of clouds; innumerable fragrances of images; innumerable fragrances of light;
innumerable fragrances of flames; innumerable fragrances of nets; innumerable fragrances of seats; innumerable fragrances of walking paths; innumerable fragrances of dwelling places;
innumerable fragrances of worlds; innumerable fragrances of mountains; innumerable fragrances of oceans; innumerable fragrances of rivers; innumerable fragrances of trees.

Clouds of scented ointments, clouds of powdered incense, clouds of robes, clouds of jewels, clouds of lamp-light, and clouds of ornaments;
likewise, mani-jewel canopies, mani-jewel banners, mani-jewel pennants, mani-jewel curtains, and mani-jewel nets.
Maṇi-jewel images; maṇi-jewel lights; maṇi-jewel flames; maṇi-jewel clouds; maṇi-jewel thrones;

garments of maṇi jewels, lotuses of maṇi jewels, and palaces of maṇi jewels— all of which were unspeakably unspeakable in number.

Countless half-moons, countless defensive towers, countless windows and lattices, countless pure jewels, and countless ornaments—with such various articles of offering, they constantly perform offerings.

In a重重 (repeatedly layered) net of Indra, the oceans of Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and holy assemblies perform great offerings. They receive these clouds of offerings and take them as their luminous terraces.
Extending throughout boundless realms, immeasurable and inexhaustible, may they perform the work of a Buddha.

*Kiṃ dānī saumanasyaṃ na bhaviṣyati hūṃ.* In the Brahma-sound praise of the Buddha, the World-Honored One, entering parinirvāṇa:
The adornments of that land shall perish; Sentient beings will no longer be vessels for the Dharma.
When the world is defiled, yet a Buddha arises in the world, everything becomes precious and excellent;
according to the purity of their minds, all adornments are fully perfected.
Through the inconceivable manifestations of the Buddhas' supernormal powers, at that time, the entire ocean of lands becomes universally pure.
Speaking directly in praise of the Buddha:
His body fills the Dharma-realm, Universally appearing before all sentient beings;
responding to conditions and fulfilling requests without exception, Yet he ever remains upon this seat of enlightenment.
Within each and every pore of the Tathāgata, Buddhas as numerous as the atoms of all lands sit amidst assemblies of Bodhisattvas who surround them; they proclaim the supreme conduct of Samantabhadra.
The Tathāgata, seated upon the seat of enlightenment, manifests within a single pore an ocean of many lands.
From every single pore, all appear in this same way; thus they pervade the entire Dharma-realm.
Within each and every land, they sit in peaceful composure, filling all buddha-fields throughout the ten directions.
Bodhisattvas gather like clouds, none of whom fail to come to the site of enlightenment.

As numerous as the atoms within all buddha-fields, oceans of Bodhisattvas of Merit and Radiance are universally present within the assemblies of the Tathāgatas; extending even to the limits of the Dharma-realm,
they pervade all lands as numerous as the atoms of the Dharma-realm, appearing before every sentient being.
Thus, within the sphere of wisdom of these emanated bodies,
One can establish oneself amidst the assemblies of all Buddhas; There, the Bodhisattvas of Supreme Wisdom sit together,
Each listening to the Dharma with joy, Practicing everywhere for immeasurable eons.
Having entered the vast vows of Samantabhadra, Each gives birth to the manifold Buddha-dharmas.
Within the ocean of Vairocana’s Dharma, One practices and realizes the stage of the Tathāgata.
Awakened by the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra, All Tathāgatas alike praise and rejoice.
Having attained the great supernormal powers of all Buddhas, they circulate throughout the entire Dharma-realm without exception;
in lands as numerous as the atoms of all worlds, they constantly manifest clouds of bodies that completely fill them.
For the sake of all sentient beings, they emit great rays of light, each raining down the rain of Dharma according to their inclinations.

the assembly of holy beings including Samantabhadra and Mañjuśrī; and all mundane and supramundane deities, by virtue of your compassionate original vows, may radiate great light that illuminates this dharma assembly.
May you bear witness, protect, and sustain us with your compassionate mindfulness.

May you take pity upon and embrace me and the ocean of all sentient beings, from beginningless time until this very moment, regarding the inexhaustible ocean of karma—its myriad, interlacing Indra-nets of all afflictions such as greed, hatred, and delusion, and every single sinful deed.
Regarding the confession of faults, the *Jieyezhang jing* (Sutra on the Elimination of Karmic Obstructions) states: "There are three grades of greed: superior, middling, and inferior.

As for superior greed, whether in body or mind, it reaches its extreme state, giving rise to defiled attachment such that there is no mind free from greed. Because of this defiled attachment, regarding all..."
To feel no shame or remorse in such circumstances—what is this lack of shame (*āhrīkya*)?

It refers to dwelling alone in a secluded place, engaging in such reflections and seeking after all manner of desired objects, praising the realm of sensual desire, and claiming for oneself the possession of virtuous qualities; this is what constitutes a lack of shame.
What is shamelessness (*anapatrāpya*)? Due to the causes and conditions of that greed, one acts with defiance and cruelty before one's parents and others, and gives rise to affliction and harm;
likewise, one feels no sense of shame before one’s venerable teachers, falsely manifesting oneself as possessing virtuous qualities. This is called shamelessness.
By reason of these causes and conditions, after the end of life, one falls into the evil destinies. This is termed "superior-grade greed. [End of middle section.]
Regarding medium-grade greed: this refers to when one approaches various objects of desire;

although there may be a temporary accomplishment from beginning to end, one immediately gives rise to a mind detached from greed and feels regret. This is called medium-grade greed. As for low-grade greed:
This refers to when one approaches various sensual objects—whether through physical contact, conversation, or even a mere glance—and desire arises only to immediately vanish;

this is called inferior-grade greed. In brief, all thoughts of desiring any articles of life for one's enjoyment are termed inferior-grade [greed]. Failing to realize this teaching, I now repent for them all.
Hatred is of three kinds: superior, middling, and inferior. Regarding superior hatred, within whatever objects of hatred arise, one gives rise to extreme malice and becomes violent and cruel;
one then commits the five crimes of immediate retribution, or commits one of the five crimes of immediate retribution, or slanders the True Dharma.
All such instances as these are collectively aggregated as the five crimes of immediate retribution, which cannot be calculated by number, fraction, part, or analogy.

...not even a fraction, nor even a part of a hundredth, nor even a part of an *upaniṣad* (a minute fraction). Due to these causes and conditions, when the body breaks up and life ends, one falls into the great hells.
Even if one should briefly obtain birth among humans, one’s physical appearance will be black, one’s eyes will be red and fierce, and one’s nature will be mostly violent and evil.
Because of these causes and conditions, one returns to birth in hell. This is called superior-grade hatred. [Next is] medium-grade [hatred].

Regarding anger: when, amidst various objects of anger, it arises even momentarily, or one commits even a slight unwholesome sinful deed, one immediately feels regret and swiftly applies an antidote to cause it to cease. This is called medium-grade anger. As for low-grade anger:
this refers to when, within an object that is dear and harmonious, one suddenly gives rise to slight slander due to some condition of anger, even though it is but momentary.
As soon as it arises, within that very instant, one should immediately give rise to regret and promptly apply the antidote to cause it to be extinguished.
This is called minor-grade anger. Failing to realize this Dharma, I now repent for all such instances.
Delusion is of three kinds: superior, middling, and inferior. As for superior delusion:
in all circumstances, whether walking or standing still, one performs no wholesome deeds and feels neither sorrow nor remorse; this is called superior delusion. As for middling delusion:
if one commits even a small amount of unwholesome karma, although it has been accomplished, one immediately feels remorse and, toward one's fellow practitioners of the holy life...
One repents one's offenses before fellow practitioners and does not manifest one's own virtues; this is called middling-grade delusion.

As for lower-grade delusion, it refers to not transgressing natural offenses (prakṛti-sāvadya) among the precepts established by the Tathāgata, yet violating the offenses concerning the training in the first category of precepts (pārājika).
This is called inferior-grade delusion. Failing to awaken to this Dharma, we now repent it all.

We were shrouded by ignorance and did not recognize the causes of sin, such as greed, anger, and delusion. Now that we have encountered this site of enlightenment (*bodhimaṇḍa*), we are finally able to realize it.
We take refuge in the Tathāgata Vairocana and the ocean-like assembly of all worthy sages. [I] burn incense.
I scatter flowers. I openly confess and repent for the transgressions of greed, anger, and ignorance; I dare not conceal them.

By virtue of these causes and conditions, may the heavy karmic offenses of my mental actions, as well as those of the ocean-like assembly of sentient beings within the Dharma-realm, be entirely purified.
Next is the mudrā and mantra for repentance to extinguish transgressions: Oṃ sarvapa pame sputa ṇada nada mardaya svāhā.
(Recite three times.)
Sins accumulated over a hundred eons are entirely swept away in a single thought; Like fire consuming dry grass, they are extinguished without remainder.
All the evil karma I have created in the past Arises entirely from beginningless greed, hatred, and delusion.
Whatever has arisen from my body, speech, and mind, I now confess it all.
Having confessed, I take refuge with a sincere heart and pay homage to the Honored One, Vairocana Buddha.
○ (Proclamation: May the assembly listen to these verses on impermanence from within the Sūtras:
All phenomena are empty; Even the high shall fall. That which is joined must inevitably separate;
Those with life all return to death. All sentient beings within the three realms— Both those of the present and the future.
Those who are born must inevitably die; there is no phenomenon that is eternal.
Just as the rising and setting of the sun is seen by all people, so it is with all who are born. The law of death shall manifest before us.

Garlands; robes of various colors; Dharma-robes of various colors; ornaments of various colors;
precious flowers of various colors; exquisite perfumes of various colors; unguents of various colors; powdered incenses of various colors;

They chant and praise the Buddha-Dharma; even the various kinds of requisites pervade the abodes of all sentient beings, filling the sites of enlightenment in all Buddha-fields and universally making offerings to all Buddhas.

With such various articles of offering, they constantly perform worship in a manner as vast and layered as Indra’s net. Thus, the ocean-like assemblies of Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and worthy sages receive these offerings.
They formed clouds of nourishment as canopies of light, vast beyond the boundaries of the infinite, immeasurable and inexhaustible, vowing to perform the work of Buddhas.
Having made these offerings, they all paid homage with deep reverence.
Next, I offer clouds of supreme offerings such as these—
vast oceans of the nature of jewels and precious gems, and mountains of the seven treasures—
which arise in this manner, and I present them to all the Buddhas and their assemblies.
Oṃ sarvamaṇḍalādhipataye pracaṇḍe asamañjara-spharaṇa samaya hūṃ. The *Ratnakūṭa Sūtra* states:
"There is a dhāraṇī called the 'Spell of Immeasurable Varieties,' which can accomplish all things and possesses great power."
It is possible. The dhāraṇī is as follows: Oṃ sīmala sīmala mīmada sīkala mahāliṅga hūṃ.
Next is the mantra of the Amoghamani Seal.
Oṃ āmābhyo bhagavate māmakīne tathāgatāya meṣaṅkine sarvamantrābhisaṃrāddhaye hūṃ. (In Sanskrit phonetics,
this praises the Buddha.)
The vast voices of all Buddhas are heard throughout the entire Dharma-realm; Bodhisattvas are able to understand them and skillfully enter the ocean of sounds.
Throughout oceans of eons they proclaim wondrous voices, and their voices are equal and without distinction.
Those whose wisdom pervades the three periods of time enter the wisdom of those vocal sounds— the sounds of all sentient beings.
And the Buddha’s voice of mastery, having attained the wisdom of sounds, understands them all;
he directly praises the Tathāgata’s physical form, marks, and characteristics, such that no one in any world can fathom them.
Even if one were to contemplate for billions of nayutas of eons, the physical marks and majestic virtue of the Tathāgata would become ever more boundless.
The Tathāgata does not take these marks as his essence; he is rather the signless, quiescent Dharma-body.
Yet, he is fully endowed with all physical marks and dignified deportment, such that all in the world may behold him according to their own inclinations.
The Buddha-dharma is subtle and difficult to measure; no verbal expression can reach it.
It is neither a composite nor non-composite; its essential nature is quiescent and devoid of all marks.
The Buddha-body is unarisen and transcends conceptual proliferation; it is not a phenomenon characterized by the aggregation of the skandhas.
Having attained the power of mastery and the certainty of vision, his conduct is fearless and transcends the path of words.
