To the assembly of light, names, and sounds of the Dharma-wheel, which is undifferentiated and unmoving;
to the realms of all Buddhas within the oceans of dust-like lands, pervading everywhere;

to the entire oceanic assembly at the sites of enlightenment of all Buddhas—I take refuge with a sincere heart. I pay homage to the Honored One of the Flower Treasury Ocean World-system in the Great Vaipulya Buddha-avatamsaka Sutra.

To Vairocana Buddha, throughout the ten directions, I take refuge; May my transgressions be extinguished and my pure faith increase; I vow to be born within the Flower Treasury Ocean, in the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss.
Next, for the repentance of the three miserable realms and the eight difficulties,
we pray that the inexhaustible Buddha, Dharma, and Sangha jewels of the Indra’s Net, Vairocana Tathāgata, the assembly of holy beings including Samantabhadra and Mañjuśrī,
and all mundane and supramundane deities, by virtue of your compassionate original vows, may emit great radiance to illuminate this dharma assembly.
Please bear witness to this and compassionately accept me with your protective mindfulness.

May I and the ocean of all sentient beings, from beginningless time until this very moment, [purify] all karmic oceans that are inexhaustible and as vast as the layered net of Indra, including all transgressions of the laws and precepts and every sinful deed.
Confess and repent.

The *Sūtra on the Questions of the Elder’s Son Bianyi* states: The Buddha told Bianyi, "Furthermore, there are five types of conduct that lead one to enter hell after death, from which one emerges only after billions of kalpas.
What are these five? First, to lack faith in the existence of the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Saṅgha, yet to practice..."

First, slandering and disparaging the Noble Path. Second, destroying Buddhist temples and sacred shrines. Third, the fourfold assembly mutually slandering one another, lacking faith in the retribution of sin, and having no sense of reverence or obedience.
Fourth, practicing rebellion and anarchy, where superiors and subordinates, ministers and sovereigns, fathers and sons do not accord with one another.
Fifth, there will be those who desire the future; those who have already attained the Way, and those who practice the Way, shall not [be so].
To follow the teacher’s instructions yet remain self-exalting, and to treat the teacher with contempt and slander—these are the five matters that lead one to enter hell after death.
Transmigrating from hell to hell, there will be no time of release. One must repent for these karmic retributions.
Furthermore, there are five types of conduct that lead to rebirth among the hungry ghosts (*preta*). First, being stingy and greedy, one is unwilling to practice giving.
Second, one commits theft and is unfilial toward one's two parents. Third, one is foolish and lacks a heart of compassion. Fourth, one amasses wealth and refuses to provide for food and clothing.
Fifth, one does not provide for one's parents, siblings, wife, children, or servants. These are the five things by which one falls [into this state].

Regarding the confession of karmic retribution for those among the hungry ghosts, there are furthermore five matters concerning the performance of animal-like conduct that leads to falling into the realm of animals. The first is: violating the precepts by secretly stealing and pilfering.
Second, to incur debts and refuse to repay them; third, to take the taking of life as a means of repayment; fourth, to have no joy in hearing or receiving the sutras and the Dharma;
fifth, to constantly use difficult circumstances as a pretext for practicing precepts and giving while remaining attached to worldly concerns.
These are the five matters by which one is born among the animals as a retribution for transgressions.
The *Sūtra on the Six Realms of Saṃsāra* says:
"Karmic actions are all caused by one's own mind, Which rushes through the six realms; It is due to the terrors of the three poisons."
Selling various living beings to sustain oneself while killing others—such a person shall fall into the Saṃjīva Hell, where their lifespan lasts for a hundred thousand years.
There, they are struck with blades, staves, and whips; though they die, they are born again to undergo such retribution for their suffering (repentance for this sinful retribution).
If one causes harm to one's parents, friends, or kinsmen, and gives rise to false speech and deception, one shall fall into the Black Rope Hell.
There, black cords are stretched across one’s body; like a worldling sawing wood, the flames blaze fiercely as one undergoes such retribution for one’s sins. (Repentance for Transgressions)
If one burns mountains and rivers, forests and plains with fire, and harms various sentient beings, one shall fall into the Reviving (Saṃjīva) Hell.
There, flames burn everywhere; the sounds of piteous wailing never cease, and the two eyes lose their sight.
One undergoes such retribution for suffering (the confession of karmic offenses).

To proclaim what is not the Dharma as being the Dharma, or to slander without basis, causing others to give rise to feverish distress and fall into the Hell of Intense Heat—these sinful beings are tormented by great fires that burn them without ceasing;
such is the retribution they receive for their offenses. (Repentance of Sinful Retribution)
Regarding pigs, sheep, foxes, rabbits, and other such living beings, If one slaughters them without limit, one shall fall into the Saṃghāta Hell.
Having been born in that hell, one undergoes all manner of agonizing torments;
though struck and tortured until extinguished, one is reborn again. Such is the retribution for suffering (the confession of karmic offenses).
Having given rise to evil in body, speech, and mind, and sowing discord through slander and incitement—such sinful beings shall fall into the Raurava Hell.

There, amidst blazing and fierce flames that burn without ceasing, they constantly utter great cries of distress as they undergo such retribution for their sins. (Repentance for the Retribution of Sin)
If one steals the property of the Buddha, the Dharma, the Saṅgha, or of those who are impoverished, one falls into the Great Howling Hell (*Raurava*).
There, scorched and roasted by fire, one undergoes the most extreme heat and affliction, emitting loud, fierce, and evil cries;
such is the retribution for this sin (the confession of karmic offenses).
Toward one's parents, teachers, elders, and virtuous sages, To conceive a superior intent to kill is certain to lead to the Avīci Hell.
In a blazing mass of great fire, Flaming through to the very marrow of the bones, one shall suffer extreme agony for a long time;
It is certain that there is not even a moment’s joy. (Repentance for the Retribution of Sins)
Giving rise to enmity, hostility, and strife, they harm one another with spears and halberds. Upon death, they fall into the Copper-Clawed Hell, where the terrain is exceedingly sharp;
they tear each other apart, or are transformed into swords and staves that vyingly hack and pierce their bodies.
Thus do they undergo such retribution for their sins. (Repentance for sinful retribution.)
Violently invading another's village, one later falls into the Iron Spike Hell. The spikes are sixteen finger-widths long;
they slice the flesh and pierce the bone. Furthermore, there are great iron dogs with flaming fangs, most terrifying, which devour from the crown of the head down to the heels.
One undergoes such retribution for suffering (the repentance for karmic offenses).
If one plots with secret schemes to harm others, one shall fall into that Forest of Sword-leaves, where rabid dogs, vultures,
and eagles chase and compete to devour [the sinner].
(Repentance for the retribution of sin) If one plundered the wealth of others, one shall undergo extreme suffering, constantly swallowing glowing iron balls.
Furthermore, one is drenched with molten copper (Repentance for the Retribution of Sin):
Having harmed sentient beings without cause, One shall fall into the Iron Hawk Hell;
With sharp talons, they strike with violence, Constantly suffering torment (Repentance for the Retribution of Sin).
If a person delights in injuring and killing the lives of aquatic creatures, they will later fall into the River of Molten Copper to be scorched and boiled by the fires of karma.
(Repentance for the Retribution of Sin) If one pursues their own greedy ends while suppressing and disparaging the virtues of others, they will fall into that Iron Grinding Hell.
Lamenting piteously with no one to save them (*Confession of the Retribution of Sin*):

If a person does not benefit others, they shall receive various forms [of suffering]. Two mountains shall press upon their body, and further, wedges shall be driven into it (*Confession of the Retribution of Sin*).
If a person speaks what is not the Dharma and destroys the bridge, they shall be driven back and forth upon a path of sharp blades.
(Repentance for the Retribution of Sin) For wounding fleas and lice with one's armor,
one falls onto Mount Two-Goat-Head, where they strike one another until death and rebirth.
Passing from one suffering to another (repentance for karmic retribution),
relying on the path of renunciation yet failing to guard the prohibitive precepts, one falls into the Hell of Hot Ashes,
where all limbs and body parts are consumed and rotted away (repentance for karmic retribution).
Feigning various dignified postures while seeking a livelihood through deceitful and heterodox means, one falls after death into the Hell of Excrement to be devoured by maggots.
(Repentance for the Retribution of Sin) Seeing insects within the five grains, one threshes and husks them without discrimination; such a person falls into the Hell of the Iron Pestle.
Constantly subjected to pounding and threshing (repentance for karmic retribution);
seeing the suffering of others, one gives rise to joy; being sycophantic, crooked, and full of doubt;
always harboring evil thoughts—one becomes a henchman of Yama (repentance for karmic retribution).
The seeds of all suffering’s fruits— briefly and concisely analyzed— Are utterly and permanently removed from the purity of body, speech, and mind.
(Repentance for the retribution of transgressions) If a person takes no delight in giving,
And further steals the food and drink of others, They will fall among the *galagaṇḍa* spirits (the goitrous ghosts).
Constantly devouring various kinds of filth and excrement (repentance for karmic retribution);
if one obstructs those who wish to give, or develops stinginess toward one’s own possessions, one will fall among the *sūcīmukha* ghosts,
with a vast belly yet perpetually hungry and thirsty (repentance for karmic retribution).
Lacking heirs and being stingy with wealth, one neither gives it away nor enjoys it; such a person falls among the *vañjula* (hungry ghost) spirits who subsist on the leavings discarded by others.
(Repentance for the retribution of these sins.
Longing for the wisdom of others' giving, yet feeling regret because one gave little oneself, one falls among the inferior *preta* spirits.
Constantly consuming saliva and spittle (repentance for karmic retribution),

delighting in hearing of others' faults and spreading malicious words— such a person falls among the *jvālāmukha* (Flame-Mouthed) hungry ghosts and undergoes various sufferings for a long time (repentance for karmic retribution).

Those who delight in inciting various disputes and lack even the slightest heart of compassion fall among the most hideous of hungry ghosts, where they feed upon wriggling insects and worms. (Repentance for the retribution of this sin.
Those who fearfully seize the wealth of others and, having obtained it, give away only a small portion, fall among the most hideous of hungry ghosts.
He fears obtaining even a small offering [of merit] (Repentance for the Retribution of Sin):
If many people feast and enjoy themselves, extensively killing the lives of various creatures, eating them themselves and giving them to others,
they will later fall among the rākṣasa demons (Repentance for the Retribution of Sin).

Regarding incense and flowers offered in worship, whether one smells them or takes them for oneself, by giving rise to even a slight mind of greed, one later becomes a Gandharva (a "seeker of fragrance" ghost). [Repentance for this karmic retribution.
If people honor and revere one, and have requests made of oneself, yet one displays an angry countenance while coveting their wealth—
Later, one becomes a fierce and evil ghost (*pāpa-paścāttāpa-pratideśana*).
If a person, regarding the marriages of others, Constantly delights in acting as a matchmaker or in inciting discord, They will later harbor malice and cause separation;
upon death, they become a *bhūta* ghost (*pāpa-paścāttāpa-pratideśana*).
If a person delights in drinking alcohol, exceeding moderation and becoming intoxicated and disorderly, or if they take it and encourage others to do so,
they will later become a yakṣa ghost (repentance for the retribution of this sin).
If one opposes and acts contrary to the wishes of one's parents and teachers, one will later be born in the palace of the yakṣas.
The brave and the impetuous (repentance for the retribution of sin):

those with the faults of stinginess and greed are constantly reborn among the hungry ghosts; suffering and joy follow one's own causes, therefore do not commit them again (repentance for the retribution of sin).
Furthermore, the Āgama Sūtras state: The World-Honored One addressed the bhikṣus, "Ordinary persons do not hear or know the proper timing for preaching the Dharma.
Bhikṣus, you should know that there are eight such occasions when one who does not hear or know them cannot practice. First:"
First, when a Tathāgata appears in the world and extensively expounds the Dharma, enabling beings to reach the state of nirvāṇa attained by a Tathāgata,
yet these sentient beings are in hell, neither hearing nor seeing it, and do not repent for their karmic retribution. Second, furthermore,
when a Tathāgata appears in the world and extensively expounds the Dharma, enabling beings to reach nirvāṇa, yet these sentient beings are among the animals.

Second, not hearing or seeing [the teachings] while among the hungry ghosts; repentance for this karmic retribution. Third, furthermore, when a Tathāgata appears in the world and extensively expounds the Dharma so that one may attain nirvana, yet these sentient beings, being among the hungry ghosts, do not hear or see it;
repentance for this karmic retribution. Fourth, furthermore, when a Tathāgata appears in the world and extensively expounds the Dharma so that one may attain nirvana...
V. Furthermore, when these sentient beings dwell in the Heaven of Longevity (Ābhāsvara), they neither hear nor see the repentance for karmic retribution. This is the fifth. VI.

Furthermore, when a Tathāgata appears in the world and extensively expounds the Dharma so that one may attain Nirvāṇa, yet these sentient beings dwell in the borderlands (pratyantajanapada), slandering the noble ones (ārya) and committing various perverse deeds—repentance for such karmic retribution. This is the sixth. Furthermore...
When a Tathāgata appears in the world, he extensively expounds the Dharma so that beings may attain nirvana.

Yet these sentient beings are born in a central land, yet lack the six sense faculties, and furthermore cannot distinguish between wholesome and unwholesome dharmas. Seventh is the repentance for karmic retribution.
Furthermore, when a Tathāgata appears in the world and extensively expounds the Dharma so that beings may attain Nirvāṇa, these sentient beings reside in the Middle Kingdom.
Although their six sense faculties are complete and without deficiency, those beings possess minds and consciousnesses of false views;
they lack wisdom and understanding, and they hold that there is no giving nor recipient, nor is there retribution for good or evil deeds, nor is there a present [life].

There is no future world; there are no parents; nor are there śramaṇas or brāhmaṇas who have attained the state of an arhat, having realized it for themselves and dwelling in their own liberation. They merely repent for the retribution of their sins. Eighth:
furthermore, if the Tathāgata does not appear in the world and does not preach the Dharma, but passes directly into parinirvāṇa, then these beings are born [into this state].

In China, people possess all six sense faculties and are capable of receiving the Dharma. Being intelligent and highly talented, they understand the teachings upon hearing them and practice with right view.
Thus, there are things, there is giving, and there are recipients; there is retribution for good and evil, and there are this world and future worlds.

Furthermore, there are śramaṇas and brāhmaṇas who cultivate right view and realize arhatship; yet they have neither heard nor seen [the teaching on] the repentance of karmic retribution for transgressions.
We have been shrouded by ignorance and failed to recognize the causes of transgression that lead to the three miserable realms and the eight difficult conditions.
Now, having encountered this site of enlightenment, we are finally able to awaken to this truth. We take refuge in the Tathāgata Vairocana and the ocean-like assembly of all worthy and holy ones.

We burn incense and scatter flowers, confessing and repenting for the causes of transgression leading to the three miserable realms and the eight difficult conditions; we dare not conceal them. By virtue of these causes and conditions, [may we be purified].
May all karmic retributions of myself and the ocean of sentient beings within the Dharma-realm be purified.
Next, the mudrā and mantra for repentance and the eradication of transgressions: Oṃ sarva-pāpa-megha-spharaṇa-damana-daraya svāhā.
(One should recite this three times:
The sins accumulated over a hundred kalpas Are all swept away in a single thought-moment; Like fire consuming dry grass, they are utterly extinguished without remainder.
All the evil karma I have created in the past, Arising from beginningless greed, hatred, and delusion,
Produced by my body, speech, and mind— I now repent it all. Having repented,
with a sincere heart I take refuge and pay homage to the Honored One, Vairocana Buddha.
○ (Proclamation: Listen, all you people, to these verses on impermanence from the Sūtras:
Once I recall your countenance, as beautiful as blossoming willows, Who would have known that your hair would fall in disheveled strands?
If you wish to recognize the messengers of King Yama who hasten one’s life, Look at these white hairs that have come to inform you!
The ghost of impermanence is difficult to evade; it pursues one immediately upon one's standing, allowing no delay.
Seeing person after person utterly worn away and extinguished, how much longer can one’s own self endure?

*The Ritual for the Constant and Universal Prostration and Repentance of the Tenfold Vows and Practices of the Sea-Seal Samādhi at the Site of Enlightenment from the Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Great Vaipulya.*
Scroll Nine:

The Ritual for the Constant and Universal Prostration and Repentance of the Tenfold Vows and Practices at the Sea-Seal Bodhimanda from the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra* (The Flower Ornament Scripture of the Buddha’s Great Extensive Enlightenment). Scroll Ten.
Compiled by the Śramaṇa Huìjué of Yíxíng, Dharma Master Hùfǎ of Cí'ēn Monastery at Yúnyán on Mount Lán during the Táng Dynasty;
supplemented with annotations by the Śramaṇa Pǔruì of Zàiguāng Monastery on Mount Cāng during the Sòng Dynasty;
and revised by the Buddhist disciple Mùzēng, Minister of Public Works (Sìchuān Bùzhèng) who was loyal, righteous, and devoted to his sovereign during the Míng Dynasty. Qīnbāozhōngyì.
Compiled by the śramaṇa Duce of Jigwang-sa on Chicken Mountain,
based on the study of the teachings and contemplations of the Tiantai school, and finalized by the śramaṇa Jeongji.
The tenth session.
With all reverence, we pay homage to the inexhaustible Triple Gem.
May these members of the assembly each kneel on their right knees and, holding fragrant flowers, make offerings according to the Dharma.
May this ocean-like cloud of offerings pervade the worlds of the ten directions. May these incalculable (*asaṃkhyeya*) worlds be filled with wondrous jewels. Incalculable...
The world was filled with garments; incalculable worlds were filled with exquisite fragrances;
incalculable worlds were filled with ornaments; incalculable worlds were filled with immeasurable mani-jewels;
incalculable worlds were filled with wonderful flowers; incalculable worlds were filled with supreme flavors; incalculable worlds...
It is filled with wealth and treasures. In incalculable worlds, seats are filled; they are covered with jeweled canopies and spread with exquisite cloths.
In incalculable worlds, variously adorned jeweled crowns are filled.

With such various articles of offering, one constantly makes offerings to the ocean-like assembly of Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and holy sages, arranged in the infinite layers of Indra’s Net. Receive this...
Clouds of offerings serve as a platform of radiance, vast as the boundless realms, immeasurable and inexhaustible; may they perform the work of a Buddha.
Having made these offerings, all pay homage with reverence.
Next, I offer clouds of offerings such as these—
vast oceans of the nature of jewels and precious gems, and most excellent seven-jeweled mountains—
arising before all the Buddhas and others. I present them as an offering.
Oṃ sarvamaṇḍatāratrottamabodhyaṅgasamaraśiṣṭarātsame hūṃ. The *Ratnakūṭa Sūtra* states:
"There is a dhāraṇī named 'Infinite Varieties of Mantras,' which can accomplish all things and possesses great power."
Yes. The dhāraṇī is: Oṃ sīmala sīmala mīmada sigrāmaha liṅga hūṃ.
Next is the seal-mantra for bestowing great wisdom.
Oṃ namas tathāgatāyāvalokiteśvarāya samara samara hūṃ. (Praise of the Buddha in Sanskrit)
The Buddha’s body is without distinction, Pervading the entire dharma-realm.
It can cause those who behold the form-body to be skillfully tamed according to their capacities.
All the sons of the Buddhas in this assembly, Who have well cultivated manifold wisdoms, These people are already able to enter Such gates of expedient means, Within each and every land.
Universally proclaiming a vast and sublime sound, he speaks of the spheres of the Buddhas' conduct;

his voice is heard throughout the lands of the ten directions as he directly praises the World-Honored Buddha for the pure deeds he cultivated in all realms of existence under countless buddhas in the past.
Thus, one obtains various jewel-lights; the vast clouds of great compassion of the Flower Treasury Adorned World-Ocean pervade all.
Having sacrificed bodies as numerous as the atoms of immeasurable lands through the power of practice during oceans of past eons, this world is now free from all defilements.
Emitting great light that pervades space, Supported by the power of the wind, it remains unshaken.
The Buddha-treasury is universally adorned with mani-jewels, Made pure by the Tathāgata’s power of aspiration.
He scatters everywhere exquisite *maṇi*-treasure flowers, Which abide in the sky through the power of his former vows.
A sea of various firm and majestic adornments, clouds of light pervading the ten directions;
within all the mani-jewels are clouds of Bodhisattvas, who universally visit the ten directions;
their blazing light forms wheels of radiant flames, adorned with exquisite flowers, circulating throughout the Dharma-realm without exception.

From within all jewels, pure light is emitted; That light shines universally upon the ocean of sentient beings, Pervading all lands throughout the ten directions, Causing them all to emerge from suffering and turn toward Bodhi.
Within the jewels, there are Buddhas as numerous as sentient beings; From their pores, they manifest emanated forms.
Brahmā Kings, Śakras, and Wheel-Turning Kings, all sentient beings,
and the light-manifestations of all Buddhas pervade the Dharma-realm; within that light,
they proclaim the names of all Buddhas and employ various skillful means to subdue and guide, universally responding to all living beings without exception.
Within every single atom of all the worlds in the Flower Treasury, the Dharma-realm is seen;
Precious lights manifest Buddhas gathering like clouds— this is the Tathāgata’s mastery over realms,
A vast cloud of vows that pervades the entire Dharma-realm, transforming sentient beings throughout all kalpas.
The practices of Samantabhadra’s ground of wisdom are all perfected; All adornments emerge from this.
Homage to the Buddha Vairocana, the Original Honored One of the Ten Unimpeded Bodies, within the Flower Treasury World-Ocean of the Great Vaipulya Buddha Avataṃsaka Sūtra.
Homage to Śākyamuni Buddha, the Greatly Compassionate and Greatly Merciful One who made five hundred vows to save sentient beings from suffering in the five turbidities.

Homage to Bhaiṣajyaguru-vaiḍūryaprabha-rāja Buddha, the King of Lapis Lazuli Light, who made twelve supreme vows to save sentient beings from suffering in the five turbidities in the Pūrṇacandra World in the eastern direction.
Homage to Amitābha Buddha of the Western World of Ultimate Bliss, who, through his forty-eight vows, rescues beings from suffering amidst the five turbidities.

Homage to the ocean of the perfect teaching of the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra* of the Great Vaipulya, within all the lands as numerous as motes of dust throughout the worlds of the ten directions and three periods of time across the entirety of empty space.
Homage to the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Samantabhadra, who presides over the truth of conduct and vows within the Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Great Vaipulya;
homage to Mañjuśrī, who presides over the wisdom of faith, understanding, and realization within the Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Great Vaipulya.
Homage to the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva,
the Greatly Compassionate and Greatly Merciful One who rescues from suffering in the five turbidities, the Thousand-Handed and Thousand-Eyed Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva.

Homage to the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Kṣitigarbha-Rāja, whose great vows are vast and profound, who rescues beings from suffering in the five turbidities, who appears in worlds where no Buddha dwells, who comforts the hearts of men, and who eternally abides in the realm of Yama.
Homage to the ten stages of faith Bodhisattvas within all the lands as numerous as atoms throughout the entirety of space in the ten directions and three periods of time.

Homage to the Bodhisattvas dwelling in the ten practices (*daśa-caryā*), the ten dedications (*daśa-pariṇāmanā*), the ten stages (*daśa-bhūmi*), and the stage of Equal Enlightenment (*samyak-saṃbodhi*);
to the assembly of all oceans of Bodhisattvas, numbering as the atoms within the oceans of lands throughout the entire Dharma-realm;
and to the fifty-five [sections] on the places of cultivation and realization in the final assembly of the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra*, the Great Vaipulya Scripture of the Buddha.
The Noble Sudhana, who paid homage to the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra* during its final assembly; a vessel of perfect capacity and superior faculties who sought the Dharma through a hundred cities;
one who perfected the bodhisattva practices within a single lifetime; and the model for cultivation and realization of the sudden gate for the final age.

The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva pays homage to all Buddha-activities— whether in the form of the Dharma-body, the form-body, physical relics, precious stupas, or temple edifices— within all the lands as numerous as atoms throughout the entirety of space across the ten directions and the three periods of time;
as well as to the treasuries of the Dharma and the places where the Dharma is preached.
Homage to the assembly of all noble and saintly Bodhisattvas, the ocean-like multitude;

to those who have donned the armor of great vows to seek birth in the Pure Land; to those who protect the True Dharma during the final dregs of the age; and to the National Preceptors who guard the nation.
With a sincere heart, I take refuge and pay homage to the World-Ocean of the Flower Treasury within the Great Vaipulya Buddha-Flower Adornment Sūtra,
the Honored One Vairocana Buddha;
Namo to the Honored Assembly of all Oceans at the Site of Enlightenment of the Ten-Bodied Unobstructed Tathāgata Vairocana.
Homage to the Dharma Gate of the Causes and Effects of Vairocana in the Flower Treasury Adorned Ocean of Worlds;
throughout the ten directions, we take refuge. May our sins be extinguished and our pure faith increase, and may we be reborn within the Flower Treasury Ocean, the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss.
Chapter Five: The Flower Treasury World.
First, the explanation of the essential nature of the cause and fruit of the Flower Treasury.
The Sūtra says: At that time, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva... [up to] ...adorned and purified by great vows as numerous as motes of dust.
May I, together with all sentient beings, be reborn in the Flower Treasury Ocean, within the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss.
Next, regarding the wind-circle upon which it rests, the *Sūtra* states: "O Sons of the Buddha, this Flower Treasury Adorned World... all its adornments emerge from this."
May I, together with all sentient beings, be reborn in the Flower Treasury Ocean within the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss.
Homage to the assembly of all oceans of beings at the Vairocana Bodhimanda, which pervades the entire Dharma-realm through the seven locations and nine assemblies in this Jambudvīpa.
Homage to the ocean-like assembly of all beings at the Vairocana bodhimanda throughout the entire dharma-realm in the hundred billion Sahā worlds of similar categories;
homage to the Vairocana bodhimanda throughout the entire dharma-realm in the twenty lands of dissimilar categories, such as those shaped like trees and so forth.

Homage to all the ocean-like assemblies in the world-system of Blazing Jewel Radiance Universally Illuminating the Ten Directions, within the ocean of fragrant waters called Boundless Wondrous Flower Light,
throughout the entire realm of reality, in the assembly of the Vairocana Bodhimanda.

Homage to the ocean-like assembly at the Vairocana Bodhimanda, which pervades the world-systems within the Flower Treasury World— world-systems as numerous as the atoms in ten unspeakable numbers of Buddha-fields.
Homage to those who dwell throughout the Flower Treasury World and beyond,
filling the oceans of lands in the ten directions of the Dharma-realm, as extensively as the Flower Treasury itself.
Homage to the assembly of all oceans of beings at the Vairocana Maṇḍala of the Dharma-realm;
before them, all lands are composed of atoms, and within each atom there are Buddha-fields of various types pervading the entire Dharma-realm—
the assembly of all oceans of beings at the Vairocana Maṇḍala of the Dharma-realm.

Homage to the infinite assemblies of the ocean-like multitude at the Vairocana Bodhimaṇḍa throughout the entire Dharma-realm, wherein every single mote of dust— whether within realms that exist or do not exist,
or realms with or without motes of dust— is pervaded by boundless realms of similar and dissimilar types.
Homage! Within each and every atom, there are gathered oceans of lands; within these lands, there are further atoms, and within those atoms, there are yet more oceans of lands.
Atom by atom, they are inexhaustible; land after land, they are uninterrupted.
Like the net of Indra, they are layered upon layer beyond measure, pervading the entire Dharma-realm at the Bodhimanda of Vairocana.
Homage to all the ocean-like assemblies!

Homage to all the ocean-like assemblies at the sites of enlightenment of all Buddhas throughout the ten directions, the three periods of time, and the entire dharma-realm of the pervasive void, in every ocean of lands—just so for all.
Homage to all the ocean-like assemblies!

Homage to all Buddhas, as numerous as all sentient beings, dwelling upon the great lotus thrones of various radiant stamen-fragrance banners within the fragrant water seas of the Flower Treasury World.
Homage to the jewel-lights of the four dharma realms seen within every single atom of all the atoms in the Flower Treasury World.
In the midst of the light, all Buddhas appear like gathering clouds;
I take refuge in those such as these, as numerous as the atoms within the Flower Treasury World’s seas of fragrant water, filling the worlds of the ten directions like dense, overhanging clouds;
and within all the mani-jewels, there are oceans of assemblies of Bodhisattvas appearing like clouds.
All in the ten directions take refuge; Sins are extinguished and pure faith increases. May they be born within the Flower Treasury Ocean and the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss.
(Part Six: The Arrayed Adornments of the Flower Treasury Ocean)
The *Vajramaṇḍala-parvata-sūtra* states:
At that time, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva... [throughout] by the Buddha’s sovereign power, causing all to be pervaded.
May I, together with all sentient beings, be reborn in the Flower Treasury Ocean within the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss.
II. The Jewel Ground of the Terrace (The realization of the nature of mind in accord with the vow).
The Sūtra says: "At that time, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva... [up to] all such miraculous transformations."
May I, together with all sentient beings, be reborn in the ocean of the Flower Treasury, within the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss.
[From] the *Three Fragrant Waters Sutra*:
At that time, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva... [up to] ...all these are the sovereign power of the Tathāgata.
May I, together with all sentient beings, be reborn in the ocean of the Flower Treasury, within the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss.
From the *Sutra on the Fragrant River* (Xihai jiangxiang jing): At that time, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva... [until] ...the reflections of all Buddhas appeared brilliantly.
May I, together with all sentient beings, be reborn in the Flower Treasury Ocean, within the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss.

At that time, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva... [up to] ...all according to their inclinations became completely pure.

[Verse 6: Summary of the Adornments] The *Sūtra* states:
At that time, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva... [omitted] ...by the power of his original vows, dwells therein.
May I, together with all sentient beings, be reborn in the Flower Treasury Ocean within the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss;
in the midst of the mani trees of the Vajra-Wheel Encircling Mountains of the Flower Treasury World, may the Great Radiance appear,
and within each ray of light, may all the Tathāgatas Vairocana be manifest.
Homage to the infinite manifestations of all colors and forms within the various adornments of the Vajra-rimmed Mountains surrounding the Flower Treasury World,
where infinite Buddhas appear; homage to the infinite,
successively arrayed, and inexhaustible rows of jewels within the various jewel grounds of the Flower Treasury World, like Indra’s net.

Homage to all the Tathāgatas who manifest their shadows throughout the Flower Treasury World, within each and every fragrant water ocean— which contains as many fragrant water oceans as there are atoms in four continents—
within the precious cloud-canopies of all those Vairocana Tathāgatas.
Homage to all Buddhas within the fragrant river jewel-cloud canopies, as numerous as the atoms in the four continents, in each and every fragrant ocean of the Flower Treasury World;
homage to the various forms and characteristics of the diverse causal practices cultivated within the swirling eddies of the fragrant rivers of the Flower Treasury World.
From within all jewels emerge all Buddhas.
Homage to the great fragrant river of the Flower Treasury World! Pure pearls and gems are like gathering clouds;
the fragrant rivers completely cover those jeweled nets, wherein all Buddhas appear with radiant brilliance.
Homage to all Buddhas who manifest vast bodies within the jewel-tree groves upon the ground between the various fragrant rivers of the Flower Treasury World;
homage to the Great Radiance Adorned with Myriad Jewels upon the ground between the various fragrant rivers of the Flower Treasury World.
I pay homage to all Buddhas throughout the ten directions;
I pay homage to all Buddhas within every single atom of dust upon the ground between the fragrant rivers of the Flower Treasury World;
I pay homage to all Buddhas within all oceans of worlds.
Homage to the ocean-like assembly of all boundless Bodhisattvas who, within the Vajra-rimmed Mountains of the Flower Treasury World, hold canopies and burn incense, pervading the entire Dharma-realm.
Homage to the great [Bodhisattvas] throughout the various jewel grounds of the Flower Treasury World, who travel everywhere throughout the ten directions proclaiming their great vows.

Homage to the ocean-like assembly of all Bodhisattvas in the Flower Treasury World, within oceans as numerous as the atoms of ten unspeakable numbers, who manifest supernatural powers while holding various canopies,
together with the ocean-like assembly of all infinite Bodhisattvas.
Homage to all the Bodhisattvas who constantly emerge from the clouds of sublime sounds within the fragrant water whirlpools of the Flower Treasury World,
pervading the entire Dharma-realm.
Homage to such sons of the Buddha, as numerous as the atoms within the unspeakable numbers of fragrant oceans in the Flower Treasury World.

All the ocean-like assemblies in the ten directions take refuge in the site of enlightenment; may their transgressions be extinguished and their pure faith increase, and may they be reborn within the Flower Treasury Ocean and the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss.
Next, for the purpose of repenting through the condemnation of transgressions against the prohibitive precepts,
I pray that the inexhaustible Triple Gem of the Buddha, Dharma, and Sangha of the Indra’s Net, Vairocana Tathāgata,

the assembly of holy beings including Samantabhadra and Mañjuśrī, and all mundane and supramundane deities, by virtue of your compassionate original vows, may emit great radiance to illuminate this Dharma assembly.
I pray that you will bear witness to me, protect me with mindfulness, and compassionately embrace me.

May I and the ocean of all sentient beings, from beginningless time until this very moment, confess and repent for our transgressions of violating the precepts—transgressions as inexhaustible as the ocean of karma and as infinitely layered as Indra’s net.
The *Mahāprajñāpāramitā-śāstra* states: "Because neither transgression nor non-transgression can be apprehended, one should fulfill the śīla-pāramitā.

Śīla (in the language of Qin, 'nature of goodness') consists in delighting in the practice of the good path and not being self-indulgent; this is called śīla. Alternatively, it refers to undertaking the precepts and practicing virtue."
Whether one has not received the precepts or practices virtue, all such acts are termed *śīla*. To speak briefly, *śīla* consists of the eightfold restraint of body and speech:
refraining from harming others, refraining from stealing, refraining from sexual misconduct, refraining from false speech, refraining from divisive speech, and refraining from harsh speech.

Abstaining from frivolous speech, abstaining from intoxicants, and maintaining a pure livelihood—this is called precept (*śīla*). If one fails to guard them and abandons them, this is called breaking the precepts.

Those who break these precepts fall into the three evil realms. If one maintains the precepts to a lesser degree, they will be born among human beings; those who maintain them to a middling degree will be born among the gods of the six heavens of the desire realm (*kāmadhātu*);

and those who maintain them to a superior degree, further practicing the four dhyānas and the four formless absorptions (*ārūpyasamāpatti*), will be born in the realm of form (*rūpadhātu*) or the formless realm (*ārūpyadhātu*).

Within the realm of the Heaven of Pure Boundaries (*dhātu-viśuddha-deva*), there are three grades of superior upholding of the precepts: through the lower purity of upholding the precepts, one attains the state of an Arhat;
through the middle purity of upholding the precepts, one attains the state of a Pratyekabuddha; and through the superior purity of upholding the precepts, one attains the Way of the Buddha.

It is unattached and independent, neither broken nor deficient, and is praised and cherished by the Noble Ones. This is called the superior purity of upholding the precepts. If [one practices] loving-kindness...
Out of compassion for sentient beings, for the sake of delivering sentient beings, and because they also know the true nature of the precepts, their minds do not cling or become attached.
Maintaining the precepts in this manner leads them to the path of Buddhahood; this is called attaining the precepts of the unsurpassed path of Buddhahood.
If a person seeks the great benefit of goodness, they should always firmly uphold the precepts as if cherishing precious treasures or protecting their own life. Why is this? For example:
Just as all things in the great earth that possess form rely upon the earth to abide, so too is it with the precepts:
the precepts are the dwelling place for all wholesome dharmas. Furthermore, it is like one who wishes to walk but has no feet, or one who wishes to fly but has no wings.
If one wishes to cross [a river] without a boat, it cannot be achieved. Likewise, if one seeks excellent fruits without the precepts, it is just the same.
If a person abandons these precepts, even if they dwell in the mountains, practice austerities, eat fruit, or take medicinal herbs, they are no different from birds and beasts.
If there are those who take only water as their precept, or consume only milk, or practice breath-retention, or shave their hair, or let their hair grow long, or...
They leave a small tuft of hair on their heads; they wear saffron robes, or white garments, or clothing made of grass, or clothing made of tree bark;
they enter the water in winter or roast themselves by fire in summer; they throw themselves from high cliffs or bathe in the Ganges River.

If one bathes three times a day, makes offerings to the fire twice, performs various sacrifices, recites various incantations, and undergoes ascetic practices, yet lacks this precept, one will achieve nothing in vain.

If there is a person who, though dwelling in a lofty hall or a grand palace and enjoying fine clothing and delicious food, is able to practice this precept, they will be reborn in a favorable realm and attain the fruits of the Path, regardless of whether they are noble or lowly. If...

Whether small or great, all who are able to practice these pure precepts will obtain great benefit. If one breaks these precepts, whether noble or lowly, great or small, none shall be able to be born at will in a favorable realm.

Furthermore, a person who breaks the precepts is like a cool, refreshing pond containing venomous snakes; it is unfit for bathing. They are also like a tree of fine flowers and fruit that is full of thorns.

It is like this: even if a person is born into a noble family, possesses a handsome body, and is widely learned and well-informed, yet does not delight in upholding the precepts and lacks a heart of compassion, it is just the same. As a verse says:
To be noble yet lacking wisdom is decline; to be wise yet arrogant is also decline.
For one who maintains the precepts to then violate them is a total decline in both this life and the next.

Though a person may be poor and lowly, if they can maintain the precepts, they surpass those who are wealthy and noble but have broken them. This is like the difference between floral fragrance and the fragrance of wood.

The fragrance of one who cannot maintain the precepts does not travel far; however, the fragrance of maintaining the precepts pervades the ten directions. One who maintains the precepts is endowed with complete peace and happiness, and their fame travels far.
Devas and humans revere and love them; in this present life, they constantly obtain various kinds of joy.
If they desire wealth, honor, and long life among devas or humans, these are not difficult to attain. Through the purity of maintaining the precepts, all that is wished for is obtained. Furthermore:

When a person who upholds the precepts sees those who break the precepts undergoing imprisonment, torture, and various forms of suffering, they rejoice, knowing for themselves that they will forever be free from such things.
Furthermore, when a person who upholds the precepts sees virtuous people receiving praise, fame, and happiness, [they likewise rejoice].

He thought to himself: "Just as he has gained such renown, I too have a share in it. When a person who has broken the precepts reaches the end of life, the 'wind-sword' dissects their body and their tendons and veins snap;
yet one who knows for themselves that they have maintained the purity of the precepts feels no fear in their heart."
As it is said in verse:
In the midst of great and grievous illness, ethical discipline is the excellent medicine;
In the midst of great terror, ethical discipline is the protection; In the darkness of death, ethical discipline is the bright lamp.
Within the evil realms, morality serves as a bridge; within the waters of the ocean of death, morality serves as a great ship.
Furthermore, one who maintains morality is always honored and supported by people in this world; their mind is joyful and free from regret, and they obtain clothing and food.
There shall be no lack. Upon death, one will be reborn in heaven and later attain the Way of the Buddha. For one who upholds the precepts, there is nothing that cannot be attained;
for one who breaks the precepts, everything is lost. It is like a person who constantly makes offerings to a deity.

This person was poor, yet he made offerings with single-minded devotion for twelve full years, seeking wealth and nobility. The deity took pity on this man, manifested his own form, and questioned him.
He asked him, "What do you seek? He replied, "I seek wealth and honor, desiring that everything my heart wishes for may be obtained.
The deva gave him a vessel named the "Vessel of Attainment" (*prāptaghaṭa*) and said to him, "Whatever objects you require shall all emerge from this vessel.
Having received it, the man obtained whatever his heart desired; there was nothing he could not attain. Having attained his wishes, he prepared [everything] accordingly.
He generously gave away his elephants, horses, and carriages, all fully equipped with the seven treasures, providing for his guests so that nothing was lacking in any matter.
A guest asked him, "Previously you were poor; by what means have you become so wealthy today? He replied, "I obtained a divine vase."
The jar was able to produce these various kinds of objects; thus, his wealth was such as this. A guest said, "Bring out the jar to show me, along with the objects produced from it.
He immediately brought out the jar. From within the jar, he drew forth various kinds of objects. That man, becoming arrogant and heedless, stood upon the jar and danced.
The jar then broke, and all the objects were simultaneously extinguished. It is the same for one who upholds the precepts.

Thus it is: there are various kinds of sublime pleasures that one who observes the precepts shall not fail to obtain. If a person breaks the precepts and becomes arrogant, indolent, and self-indulgent, they are like that person who broke the jar and lost their profit.
Furthermore, the fragrance of the name of one who maintains the precepts pervades the heavens and among humans in both this life and future lives.
Moreover, one who maintains the precepts is someone whom others delight in giving to, never begrudging their gifts.
Regarding wealth and material goods: though one does not cultivate worldly profit, one shall lack for nothing and attain rebirth in the heavens.

Before the Buddhas of the ten directions, one enters the path of the Three Vehicles and attains liberation. However, those who maintain precepts while holding various wrong views will have no attainment thereafter.

Furthermore, even if a person does not leave the household life, if they are able to practice the Dharma of the precepts, they too shall be born in heaven. If a person maintains the precepts with purity...
Purity. One who practices meditation and wisdom, desiring to transcend the suffering of old age, sickness, and death, will surely attain this vow.
For one who upholds the precepts, though they possess no weapons, no evils shall befall them. No one can seize the wealth of those who uphold the precepts.

The kinship of those who uphold the precepts does not part even in death. The adornment of upholding the precepts surpasses that of the seven treasures. For these reasons, one should protect [the precepts].

Precepts are like protecting one's life, and like cherishing precious objects. A person who breaks the precepts undergoes myriad forms of suffering, like a poor man who shatters a jar and loses his possessions.
Furthermore, a person who upholds the precepts should observe the transgressions of those who break them and exert themselves with diligence.
One should maintain the precepts with a single mind. What is called the transgression of a person who breaks the precepts? A person who breaks the precepts is not respected by others;
their home is like a cemetery, a place where people do not go. A person who breaks the precepts loses all merits, just like a withered tree.
People do not love or delight in them; one who has broken the precepts is like a frost-bitten lotus, which people do not wish to behold.
One who has broken the precepts has a malevolent mind that is fearsome, like a rākṣasa. One who has broken the precepts is not sought after by others, like a person suffering from thirst.

One does not draw water from a dry well. The mind of one who has broken the precepts is constantly filled with doubt and regret, just like a person who has committed a crime and is perpetually afraid that punishment will arrive.
A person who has broken the precepts is like a field struck by hail; one cannot rely upon it. A person who has broken the precepts is like a bitter gourd;
though its form resembles a sweet seed, it is unfit for consumption. A person who has broken the precepts is like a village of bandits. It is not...
One may rely upon [the precepts]. A person who has broken the precepts is like a grave illness; people do not wish to draw near them. A person who has broken the precepts cannot escape suffering;
they are like an evil path that is difficult to traverse. One should not dwell together with a person who has broken the precepts;
they are like a wicked thief who is difficult to approach. A person who has broken the precepts is like a pit of fire; the practitioner avoids them.
It is difficult to dwell together with one who has broken the precepts; they are like a venomous serpent. One must not approach or touch a person who has broken the precepts;
they are like a great conflagration. A person who has broken the precepts is like a wrecked ship; one cannot board it to cross over.
A person who has broken the precepts is like vomited food; it cannot be eaten again. Such a person, even while amidst a virtuous assembly, is like a vicious horse...
Among a herd of noble horses, one who has broken the precepts is distinct from the virtuous, like a donkey among a herd of oxen.
A person who has broken the precepts within a community of those who are diligent is like a sick child among healthy people.
Although a person who has broken the precepts resembles a bhikṣu, they are like a corpse among sleeping people. A person who has broken the precepts is like a counterfeit pearl among genuine pearls.
Among these, a person who has broken the precepts is like an *eranda* tree growing in a sandalwood grove.

Although such a person’s outward form resembles that of a virtuous one, they lack virtuous qualities within. Though they shave their heads, dye their robes, and receive the tally-sticks in succession, they are called "bhikṣus" in name only;
in reality, they are not bhikṣus. If a person who has broken the precepts wears the Dharma robes, it is as if they were wearing sheets of hot copper or iron.
It wraps around his body. If he holds an alms bowl, it is a vessel for molten copper.
If he eats what is offered, he is swallowing glowing iron balls and drinking hot molten copper. If he receives offerings and provisions from others, he is a jailer guarding people in hell.
If he enters a vihāra, he is entering a great hell. If he sits upon the couches and beds of the monastic community, it is as follows:
They sit upon beds of hot iron. Furthermore, a person who has broken the precepts is constantly filled with fear, like a gravely ill person who always dreads the arrival of death;
they are also like one who has committed the five heinous crimes, whose mind constantly thinks, "I am a thief of the Buddha," and who hides and flees in dread, like a robber fearing people.
As the months, years, and days pass, they are never at peace. Although a person who has broken the precepts may receive offerings...
To cultivate benefit and happiness is itself an impure pleasure; it is like a fool offering sustenance and adorning a corpse.
When a wise person hears of this, they loathe it and do not wish to see it. Such various and immeasurable transgressions of the precepts are beyond description.
A practitioner should, with a single mind, uphold the precepts.

We have been shrouded by ignorance and failed to recognize the causes of the transgression of violating the precepts. Now that we have encountered this site of enlightenment, we have finally awakened to this knowledge.
We take refuge in the Tathāgata Vairocana and the ocean-like assembly of all worthy sages and saints. We burn incense and scatter flowers.

I openly confess and repent for the karmic offenses of violating the precepts, not daring to conceal them. By these causes and conditions, may all karmic retributions—both my own and those of the ocean-like assembly of sentient beings within the Dharma-realm—be entirely purified.
Next, the mudrā and mantra for repentance and the eradication of transgressions: Oṃ sarvapāpam me kṣayaṃ kuru svāhā.
(Recite three times.)
Sins accumulated over a hundred eons are entirely swept away in a single thought; Like fire consuming dry grass, they are extinguished without remainder.
All the evil karma I have created in the past Arises entirely from beginningless greed, hatred, and delusion.
Whatever has arisen from my body, speech, and mind— I now confess it all.
Having confessed, I take refuge with a sincere heart and pay homage to the Honored One, Vairocana Buddha.
○ (Proclamation: May the assembly listen to these verses on impermanence from the Sūtra:
Thus one should know all phenomena: All are subject to arising and ceasing. Do not act with a heedless mind;
Heedlessness encounters poison and harm. To be cautious and not heedless— This state is called the nectar of immortality.
One who acts with a heedless mind is called a dead dog. Seeing this perilous, fragile suffering, abandon desire and practice meditation early;
only through meditative concentration is there true happiness. As a verse in the Sūtra says:
"If one possesses a mind like that of a fool, delighting in sensual desires, and later encounters decline and affliction..."
Their minds immediately give rise to regret; those who are scorched by the fire of desire, deceived by sensory objects, fail to attain the path of tranquility.

Third, in the Assembly for the Adornment of the Flower Treasury World-System Network, all pay homage with the utmost reverence to the inexhaustible Triple Gem.
All members of this assembly kneel on their right knees, holding fragrant flowers and making offerings according to the Dharma. May this ocean of offerings...
Clouds filled the worlds of the ten directions. He sat upon a lion throne according to his station; that throne was high and vast, extraordinary and exquisite.
Its legs were made of lapis lazuli and fashioned with golden threads; soft garments were spread upon the seat.
Precious banners were erected, and it was perfumed with various wonderful incenses. It was adorned with ornaments of immeasurable miscellaneous jewels and covered with a golden net.
Above, wind-stirred jeweled bells emit wondrous sounds; rare treasures serve as the design, adorning the perimeter.
With such various treasuries of jewels and manifold offerings, they constantly perform worship.

Layer upon layer like a celestial net, the ocean-like assemblies of Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and holy sages receive these clouds of offerings, taking them as luminous terraces that extend throughout boundless realms.
Immeasurable and inexhaustible, may they perform the work of a Buddha.
Having made these offerings, all pay homage with reverence.
Next, they present the jeweled casket.
Clouds of offerings such as these— vast oceans of the intrinsic nature of precious jewels, the most excellent emergence of the seven-jeweled mountains, and so forth—
I offer to all the Buddhas and others. Oṃ sarva-tathāgata-arcana-pūjā-megha-samudra-spharaṇa-samaye hūṃ.
*Phraṇatsamaing Hūṃ*. The *Ratnakūṭa Sūtra* states:
"There is a dhāraṇī named 'The Mantra of Immeasurable Varieties,' which can accomplish all things and possesses great efficacy. The dhāraṇī says:
Oṃ sīmala sīmala maimada sīkala mahāliṅga hūṃ. Next, the mantra of the Amoghamani-mudrā: Oṃ amoghapuṣpamaṇi parame mañjiri tathāgata-milā.
Kīṃ ḍe sa maṃ ta pra sa ra hūṃ. In the Sanskrit praise of the Buddha:
The Buddha-body does not abide within, Nor does it abide without; It manifests through the power of spiritual transformation.

Such is the nature of the Dharma of the Teachers: according to the various classes of sentient beings and the diverse karmic accumulations gathered throughout their births in the world, they manifest various supernatural powers, each appearing differently.
The bodies of all Buddhas are likewise immeasurable and incalculable; none but the Great Awakened Honored One can conceive of them.

To speak directly, when the Buddha, the Tathāgata, attained perfect enlightenment, he entered the samādhi of the wisdom of excellent awakening through the skillful means of a single characteristic (*ekalakṣaṇopāya*).
Having entered it, within his single, vast body of perfect enlightenment, he manifested bodies equal in number to all sentient beings, dwelling within those bodies. As...
The vast body of one who has attained perfect enlightenment is such that the vast bodies of all those who have attained perfect enlightenment are likewise so.
A Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva should understand it thus. O Son of the Buddha, the Tathāgata possesses such immeasurable gateways to the attainment of perfect enlightenment;
therefore, you should know that the bodies manifested by the Tathāgata are immeasurable. Because they are immeasurable, he is called the "Tathāgata."

Regarding the future body within immeasurable realms, which is equal to the realm of sentient beings, O Son of the Buddha, a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva should know that within a single pore of the Tathāgata’s body, there are bodies of Buddhas as numerous as all sentient beings. Why is this?
Because the body of the Tathāgata who has attained perfect enlightenment is ultimately without arising or ceasing; thus, as a single pore pervades the entire Dharma-realm, so do all [bodies].
It is likewise with every pore. You should know that there is not even the slightest place empty of the Buddha’s body. Why is this?

Because the Tathāgata, having attained perfect enlightenment, reaches everywhere. According to their capacities and according to their powers, beneath the Bodhi tree at the site of enlightenment, upon the lion throne, he attains equal and right enlightenment through various bodies. O Son of the Buddha, regarding Bodhi...
Sā-ma-ha-ma, you should know that in every moment of thought, this mind always possesses the perfect enlightenment of the Buddha. Why is this?
Because the Tathāgatas do not depart from this mind when they attain perfect enlightenment. Just as it is with one's own mind, so it is with the minds of all sentient beings;
all possess the Tathāgata’s attainment of equal and perfect enlightenment, vast and pervasive, existing everywhere without exception. It does not...
Uninterrupted and without cessation.

Homage to Śākyamuni Buddha, the Greatly Compassionate and Greatly Merciful One, who made five hundred vows to save suffering beings in the five turbidities.
Homage to Bhaiṣajyaguru-vaiḍūryaprabharāja Buddha, the King of Lapis Lazuli Light, who made twelve supreme vows to save suffering beings in the eastern world-realm of Pūrṇacandra.

Homage to the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Samantabhadra, who presides over the truth of conduct and vows within the Great Vaipulya Buddhāvataṃsaka Sūtra.
