Next, for the repentance of the sixty-four hells:
I take refuge in the inexhaustible Buddha, Dharma, and Sangha jewels of the Indra’s Net; Vairocana Tathāgata; the assembly of holy beings including Samantabhadra and Mañjuśrī;
and all mundane and supramundane deities. By virtue of your compassionate original vows, may you emit great radiance to illuminate this dharma assembly.
May you bear witness and protect us with your mindful regard; may you compassionately accept and sustain me and the ocean of all sentient beings.

From beginningless time until this very moment, the ocean of karma has been inexhaustible, unfolding in the layered complexity of Indra’s net. I now openly confess and repent for all karmic offenses committed in every hell.
The *Jīnglǜ yìxiàng* states: Regarding the sixty-four hells, the first is called "Foot Treading.
In this hell, one is first crushed to death by treading; now, one is trampled by hell-ghosts for two hundred years. One must repent for the retribution of their offenses.

The second is the Mountain of Blades. Having previously killed sentient beings, one now undergoes punishment for two hundred years. To repent for this retribution of sin: The third is the Realm of Thorough Scrutiny.
During life, one spoke with a mind of anger, reviling others as mere birds or beasts. For five hundred years, one’s mouth is pounded with iron pestles.
When the punishment is completed, one receives birth with a human head and a bird’s body, constantly speaking of one’s sins from the mouth. To repent for this retribution of sin.
The fourth is called "Embracing Swords": having committed sexual misconduct oneself during life, or having violated those who maintain the precepts, one repents for this retribution.
The fifth is called "Boiling Sand": first covering sentient beings with hot ashes; one repents for this retribution.

The sixth is the Boiling Well. The water in this well is constantly boiling. Those who first harbor evil intentions and cast impure objects into the well must, upon the exhaustion of their transgressions, remain as frogs within the well for a hundred years.
This is the retribution for their sins; one must repent for it.

The seventh is the "Kitchen Window. The hell-wardens take people and thrust them headfirst into a kitchen window. This woman, when she was born, dragged other men along with her by pulling on their clothes while looking at her own reflection;
this is the retribution for that sin, which is now being expiated.

The eighth is the Mute Ghost (mūka-piśāca). The hell-wardens constantly burn iron combs to cauterize their tongues. During their lifetimes, when their parents or teachers called them, they did not respond.
After two hundred years, they are reborn as mute humans. This is the retribution for their sins; one must repent.

The ninth is Hot Ashes. It is seven hundred li wide and filled with hot ashes. When these people were born into this world, they gave rise to lustful desires and sought out chaste women, but in the end they never achieved their aim.
They undergo punishment for two hundred years. Subsequently, they suffer from sores and terror.
This is the retribution for their sins; one must repent.
The tenth is Boi-xi (Boiling Excrement). It is thirty thousand *li* wide and filled with feces and urine. People are driven into it;

having been given fine food in the past, they now suffer for five hundred years because they spoke with anger, saying the food was impure. Afterward, they are reborn as pigs. One must repent for this retribution of sin.
Eleventh is the Pond of Foul Odor. It is two thousand five hundred li in length and breadth, filled with pus and blood.

When this person was alive, they entered the chambers of a sage with an unwholesome mind, causing them to emit foul odors and discharge filth. They shall undergo punishment for two hundred and forty years.
In future lives, one will be born among the poor and lowly, and one’s body will constantly emit a foul odor. This is the repentance for the retribution of that sin.
Twelfth: Impurity. Even if a space a thousand li square were filled with tears and saliva, one might, out of an arrogant mind, take such impure hands to grasp incense and offer it to the Great Sage.
Consequently, when reborn among humans, one will always be arrogant. This is the repentance for the retribution of that sin.
Thirteen: Impurity. Within six hundred li, there is pus. At birth, one casts mouse droppings and dog food—impure substances—into pure food.
One undergoes punishment for two hundred years. Upon being born, one becomes a dog. This is the retribution for the offense; one must repent.
Fourteenth: Constant Darkness. Because one gave rise to unwholesome thoughts at the time of birth, obstructing the Buddha’s radiance, one undergoes punishment for seven hundred years.
Through the repentance for this retribution of sin, [one is liberated].
Fifteenth: □□. It is forty thousand *li* in length and breadth; there, one is constantly subjected to being hacked, shot at, beaten, prodded, and crushed with stones. This person...

When one is born [into such states] and commits the five heinous crimes (*ānantarya-karma*), one undergoes retribution for kalpas on end. Even as one wanders through various hells, there are likewise kalpas of duration.
For ten thousand years, one must repent for the karmic retribution of these offenses.
The sixteenth is mutual killing: wives kill husbands, husbands kill wives, mothers kill children, and children kill mothers.

Such people, having previously killed the parents of others, as well as the parents and children of sentient beings, will find that when they are later reborn among humans, their parents, children, and grandchildren will all die prematurely.
This is the retribution for their sins; one must repent of it.

Seventeenth is "Mutilating the Body. One is constantly mutilated by hell-demons because one previously mutilated sentient beings. Consequently, in later lives, one encounters officials and legal punishment.
This is the retribution for one's sins; one must repent.

Eighteenth is the "Fire-Cart" hell. Because these people burned and killed sentient beings, they are subsequently born there to be burned; this is the retribution for their sins, which may be expiated through repentance.
Nineteenth is the "Ignorant of the Dharma" hell, filled with deluded people who, upon being born, hear the sound of the *gandī* drum and yet lie down out of arrogance.
In a future life, one will be born in a remote borderland; this is the repentance for the retribution of that sin.

Twenty: the Iron Griddle. Because of roasting shrimp and crabs upon it during one's lifetime, one will subsequently be born with a short lifespan; this is the repentance for the retribution of that sin.
Twenty-first are the hungry ghosts (*preta*). Their bodies are forty *li* in height; their bellies are like granaries of ten thousand *hu*;

their necks are ten *li* long; they constantly suffer from hunger and thirst; their breath is perpetually foul; when they see food, it transforms into burning charcoal, and when they drink, it turns into pus and blood.

This is due to eating vegetarian food while not observing the precepts of fasting. For eight hundred subsequent lifetimes, they will constantly become *rākṣasa*. One must repent for these karmic retributions.
Twenty-second: Hard Charcoal. Having stolen another's property with a covetous mind while alive, one holds hard charcoal in one's hands;
subsequently, one is born into poverty and low status, being employed by others. This is the retribution for sin; one must repent.
The twenty-third is the Boiling Cauldron Hell. Having, while alive, maliciously poured hot water upon insects on the ground, one must repent for this retribution of sin.

The twenty-fourth is the Iron Bed Hell. Having, while alive, committed adultery with another’s wife or forcibly violated a woman who observes the precepts, men shall embrace a copper pillar and women shall lie upon an iron bed; one must repent for this retribution of sin.

Twenty-five is the Iron Ball Hell. Because one roasted and boiled chickens and ducks, one subsequently undergoes constant suffering and confusion. This is the confession for the retribution of that sin.
Twenty-six is the Hell of the Arrogant High Seat. During life, one consumed the offerings of others while relying on one's own perceived virtue.
To give rise to a haughty mind is a karmic retribution for which one must repent.
Twenty-seventh: The hell-demon Black-Ear uses a blade to dismember the body limb by limb; this is the retribution for having committed sexual misconduct with a bhikṣu during his lifetime.
Thereafter, one is born among women of low station; for five hundred years, one takes the body of a eunuch. This is the repentance for the retribution of sin. Twenty-eighth is the Cold Ice [Hell]:
at birth, sentient beings are cast into places of freezing cold. Thereafter, one is born into poverty and is constantly without clothing.
This is the repentance for the retribution of sin.
Twenty-nine is called the Cave of Stone. It is filled with smoke and fire; while alive, one’s evil mind熏 (xūn) and killed sentient beings.

This is the retribution for that sin; now one repents. Thirty is called the Fist and Fork. The hell-demons impale one with forks because of one’s wrathful mind. While alive, one crushed and killed lice and nits. This is the retribution for that sin; now one repents.
31. *Kai* (Regret). This refers to those who crushed lice and nits; they will subsequently be reborn with short lifespans. One must repent for this retribution of sin.
32. Pouring hot water over one's body. This refers to those who, wearing fine garments, seduced other women; after their karma is exhausted, they become birds.

Regarding the animal realm: as for the confession of karmic retribution, the thirty-third [section] states: hungry ghosts have bodies thirty *li* in length. Beneath their throats there is a tumor; they burst it open and eat the pus.
Or, when they see fine food, many ghosts compete to seize it, so that they cannot eat it. This is because, upon obtaining fine food from another, they do not first offer it [to others].
Eating while seated [in a row]. In a future life, one will be born into poverty.
This is a karmic retribution for which one must repent. Thirty-fourth: The bodies of hungry ghosts are ten *li* long, or perhaps five *li*. The hair on their bodies is coarse and sharp.

Because of stinginess and not giving food, they claim things exist when they do not. In a future life, one will be born into poverty and frequently lack food and drink. This is a karmic retribution for which one must repent.
Thirty-fifth is the "Evil Dog" hell. There are many evil dogs there, their fangs as sharp as swords. The hell-demons incite the dogs, which compete with one another to bite the inhabitants.

Because [the beings] called upon dogs to bite and kill sentient beings during their lifetimes, they later obtain human form but take pleasure in being bitten by dogs. This is the retribution for their sins;
one must repent.
Thirty-sixth: To drive people onto iron spikes with one's feet; having harbored poison toward one's parents, teachers, and elders during life, one is subsequently reborn among venomous snakes.
This is the retribution for sin; one must repent.

Thirty-seventh is "Flaying the Skin. This ghost constantly uses sharp knives to flay its own skin. In its previous life, it harbored an evil mind and stripped people of their clothing and bedding, as well as flaying the skins of sentient beings.
When later reborn among humans, it is always robbed and plundered by others. One must repent for this retribution of sin.
Thirty-eight is "Hanging Upside Down. The hell-wardens take the people and hang them upside down. This is the retribution for the sins of hanging living beings upside down during their lifetime;

one must repent for this. Thirty-nine is "Beastly Existence. The hell-demons pour molten copper into the mouths of the offenders. This is the retribution for failing to repay debts incurred during one's lifetime.

Furthermore, in the final five hundred years, one will become a human being’s ox, horse, slave, or servant, often subjected to whipping and beating. This is the retribution for sin; one must repent for it.
The fortieth [hell] is called "Plowing the Body": the hell-demons plow the body with iron plows. This is because in life one plowed fields, harming living beings with an evil mind.
[The assembly] rejoiced. [Next is] the confession for the retribution of sin:
the forty-first is the Iron Arrow Eye Hell. The hell-demons constantly pierce the eyes of the inhabitants with iron arrows.

Because in their previous lives they looked upon their parents with an evil mind and an evil gaze, when they are later reborn among humans, their eyes are always bulging and staring. [This is] the confession for the retribution of sin.
Forty-second is the calamity of weapons. In hell, demons hack and shoot them; in their previous lives as humans, they killed one another with hearts full of anger.
Consequently, when reborn among humans, they frequently encounter being hacked and shot. This is the retribution for their sins; one must repent.
Forty-third is Carving and Piercing. The hell-demons carve the flesh from the inhabitants alive. When this person was in life, they used an evil mind to carve the flesh of others;
once their retribution for this sin is exhausted, they will be born as humans who are prone to carving and piercing. One must repent for this karmic retribution.
The forty-fourth is the Iron Grinding Hell. The hell-demons grind people with iron mills. When these people were alive, they used malicious intent to grind and kill various insects;
this is the retribution for their sins, which must be repented.
Forty-fifth is the [Hell of] Grinding. It is filled with iron grinders. The hell-demons drive the offenders into the grinders to grind them. One must repent for this retribution of sin.
Forty-sixth is Deception. When this person was alive, they saw sentient beings entering into deception and gave rise to an evil mind.
"I vow not to save them. Later, when reborn among humans, their bodies will be yellowish and withered; they must repent for this retribution of sin. Forty-seven is the Stone Mortar Hell:
the hell-wardens drive the offenders into mortars and pound them. When this person was alive, they used an evil mind to pound sentient beings to death.
Once the retribution for the sin is exhausted, they become snails or clams; they must repent for this retribution of sin.
Forty-eighth: The "Proud Person with a Snake’s Body. During this person's lifetime, they would lie on the ground while reciting sutras;

[this hell is for those who] fail to repent for their karmic retributions. Forty-ninth: The "Water Hell. Water remains stagnant and does not flow; during this person's lifetime, they would have suppressed others within water.
They die by drowning. This is the retribution for their sins; they must repent.
The fiftieth [hell] is called *Yinuo* (Submissive). Here, the hell-demons press down on people's heads with stones.

When these individuals were alive, their arrogance led them to make their parents, teachers, and elders rely upon their children, and they spoke without respect. This is the retribution for their sins; they must repent.
Fifty-one is called the Iron Club. The hell-demons constantly cause their bodies to be struck with iron clubs. When these people were alive, they killed lice and nits with malicious intent;
this is the retribution for that sin, which is now being expiated.

Fifty-second is "Terror. One is constantly terrified by the ox-headed *ābhas* demons. Because this person was constantly afraid of others during their lifetime, they must repent for the retribution of their sins.
Fifty-three is called the Iron Stake. Iron stakes are laid at the bottom of the water. The hell-demons drive people into the water, piercing their bodies until they bleed.
In life, they were jealous and used stakes to injure others; this is the retribution for their sins, for which one must repent.
Fifty-fourth: Drinking molten copper. During life, one spoke with arrogance, mimicking the words of parents, teachers, and elders;
consequently, one suffers from stammering as the retribution for this sin.
Through repentance, one may seek relief. Fifty-fifth: Iron Barbs. The hell-wardens pierce the eyes of this person with iron barbs. During life, this person harbored an evil mind.

The fifth and sixth [hells] are called "Piercing the Pupils. Having completed their retribution, they become blind. This is the repentance for the karmic retribution of those who, while alive, harbored evil intentions and pierced the eyes of fish and other sentient beings.
The fifty-sixth is called "Iron Forks. The hell-demons pierce people with iron forks. This person, while alive, used an evil mind to spear fish and other sentient beings.
This is the repentance for the karmic retribution of such deeds.
Fifty-seven is called the "Worms. These gnaw and devour the human body. During this person's lifetime, they injured others and domestic animals out of envy.
When their retribution is exhausted, they become afflicted with malignant sores on the human body. This is the karmic reward for their offenses; one must repent.
Fifty-eight is "Hands Severed with Knives. The hell-demons use sharp knives to sever both hands of this person.
During their lifetime, they used their impure hands to grasp the scriptures out of arrogance; this is the retribution for that sin, which must now be repented.
Fifty-nine is named Weeping. The hell-wardens constantly come to terrify them, causing them to wail.

When this person was alive, they were always anxious about wealth and devoted themselves to carnal desires; consequently, when reborn as a human, they constantly suffer from a lack of resources. One must repent for this retribution of sin.
The sixtieth is called the Iron Hook. The hell-ghosts constantly use iron hooks to hook their bodies. When these people were alive, they used hooks to kill sentient beings;
this is the retribution for their sins, which may be expiated through repentance.

The sixty-first is Molten Copper. The hell-wardens pour molten copper into the mouths of these beings. During their lifetimes, they harbored evil intentions and engaged in false speech, double-tongued talk, harsh abuse, and frivolous chatter.
When their retribution is exhausted, they will have breath that is constantly foul. This is the karmic retribution for their offenses; one must repent for it.

The sixty-second is Molten Copper. The hell-demons pour molten copper over the hands of those who, while alive, did not revere the Way with a respectful mind, but instead grasped the robes of śramaṇas with impure hands; this is the retribution for their sins, which they must now repent.
The sixty-third is Shooting the Body. The hell-demons shoot him with arrows. During his lifetime, this person used an evil mind to shoot and kill living beings;
this is the retribution for that sin, though it may be expiated through repentance.
The sixty-fourth is Avīci (the Liang translation says "Birth and End"). There are five kings in total: first, King Anuvartin; second, King Anukārin;
third, King Kṣetrapati; fourth, King Svayambhū; and fifth, King Sattvapati.
They all give rise to faith and take Mahāyāna vows to deliver sentient beings from the hells. Those whose offenses in the various hells have been exhausted come to enter this realm.

He severed his former practices. According to the amount of sins he had committed, he cast off his hellish body and assumed an intermediate state (*antarābhava*) form, like that of a three-year-old child.
Following his karmic actions once more, he was conceived through his parents. Thus, one should repent for such retributions for sin.
We were shrouded by ignorance and did not recognize the karmic retribution of the hells; now that we have encountered this site of enlightenment, we are finally able to awaken to this knowledge.
We take refuge in the Tathāgata Vairocana and the ocean-like assembly of all worthy and holy ones. We burn incense and scatter flowers.

Regarding the retributions for sins in the hells, I openly confess and repent, not daring to conceal them. By virtue of these causes and conditions, may the retributions for all hellish sins of myself and the ocean of sentient beings within the Dharma-realm be entirely purified.
Next, the mudrā and mantra for repentance and the eradication of transgressions: Oṃ sarvapāpam me kṣayaṃ kuru svāhā.
(Recite three times.)
Sins accumulated over a hundred kalpas are all swept away in a single thought; like fire consuming dry grass, they are extinguished without remainder.
All the evil karma I have created in the past arose entirely from beginningless greed, hatred, and delusion.
I now repent of everything produced by my body, speech, and mind.
Having repented, I take refuge with a sincere heart and pay homage to the Honored One, Vairocana Buddha.
○ (Recitation: May the assembly listen to these verses on impermanence from the Sūtras:
Vigorous physical beauty does not remain, Like a galloping horse; Human life is impermanent, passing away faster than water flowing over a mountain.
Though one exists today, it is difficult to guarantee one’s presence tomorrow.
Why do you let your mind run wild, dwelling now in unwholesome dharmas?
Why do you rely on [these things] to give rise to arrogance, like an evil spirit watching for a person's faults?
The four great evil spirits are just like this; it is also like a decaying house.
The chamber where the master is about to pass away; my own body is likewise so. How could I give rise to evil?

The Twelfth Section: The Samantabhadra’s Practice of Teaching and Contemplation by the Śramaṇa Zhengzhi, for the Stabilization of Concentration;
Part One of the Ten Seas of Rightward Circulation, comprising the first five assemblies.
With all sincerity, we pay homage to the inexhaustible Triple Gem.
May these members of the assembly each kneel on their right knees and, holding incense and flowers, make offerings according to the Dharma.

We pray that this ocean-like cloud of offerings shall pervade the worlds of the ten directions, becoming as many as the sands of the Ganges; may it flow forth from these rivers of jewels all manner of pure and wholesome dharmas. A...
The ocean of jewels of the Saṃgha is filled with the waters of the Dharma. From the asaṃkhyeya lotus flowers of jewels, the sublime sound of the *puṇḍarīka* of the Dharma constantly issues forth.
The asaṃkhyeya Sumeru mountains of jewels—the sovereign kings of wisdom—emerge in exquisite purity.
They are adorned by an incomparable array of asaṃkhyeya eight-faceted, majestic, wondrous jewels strung upon jeweled threads. [Therein are] asaṃkhyeya pure lights...
The jewels constantly emit the great light of unimpeded wisdom, universally illuminating the dharma-realm.
Countless (*asaṃkhyeya*) jewel bells and chimes strike one another, producing sublime sounds. Countless pure jewels manifest all the bodhisattvas, filling [the space] completely.
Countless precious silken streamers hang down everywhere, their colors and forms radiant and pure. Countless wondrous jewels...
The banners were adorned with various jewels and crescent moons. Incalculable jewel-banners could universally rain down immeasurable jeweled pennants.
Incalculable jeweled sashes hung suspended in mid-air, their adornments exquisite and wondrous.
Incalculable jeweled couches produced various subtle and exquisite tactile sensations. Incalculable wonderful jewel-spirals manifested the [virtues] of a Bodhisattva.
The eye of all-knowledge; incalculable (*asaṃkhyeya*) jewel necklaces, each necklace being the sublime and exquisite adornment of hundreds of thousands of bodhisattvas;
incalculable jewel palaces surpassing all others, peerless and incomparable;
incalculable jewel ornaments adorned with *vajra-maṇi* gems; and incalculable various kinds of exquisite jewel ornaments.
It constantly manifests all pure and wondrous colors; incalculable (*asaṃkhyeya*) pure and wondrous jewels of diverse forms and variegated hues shine with penetrating clarity.
Incalculable jewel-mountains form a surrounding wall that encircles it, pure and unobstructed.
Incalculable precious incenses spread their fragrance throughout all worlds;
incalculable precious manifestations—each and every manifestation—pervade the entire Dharma-realm. With such various articles of offering, they constantly perform worship.

The Indra’s Net is infinitely layered. May all Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and the ocean-like assembly of worthy sages receive these clouds of offerings as luminous pedestals, extending throughout boundless realms, immeasurable and inexhaustible, and may they perform the work of the Buddha.
Having made these offerings, with all due reverence,
they next present the most excellent vast oceans of the nature of precious jewels and mountain ranges of the seven treasures.
I bring forth such clouds of offerings as these and present them to all the Buddhas. Oṃ sarva-tathāgata-arcanavidhi-samaya-pratijñā-samaye hūṃ.
The *Ratnakūṭa Sūtra* states: There is a dhāraṇī called the "Mantra of Immeasurable Varieties," which can accomplish all things and possesses great efficacy.
The dhāraṇī is: Oṃ sīmala sīmala maimada sigrāmaha liṅgaṃ hūṃ.
Next is the Mantra of the Mind-Visualization Offering Mudrā (one should place the two hands in vajra-añjali at the crown of the head and recite this mantra):
Oṃ sarvamalida me unne aḥ ṣṭrī ma ahaṃ gane svāhā.

When reciting mantras and forming mudrās, one should visualize with the mind that all flowers of water and land, unclaimed by any owner, fill the ten directions throughout the entirety of the realm of empty space.
Furthermore, there are clouds of exquisite ointments for humans and devas, along with burning incense, lamps and lights, banners, pennants, and precious canopies;
various kinds of drums, music, song, dance, and vocal performances; pearl nets, suspended jeweled bells, flower garlands, and white whisks.
Subtle and wondrous bells and chimes; *kaṅkani* nets; wish-fulfilling jewels; clouds of garments; celestial foods of the most exquisite fragrance and flavor;
various pavilions adorned with precious pillars; and the ornaments for the bodies of the gods, such as crowns and necklaces.
With such clouds as these, the practitioner directs the mind so that they pervade all of space. To perform such offerings with a heart of utmost sincerity is the most supreme and excellent.

This practitioner, with a resolute mind, performs this rite, directing the mind to offer worship to the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, the ocean-like assembly of Prajñā, the Vajra-devas, and all the infinite worthies and sages of the various paths of karma.
I pray that out of your compassion you will descend to this assembly and accept my humble offering.
With your Brahma-voice,
you praise the Tathāgata who manifests his body everywhere, entering universally into the world according to the inclinations and desires of sentient beings.
He manifests supernormal powers, Neither dwelling nor departing;
Everywhere he appears, and the Buddha’s radiance Pervades all places without exception. His fame is heard afar;
He has no substance, no place of abiding, And no birth can be found. He is without marks and without form; All that he manifests is like a shadow.
Speaking directly, I praise the Buddha:
like the sun spreading its light to illuminate the Dharma-realm, when the vessel is broken and the water leaks away, the reflection perishes accordingly.
The sun of supreme wisdom is likewise; when sentient beings lack faith, they perceive it as entering nirvana.
Just as when people in the world perform fire rituals, they may sometimes cease within a single city;
so too, the Supreme among Men, having completed his transformative activities throughout the entire Dharma-realm, likewise brings them to an end.
When the time for the manifestation of illusions has passed, he appears in all lands; yet once his purposeful deeds are finished, he then passes away.
The Tathāgata’s transformation is likewise so; in all lands, he is constantly seen as a Buddha.
The Buddha has a samādhi named "Immovable"; having finished transforming sentient beings, he enters this concentration.
In a single thought-moment, his body emits immeasurable light, and from that light emerge lotus flowers, upon which Buddhas reside.
The Buddha’s bodies are numberless, equal to the Dharma-realm, visible only to sentient beings who possess merit.
Thus, each of these countless bodies is fully endowed with majestic adornments at the end of its life.
Like the nature of non-arising, the Buddha appears in the world; like the nature of non-extinction, the Buddha enters parinirvāṇa.
All words and metaphors are utterly transcended; all meanings are accomplished, peerless and beyond compare.
*Namo* to the Buddha Vairocana, the Original Honored One of the Ten Unobstructed Bodies, in the Flower Treasury World-Ocean of the Great Vaipulya Buddhāvataṃsaka Sūtra.
Homage to Śākyamuni Buddha, the Greatly Compassionate One who made five hundred vows to save sentient beings from suffering in the five turbidities.

Homage to Bhaiṣajyaguru-vaiḍūryaprabhārāja Buddha, the King of Lapis Lazuli Light, who made twelve supreme vows to save sentient beings from suffering in the five turbidities in the Pūrṇacandra world in the eastern direction.
Homage to Amitābha Buddha of the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss, who, through his forty-eight vows, rescues sentient beings from suffering amidst the five turbidities.

Homage to the ocean of the perfect teachings of the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra*, the Great Vaipulya Scripture of the Buddhas, throughout all the lands as numerous as atoms within the entirety of space across the ten directions and three periods of time.
Homage to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Samantabhadra, who presides over the truth of conduct and vows within the Great Vaipulya Buddha Avataṃsaka Sūtra;
homage to Mañjuśrī, who presides over the wisdom of faith, understanding, and realization within the Great Vaipulya Buddha Avataṃsaka Sūtra.

Homage to the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva of Great Kindness and Great Compassion, the Thousand-Handed and Thousand-Eyed Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva, Savior from Suffering in the Five Turbidities.
Homage to the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Kṣitigarbharāja, whose great vows are vast and profound; who rescues beings from suffering in the five turbidities and appears in worlds where no Buddha dwells;
who comforts the hearts of sentient beings and eternally abides in the realm of Yama.
Homage to the ten [stages of] faith Bodhisattvas within all the lands as numerous as atoms throughout the entirety of space in the ten directions and three periods of time.

Homage to the Bodhisattvas dwelling in the ten practices (*daśa-caryā*), the ten dedications (*daśa-pariṇāmanā*), the ten stages (*daśa-bhūmi*), and the stage of Equal Enlightenment (*samyak-saṃbodhi*);
to the assembly of all oceans of Bodhisattvas, numbering as many as the atoms within the oceans of lands throughout the entire Dharma-realm;
and to the fifty-five locations for the cultivation and realization of the five marks during the final assembly of the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra*.
The Noble Sudhana, who paid homage to the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra* during its final assembly; a vessel of perfect capacity and superior faculties who sought the Dharma through a hundred cities;
one who perfected the bodhisattva practices within a single lifetime; and the model for cultivation and realization according to the sudden teaching for the final age.
Homage to the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas,

and to all Buddha-activities— including the Dharma-body, the form-body, physical relics, precious stupas, and monasteries— within all the lands as numerous as the atoms of the entirety of space throughout the ten directions and the three periods of time;
as well as to the treasuries of the Dharma and the places where the Dharma is preached.
Homage to the assembly of all noble and saintly Bodhisattvas of the ocean-like multitude;
homage to the Great Vow-Armored One who seeks birth in the Pure Land; homage to the Dharma Master who protects the True Dharma during the final dregs of the summer nation.
With a sincere heart, I take refuge and pay homage to the World-Honored One Vairocana, the Honored One of the Flower Treasury Ocean-World System in the Great Vaipulya Buddha Avataṃsaka Sūtra.
May all those throughout the ten directions take refuge; may their sins be extinguished and their pure faith increase, and may they vow to be born in the Flower Treasury Ocean.
In the *Sūtra on the Fragrant Water Ocean of the Stainless Flame Treasury* located next to the east within the Land of Ultimate Bliss, it says:
"At that time, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva... [omitted] ...the Buddha’s name is Universal Illumination Lamp of Space."
May I, together with all sentient beings, be reborn in the Flower Treasury Ocean within the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss.
[Verse 1] First is the world-system called Able to Sustain;
*Namo*. Next, there are worlds as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many Buddha-fields, containing the world called Fragrance of the Stainless Flame Treasury.

I take refuge in all the assemblies in the oceans of Buddha-assembly sites throughout the world-system of the Universal Radiance of the Great Lotus Adorned with All Fragrant Mani-King Jewels, which emerges from the Ocean of Waters;
may my sins be extinguished, may my pure faith increase, and may I be reborn in the Flower Treasury Ocean.

the World of Palace Adornments with Banners of the Most Lower Level, where the Buddha眉間光徧照 (Bhrūmadhyaprabhā-samantaprakāśa) resides; I take refuge in him.

who are surrounded by as many buddha-fields as there are atoms in a single buddha-field; homage to all the ocean-like assemblies at the sites of enlightenment of all Buddhas.

All in the ten directions take refuge; Sins are extinguished and pure faith increases.
May they be born in the Flower Treasury Ocean, within the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss, in the second inexhaustible wheel of light of the fragrant water ocean.
The Sūtra says: "O Sons of the Buddha, this Fragrant Water Sea of the Stainless Radiant Treasury... [is] named Pure Light of the Dharma Realm.
May I, together with all sentient beings, be reborn in the Flower Treasury Sea and within the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss. [This concludes] the first:

Confess and repent openly.
The *Śūraṅgama Sūtra* states: "Ānanda, all sentient beings are fundamentally true and pure. Because of their deluded vision, deluded habits arise;
because of this, they differentiate between the internal and the external. Ānanda, the internal aspect refers to that which is within the realm of sentient beings."
Due to various attachments and defilements, the deluded sentiments of ignorance arise. As these sentiments accumulate without ceasing, they are able to produce the water of craving.
Therefore, when sentient beings mentally recall delicacies, water flows from their mouths; when they recall past associates—whether with affection or resentment—tears fill their eyes;

when they greedily seek wealth and treasures, their hearts emit a flow of craving that makes their entire bodies glisten and moist; and when their minds are attached as they engage in sexual intercourse, men and women...
The two organs naturally discharge fluids. Ānanda, although various cravings differ, their flowing and binding are the same.
Moistening and not rising upward, they naturally fall downward; this is called the internal constituent. Ānanda, the external constituent refers to that which is outside the realm of sentient beings.

Due to various thirsts and yearnings, empty conceptions are manifested. As these conceptions accumulate without ceasing, they can produce a superior vital energy. Therefore, sentient beings maintain it within their minds.

Observing the prohibitive precepts, the entire body becomes light and pure. With the mind maintaining mantras and mudrās, one’s gaze is majestic and resolute. Desiring to be born in the heavens, one dreams of soaring through the air.
With the mind fixed upon the Buddha-lands, sacred realms manifest in the darkness. Serving spiritual friends, one regards even one’s own body and life as insignificant. Ānanda!
Although various perceptions differ, their lightness and buoyancy are the same; they fly and move without sinking, naturally transcending. This is called the external constituent.
Ānanda, throughout the entire world, birth and death continue in succession: birth follows from habitual tendencies, and death follows from the flux of transformation.

At the moment of the end of life, before warmth and tactile sensation have been abandoned, the good and evil of one’s entire life manifest simultaneously. Death is contrary to birth, yet both follow two types of habitual tendencies.
When these two intersect, if one consists purely of thought, one will immediately fly up and will certainly be reborn in the heavens.

If the mind that flies is accompanied by both merit and wisdom, as well as pure vows, the mind will naturally open, one will see the Buddhas of the ten directions, and one will be reborn in any pure land according to one's wish.
If passion is slight while thought is predominant, one will ascend lightly but not very far, becoming a flying immortal (*fei-xian*), a powerful ghost king, a flying *yakṣa*, or a terrestrial spirit.
Rākṣasas who roam through the four continents encounter no obstacles wherever they go. Among them, if there are those with virtuous vows and virtuous minds who protect and uphold my Dharma;
or those who protect the prohibitive precepts, following those who observe the precepts; or those who protect divine mantras, following those who recite the mantras;

or those who protect meditative concentration (*dhyāna*), preserving and stabilizing the patience of the Dharma (*dharmakṣānti*)—these shall personally dwell beneath the seat of the Tathāgata, their mental dispositions and conceptions being equal and impartial. They shall not...

Those whose thoughts soar do not fall; they are born among humans. When thoughts are clear, the faculties are sharp; when the emotions are obscure, the faculties are dull. [Repentance for the retribution of offenses.

When emotion predominates and thought is scant, one flows into the realm of horizontal birth. The heavy become the fur-bearing multitudes; the light become the winged tribes. [Repentance for the retribution of offenses.

With seven parts emotion and three parts thought, one sinks into the water-wheel and is born at the edge of fire. One receives the breath of fierce flames and becomes a hungry ghost. [Repentance for the retribution of offenses.]

As ghosts, they are constantly burned by fire; water harms them, and for hundreds of thousands of kalpas they have neither food nor drink. This is the repentance for karmic retribution [of the nine-thoughts-and-one-feeling state].
With nine thoughts and one feeling, they descend into the wheel of fire. Their bodies enter the ground where wind and fire intersect.

According to the lightness or heaviness of their offenses, they are reborn in either the *Avīci* (Uninterrupted) or the *Sāntara* (Interrupted) hells. This is the repentance for karmic retribution in these two types of hells. If they are purely emotional, they sink down and enter...

In the Avīci Hell, if one harbors within their heart the slandering of the Mahāyāna, the violation of the Buddha’s prohibitions and precepts, the deceptive and false preaching of the Dharma, the empty consumption of offerings from the faithful, or the unwarranted acceptance of reverence—committing the five heinous crimes and the ten grave offenses—one will be reborn in the Avīci Hells throughout the ten directions.

Although such karmic retribution for the commission of sinful deeds is self-invited, within the commonality of sentient beings there also exists a fundamental ground [of shared karma]. Thus, one must repent for these retributive sins.
Ānanda, all these are the results of the karma produced by those sentient beings themselves. They create ten causes of habitual practice and undergo six types of intersecting retributions.
What are the ten causes? Ānanda, the first is the habit of sexual desire. Through mutual friction it is aroused;
as this grinding continues without ceasing, a great and fierce fire is thereby ignited within. It is like a person using their own hands to rub them together.
Through physical contact, the sign of heat manifests; as these two signs ignite one another, there arise such things as iron beds and copper pillars.
For this reason, all Tathāgatas of the ten directions designate sexual misconduct by the same name: the fire of desire. When Bodhisattvas encounter desire, they avoid it as they would a pit of fire.
This is the repentance for the retribution of such offenses.

Second: When the habit-energies of greed intermingle and calculate, they give rise to mutual attraction. This attraction and grasping do not cease; thus, there comes to be accumulated cold and solid ice.
Within it, one freezes and cracks, just as when a person draws in air with the mouth, a sensation of cold arises.
Because these two habit-energies mutually assail one another, there exist the phenomena of the *ṭaṭa*, *papa*, and *lala* hells, as well as the blue, red, and white lotus cold-hells. Therefore...
All Tathāgatas of the ten directions designate excessive seeking by the same name: "the water of craving. When Bodhisattvas perceive craving, they avoid it as they would a sea of miasma.
This is the repentance for the retribution of transgressions.
Third: The habit of pride intermingles with mutual arrogance, arising from mutual reliance; it flows and surges without ceasing. Because of this, there are the leaping, galloping, and tossing waves.
The accumulation of these waves constitutes water. It is like when the mouth and tongue taste each other’s flavors, whereby water is produced;
as the two habits strike against one another, there arise such phenomena as rivers of blood, rivers of ash, seas of hot sand and poison, and the pouring and swallowing of molten copper. Therefore...
All Tathāgatas of the ten directions identify arrogance as "drinking the water of delusion. When Bodhisattvas encounter arrogance, they avoid it as if fleeing from a great drowning.
[I now] repent for this karmic retribution of sin.
Fourth: The habitual tendencies of anger clash and collide, giving rise to mutual antagonism. This antagonism binds without ceasing, heating the mind until it emits fire;
it smelts the vital breath (*prāṇa*) into metal. For this reason, there exist mountains of knives, iron fetters, sword-trees, wheels of swords, axes, halberds, spears, and saws.

Just as when a person harbors resentment, their murderous intent flies forth and moves; as these two habitual tendencies strike one another, there arise [tortures] such as castration, slicing, beheading, hacking, mincing, piercing, and hammering.
For all these reasons, the Tathāgatas of the ten directions designate anger as the "sharp sword.
When Bodhisattvas see anger, they avoid it as they would an execution; they repent for its karmic retribution.

Fifth: Deceitful practice involves mutual seduction, arising from flirtatious banter that incites an unceasing cycle. Thus there are wooden stocks and fetters, just as when water drenches a field and grasses and trees grow therein;
because these two habits perpetuate one another, there are the various matters of cangues, shackles, pillories, locks, whips, staves, clubs, and maces.
Therefore, all Tathāgatas of the ten directions designate deceit and falsehood with the same name: [the "Deceitful Habit"].
Slander and villainy. When a Bodhisattva encounters deception, he views it as if fearing a jackal or a wolf. Sixth, regarding the repentance for the retribution of offenses:
the habit of deceit involves mutual cheating that arises from mutual entrapment. When such false accusations do not cease, the mind flies into wickedness.
Consequently, there arise dust, excrement, urine, and other foul impurities, like dust driven by the wind, such that each person can see nothing at all. These are the two habits.

These combine; thus there arise various matters such as drowning, leaping, flying, falling, drifting, and sinking. For this reason, all Tathāgatas of the ten directions designate deception and falsehood by the same name:
"Killing. When a Bodhisattva encounters deception, they regard it as treading upon venomous snakes. This is the confession for the retribution of such sins.

Seventh: The habitual tendencies of enmity intermingling with mutual resentment give rise to harbored hatred. Because of this, there are flying stones, thrown rocks, boxes, storage chests, carriage enclosures, jars, and sacks used for crushing.
Just as a person of hidden malice harbors and nurtures evil within, these two habits consume one another;
thus there are various acts of throwing, seizing, striking, shooting, tossing, and grasping. For this reason, all Tathāgatas of the ten directions characterize [this habit] as follows:
"Enemy" refers to the same name as a harmful ghost. When a Bodhisattva sees an enemy, it is like drinking poisoned wine. This is the eighth [aspect of] repentance for karmic retribution:

the mutual illumination of the habit-energy of views. It is like the view of a self-identity (*satkāya-dṛṣṭi*), the grasping at precepts and prohibitions (*śīlavrataparāmarśa*), and various karmas of false awakening that give rise to opposition and produce contrary results.
Because of this, there are kings, messengers, royal officials, witnesses, and legal documents, just as when one is being led away.
As passersby on the road come and go and meet one another, their two habits intersect;
thus there arise interrogation, guile, cross-examination, investigation, scrutiny, searching out, and illumination of good and evil. A youth holds a register in his hand to adjudicate all matters.
For this reason, all Tathāgatas of the ten directions designate this evil view with the same name: "The Pit of Views. When Bodhisattvas perceive all such delusions...
Pervasive Grasping: Like standing on the brink of a precipice filled with poison.
Regarding the Repentance for Karmic Retribution: Ninth, when the habits of injustice and slander intermingle, there arise mountains of rock and stones that crush, grind, plow, and rub.
This is like malicious slanderers who oppress and wrong the virtuous; as these two habits clash, there is pressing down, crushing, and pounding.

Because [such acts] involve the squeezing, filtering, and weighing of all matters, all Tathāgatas of the ten directions identify this with enmity and slander, giving it the common name "the tiger of calumny.
When a Bodhisattva is subjected to such injustice, it is like encountering a thunderbolt. This is the repentance for the retribution of these offenses.

Tenth: The habit of litigation leads to mutual clamor, which arises from concealment and hiding. Because of this, there is the illumination that clearly sees all, such that one cannot hide even in the midst of the sun.
As these two habits confront one another, there are the karmic mirrors and fire-pearls of evil friends that reveal and verify past deeds through various phenomena.
Therefore, the Tathāgatas of the ten directions designate the act of concealment with the same name: [The Name of the Evil Habit] (Note: The specific name is omitted in the source text).
The hidden thief. When a Bodhisattva observes concealment, it is as if one were wearing a high mountain upon one’s head while treading upon a vast ocean.
Regarding the repentance for the retribution of offenses: what are the six types of retribution? Ānanda, all sentient beings create karma through the six consciousnesses;

the evil retributions they attract emerge from the six sense organs. How do these evil retributions emerge from the six sense organs? First, the retribution of seeing invites and draws forth evil fruits. This seeing...
When karma intersects, at the time of death, one first sees fierce fires filling the ten directions.

The deceased’s consciousness flies and falls, riding upon the smoke to enter the Avīci Hell. Two manifestations arise: first, clear vision, through which one can see all manner of evil things and give rise to immeasurable fear;
second, dark vision, wherein one sees nothing in the silence and gives rise to immeasurable terror. Thus it is.
Seeing fire burn, it manifests as hot sand and hot ashes; hearing it burn, it manifests as boiling cauldrons and molten copper;
smelling it burn, it manifests as black smoke and purple flames; tasting it burn, it manifests as scorched pellets and iron gruel; touching it burn, it manifests as hot ashes, furnaces, and charcoal;
and when the mind burns, it produces sparks that scatter and fly, fanning and filling the realm of space. Thus one repents for these retributions of sin.

Second: hearing [teachings] that invite and draw forth evil fruits. When this karmic hearing intersects with such conditions, at the time of death, one first sees surging waves that submerge heaven and earth.
The deceased’s spirit descends and flows along the current, entering the Avīci Hell, where two appearances manifest.

First, when listening with the ears open, one hears various clamors, causing the spirit and mind to become muddled and disordered. Second, when listening with the ears closed, there is silence and nothing is heard, causing the dark soul to sink into oblivion.
Thus, the waves of hearing: when they pour forth through hearing, they can act as reprimands and interrogations;

when they pour forth through seeing, they can act as thunder, roars, and noxious poisonous vapors; when they pour forth through breathing, they can act as rain and mist, drenching all venomous insects.
Pervading the entire body, if the flavor-element is infused, it can become pus and blood, as well as various kinds of filth;
if the touch-element is infused, it can become animals, ghosts, excrement, and urine; if the thought-element is infused, it can become lightning and hail, crushing the heart and soul.

Third, regarding the confession for the retribution of smelling: this karmic act of smelling draws forth evil fruits. When this karma of smelling intersects with death, at the moment of passing, one first perceives poisonous vapors filling the near and far surroundings.
The consciousness of the deceased surges up from the earth and enters the Avīci Hell, where two phenomena manifest.

First is "pervasive hearing": being permeated by various evil vapors, the mind becomes extremely disturbed. Second is "obstructed hearing": the vapors block the senses so they do not pass through, causing one to faint and fall to the ground.
Thus, when these vapors strike the breath, they can manifest as solid matter or as footwear; when they strike the sight, they can manifest as fire or as torches;
when they strike the hearing, they can manifest as drowning or submersion, or as boiling and seething liquids; when they strike the sense of taste, they can manifest as...
It causes hunger and exhaustion; when it strikes, it can cause tearing and rotting, becoming a great mountain of flesh with hundreds of thousands of eyes, where immeasurable beings swarm and devour.
When it strikes the mind, it can turn one into ash or pestilence, or into flying sand and gravel that crushes the body.
Fourth, the retribution for offenses is repented.

Furthermore, the retribution for flavors invites evil fruits; when the karma of such flavors intersects, at the time of death, one first sees an iron net with fierce, blazing flames that completely covers the world.
The deceased’s consciousness passes through and becomes entangled in the net, with its head hanging upside down.
They enter the Avīci Hell, where two manifestations arise: first, the inhalation of breath congeals into freezing ice that freezes and tears the flesh from the body;
second, the exhalation of breath flies forth as fierce fire that chars and rots the bones. Thus, when tasted, it becomes capable of crushing and enduring;
when seen, it can incinerate metal and stone; and when heard, it can become sharp-edged weapons.
When one breathes out, it can become a great iron cage that completely covers the land; when one touches, it can become bows and arrows, crossbows and projectiles;
when one thinks, it can become flying glowing iron raining down from the sky. This is the retribution for sins; one must repent.

Fifth, the retribution of contact invites and draws forth evil fruits. When this contact and karma intersect, at the moment of death, one first sees great mountains approaching from all four sides and closing in, leaving no way out.
The deceased’s consciousness perceives a great iron city with fire-snakes, fire-dogs, tigers, wolves, and lions;
ox-headed jailers and horse-headed rākṣasas, holding spears and lances, drive them into the city gate.
Heading toward the Avīci Hell, two types of manifestations arise: first, contact through conjunction, where mountains close in upon the body, crushing bone, flesh, and blood;

second, contact through separation, where knives and swords strike the body, rending the heart and liver. Such contact through conjunction, when encountered, can become the path, the contemplation, the hearing, and the examination;
such contact through seeing, when encountered, can become burning and heat; and such contact through hearing, when encountered, can likewise [become the path].
As for striking and hitting, stabbing and shooting; when applied to the breath, it can serve as a trigger or a pouch, and as a cudgel or a bond.
When applied to the sense of taste, it can serve as a plow, a pincers, a sword, or a saw. When applied to thought, it can cause things to fall or fly.
They are fried or roasted as retribution for their sins; this is the sixth [point]:
contemplating how retribution invites evil fruits. When these mental activities of karma intersect, at the time of death, one first sees an evil wind blowing away and destroying the land.
The deceased’s consciousness is blown upward into the air, then falls back down with the wind and plunges into the Avīci Hell.

This clarifies two aspects. First, non-awakening: when delusion reaches its extreme, one runs wild and frantic without ceasing. Second, non-delusion: when awakening and awareness arise, suffering is immeasurably searing;
the pain is so profound it is difficult to endure. Such perverse thoughts—when these thoughts are congealed, they can act as the "direction" and the "object";
when these views are congealed, they can act as the "mirror" and the "witness"; when this hearing is congealed, it can act as the "great closing stone."
It becomes ice and frost; it becomes earth and mist. When the breath is bound, it can become great fire-carts, fire-boats, and fire-enclosures.
When the breath is bound in tasting, it can become the Great Screaming Hell, as well as remorse and weeping. When the breath is bound in touch, it can become large or small.
Within a single day, they undergo ten thousand deaths and ten thousand births; they are cast face down or face up. This is the repentance for the retribution of their offenses.
Ānanda, these are called the ten causes and six effects of the hells, all of which are created by the deluded ignorance of sentient beings.
If sentient beings fully commit evil karma, they enter the Avīci Hell and undergo immeasurable suffering for immeasurable kalpas. Their six sense faculties—

If one performs each [of the three acts] individually, and they are committed against their respective objects and faculties, such a person enters the Eight Uninterrupted Hells (*aṣṭāv-avīci-niraya*).
If one commits the three acts of killing, stealing, and sexual misconduct through body, speech, and mind, such a person enters the eighteen hells.

If the three karmas are not all present together, but one occasionally commits a single act of killing or a single act of stealing, such a person enters the thirty-six hells. This applies to each individual faculty.
If one commits a single transgression, that person shall enter one hundred and eight hells. Because sentient beings act and create individually within the world, they enter the realm of commonality;
these arise from deluded conceptualization and do not exist inherently. One must repent for the retribution of such offenses.
Furthermore, Ānanda, these sentient beings have not violated the codes of discipline, nor have they transgressed the bodhisattva precepts, nor have they defiled the Buddha’s nirvāṇa.

Yet, due to various other miscellaneous karmas that have burned them throughout kalpas, their offenses are eventually exhausted, and they receive the forms of various hungry ghosts. This occurs based on their original causes.

To covet material objects is a transgression. When this person’s retribution for their sins is exhausted, they encounter matter and take form; they are called a *guàiguǐ* (strange ghost). Repentance for the retribution of this sin. To covet sensual forms is a transgression.

When this person’s retribution for their sins is exhausted, they encounter wind and take form; they are called a *bòguǐ* (drought ghost). Repentance for the retribution of this sin. To covet delusions is a transgression.
When this person’s retribution for their sins is exhausted, they encounter animals and take form; they are called a *mèiguǐ* (possessing ghost). Repentance for the retribution of this sin.

Confession: Greed and resentment constitute an offense. When this person’s retribution for their offense is exhausted, they encounter insects and take form, becoming what is called a *gudu* (poisonous) ghost.

Confession of the retribution for this offense. Confession: Greedy recollection constitutes an offense. When this person’s retribution for their offense is exhausted, they encounter decay and take form, becoming what is called a *li* (pestilential) ghost.

Confession of the retribution for this offense. Confession: Greedy arrogance constitutes an offense. When this person’s retribution for their offense is exhausted, they encounter vapors and take form, becoming what is called a... [ghost]. Confession of the retribution for this offense.

Hungry ghosts: for the retribution of their offenses, they must repent. Those who commit the offense of greed and deception, when their retribution is exhausted, encounter a subtle essence that takes form;

these are called "demon-ghosts" (*yān-guǐ*). For the retribution of their offenses, they must repent. Those who commit the offense of greed for brightness, when their retribution is exhausted, encounter a vital spirit that takes form.

They are called *wangliang* ghosts. Confess the retribution for their sins. Greed constitutes sin; when these people have finished their punishment, they encounter light and take form, becoming what are called *yishi* ghosts.
Confess the retribution for their sins. Greed for factions constitutes sin; when these people have finished their punishment, [they encounter light and take form...]
When they encounter people, they take form; these are called the *shouzhuang* (transmission) ghosts.
Through repentance for their karmic retribution, Ānanda, these beings all fall due to their pure delusion. Once the fire of karma has burned them dry, they emerge above as ghosts.

All such beings are summoned and led forth by the karma of their own false imaginings. If one awakens to Bodhi, then it is wondrous, perfect, and luminous, fundamentally non-existent [as such ghosts].
All karmic retributions for transgressions are thus repented.
Furthermore, Ānanda, once the karma of the ghost is exhausted, both emotion and perception become empty; only then does one truly exist within the world.
Those who have been mutual debtors with others from previous lives encounter one another as enemies; having become animals, they repay their past debts.

When the strange and ghostly retributions are exhausted, they are born into the human world, mostly as a class of *niǎo* (snakes or serpents). [For this] karmic retribution, one must repent. The ghosts of wind-drought spirits have their retributions extinguished by the wind;
when born into the human world, they mostly become portents of calamity and all manner of anomalous creatures. For this karmic retribution, one must repent.

The ghosts who possess through sorcery and bewitchment, when their retribution for possessing and killing is exhausted, are born into the human world; they mostly become foxes. Repentance for this karmic retribution.

The ghosts of insect-pestilence and sorcery, when their retribution for the destruction by sorcery is exhausted, are born into the human world; they mostly become poisonous creatures. Repentance for this karmic retribution.
The ghosts of decay and pestilence, when their retribution for decay and poverty is exhausted, are born into the human world; they mostly become intestinal worms.

Repentance for the Retribution of Sin: Ghosts of received breath have their qi extinguished and their retribution exhausted; they are born into the human world, mostly as species of food. Repentance for the Retribution of Sin:
Ghosts of lingering gloom have their gloom extinguished and their retribution exhausted; they are born into the human world, mostly as species of clothing. Repentance for the Retribution of Sin:
Ghosts of blended essence have their blending extinguished and their retribution exhausted; they are born into the human world, mostly...

For those of the corresponding category: the spirits of karmic retribution for sins repent and transform; their brilliance fades and their retribution is exhausted, and they are reborn into the human world, mostly appearing as auspicious omens among all classes of beings.

Those who repent for the retribution of their sins—those spirits who depend on humans: when the person dies and their retribution is exhausted, they are reborn into the human world, mostly appearing as ordinary beings. Those who repent for the retribution of their sins.
Ānanda, all these beings have been withered by the fires of karma and are repaying their past debts as animals.
These, too, are all brought forth by their own deluded karmic actions. If they were to awaken to Bodhi, then these deluded conditions would fundamentally be non-existent.
It is as you have said regarding those such as Ratnapadmagandhā, King Vairadeva, and the bhikṣu Sunakṣatra; it is thus.
Evil karma originates from within oneself; it does not descend from heaven, nor emerge from the earth, nor is it bestowed by others.

It is summoned by one's own delusions and must be experienced by oneself. Within the mind of Bodhi, all such things are merely the solidification of empty and floating false thoughts. Thus, one repents of these karmic retributions.
He further addressed Ānanda: "From these animals, they shall repay their former debts.

If those who owe the debt pay more than what is owed, these sentient beings, upon returning to human form, will in turn demand the surplus. This occurs when the debtor possesses both power and merit."
Thus, among human beings, they do not lose their human form as they repay that labor. If they lack merit, they return to the state of an animal to pay off the remaining value of that debt.
Ānanda, you should know that whether one uses money and goods or employs their labor, once the repayment is complete, the obligation ceases.

If, during that interval, one kills another’s life or eats their flesh, and so continues for as many eons as there are motes of dust, they will devour and slaughter one another like a turning wheel, alternating between high and low status without rest.

This cannot cease except through *śamatha* or the appearance of a Buddha in the world. You should now know that those of the owl kind, once their retribution is exhausted, will regain their original forms.
Born among the human race, they are mixed with the dull-witted; repentance for their karmic retribution.
Those who bore the mark of that fault, having fulfilled their requital and regained their form, are born among the human race, mixed with the ignorant; repentance for their karmic retribution.

Those who bore the nature of that fox, having fulfilled their requital and regained their form, are born among the human race, mixed with the mediocre; repentance for their karmic retribution. Those who bore the nature of that poison, having fulfilled their requital...

Their feet are restored to form; they are born among the human race, merging with those of a vigorous nature. Through the repentance for their karmic retribution—○ Those of the class of *ō* (worms) repay their debt, their feet are restored to form;

they are born among the human race, merging with those of a subtle nature. Through the repentance for their karmic retribution—○ Those of the class of *shoku* (eaters) repay their debt, their feet are restored to form;
they are born among the human race, merging with those of a gentle nature. Through the repentance for their karmic retribution—○ Those of the class of *fuku* (those who serve)...

Those who belong to the category of *lun* (倫) have fulfilled their retribution and returned to form; they are born into the human realm, integrated among the class of laborers. They repent for their karmic offenses.

Those who belong to the category of *yinglun* (應倫) have fulfilled their retribution and returned to form; they are born into the human realm, integrated among the class of scholars. They repent for their karmic offenses.

Those who belong to the category of *xiuzheng* (休徵) have fulfilled their retribution and returned to form; they are born into the human realm, integrated among the class of the enlightened. They repent for their karmic offenses.
Those various fellow beings, having fully repaid their debts, returned to human form and were integrated among the ranks of the enlightened.

Having repented for their karmic retributions, Ānanda, all of these have now settled their past debts and returned to the human realm; this has been due to the reckoning of their karma from time immemorial.
Inverted, they harm one another and destroy one another. Failing to encounter the Tathāgata and failing to hear the True Dharma, they naturally revolve within the midst of worldly afflictions.
Such people are called those who are to be pitied; they must repent for their karmic retributions.
We have been shrouded by ignorance and failed to recognize the causes of evil retribution. Now that we have encountered this site of enlightenment, we are finally able to awaken to this truth.
We take refuge in the Tathāgata Vairocana and the ocean-like assembly of all worthy and holy ones. We burn incense and scatter flowers.

For these heavy and evil karmic retributions, I openly confess and repent, not daring to conceal them. By virtue of these causes and conditions, may the heavy sins and evil karma of myself and the ocean-like assembly of sentient beings within the Dharma-realm all become purified.
Next, the mudrā and mantra for repentance and the eradication of transgressions: Oṃ sarvapa-pame-spuṭanadahanadarmaya svāhā.
(Recite three times.)
Sins accumulated over a hundred eons are entirely swept away in a single thought; like fire consuming dry grass, they are extinguished without remainder.
All the evil karma I have created in the past arose from beginningless greed, hatred, and delusion.
Whatever has arisen from my body, speech, and mind, I now confess it all.
Having confessed, I take refuge with a sincere heart and pay homage to the Honored One, Vairocana Buddha.
○ (Proclamation: May the assembly listen to these verses on impermanence from the Sūtra:
If a person acts with heedlessness, it is like poison or fire;
For those who practice heedlessness, at the end of life they suffer affliction. But if a person is not heedless, wherever they go, they should be honored.
Able to reach the state of quiescent extinction, forever free from all negligence.

Scroll Thirteen. Compiled by the Śramaṇa Huìjué, Dharma Master Hùguó of Yíxíng, Yunyán Cí’ēn Monastery on Mount Lán during the Tang Dynasty, based upon the Sūtra.

Supplemented by the Śramaṇa Pūrui of Zàiguāng Temple on Mount Cāngshān during the Sòng dynasty; verified by the Buddhist disciple Mùzēng, Provincial Governor of Sīchuān, who was loyal and devoted to his sovereign;

and reviewed by the Śramaṇa Dúchè of Jìguāng Temple on Mount Jī during the Míng dynasty. This is the most ancient form of Indian writing, dating back to the 4th century BCE. It is written from left to right and is the ancestor of many modern South Asian scripts, including Devanagari (Sanskrit/Hindi), Bengali, Gujarati, Marathi, and Oriya. The script is characterized by its symmetrical, box-like characters where the top of each letter is enclosed by a horizontal line. It was used to write Vedic texts and early Buddhist scriptures. **Key Features:** * **Direction:** Left-to-right. * **Structure:** Characters are composed of vertical strokes with a horizontal serif at the top. * **Vowels:** Most consonants are inherently followed by the vowel "a"; other vowels are indicated by diacritic marks attached to the base character. * **Usage:** Primarily used for religious and scholarly purposes in ancient India. The Thirteenth Session of the *Zhiguan Chuxiu Chanyi* (Manual for the Practice of Stopping and Contemplation) by the Tiantai Śramaṇa Zhizhe:
Following the Rightward Rotation through the Ten Oceans, the Assembly of the Final Five Oceans.
With all reverence, we pay homage to the inexhaustible Triple Gem.
May these members of the assembly each kneel upon their right knees and, holding fragrant flowers, make offerings according to the Dharma.
May this ocean-like cloud of offerings pervade the worlds of the ten directions and be able to bestow all manner of vessels, such as golden vessels filled with...
They were filled with various jewels: silver vessels were filled with many exquisite gems; lapis lazuli vessels were filled with all kinds of treasures;
crystal vessels were filled with immeasurable ornaments; musaragalva vessels were filled with red pearls; agate vessels were filled with coral and maṇi-jewels;
white jade vessels were filled with various fine foods; and sandalwood vessels were filled with celestial garments.
Vajra vessels were filled with various exquisite incenses and flowers; immeasurable and innumerable vessels made of various jewels were filled with immeasurable and innumerable varieties of jewels.
With such jewel vessels, complete with all manner of offering articles, they constantly performed worship.

The Indra-net is infinitely layered. May the ocean-like assembly of Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and holy sages receive these clouds of offerings and transform them into luminous pedestals, vast as the boundless realms, immeasurable and inexhaustible, performing the work of the Buddha.
Having made these offerings, with all due reverence,
they next present the most excellent vast oceans of the nature of precious jewels and the seven-jeweled mountains.
I issue forth such clouds of offerings and present them to all the Buddhas and their equals. Oṃ sarvam-tathāgata-ākarṣaṇa-samaya-spharaṇa-maye hūṃ.
The *Ratnakūṭa Sūtra* states: There is a dhāraṇī called the "Spell of Immeasurable Varieties," which can accomplish all things and possesses great efficacy.
The dhāraṇī is: Oṃ sīmala sīmala maimada sigrāmaha liṅga hūṃ.
Next, the offering of the dhāraṇī: *Namaḥ devadevāya namaḥ amoghavajrasārapratiṣṭhitāya arhatte tathāgatāya alim*.
Khaḍga-saṃhata-mogdhye-tattvānām oṃ mañjira mañjira mā ha mañjira mā ha khaḍga mañjiri mā ha mṛtyu mañjira mā ha mṛtyu-jit-tva mañjiri.
Maha-māna-stambhana-paśana-karmanye-mañjari-sarva-karmanya-avakrānta-mṛṣaṇa-mañjara svāhā.
The Brahma-voice praises the Buddha’s body as it appears in the world; the bodies of all Buddhas are likewise so.
To thoroughly understand their own nature is what is called "Buddha. The Tathāgata knows and sees universally, clearly comprehending all phenomena.
The Buddha-dharma and bodhi—both are unattainable. The Guide has neither coming nor going, nor does he abide anywhere;
being far removed from all perversions, this is called Equal and Perfect Enlightenment.
These are the direct words in praise of the Buddha.
Between the eyebrows of the Tathāgata is a mark of a great man called the "Cloud of Radiance Pervading the Dharma Realm.
It is adorned with *maṇi* jewel flowers and emits a great radiance endowed with the colors of all jewels. Like the sun and moon, it is transparently pure;
its light universally illuminates the lands of the ten directions, manifesting the bodies of all Buddhas. Furthermore, it issues forth wondrous sounds proclaiming the Dharma.
O Sea, even unto the tip of the Tathāgata’s left toe there is a mark of a great man called "Cloud of Manifesting the Transformation-Bodies of All Buddhas.
It is adorned with inconceivable Buddha-light, moon-flames, and universal-fragrance maṇi-jewel flame-wheels,
emitting pure radiance of various jewel colors that fills all oceans of worlds, wherein it manifests—
He manifests all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, expounding the ocean of all Buddha-dharmas.
The Tathāgata Vairocana possesses such great marks of a man as are equal in number to the atoms within ten Flower Treasury World-Oceans;
each and every part of his body is adorned with the wondrous signs of various jewels.
Homage to the Vairocana Buddha, the Original Honored One of Unobstructed Ten Bodies in the Flower Treasury World-Ocean within the Great Vaipulya Buddhāvataṃsaka Sūtra.

All in the ten directions take refuge; Sins are extinguished and pure faith increases.
May they be born within the Flower Treasury Ocean, In the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss, amidst the tenth celestial city, The jeweled battlements, and the fragrant water seas.
The Sūtra says: "O Sons of the Buddha, this mass of vajra-jewels... [up to] the Buddha named Unobstructed Light Universally Illuminating the Dharma Realm.
May I, together with all sentient beings, be reborn in the Flower Treasury Ocean within the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss. [This concludes] the first:
the world-system that can be sustained.

Homage to all the assemblies in the oceans of dharma-assembly sites of all Buddhas within the world-system called Lamp Flame Radiance, located in the Fragrant Water Ocean Jewel Rampart Celestial City, amidst world-spheres as numerous as the atoms in successive Buddha-fields throughout the ten directions.
May all transgressions be extinguished, may pure faith increase, and may we be born in the Flower Treasury Ocean.
In the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss...
Next, [homage] to the Buddha Sun-Moon Sovereign Radiance in the World of Jewel Moonlight Flame-Wheel, which is the very lowest among these worlds.

To all the ocean-like assemblies in the sites of enlightenment, surrounded on all sides by as many worlds as there are atoms in a Buddha-field; to all the ocean-like assemblies in the sites of enlightenment of all Buddhas, we pay homage!
(Namo!)

and to the ocean-like assemblies at the site of enlightenment of the Buddha Virtuous Jewel Flower Light in the World of Boundless Pure Radiance, located beyond as many worlds as there are atoms in a buddha-field.

and to the entire ocean-like assembly at his place of enlightenment.

and to the ocean-like assemblies at the site of enlightenment of the Buddha Sarvamahāpraṇidhāna-raśmi in the world-system Vajramandārava-pradīpa.
