Homage to the Tathāgata Sarvapāpavivarjita. Homage to the Tathāgata Sarvajña.
Homage to these and other hundreds of billions of various names and titles, which cause all sentient beings to individually know and see them,
so that all may take refuge throughout the ten directions, extinguish their sins, increase their pure faith, and vow to be born within the Flower Treasury Ocean and the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss.
The Sūtra says: "O Sons of the Buddha, just as it is in this Sahā world, so it is in the eastern direction (and so on until) he preaches the Dharma for them.
May I, together with all sentient beings, be reborn in the Sea of Flower Treasury, within the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss.
[This] sequence applies universally to all Buddhas throughout the ten directions.
Homage to the Tathāgatas whose names are variously different throughout the worlds of the eastern direction— hundreds of thousands of billions,
infinite, immeasurable, boundless, incomparable, incalculable, ineffable, inconceivable, unfathomable, and unspeakable in number,
as many as exist within the entire dharma-realm and the realm of empty space— and likewise in the south, west, and north.
In the four intermediate directions, above, and below, likewise in all places,

I take refuge with the utmost sincerity in all Tathāgatas. I pay homage to the World-Honored One Vairocana, the Honored One of the Flower Treasury Ocean World-System, the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra* of the Great Vaipulya.
Homage to the assembly of all oceans of beings at the site of enlightenment of the Tathāgata Vairocana, whose ten bodies are unimpeded.
Homage to the Dharma-door of the "Chapter on the Four Noble Truths" from the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra*.
Homage to all four hundred billion ten-thousand names for the Four Noble Truths as spoken within this Sahā world-system.

I take refuge in this Dharma door throughout the ten directions; May my transgressions be extinguished and my pure faith increase; May I be reborn within the Flower Treasury Ocean, the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss.
The *Sūtra on the Chapter of the Four Noble Truths*, Fascicle Eight, states:
At that time, Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva... [leading them] according to what their hearts desire, so as to bring them to subdual.
May I, together with all sentient beings, be reborn in the Flower Treasury Ocean and within the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss.
Homage to all the Four Truths and all dharmas within all worlds throughout the entire dharma-realm and space-realm—
countless, immeasurable, boundless, incomparable, innumerable, ineffable, inconceivable, unfathomable, and unspeakable—
in the hundreds of thousands of billions of worlds to the east, south, west, north, the four intermediate directions, and above and below, in this Sahā world.
I take refuge in these and other such gateways to all dharmas of the four noble truths in a hundred thousand million varieties, as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many Buddha-fields.
With a sincere heart, I take refuge and pay homage to the World-Honored One Vairocana, the Honored One of the Flower Treasury Ocean-World System in the Great Vaipulya Buddhāvataṃsaka Sūtra;
throughout the ten directions, I take refuge, extinguish my sins, increase my pure faith, and vow to be born in the Flower Treasury Ocean.
In the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss, next is the lay repentance:
I take refuge in the inexhaustible Buddha, Dharma, and Sangha jewels of the Indra’s Net; in Vairocana Tathāgata; and in Samantabhadra and Mañjuśrī.

The assembly of noble ones gathered like the ocean; the world-protecting gate-guardian deities, by virtue of their compassionate original vows, radiate great light that illuminates this dharma assembly.

May they bear witness, protect, and keep us in mind; may they look upon us with pity and compassionately accept us. I pray that for myself and the ocean of all sentient beings, from the beginningless past...
Up to the present time, I openly confess all the karmic actions of a householder. The *Ratnakūṭa Sūtra* states:
"What is called 'home' is named the slayer of roots of goodness; it is named the failure to abandon faults and the harming of those who assist in wholesome karma."
Therefore, it is called the "name-group" (*nāmakāya*). Why is it said to be "contained"? Because all fetters (*saṃyojana*) abide within it; thus it is called "contained.
Furthermore, because they abide in unwholesome thoughts, abide in lack of self-control, and abide in shamelessness and lack of dread of blame, they are foolish, petty worldlings (*pṛthagjana*).
One dwells amidst unwholesome conduct and the faults of various evils; therefore, it is called "home" (*gṛha*). Furthermore, all the sufferings and afflictions of household life manifest therein;
because it destroys prior roots of goodness, it is called "householder" (*gṛhastha*). Moreover, as for "home," one dwells within it.
There is no evil that one does not commit while dwelling within this. Thus, toward parents, śramaṇas, and brāhmaṇas, one lacks respect and compliance;
this is what is called "home. Furthermore, as for "home," it is where the branches of long-standing attachment, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, and affliction all arise;

it is where killing, binding, scolding, beating, anger, reviling, and the production of harsh words are gathered together. For this reason, it is called "home. One has not yet performed any wholesome deeds.

Roots. They are restless and do not perform [virtue]; they cause all roots of goodness already performed to be scattered and extinguished. They are censured by the wise—namely, by the Buddhas and their śrāvakas.
If one dwells within these, one falls into the evil realms; if one dwells within these, one falls into greed, hatred, and delusion. Therefore, they are called "households.

If one dwells within these, they obstruct and cause the abandonment of the aggregate of morality, the aggregate of concentration, the aggregate of wisdom, the aggregate of liberation, and the aggregate of the knowledge and vision of liberation.

It is a collection of views; therefore, it is called a "home. If one dwells within it, one is encompassed by craving for parents, wife, children, sisters, relatives, friends, and acquaintances, constantly preoccupied with wealth.
Greed is never satisfied, like the ocean swallowing rivers—it is ultimately insatiable.
If one dwells in the household life, it is like fire consuming wood; one's thoughts are unsettled, like the wind that does not abide. This is dwelling at home.
The body perishes, like having ingested poison; all manner of sufferings converge upon it. Therefore, one should renounce it as if avoiding an enemy.
If one dwells in the household life, the noble Dharma creates obstacles, and causes for dispute arise frequently, always in opposition.
Living at home, one is entangled in a mixture of good and evil conditions and burdened by many affairs. Life in the household is impermanent; one cannot remain there for long. This is...
The dharma of dwelling at home is extremely painful because one must seek protection; it is full of many anxieties regarding enemies and kin.
Dwelling at home is devoid of self, yet one erroneously conceives of "mine. Dwelling at home is deceptive and lacks substantial reality, appearing as if real though it is not.
Dwelling at home involves separation, for it is a place where many people reside. Dwelling at home is like a phantom, containing many gathered beings who lack true substance. Dwelling at home...
A household is like a dream, for its rise and fall alternate; a household is like dew, for it quickly breaks and falls; a household is like a drop of honey, for its flavor lasts but a moment;

a household is like a web of thorns, for one is greedily attached to forms, sounds, smells, tastes, and tangibles; a household is like a needle-mouthed insect, for one does not perceive the nature of food;
a household is like a venomous snake, for members mutually encroach upon one another; a household is full of longing, for the mind is constantly restless.
Householders have many fears, for they are plundered by kings, thieves, water, and fire. Households abound in disputes and are fraught with many afflictions.

One must repent for the retribution of transgressions. Householders are defiled by dust; those who have left the home life possess sublime excellence. Householders are bound by fetters; those who have left the home life are without bonds. Householders...

The householder life is full of defilements; the life of renunciation is free from them. The householder is encompassed by evil; the one who has gone forth is encompassed by goodness. The householder is submerged in the mire of sensual desire;
the one who has gone forth remains far removed from the mire of sensual desire. The householder dwells with the vulgar; the one who has gone forth dwells with wisdom.

The householder maintains a livelihood through wrong means; the one who has gone forth maintains a pure livelihood. The householder is full of defilements; the one who has gone forth is stainless. The householder is subject to decline; the one who has gone forth...
There is no cessation [of suffering] for those at home; they dwell in sorrow. Those who have gone forth rejoice. Dwelling at home is a ladder to all evils; going forth is the removal of that ladder.
Dwelling at home is bondage; going forth is liberation. Dwelling at home is accompanied by fear; going forth is fearless.

Those who live at home are subject to punishment; those who have left the home life are free from punishment. Those who live at home have many afflictions; those who have left the home life are free from affliction. Those who live at home experience feverish distress;

those who have left the home life are free from such distress. Those who live at home suffer the pain of much seeking; those who have left the home life are free from the pursuit of pleasure. Those who live at home are restless and agitated; those who have left the home life are free from agitation.

Those who live at home are impoverished and miserable; those who have left the home life are free from misery. Those who live at home are timid and weak; those who have left the home life are free from timidity. Those who live at home...
The householder’s life is lowly; the life of one who has gone forth is noble. The householder’s life is burning; the life of one who has gone forth is tranquil.

The householder’s life is for the benefit of others; the life of one who has gone forth is for one’s own benefit. The householder lacks vital moisture; the one who has gone forth possesses great nourishment.

The householder cultivates the joy of fetters; the one who has gone forth cultivates the joy of cessation. The householder increases thorns; the one who has gone forth is free from thorns. The householder accomplishes minor dharmas; the one who has gone forth...

The household life brings about the great Dharma; yet, while remaining at home one is undisciplined, whereas upon leaving home one is tamed. At home one is separated from the precepts, whereas leaving home one protects the precepts.
The householder increases the oceans of tears, milk, and blood; leaving home dries up these oceans of tears, milk, and blood.
Householders are censured by all Buddhas, Śrāvakas, and Pratyekabuddhas; those who have left home are praised by all Buddhas, Śrāvakas, and Pratyekabuddhas.
The householder lacks contentment; the renunciant possesses contentment. The householder delights the Māra; the renunciant causes the Māra sorrow.
The householder is unsubdued; the renunciant is subdued. The householder is a servant; the renunciant is a master. The householder dwells at the limit of birth and death;

the renunciant dwells at the limit of *nirvāṇa*. The householder falls into ruin; the renunciant extracts one from ruin. The householder is in darkness; the renunciant is illuminated by light. In the house...

The faculties of those who live as householders are not self-mastered; the faculties of those who have gone forth are self-mastered. Those who live as householders are wild and dissolute; those who have gone forth are not dissolute.

Those who live as householders are inconsistent with the Dharma; those who have gone forth are consistent with the Dharma. Those who live as householders look downward; those who have gone forth look upward.

The householder has many undertakings; the renunciant has few undertakings. The householder has little strength; the renunciant has great strength. The householder is crooked and deceitful; the renunciant is upright and honest.
The householder has much sorrow; the renunciant is without sorrow. The householder is pierced by arrows; the renunciant is free from arrows.
The householder is subject to illness; the renunciant is free from illness. The householder is subject to the law of aging; the renunciant possesses the vigor of youth.
The householder is characterized by negligence; the renunciant cultivates the life of wisdom. The householder is full of deceit; the renunciant is without deceit.

The householder performs much worldly activity; the renunciant is free from such activity. The householder is a vessel of poison; the renunciant is ambrosia. The householder is beset by calamities; the renunciant is free from calamities. The householder...
They do not renounce. Those who have left the home life practice relinquishment; those who live at home take up poisonous fruits, while those who have left the home life take up non-poisonous fruits.
Those who live at home are associated with what is unloved, whereas those who have left the home life are not associated with what is unloved.

For those who live at home, delusion is heavy; for those who have left the home life, wisdom is light. Those who live at home lose their skillful means; those who have left the home life possess pure skillful means. Those who live at home lose the correct [path].

The mind. Those who have left the household life possess a pure and upright mind; those who remain in the household lose the ultimate mind. Those who have left the household life possess the ultimate mind;

those who remain in the household cannot provide salvation, whereas those who have left the household life provide salvation. Those who remain in the household create poverty and inferiority; those who have left the household life do not create poverty.

Remaining in the household is no refuge; leaving the household life constitutes a refuge. Remaining in the household is no sanctuary; leaving the household life constitutes a sanctuary. Remaining in the household is no destination; leaving the household life constitutes a destination. Those who remain in the household are full of anger; those who have left the household life...
Abounding in loving-kindness. The householder bears burdens; the renunciant casts off the burden. The householder does not bring all disputes to an end;
the renunciant brings disputes to an end. The householder has faults; the renunciant is without fault. The householder is occupied with busywork; the renunciant is free from busywork.

The householder suffers from feverish affliction; the renunciant is free from fever. The householder has many enemies; the renunciant has no enemies. The householder accumulates stores; the renunciant...
There is no accumulation. For those at home, wealth is firm; for those who have left home, virtue is firm. Those at home are accompanied by sorrow; those who have left home are tranquil from sorrow.
Those at home suffer depletion; those who have left home experience increase. Those at home are easy to attain; those who have left home are difficult to find even in hundreds of millions of eons.

Those at home are easy to practice; those who have left home are difficult to practice. Those at home follow the current; those who have left home go against the current. Those at home abide in worldly dharmas; those who have left home [abide in the Dharma].

The boat and raft: the householder is bound by the river; the renunciant crosses and ferries across. The householder is on this shore; the renunciant is on the other shore. The householder is entangled in fetters; the renunciant is free from fetters.
The householder harbors resentment; the renunciant pacifies resentment. The householder follows the laws of kings; the renunciant follows the Dharma of the Buddha.
The householder is defiled by craving and attachment; the renunciant is free from such defilement. The householder gives rise to suffering; the renunciant gives rise to happiness.

Living at home is shallow and near; leaving home is profound and far-reaching. Living at home has easy companions; leaving home has difficult companions. For those living at home, the wife is their companion; for those who have left home, the mind is their companion.
Living at home involves sudden and busy affairs; leaving home means being free from such affairs. Living at home brings suffering upon others; leaving home brings joy to others.
Living at home consists of the gift of material wealth; leaving home consists of the gift of the Dharma. Living at home holds the banner of Māra; leaving home holds the banner of the Buddha.
The householder dwells in a nest; the renunciant leaves the nest. The householder follows what is not the Path; the renunciant leaves what is not the Path.
The householder dwells in a dense forest; the renunciant leaves the forest. Thus one repents of the retribution for transgressions.
Furthermore, the *Sūtra on the Merit of Image-Making* states: "Maitreya, there are four causes and conditions by which men receive the body of a woman.
What are these four? First, to address the Buddha, various bodhisattvas, and all holy ones with a woman’s light voice while laughing and calling out to them.
Second, to speak with a slanderous mind against those who purely maintain the precepts, saying that they have violated them. Third...
First, one is fond of practicing flattery and deceiving others; second, upon seeing another who surpasses oneself, one gives rise to jealousy in the heart.
If a man commits these four deeds, after his life ends, he will certainly receive a female body and undergo the sufferings of immeasurable evil realms.
However, if he deeply arouses faith, repents of what he has previously done, and fashions an image of the Buddha, then all those transgressions [will be extinguished].
Extinction. He shall certainly never again receive the retribution of a woman’s body. Maitreya, there are four causes and conditions by which men receive the body of a *paṇḍaka* (eunuch).
What are these four? First, mutilating the bodies of others, even down to animals.
Second, becoming angry at, laughing at, slandering, or defaming śramaṇas who uphold the precepts. Third, because of excessive lust, violating the precepts with the mind. Fourth...

One who personally violates the precepts and further encourages others to do so, or a man who first commits such an act but later develops faith and fashions an image of the Buddha—until his attainment of Buddhahood—shall not suffer this retribution. He shall instead become a man with all male faculties complete.
Maitreya, there are four kinds of karma that cause a man to receive a body with both sexual organs, making him the most wretched among all people.
Regarding those of lower status: what are the four? First, committing impurity with one who is to be revered.
Second, being defiled by attachment to improper places on a male body. Third, engaging in sexual acts with oneself. Fourth, prostituting one's own female form to others.
If there are sentient beings who have previously committed such acts, they should deeply reproach themselves and repent.
Regarding past transgressions, if one gives rise to pure faith and creates an image of the Buddha, one shall not receive this body until the attainment of Buddhahood.

Furthermore, Maitreya, there are four conditions that cause certain men’s minds to constantly give rise to feminine desires and to take pleasure in others, while performing the roles of men toward themselves.
What are these four? First, they may harbor resentment or engage in playful slander and defamation of others. Second...
First, they delight in making women's clothing and ornaments. Second, they commit lewd acts with women of their own kin.
Third, though lacking true superior virtues, they falsely accept the honors due to them. By these causes and conditions, they cause the great householders to give rise to such distinct afflictions.
If they repent of their past transgressions and do not create new ones, their minds will develop faith and joy, and they will manifest the form of a Buddha.
When their offenses are thus extinguished, this mind also ceases. Maitreya, there are five kinds of stinginess that can ruin sentient beings.

What are these five? First is stinginess regarding the neighboring villages where one dwells; because of this, one will be born in the wilderness. Second is stinginess regarding the house and dwelling where one resides;
one will take the body of an insect and dwell constantly in filth and excrement. Third is stinginess regarding physical beauty...

First, if one is attached to beautiful forms, one will experience ugliness and unsatisfactory appearances. Second, if one is stingy with one's own possessions and wealth, one will suffer poverty and a lack of clothing and food.

Third, if one is stingy with the Dharma one has learned, one will receive the retribution of being dull-witted or reborn as a beast. Fourth, if one is stingy with all one’s resources, one will undergo the state of poverty where clothing and food are scarce. Fifth, if one is stingy with the teachings one knows, one will receive the retribution of being stubborn and dull like an animal.
However, if one regrets one’s past karma and creates a majestic image of the Buddha, one will forever be free from the mind of stinginess and shall not suffer what was mentioned above.

[The Buddha] said, "Maitreya, there are furthermore five conditions that cause sentient beings to be born in frontier regions or during times when the Buddha-dharma does not exist. What are these five?

First, they do not produce pure faith toward the Triple Gem, which is the field of merit. Second, they turn their backs on reality and violate the principles [of the Dharma], yet they settle into the practice of the instructions.
Third, they provide instruction that is not in accordance with reality. Fourth, they break the harmony [of the Saṃgha]."
To cause a harmonious Saṃgha to split into two factions; fifth, to cause even the very fewest number—down to two bhikṣus—to become discordant.
If one permanently abandons these karmic actions and creates images of the Buddha, they will always encounter the appearance of a Buddha and constantly hear the essential teachings of the Dharma.
Furthermore, there are five causes and conditions by which Maitreya’s sentient beings are constantly reviled and driven away by others, even by their own close relatives.
Nor do they take pleasure in seeing them. Why? Because there are five [faults]: first, double-tongued speech; second, harsh speech; third, frequent quarreling; fourth, excessive anger;
and fifth, skillfully speaking words that appear similar [to the truth] in order to practice slander. If, later on, they should resolve their minds [toward awakening]...
By fashioning images of the Buddha, repenting of one's prior evil karma, and vowing never again to commit the transgressions one has committed, all such offenses shall be extinguished.
One will be beloved and respected by all people. Why is this? Because the Buddhas possess immeasurable and boundless supreme merit and virtue;
immeasurable and boundless great wisdom; and immeasurable and boundless samādhis, liberations, and other such seeds.
Because we have planted seeds of rare and wondrous meritorious dharmas, we now repent for the retribution of our transgressions.
Enshrouded by ignorance, we did not recognize the causes of our offenses; only now, having encountered this site of enlightenment (*bodhimaṇḍa*), are we able to awaken to them.
We take refuge in the Tathāgata Vairocana and the ocean-like assembly of all worthy sages. We burn incense and scatter flowers, [forming] a net of Indra.
Again and again, I confess and reveal all sinful karmas, not daring to conceal them.
By this cause and condition, may all karmic retributions for myself and the ocean of sentient beings within the Dharma-realm be completely purified.
Next, the mudrā and mantra for repentance and the eradication of transgressions: Oṃ sarvapāpam me kṣayaṃ kuru svāhā.
(Recite three times.)
Sins accumulated over a hundred eons are all swept away in a single thought; like fire consuming dry grass, they are extinguished without remainder.
All the evil karmas I have created in the past arose entirely from beginningless greed, hatred, and delusion.
I now repent of everything produced by my body, speech, and mind.
Having repented, I take refuge with a sincere heart and pay homage to the Honored One, Vairocana Buddha.
○ (Proclamation: May the assembly listen to these verses on impermanence from the Sūtra:
All pleasures are impermanent; They must inevitably end in exhaustion. Do not indulge in these delusive pleasures To take as your own source of joy.
When there is no pleasure, there is also no permanence; When life ends, one must surely face calamity.
Having already understood this Dharma, One should diligently practice the bodhisattva path;
Seeking with diligence and without negligence, One shall attain the place of deathlessness. Those who constantly practice negligence Constantly tread the path toward death.

The Nineteenth Session of the *Zhiguan Chuyao* for Practicing Teaching and Contemplation by the Tiantai Śramaṇa Zhizhe:
All Pay Homage with Reverence to the Three Inexhaustible Jewels.
All these people knelt with their right knees on the ground, solemnly holding incense and flowers to make offerings according to the Dharma. They made this vow:
"May this ocean-like cloud of offerings pervade the worlds of the ten directions. May there be incalculable (*asaṃkhyeya*) jewels as its ground;
incalculable palaces, incalculable gates and portals, incalculable windows, incalculable stairways, and incalculable railings."
The roads of the saṃghārāma were all composed of the seven precious jewels. Countless (*asaṃkhyeya*) banners and countless parasols were arranged in rows all around.

Countless necklaces of various jewels, countless necklaces of pearls, and countless necklaces of red pearls, as well as countless necklaces of *siṃhamaṇi* beads, hung down everywhere. There were countless crescent moons and...
It was adorned with incalculable silk ribbons and incalculable jeweled nets. Incalculable jeweled bells produced melodic sounds when stirred by the wind.
Incalculable varieties of celestial flowers were scattered; incalculable celestial jewel-garlands and sashes were suspended;
and incalculable clusters of precious incense burners were arrayed. Incalculable fine powdered incense and gold dust rained down, and incalculable jewels were suspended.
Mirrors. Burn incalculable jewel lamps. With such various articles of offering, constantly perform offerings.
Like the Indra-net of Indra, layer upon layer, may the ocean-like assembly of Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and holy sages accept these offerings.
May clouds serve as luminous platforms, vast beyond boundless realms, immeasurable and inexhaustible, vowing to perform the work of the Buddha.
Having made these offerings, they pay homage with all reverence.
Next, they present oceans of vast self-natures of precious lattices and jewels, along with the most excellent seven-jeweled mountains and the like.
I bring forth such clouds of offerings as these and present them to all the Buddhas.
Oṃ sarva-tathāgata-arcana-pramukha-samagra-siddhaye svāhā hūṃ.
The *Ratnakūṭa-sūtra* states: "There is a dhāraṇī named 'Innumerable Kinds of Mantras,' which can accomplish all things and possesses great efficacy.
The dhāraṇī is: Oṃ sīmala sīmala mīmada sīkala mahāliṅga hūṃ."
Next, bind the seal and recite the mantra of the Vast Amogha-maṇi (the same as before for binding the seal):
Oṃ amoghapāśa mahāvidyārāja tathāgatamūrdhābhiṣikta sarvamantrapadānāṃ adhipati hūṃ.
With Brahma-like voice he praises the Buddha;
the Buddha-body cannot be grasped. Without birth and without arising, it manifests universally before all things in accordance with their needs.
Equal as space, within a single pore it displays transformations, And all Buddhas speak in unison.
Passing through immeasurable eons, those [eons] have no limit. The power of Vairocana Buddha’s vows pervades the entire realm of sand-grains;
Within the lands of the ten directions, he constantly turns the unsurpassed wheel.
[Thus] directly praising the Buddha.
Just as true suchness is neither born nor extinguished, And, being without location, universally manifests great benefit;
So too is the conduct of the Great Benefactor: Transcending the three times, it is immeasurable;
It is neither the realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*) nor not the realm of phenomena, Neither finite nor infinite.
The conduct of those of great merit is likewise: It is neither measurable nor immeasurable, for it has no body.
Just as a bird flies through space for two thousand years, With no distinction between the space before and behind;
So too, though one were to expound the Tathāgata’s conduct Throughout many eons, what has been said and what remains unsaid Cannot be measured.
The Golden-Winged Bird surveys the great ocean from the sky, Parting the waters to seize the male and female dragons;
The One of Ten Powers can uproot those with wholesome roots, Causing them to emerge from the sea of existence and eliminate all delusions.
Like the sun and moon traveling through space, They illuminate all things without making distinctions.
Wandering throughout the world within the Dharma-realm, Teaching and transforming sentient beings without a single stirring thought—
Namo to the Vairocana Buddha, the Honored One of Ten Unobstructed Bodies, the Ocean of Flower Treasury Worlds within the Great Vaipulya Buddhāvataṃsaka Sūtra.
Homage to Śākyamuni Buddha, the Greatly Compassionate One who made five hundred vows to rescue beings from suffering in the five turbidities.
Homage to Bhaisajyaguru-vaidūryaprabhārāja Buddha, the King of Lapis Lazuli Light, who made twelve supreme vows to rescue beings from suffering in the eastern world-realm of Pūrṇacandra.
Homage to Amitābha Buddha of the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss, who, through his forty-eight vows, rescues those suffering in the five turbidities.

Homage to the Ocean of the Perfect Teachings of the Great Vaipulya Buddhāvataṃsaka Sūtra within all the lands as numerous as atoms throughout the entirety of space across the ten directions and three periods of time.
Homage to the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Samantabhadra, who presides over the truth of conduct and vows within the Great Vaipulya Buddha-avatamsaka Sūtra.
Homage to Mañjuśrī, who presides over the wisdom of faith, understanding, and realization within the Great Vaipulya Buddha-avatamsaka Sūtra.

Homage to the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva of Great Kindness and Great Compassion, the Thousand-Handed and Thousand-Eyed Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva, Savior from Suffering in the Five Turbidities.

Homage to the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Kṣitigarbharāja, who possesses great vows profound and vast, who rescues beings from suffering in the five turbidities, appears in worlds where no Buddha dwells, comforts the hearts of people, and eternally abides in the realm of Yama.
Homage to the ten [stages of] faith Bodhisattvas within all the lands as numerous as atoms throughout the entirety of space across the ten directions and three periods of time.

Homage to the Bodhisattvas dwelling in the ten practices (*daśa-caryā*), the ten dedications (*daśa-pariṇāmanā*), the ten stages (*daśa-bhūmi*), and the stage of Equal Enlightenment (*samyak-saṃbodhi*);
to the assembly of all oceans of Bodhisattvas, numbering as many as the atoms within the oceans of lands throughout the entire Dharma-realm;
and to the fifty-five [sections] on the places for cultivating and realizing the five states within the final assembly of the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra*.
The Noble Sudhana, who paid homage to the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra* during its final assembly; a vessel of perfect capacity and superior faculties who sought the Dharma through a hundred cities;
one who perfected the Bodhisattva practices within a single lifetime; and the model for cultivation and realization of the sudden gate for the final age.
Homage to the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas,
and to all Buddha-activities— whether in the form of Dharma-bodies, physical bodies, images, śarīra relics, precious stupas, monasteries,

or within the treasuries of the Dharma and the places where the Dharma is preached— throughout the entirety of the realm of empty space and the lands as numerous as motes of dust in the ten directions and the three periods of time.
Homage to the assembly of all noble bodhisattvas, oceans of merit;
to those who have donned the armor of great vows to seek rebirth in the Pure Land; and to the Dharma-protecting National Preceptors who safeguard the True Dharma in this degenerate age.

With a sincere heart, I take refuge and pay homage to the World-Ocean of the Flower Treasury within the Great Vaipulya Buddha-Flower Adornment Sūtra, to the Honored One Vairocana Buddha, and to the entire ocean-like assembly at the site of enlightenment of the Tathāgata Vairocana of Ten Unobstructed Bodies.
Namo! To all the ocean-like assemblies at the site of enlightenment of the Tathāgata Vairocana of Ten Unobstructed Bodies.
Homage to the Dharma-gate of the Chapter on the Enlightenment of Radiance within the Great Vaipulya Buddhāvataṃsaka Sūtra;
I take refuge in all directions. May my transgressions be extinguished and my pure faith increase, and may I be reborn in the ocean of the Flower Treasury and the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss.

The *Jingguangming jue pin* (Chapter on the Awakening of Radiance), the Ninth Scripture, states: At that time, from beneath the wheels on the two feet of the World-Honored One... [up to] ...the Buddha pervades empty space in this same manner.
May I, together with all sentient beings, be reborn in the ocean of the Flower Treasury and within the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss.
Next, I pay homage to the Buddhas of the Dharma-realm,
both principal and attendant, and to the ocean-like assembly at the site of enlightenment of the Tathāgata Vairocana, whose ten bodies are unimpeded;
I pay homage to the World-Honored Buddhas seen sitting within the ten billion Jambudvīpas of this trichiliocosm.
Homage to the Lotus-Treasury Lion Throne, surrounded by bodhisattvas as numerous as the atoms in ten buddha-fields;
and to all the Tathāgatas who sit upon Lotus-Treasury Lion Thrones throughout the hundreds of millions of Jambudvīpas in the ten directions beyond this world,
in each of the ten buddha-lands, as numerous as the atoms in ten buddha-fields.
Surrounded by a multitude of bodhisattvas,

I pay homage to the Tathāgata who is seen sitting upon a lion throne within the Lotus Treasury, amidst hundreds of millions of Jambudvīpas throughout the hundreds of worlds in the ten directions beyond ten worlds—
[a sight] visible to all as numerous as the atoms of ten buddha-fields.
Homage to the Tathāgatas seated upon lotus-treasury lion thrones within the ten billion Jambudvīpas across a thousand worlds beyond a hundred worlds in the ten directions,
surrounded by all the bodhisattvas as numerous as the atoms in ten buddha-fields.

Together they surrounded [the Buddha] who was seated upon a lion throne within a lotus treasury in the midst of ten billion Jambudvīpas throughout the thousands of worlds in the ten directions beyond a thousand worlds,
amidst all the bodhisattvas as numerous as the atoms in ten buddha-fields.
Together they surrounded [the Buddha],
who was seated upon a lion throne within the Lotus Treasury, amidst ten billion Jambudvīpas across a hundred thousand worlds in the ten directions beyond ten thousand worlds,
together with all the bodhisattvas as numerous as the atoms of ten buddha-fields.
Surrounded by all the bodhisattvas,

I take refuge in the Tathāgatas who sit upon lion thrones within the Lotus Treasury amidst hundreds of millions of Jambudvīpas across a hundred million worlds throughout the ten directions, beyond more than a hundred thousand worlds—
Tathāgatas as numerous as the atoms in ten buddha-fields, together with all their bodhisattvas.
Homage to all those Tathāgatas,

numbering as many as the atoms in ten buddha-fields, who sit upon lion thrones within the Lotus Treasury amidst the hundred koṭis of Jambudvīpas in each of one billion worlds throughout the ten directions, beyond more than a million worlds, and who are surrounded by their respective assemblies.
Homage to the Tathāgatas seated upon lotus-treasury lion-thrones within ten billion Jambudvīpas across ten billion worlds in the ten directions— beyond more than one hundred million worlds—
surrounded by all Bodhisattvas as numerous as the atoms in ten Buddha-fields.
Surrounded by all the bodhisattvas,
I pay homage to those [Buddhas] beyond ten billion worlds, throughout the ten directions, across a hundred billion worlds, a thousand billion worlds,
a hundred thousand billion worlds, a nayuta of billions of worlds, a hundred nayutas of billions of worlds, and a thousand nayutas of billions of worlds.
In every one of the hundreds of thousands of nayutas of billions of worlds, within each Jambudvīpa,
there was a Tathāgata seated upon a lion throne of lotus-treasury, surrounded by as many bodhisattvas as there are atoms in ten buddha-fields.

Homage to all such Tathāgatas who sit upon lotus-treasury thrones within the billions of Jambudvīpas in all worlds throughout the entirety of the dharma-realm and the realm of empty space— worlds that are innumerable, immeasurable, inexhaustible, boundless, unequaled, incalculable, ineffable, inconceivable, unfathomable, unspeakable, and unspeakably infinite.
Surrounded by all Bodhisattvas as numerous as the atoms within ten Buddha-fields, you whose seat is thus honored—

may all in the ten directions take refuge in you; may their sins be extinguished and their pure faith increase, and may they vow to be born within the Flower Treasury Ocean and the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss.
Next, the ten Bodhisattvas of the Universal Radiance of the Dharma Realm, facing the Buddhas of their own realms:

Homage to the Buddhas of the Ten Buddha-lands as numerous as atoms in the eastern direction, in the Golden World beyond worlds as numerous as atoms in ten Buddha-lands, to the Buddha Immovable Wisdom,
and to the entire ocean-like assembly at the site of enlightenment of Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva, numbering as many as atoms in ten Buddha-lands.
Homage to the Buddha Unobstructed Wisdom in the World of Wondrous Colors, ten buddha-field atoms of worlds away to the south,
together with the Bodhisattva Chief of Enlightenment and the ocean-like assembly at the site of enlightenment numbering ten buddha-field atoms;
homage to the Buddha Liberation in the World of Lotus Color, ten buddha-field atoms of worlds away to the west.
Homage to the assembly of all oceans of beings at the ten buddha-field-microdust number of sites of enlightenment of the Bodhisattva Jñānabuddhivibhūṣaṇarāja;
and homage to the assembly of all oceans of beings at the ten buddha-field-microdust number of sites of enlightenment of the Bodhisattva Ratnaśrī,
in the world named Campakapuṣpavarṇa located beyond ten buddha-field-microdust number of worlds in the northern direction, where the Buddha Vinayajñāna resides.
Homage to the Buddhas of the ten Buddha-lands as numerous as atoms in ten Buddha-fields beyond the world-system of Utpala-flower Color in the northeast,

to the Buddha Wisdom of Radiant Appearance, to the Bodhisattva Foremost in Merit, and to the ocean-like assemblies of all those at the sites of enlightenment, as numerous as atoms in ten Buddha-fields.
Homage to the Buddhas of the Southeast, as numerous as the atoms in ten Buddha-fields, in the world-system called Golden outside those ten Buddha-fields;
to the Buddha Ultimate Wisdom, the Bodhisattva Eye-Head, and the entire ocean-like assembly at their sites of enlightenment, as numerous as the atoms in ten Buddha-fields.
Homage to the Buddha Most Victorious in the world-system called Jewel-Colored outside the ten Buddha-fields as numerous as the atoms in ten Buddha-fields in the Southwest.
Homage to the Bodhisattva Jñānabuddhavīryaśīrṣa and the ocean-like assemblies at all the sites of enlightenment, as numerous as the atoms in ten buddha-fields;

and homage to the Bodhisattva Vairocanajñānadharmendrarāja and the ocean-like assemblies at all the sites of enlightenment, as numerous as the atoms in ten buddha-fields, in the world-system called Vajravarna located beyond worlds as numerous as the atoms in ten buddha-fields in the northwestern direction.

Homage to the assembly of all oceans of beings at the ten *buddhakṣetra*-rajas sites of enlightenment in the world-system of Brahma-Wisdom and Wisdom-Head Bodhisattva, located in the crystal-colored world beyond worlds as numerous as the atoms in ten *buddhakṣetras* below;
homage to the world-system of Equal Color, located in the world beyond worlds as numerous as the atoms in ten *buddhakṣetras* above, where [the Bodhisattva] Contemplation dwells.
Homage to the ocean-like assemblies at all the sites of enlightenment, numbering as many as the atoms in ten buddha-fields, of the Buddha Jñāna-bhadra-mukha Bodhisattva;
and to the ocean-like assemblies at all the sites of enlightenment, numbering as many as the atoms in ten buddha-fields,
of each of the ten-headed bodhisattvas— such as the Buddha Akṣobhya-jñāna and others— in the ten directions within ten buddha-lands beyond this world.
Homage to the ten Buddhas, such as Akṣobhyajñāna, and the ten-headed Bodhisattvas, each numbering as many as the atoms within ten Buddha-fields,
together with the entire ocean-like assembly at their respective sites of enlightenment throughout the hundred worlds of the ten directions beyond ten worlds.
Homage to the ten Buddhas, such as Akṣobhyajñāna, and the ten-headed ones throughout the thousand worlds of the ten directions beyond a hundred worlds.
To each of the Bodhisattvas—one for each, numbering as many as the atoms in ten Buddha-fields—belong the entire ocean-like assemblies at their respective sites of enlightenment (*bodhimaṇḍa*).

Homage to the ocean-like assemblies at the sites of enlightenment belonging to each of the ten Buddhas, such as Acalajñāna, and each of the ten-headed Bodhisattvas, throughout the ten thousand worlds of the ten directions, exceeding a thousand worlds; to each of these, numbering as many as the atoms in ten Buddha-fields.
Homage to the ten Buddhas, such as Akṣobhyajñāna, and the ten Chief Bodhisattvas, each numbering as many as the atoms within ten Buddha-fields,
together with all the ocean-like assemblies at their respective sites of enlightenment throughout the hundred thousand worlds in the ten directions beyond ten thousand worlds.
Homage to the ten Buddhas, such as Akṣobhyajñāna, throughout the million worlds in the ten directions beyond one hundred thousand worlds.
To each of the ten-headed Bodhisattvas, who are as numerous as the atoms in ten Buddha-fields, and to all the ocean-like assemblies at their respective sites of enlightenment;

to the ten Buddhas, such as Akṣobhyajñāna, and the ten-headed Bodhisattvas, each residing in sites of enlightenment as numerous as the atoms in ten Buddha-fields, throughout one hundred million worlds in the ten directions across more than a million worlds— to all these, I pay homage.
Homage to the Buddhas of the ten directions beyond one hundred million worlds— namely, the ten Buddhas beginning with Acalamati (Immovable Wisdom) and their ten chief Bodhisattvas,
each accompanied by an assembly from all oceans of bodhimandas numbering as many as the atoms within ten Buddha-fields;
homage to those beyond ten billion worlds, those beyond a hundred billion worlds, those beyond a thousand billion worlds, and those beyond a nayuta of worlds in the ten directions.
In worlds numbering one billion, ten billion, one hundred billion, and one trillion,
there were the ten Buddhas beginning with Acalamati and the ten-headed Bodhisattvas,
each accompanied by assemblies of all oceans of beings at as many sites of enlightenment (bodhimaṇḍa) as there are atoms in ten Buddha-fields.
Homage to all these and others— numberless, immeasurable, inexhaustible, boundless, unequaled, unspeakable, incomparable,
inconceivable, unfathomable, and beyond description— even unto the unspeakably unspeakable worlds throughout the entirety of the Dharma-realm and the realm of empty space;
to each of the ten Buddhas beginning with Acalamati and the ten leaders among the Bodhisattvas, ten for each.
To all the ocean-like assemblies at the sites of enlightenment, as numerous as the atoms within a Buddha-field, throughout the ten directions, I take refuge.
May my transgressions be extinguished and my pure faith increase; may I be reborn in the Flower Treasury Ocean and the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss.

Next, I take refuge in the Buddhas who have realized the Dharma through the Universal Radiance of the Dharma-realm (*dharmadhātu-samantaprabhā-prativedha-buddha*). I take refuge in all Buddhas throughout the lands as numerous as the atoms within the entirety of space across the ten directions and the three periods of time.
I take refuge in all of them throughout the ten directions. May my sins be extinguished and my pure faith increase; may I be reborn in the Flower Treasury Ocean (*puṣpa-garbha-sāgara*).
The Dharma Gate of the Perfectly Interfused Ocean of Fruition within the Ten Stages of Faith in the Land of Ultimate Bliss;

Homage to the Bodhisattva Dharmadhātusthiticitta; The Profound Meaning of the Dependent Origination that Universally Encompasses All Dharmas; The [Dharma Gate of] the Extremely Profound Dependent Origination.
Homage to the Profound Dharma Gate!
Homage to the Bodhisattva Who Contemplates the Dharma Realm! Because sentient beings are deluded regarding this, the profound dharma gate must be taught and admonished.
Homage to the Bodhisattva Maṇikūṭarāja for the profound Dharma-gate of instructing and transforming beings according to the presence of good and evil karmic fruits;
homage to the Bodhisattva Dharmadhātuhṛdaya for the corresponding teaching of the Dharma and the preaching of this karma for those who wish to know it.
The Profound Dharma Gate:
Homage to the Bodhisattva Dharmadhātu-praṇidhāna-citta; the Teaching that Accomplishes Goodness; the Most Profound Dharma Gate of the Buddha, the Field of Merit.

Homage to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vimalacittābhiprāya for the sake of the Dharma-realm; this essential upholding of the noble Dharma, the True Dharma, the profound Dharma-gate is taught for the sake of accordance with the field.
Homage to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Anivartitacitta for the sake of the Dharma-realm; that True Dharma of his resides in the state of diligent practice.
Homage to the Bodhisattva Dharmadhātumati, who practices the profound Dharma-gate; he walks the true path and employs the merit of the aids to enlightenment through this profound Dharma-gate.
Homage to the Bodhisattva Who Is the Mind of Dedication to the Dharma-realm, who assists the King of Samādhi, and who dwells in the profound dharma-gate of the single path shared by all;
homage to the Bodhisattva Who Is the Mind of Wisdom of the Dharma-realm, who realizes the profound samādhi within the stage of the fruit of realized wisdom, the realm of the Buddhas.

To this profound Dharma-gate, the ten directions all turn in refuge; Sins are extinguished and pure faith increases; May I be reborn within the Flower Treasury Ocean, in the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss.
Next, the Bodhisattvas of the Ten Faiths of the Universal Radiance of the Dharma Realm:

Homage to all the assemblies of the ocean-like multitude of Bodhisattvas of the faith-stage within the lands as numerous as the atoms in all the worlds throughout the entirety of space across the ten directions and the three periods of time.
Homage to all the ocean-like assemblies of Bodhisattvas with the Mind of Diligence throughout the dust-mote lands of the entirety of space in the ten directions and the three periods of time.
Homage to the Bodhisattvas with the Mind of Mindfulness throughout the dust-mote lands of the entirety of space in the ten directions and the three periods of time.
Homage to the ocean-like assembly of all Bodhisattvas of Wisdom-Mind throughout the lands as numerous as atoms within the entirety of space across the ten directions and the three periods of time;
homage to the ocean-like assembly of all.
Homage to the Bodhisattvas of the Samādhi-mind and to the entire ocean-like assembly within all dust-mote lands throughout the ten directions and three periods of time, as far as the limits of space.
Homage to the Bodhisattvas of the Precept-mind within all dust-mote lands throughout the ten directions and three periods of time, as far as the limits of space. (1)
Homage to the ocean-like assembly of all Bodhisattvas of the mind of dedication within all dust-mote lands throughout the entirety of space in the ten directions and the three periods of time;
homage to the ocean-like assembly of all [beings].

Homage to the Bodhisattvas who protect the mind, and to the entire ocean-like assembly, within all the lands as numerous as atoms throughout the entirety of space across the ten directions and the three periods of time.
Homage to the Bodhisattvas of non-retrogressive mind, within all the lands as numerous as atoms throughout the entirety of space across the ten directions and the three periods of time.

Homage to the Ocean-like Multitudes of all Bodhisattvas of Wisdom-Mind within the lands as numerous as atoms in all the realms of empty space throughout the ten directions and the three periods of time. Homage to the Ocean-like Multitudes of all.
With a sincere heart, I take refuge and pay homage to the World-Honored One Vairocana Buddha, the Honored One of the Flower Treasury Ocean-World System in the Great Vaipulya Buddha-Avatamsaka Sūtra;
Namo to the Honored Assembly of all Oceans at the Site of Enlightenment of the Ten-Bodied Unobstructed Tathāgata Vairocana.
Homage to the Dharma-gate of the "Chapter on the Questions of the Bodhisattvas" within the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra*.

To all those throughout the ten directions, I take refuge; may my transgressions be extinguished and my pure faith increase, and may I be reborn in the ocean of the Flower Treasury and the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss.
The *Bodhisattva-paripṛcchā-prakāśa-varga*, Chapter Ten, states:
At that time, Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva... [as far as] the four intermediate directions, above, and below, was likewise so.
May I, together with all sentient beings, be reborn in the Flower Treasury Ocean, within the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss.
Homage to the Buddha Vairocana, the Original Honored One of Unobstructed Ten Bodies in the Flower Treasury World-Ocean within the Great Vaipulya Buddhāvataṃsaka Sūtra.
Homage to the entire ocean-like assembly at the site of enlightenment of the Tathāgata Vairocana of Unobstructed Ten Bodies.
Homage to the Dharma-gate of the "Chapter on Pure Conduct" within the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Great Vaipulya*.
I take refuge in all directions; may my transgressions be extinguished and my pure faith increase. May I be reborn in the Ocean of Flower Treasury and the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss.
The *Pure Conduct Chapter*, the eleventh sūtra, states:
At that time, the Bodhisattva Jñānaśrī [and others]... [are] such that they cannot be moved by any śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas.
May we, together with all sentient beings, be reborn in the Flower Treasury Ocean within the Pure Land of Sukhāvatī.
Homage to the Buddha Vairocana, the Original Honored One of Unobstructed Ten Bodies in the Flower Treasury World-Ocean of the Mahāvaipulya Buddhāvataṃsaka Sūtra.
Homage to the entire ocean-like assembly in the place of enlightenment of the Tathāgata Vairocana of Unobstructed Ten Bodies.
Homage to the Dharma-gate of the "Chapter on the Worthy Leader" within the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra*.
May all throughout the ten directions take refuge; may sins be extinguished and pure faith increase; and may we be reborn in the ocean of the Flower Treasury and the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss.
The *Bhadrapāla-parivarta*, Chapter Twelve, states: At that time, Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva... (omitted)... we all rejoice together.
May we, along with all sentient beings, be reborn in the Flower Treasury Ocean within the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss.
With a sincere heart, I take refuge and pay homage to the World-Honored One Vairocana, the Honored One of the Flower Treasury Ocean-world of the Great Vaipulya Buddha Avataṃsaka Sūtra.
To all throughout the ten directions, I take refuge: may my transgressions be extinguished, my pure faith increase, and may I be born in the Flower Treasury Ocean.
In the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss, next is the repentance for slandering the Dharma:
I take refuge in the inexhaustible Jewels of the Buddha, Dharma, and Sangha, which are like Indra’s net; in Vairocana Tathāgata; and in Samantabhadra and Mañjuśrī.

The assembly of noble ones gathered like an ocean, and the world-transcending and worldly deities, by virtue of their compassionate original vows, emit great radiance that illuminates this Dharma assembly.

May they bear witness, protect, and keep us in mind; may they look upon us with pity and grant their acceptance. I pray that for myself and the ocean of all sentient beings, from the beginningless past...
Up until the present time, I openly confess all karmic offenses committed through slandering the Dharma.
The *Mahādharmanirbhāsa-sūtra* states: At that time, the Tathāgata Prabhāsa addressed the bodhisattvas, saying:
"Māṇava, if there are sentient beings who, regarding the Buddha, the World-Honored One’s profound secret wisdom, supreme and victorious wisdom, and most subtle and wondrous wisdom..."
As for those who give rise to slander against even a single phrase, such persons shall receive immeasurable retribution for their evil deeds.

Furthermore, if there are others who speak these words, saying, "This is not the word of the Buddha; this is not the teaching of the Tathāgata," thereby increasing their slander, they will lack faith in all such teachings of the Buddhas.
Having slandered them themselves, they further cause immeasurable and boundless sentient beings [to do the same].
Within such a great gate of wisdom as that of the Buddha, even to slander and disbelieve a single phrase creates many obstacles;
even to prevent others from reading or reciting it, because of the karma of one's speech, one commits various evils and will certainly undergo immeasurable retribution for those evils.
O Māṇava, it would be better for this person not to hear anything at all than to let them hear it.

They give rise to coarse and heavy slander. Māṇava, it would be better for such a person to have their mouth filled with shards and stones for a full hundred years than to commit such an act of slander by saying that this Dharma-gate was not spoken by the Tathāgata.
Māṇava, such a deluded person, dwelling in a mind of false pride, slanders the sūtras and becomes a great [obstacle] to other sentient beings.
Obstacle! Māṇava, those evil persons are not merely foolish to speak thus; they further dwell in stinginess and envy, slandering and reviling this sutra.
How can I now cause all sentient beings to fail to achieve accomplishment within this Dharma?
Māṇava, I would rather let such people eat cow dung for immeasurable hundreds of thousands of billions of years.
I would not allow this person, for the sake of food and drink, to slander this Dharma.

Māṇava, I would rather let this person lie upon beds of *kuśa* grass, thorns, and spikes for a thousand billion years than allow this person, for the sake of bedding, to revile and destroy this Dharma.
Māṇava, I would rather let this person remain with their body naked for a thousand billion years than—
For the sake of clothing, these people slander and revile this Dharma. Māṇava, I have already described the present evil karma of those wicked men who defame the Buddha-Dharma.

As for what you previously asked me regarding the retribution they will receive in future lives, Māṇava, I ought not to speak of the retribution received by such people who slander the Dharma. Why is this?

Why? If I were to speak of the retribution for this offense, there might be immeasurable and boundless sentient beings who, upon hearing of this matter, would further increase their slander. [Therefore,] one must repent for the karmic retribution of such sin.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Candana rose from his seat, adjusted his dignified demeanor, bared his right shoulder,
knelt with his right knee on the ground, and with palms joined in reverence, addressed the Tathāgata Prabhāsa: "World-Honored One,
I now stand before the World-Honored One to sincerely repent for such evil beings, and for those who have slandered the Dharma."
Those evil sentient beings who, regarding this gateway of dhāraṇī, give rise to a mind of slander toward even a single phrase— whether they have already slandered it,
are about to slander it, or destroy, revile, and disparage it— even if they create an obstacle for a single sentient being regarding a single phrase—
for their sake, O World-Honored One, I now [act] for those evil sentient beings, even unto the measureless and boundless.
In all worlds, there are likewise many such evil sentient beings who practice perversity and slander the True Dharma.

For their sake, I now, before the Buddha, sincerely repent. World-Honored One, because those sentient beings have no protector, no eyes, no wisdom, and are possessed of evil speech, I now, for their sake, with utmost sincerity—

"Repentance. World-Honored One, if there were another person who, in the presence of the World-Honored One, repented in this manner, what roots of goodness would they obtain therein, and what merit would they acquire?
At that time, the Tathāgata Emitting Light addressed the Bodhisattva Candana, saying: "Excellent, excellent!
Māṇava, it is well that you are able to perfume your mind with such skillful means and inquire of the Tathāgata."

If a son of good family, for the sake of those evil sentient beings who destroy the Dharma, sincerely repents their transgressions, they shall obtain an immeasurable mass of great merit. Māṇava, this mass of merit is difficult to measure.
Now, I shall provide a brief illustration by way of analogy to inspire a heart of joy in these sentient beings. Māṇava, consider all that exists in the eastern direction...
In this world, all sentient beings therein are entirely great donors (mahādānapati).
Likewise, in the south, west, north, the four intermediate directions, and above and below—throughout the ten directions—all sentient beings everywhere are entirely great donors.

Having passed through immeasurable, boundless, unspeakable, and incomparable numbers of great kalpas, he constantly practiced giving—namely gold, silver, various jewels, clothing, food and drink, medicinal decoctions, dwellings, and all kinds of requisites.
Then, he gathered immeasurable and boundless sentient beings together in one place to serve as recipients of these gifts. Māṇava, what do you think?
"How so? Could this mass of merit be considered great? Candana replied, "World-Honored One, this mass of merit is truly vast and expansive.
Why is this? World-Honored One, if there were a single person who practiced the merit of giving for immeasurable eons, even they could not exhaust it;
how much less could it be measured by the mass of merit from the practice of giving by immeasurable sentient beings over countless eons?"
He measured their extent. The Buddha said, "So it is, so it is, māṇava.

Although the immeasurable sentient beings, throughout immeasurable kalpas, have performed immeasurable acts of giving and accumulated immeasurable masses of merit, such that they cannot be known [fully], they still do not equal this."

Good sons and good daughters, if among all those previously mentioned assemblies who slandered the Dharma, one were to sincerely repent for the sake of even a single person, the roots of goodness produced and the merit obtained would be immeasurable, boundless, and beyond compare;
how much more so if one sincerely repents for the sake of immeasurable sentient beings? Furthermore, O Māṇava, let alone all that exists in this world...

Regarding those sentient beings who slander the Dharma: even if one were to take but a single individual from among all the sentient beings who revile the True Dharma throughout the infinite and boundless worlds of the ten directions—

should such a māṇava sincerely repent for their transgressions within that assembly of dharma-slandering beings across the ten directions— the mass of merit obtained and the roots of goodness produced would still be beyond measure.
How much more so for one who sincerely repents on behalf of all sentient beings throughout the ten directions!
Such a mass of merit and roots of goodness sustains, gathers, and increases a multitude of virtues that are incalculable, immeasurable, and inconceivable.
"Who would be able to believe in such merit? Only non-regressive Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas are capable of having even a slight degree of faith.
At that time, Candana again addressed the Buddha, saying, "When those sons of good family practice in this manner, what do they seek?
The Buddha said, "Candana, for the sake of Bodhi, those sons of good family shoulder this heavy burden out of compassion for others."

There are no deluded sentient beings; it is likewise because they depend upon awakening. If delusion were separate from the nature of awakening, there would be no non-awakening.
Because the delusive mind of non-awakening exists, one is able to know names and meanings, and thus true awakening can be taught.

If one were separated from the mind of non-awakening, there would be no self-characteristic of true awakening that could be taught. Furthermore, based on non-awakening, three kinds of marks arise. And...
That [mind] is unaware; it is associated with and not separate from [ignorance]. What are these three? First is the characteristic of the activity of ignorance (*avidyā-karma-lakṣaṇa*).

Because it relies on non-awakening, the mind moves; this is designated as "activity. If there were awakening, there would be no movement. Movement results in the fruit of suffering because one is not separated from its cause. Second is the characteristic of the capacity for seeing (*darśana-lakṣaṇa*).
Because it relies on movement, it is able to see; if there were no movement, there would be no seeing. Third is the characteristic of the object (*viṣaya-lakṣaṇa*).
Regarding the characteristics of the realms (*dhātu-lakṣaṇa*): because one relies upon the capacity for seeing, objects appear as delusions. Apart from seeing, there are no objects.

Because there are conditions consisting of objects, six further types of characteristics arise. What are these six? The first is the characteristic of cognition (*jñāna-lakṣaṇa*), which relies upon objects.

First is the characteristic of conceptualization, because it gives rise to discrimination between the beloved and the unloved. Second is the characteristic of continuity, because based upon cognition, it produces suffering and pleasure;
as the mind awakens and thoughts arise, they continue in an uninterrupted succession. Third is the characteristic of grasping, which depends upon this continuity.

1) The characteristic of abiding in the objects of perception through mental engagement: because the mind gives rise to attachment by dwelling upon pleasure and pain. 2) The characteristic of the conceptualization of names:

because one relies on false grasping and discrimination to falsely designate names and appearances. 3) The characteristic of the dependence on names: because one relies on names to seek them out and grasp at them, thereby creating various kinds of karma.
4) The characteristic of suffering bound by karma: because one undergoes retribution based on karma, [and is not...]* *Note: The source text appears to be truncated at this point.*

For this reason, one should know that ignorance (*avidyā*) is able to give rise to all defiled phenomena (*saṃkleśa-dharma*), because all defiled phenomena are characterized by non-awakening (*abodha*).
Furthermore, regarding the causes and conditions for arising and ceasing: it refers to sentient beings turning according to mind (*citta*), thought (*manas*), and consciousness (*vijñāna*).
What is the meaning of this? It is because, based upon the *ālayavijñāna*, there is said to be the non-awakening of ignorance, which gives rise to the capacity [to manifest].
It is called "mind" (*manas*) because it is able to manifest, is able to grasp objects, and gives rise to a continuous stream of thought.

This mind has five further names. What are these five? First, it is called the "karmic consciousness" (*ālaya-vijñāna*); this means that through the power of ignorance, the mind moves without awareness.
Second, it is called the "evolving consciousness" (*pravṛtti-vijñāna*); this means that based on the moving mind, one is able to perceive appearances. Third, it is called "manifestation" (*darśana*).
Consciousness (vijñāna). That which is able to manifest all objective realms is like a clear mirror that manifests forms and images; the manifesting consciousness is also thus.
As each of the five sense-objects encounters it, they are immediately manifested without any sequence of before or after, because at all times it arises spontaneously and is always present.
Fourth is called the wisdom-consciousness (jñāna-vijñāna), which means it discriminates between defiled and pure phenomena. Fifth—

It is called the "continuum-consciousness" (*saṃtati-vijñāna*). Because it is associated with mindfulness and remains uninterrupted, it maintains the wholesome and unwholesome karma of immeasurable past lives and so forth, ensuring that it is not lost;
furthermore, it is able to bring to fruition the retributions of suffering, pleasure, and so on, in the present and future.
Because there is no discrepancy [between past and future], one can suddenly recollect events already past in the present and unexpectedly contemplate future matters.
For this reason, the three realms are illusory and are produced solely by the mind; apart from the mind, the objects of the six sense-fields do not exist.
What is the meaning of this? It is because all phenomena arise from the deluded thoughts of the mind, and thus give rise to everything.
Discrimination is precisely the discrimination of one's own mind; the mind does not perceive the mind, for no characteristic can be apprehended.
One should know that all worldly objects abide and are sustained solely by the ignorant, deluded mind of sentient beings. Therefore, all phenomena—
Like an image in a mirror, no substance can be apprehended; it is merely the mind’s delusion. For when the mind arises, all manner of phenomena arise;
when the mind ceases, all manner of phenomena cease.

We have been shrouded by ignorance and failed to awaken to the ten types of defiled afflictions, both fundamental and derivative, which undergo conceptual transformation and constitute the inherent basis of the two sufferings.
Now, having encountered this site of enlightenment (*bodhimaṇḍa*), we have finally come to realize them. We take refuge in the Tathāgata Vairocana and the ocean-like assembly of all worthy sages.
Burning incense and scattering flowers, we openly confess and repent for these ten layers of defiled afflictions.

I dare not conceal anything. By this cause and condition, may all the tenfold grave defilements and sinful karmas—both root and branch—of myself and the ocean of sentient beings within the Dharma-realm be entirely purified.
Next, the mudrā and mantra for repentance and the eradication of transgressions: Oṃ sarvapāpam me kṣayam kuru svāhā (recite three times).
Sins accumulated over a hundred eons are entirely swept away in a single thought; like fire consuming dry grass, they are extinguished without remainder.
All the evil karma I have created in the past arose from beginningless greed, hatred, and delusion.
Whatever has arisen from my body, speech, and mind, I now confess it all.
Having confessed, I take refuge with a sincere heart and pay homage to the Honored One, Vairocana Buddha.
○ (Proclamation: Listen, all you members of the assembly, to these verses on impermanence from the Sūtras:
For all classes of sentient beings, The nature of death is ever present.
Even by employing every skillful means, One cannot obstruct this law. Though one has long enjoyed immeasurable bliss, Inevitably, one must eventually fall away.
Therefore, all you humans and devas, you should not give rein to greed and desire.

With a Brahma-voice,
he praises the Tathāgata’s great wisdom— Rare and without equal, such that no one in any world can fathom it;
He fully understands all phenomena, Knowing that their intrinsic nature is non-existent.
Thus understanding the nature of phenomena, one beholds Vairocana;
The Tathāgata’s vast body is ultimately coextensive with the dharma-realm. Without leaving this very seat, he pervades all places.
(Direct praise of the Buddha)
Just as the pure moon in the sky Can obscure the multitude of stars and manifest its waning and waxing,
And can cast its reflection in all waters, Appearing before everyone who gazes upon it—
So too is the Tathāgata like the pure moon: He can obscure other vehicles and manifest their varying lengths of duration.
He universally manifests before the pure waters of the hearts of devas and humans; all say he stands before them.
Like the Brahma King dwelling in his own palace, he universally appears in all the Brahma abodes throughout the three thousandfold world-system;
all humans and devas behold him, yet in truth he does not divide his body to go toward them.
The manifestation of the bodies of all Buddhas is likewise; throughout all ten directions, there is nowhere they do not pervade.
Their bodies are infinite and beyond measure; yet they neither divide their bodies nor engage in conceptual discrimination.
