All these members of the assembly kneel with their right knees to the ground, solemnly holding incense and flowers to make offerings according to the Dharma. May this ocean of offerings...

Clouds that pervade the realms of the ten directions; canopies of robes, canopies of garlands, canopies of flowers, canopies of incense, canopies of branches, canopies of *maṇi* jewels, canopies of pure gold, canopies of ornaments, canopies of music, canopies of the miraculous transformations of the elephant kings, and canopies of the miraculous transformations of the horse kings.
Furthermore, there were nets of precious bells, nets of precious parasols, nets of precious bodies, nets of sea-treasure pearls, and nets of deep-blue lapis lazuli *maṇi* jewels.
Moonlight maṇi nets; multi-layered forms of various fragrant nets; jewel-crown nets; jewel-garland nets; the radiance of flame-light maṇi jewels;
the radiance of moon-treasury maṇi jewels; the radiance of banner maṇi jewels; the radiance of fragrance-flame maṇi jewels;
the radiance of supreme-treasury maṇi jewels; and the radiance of lotus-treasury maṇi jewels.
The radiance of the *jvālādhvaja-maṇi-ratna*; the radiance of the *mahādīpa-maṇi-ratna*; the radiance of the *sarvadig-vyāpin-maṇi-ratna*;
and the radiance of the *gandha-maṇi-ratna*. From ten million black *candana* incenses, wondrous sounds issued forth.
A hundred thousand *mandārava* flowers surpassing those of the devas were scattered upon it. With such various articles of offering, they constantly made offerings.

Within the infinitely layered Indra-nets, the ocean-like assemblies of Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and holy sages received these clouds of incense and flowers, making them into canopies of light that extended throughout boundless realms, immeasurable and inexhaustible. May they become Buddhas.
Having performed these services and offerings with all reverence,
he next presented a jeweled casket.
With clouds of offerings such as these— vast oceans of the intrinsic nature of precious jewels and the most excellent emergence of the mountains of the seven treasures—
I offer them to all the Buddhas and their equals. Oṃ sarva-tathāgata-udāra-bhoga-samagra-siddhi.
*Phraṇat samaye hūṃ*. The *Ratnakūṭa Sūtra* states:
"There is a dhāraṇī named 'The Mantra of Immeasurable Varieties,' which is capable of accomplishing all things and possesses great efficacy. The dhāraṇī says:
Oṃ smara smara mīmada smara mā hūṃ phaṭ svāhā. Next is the mantra and mudrā for bestowing great wisdom: Oṃ dharma-saṃgraha-tathāgatāvalokite samaya.
(raṃ-saṃ-raṃ raḥ hūṃ) In the Sanskrit language,
I praise the Tathāgata’s wondrously colored body, which constantly proclaims the voice of great wisdom with unimpeded eloquence.
Opening the gate of the Buddha’s bodhi, awakening all sentient beings, Causing immeasurable and inconceivable numbers to enter the gate of wisdom, Bestowing upon them the prediction of bodhi.
The Tathāgata appears in the world as the great field of merit for the world; Universally guiding all conscious beings, Causing them to accumulate meritorious deeds.
Speaking directly, I praise the Buddhas, the Tathāgatas, the abodes of all Buddhas; No worldly analogy can equal them.
To cause sentient beings to attain awakening and understanding, I employ that which is not an analogy as an analogy to reveal them.
The subtle, secret, and profound Dharma of the Tathāgata, Which is difficult to hear even for hundreds of thousands of millions of beings—
Only those who possess diligence, wisdom, and self-mastery, And who have heard this secret and profound meaning,
Or who, upon hearing this Dharma, give rise to joy and celebration, Have in the past made offerings to immeasurable Buddhas.
Sustained by the empowerment of the Buddha and revered with constant offerings by gods and humans, this is the supreme wealth that transcends the world;
it can deliver all living beings and give rise to the path of purity. You should uphold this and never be negligent.
The merit obtained from seeing, hearing, and making offerings to all Tathāgatas is immeasurable;
within the realm of conditioned existence, it will never be exhausted.
It is like swallowing a small amount of *vajra*: it will ultimately not be digested, but must inevitably pass through.
By making offerings to the virtues of the One of Ten Powers, one extinguishes delusions and will surely attain vajra-wisdom;
even if heaps of dry grass equal to Mount Sumeru were cast into a fire of mustard seeds, they would all be completely consumed.
Likewise, by making even a small offering to the Buddhas, one will surely sever the afflictions and reach nirvāṇa.
In the Snowy Mountains there is a medicine named Sudarśana, Which surely severs afflictions and leads to Nirvāṇa;
If one sees or hears of the One of Ten Powers, One attains supreme merit and reaches Buddha-wisdom.
Homage to the Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Great Vaipulya, To the World-Ocean of the Avataṃsaka, And to the Original Honored One of Unobstructed Ten Bodies.
Homage to Vairocana Buddha;
homage to Śākyamuni Buddha, the Greatly Compassionate One who made five hundred vows to save sentient beings from suffering in the five turbidities;
homage to Bhaiṣajyaguru-vaiḍūryaprabha, who made twelve supreme vows to save sentient beings from suffering in the five turbidities in the Pūrṇacandra world of the eastern direction.

Homage to the Buddha Prabhāpāla-rāja. Homage to Amitābha Buddha, who dwells in the Western World of Ultimate Bliss, who made the forty-eight vows, and who rescues beings from suffering amidst the five turbidities.
Homage to the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra* within all the lands as numerous as motes of dust throughout the entirety of space across the ten directions and the three periods of time.

The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Samantabhadra, who presides over the truth of the Vows and Conduct within the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra*, the Great Vaipulya Buddha-Flower Adornment Sūtra, the Perfect Teaching of the Sea of Dharma.
Homage to Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva Mahāsattva, the Lord of Faith, Understanding, and Realization-Wisdom within the Great Vaipulya Buddha-avatamsaka Sūtra.
Homage to Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva,
the Greatly Compassionate One with a Thousand Hands and a Thousand Eyes, who rescues beings from suffering in the five turbidities.
Homage to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Kṣitigarbharāja, whose great vows are vast and profound; who rescues those suffering in the five turbidities and appears in worlds where no Buddha dwells;
who comforts the hearts of sentient beings and eternally abides in the realm of Yama.
Homage to the Bodhisattvas of the Ten Faiths, the Bodhisattvas of the Ten Abodes, the Bodhisattvas of the Ten Practices,
the Bodhisattvas of the Ten Dedications, the Bodhisattvas of the Ten Grounds, the Bodhisattvas of Equal Enlightenment,

and all the ocean-like assemblies of Bodhisattvas as numerous as the atoms within the oceans of lands throughout the entirety of the dharma-realm and the space of the ten directions and three periods of time— namo! All you hosts of the ocean of assemblies!
Homage to the fifty-five holy ones who practiced and realized the five stages of cultivation in the final assembly of the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra*.
Homage to those of superior capacity and perfected vessels who sought the Dharma through a hundred cities in the final assembly of the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra*.
The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Sudhana, who perfected the bodhisattva practices within a single lifetime and serves as the model for cultivation and realization for the sudden gate of the final age—
homage to the forms of the Dharma-body and the form-body throughout all lands as numerous as the atoms within the entirety of space across the ten directions and three periods of time.
To the stūpas enshrining the relics, the temple buildings, and all Buddhist activities; to the Dharma-treasuries and the places where the Dharma is preached;
to the ocean-like assemblies of Bodhisattvas, worthies, and sages;

to those who have donned the armor of great vows to seek rebirth in the Pure Land; to those who protect and uphold the True Dharma during this degenerate age in the land of Xia; and to all who guard the Dharma—homage to you!
The National Preceptor,
with a sincere heart, takes refuge and pays homage to the World-Ocean of the Flower Treasury within the Great Vaipulya Buddha Avataṃsaka Sūtra,
the Honored One Vairocana Buddha.
Homage to the assembly of all oceans of beings at the site of enlightenment of the Tathāgata Vairocana, whose ten bodies are unimpeded.
Homage to the Dharma-gate of the "Chapter on Leaving the World" within the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra*, the Great Vaipulya Scripture of the Buddha.
To all throughout the ten directions, I take refuge. May my transgressions be extinguished and my pure faith increase; may I be born in the Flower Treasury Ocean.
The *Sutra on the Chapter on Transcending the World in the Land of Ultimate Bliss*, Fascicle Thirty-Eight, states:
"At that time, the World-Honored One was in the kingdom of Magadha... [omitted] ...and entered the unimpeded, pure Dharma-realm."
May I, together with all sentient beings, be reborn in the Flower Treasury Ocean within the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss.
Next, for the ocean-like assembly of Bodhisattvas headed by Samantabhadra of the Dharma-realm:
Namo Samantabhadra Bodhisattva. Namo Samantanetra Bodhisattva.
Homage to the Bodhisattva Universal Transformation; homage to the Bodhisattva Universal Wisdom;
homage to the Bodhisattva Universal Vision; homage to the Bodhisattva Universal Radiance;
homage to the Bodhisattva Universal Contemplation; homage to the Bodhisattva Universal Illumination.
Homage to the Bodhisattva Universal Banner; homage to the Bodhisattva Universal Awakening;
and homage to all such assemblies of the ocean-like multitude of bodhisattvas, numbering as many as the atoms in ten unspeakably many hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of buddha-fields.
All in the ten directions take refuge; Sins are extinguished and pure faith increases. May they be born within the Flower Treasury Ocean, in the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss.
The Sutra says: "At that time, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva... [up to] ...the Bodhisattvas of sovereign wisdom and spiritual power."
May I, together with all sentient beings, be reborn in the Flower Treasury Ocean within the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss.
From the remainder of the "Chapter on Leaving the World" in the sutra, it says: "O Son of the Buddha, when Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas [up to] then attain the Tathāgata’s unsurpassed great lion’s roar."
May I, together with all sentient beings, be reborn in the Flower Treasury Ocean within the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss.
From the remainder of the "Chapter on Leaving the World" in the Sūtra, it says:
"O Son of the Buddha, Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas... [up to] because they contemplate ten meanings, they manifest parinirvāṇa."
May I, together with all sentient beings, be reborn in the Flower Treasury Ocean within the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss.
Next, the Dharma Gate of the Six Stages of Causal Practice:
Homage to the Dharma Gate of Two Hundred Practices Accomplished Based on Understanding; The Dharma Gate of the Perfectly Interfused and Unobstructed Sublime Practice of the Ten Faiths.
Homage to the Dharma-gate of the Wondrous Practice of the Ten Abodes, Perfectly Interfused and Unobstructed, Based on the Two Hundred Practices Accomplished through Understanding;
Homage to the Dharma-gate of the Wondrous Practice of the Ten Practices, Perfectly Interfused and Unobstructed, Based on the Two Hundred Practices Accomplished through Understanding;
Homage to the [Dharma-gate of the] Ten Transferences, Perfectly Interfused and Unobstructed, Based on the Two Hundred and Ninety Practices Accomplished through Understanding.
The Dharma-gate of Practice:

Homage to the Dharma-gate of Five Hundred Practices Accomplished through Understanding and Realization; the Dharma-gate of Wondrous Practice of the Perfect Interfusion and Non-obstruction of the Ten Stages;

the Dharma-gate of Wondrous Practice of the Perfect Interfusion and Non-obstruction of Equal Enlightenment; Homage to the Dharma-gate of Five Hundred Practices Accomplished through Understanding and Realization.
All in the ten directions take refuge; Sins are extinguished and pure faith increases. May we be born within the Flower Treasury Sea, in the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss.
The Sūtra says: "O Son of the Buddha, this Dharma-gate is named [as follows]... one should arouse the vajra-mind and study these meritorious practices."
May I, together with all sentient beings, be reborn in the Flower Treasury Ocean and within the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss,
wherein we shall successively realize the Dharma-Buddha. Homage to the Great Bodhisattvas assembled in the Samantāvabhāsa Hall within the Mahāvaipulya Buddhāvataṃsaka Sūtra.
Homage to all Buddhas who testify to the Dharma within the palace,
to the assembly of the ocean-like multitudes of the six stages of the Dharma-realm,
and to the Bodhisattvas of the Ten Faiths throughout the lands as numerous as motes of dust in the palaces of empty space across the ten directions and the three periods of time.
Homage to the ocean-like assembly of all Bodhisattvas of the Ten Abodes throughout the dust-mote lands of the ten directions and three periods of time,
as far as the limits of empty space.
Homage to the ocean-like assemblies of all Bodhisattvas of the Ten Practices within the dust-mote lands of the entirety of space throughout the ten directions and three periods of time.
Homage to the Bodhisattvas of the Ten Dedications within the dust-mote lands of the entirety of space throughout the ten directions and three periods of time.

Homage to the ocean-like assembly of all Bodhisattvas of the Ten Stages within all lands as numerous as atoms throughout the entirety of space in the ten directions and the three periods of time. Homage to the ocean-like assembly of all [beings].
Homage to the ocean-like assembly of all Bodhisattvas of Equal Enlightenment throughout the dust-mote lands of the entirety of space in the ten directions and the three periods of time.
Homage to the Bodhisattvas of Wondrous Enlightenment throughout the dust-mote lands of the entirety of space in the ten directions and the three periods of time.
All the assemblies of the ocean [of beings] with sincere hearts take refuge and pay homage to the World-Honored One Vairocana, the Honored One of the Flower Treasury Ocean World-System,
the Great Vaipulya Buddha Avataṃsaka Sūtra.
All in the ten directions take refuge; Sins are extinguished and pure faith increases. May I be born within the Flower Treasury Sea, In the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss.
Next is the Ocean of Repentance for the Delusions of Greed, Attachment, and Karmic Action.
I pray that the inexhaustible Jewels of the Buddha, Dharma, and Sangha, as vast as the celestial net; Vairocana Tathāgata;

the assembly of holy beings of Samantabhadra, Mañjuśrī, and the ocean-like gathering; and all mundane and supramundane deities, by virtue of your compassionate original vows, may emit great radiance to illuminate this Dharma assembly.
May you bear witness, protect, and sustain us with your compassionate mindfulness. I pray that for myself and the ocean of all sentient beings,

from beginningless time until this very moment, we may confess and purify the ocean of all greed, craving, delusions, and karma— the inexhaustible ocean of karma that unfolds in infinite, interlacing layers like Indra’s net.
The *Sūtra of the Vows of Samantabhadra* says:
"The minds of ordinary beings are submerged in various sorrows and afflictions, As if they were beset by the缠縛 (entanglements) of a grave illness.
Yet, because of the pleasures derived from a wife's seductive charms, They falsely claim that this is the supreme joy that dispels sorrow."
Sentient beings with false views give rise to this thought: "A woman can serve as the cause for the world’s birth and growth, providing prosperity and adornment;
The transformations of heaven and earth cannot surpass her, for the diligent labor of worldly affairs depends solely on women;
She encourages her husband to universally perform all manner of virtuous deeds."
She can cause a man to change his mind at will; this woman is free from attachment to the minds of others.
Regarding the afflictions spoken of by the wise, all faults and karmic consequences arise from women.
How much more so when one takes a wife from a low-born family—nothing in this world is more utterly evil than this.
Women are stubbornly attached to their own nature, Like the earth, firm and stable, unable to be moved;
Yet they shift according to wealth, pleasure, honor, and nobility, Abandoning all poverty, lowliness, decline, and frailty.
Even seers with the five supernormal powers and great majesty Lose their supernatural faculties because of women.
Riding freely at will upon one's neck, the jade maiden can cause even the King of the Yama demons and fierce winds to become tranquil; she is like the Vajrākṣa sea beneath the earth,
or like blazing fire, black serpents, knives, and poisons— yet the harm wrought by a woman exceeds all of these.
Though one respectfully provides them with all manner of wealth and treasures, and serves them with sincerity and an unwavering mind;
though one employs wisdom and skillful means, whether firm or gentle—there is no one who can truly know a woman’s heart.
Whether seeing someone weep or laugh, she surpasses them both; like a sowing person using illusions, she entices and deludes their mind.
Their appearance is respectful and coquettish toward men, yet their hearts harbor cruelty;
they show utter falsehood as truth and speak absolute truth as lies.
Always like venomous beasts harming sentient beings—alas, O man, how could you dwell with such as these?
Constantly serving with respect only increases her arrogance; when encountering even a moment of adverse circumstance, her wickedness grows further.
Whether at home or abroad, at all times, she treats her husband with insolence and lacks any sense of shame.
Like fire consuming wood, she is never satisfied; like the ocean swallowing rivers, she is never full.
Yama never tires of killing sentient beings; the woman’s desire for men is likewise.
Without regard for lineage—whether old or young, noble or base, or beautiful—the woman pursues every man.
Thus she indulges her lustful passion without satiety.
A woman’s desires are insatiable; she never has even the slightest attachment to her husband’s heart.
Like a wild buffalo roaming at will, she constantly thinks of gradually eating fresh grass.
Her youthful beauty flows away with the mind; though she possesses wealth and status through her husband, she remains bound to others.
Abundant jade delicacies and jeweled robes— may the poor always have their various offerings and services fulfilled according to their wishes;
may they never feel shame for the kindness of their husbands, nor cease from indulging in perverse thoughts.
Some utter words of lustful passion while others speak with compassionate pity;
yet from their tongues, which are like nectar, there arises within their hearts the fierce malice of poison. Therefore, the speech of women is difficult to trust.
Women can cause estrangement between husbands and their kinsmen, preventing them from living in harmony even for a brief time.
Parents and brothers are like bitter enemies; all kinsmen and relatives have abandoned them.
Though they outwardly display a handsome appearance, they harbor flattery within; their bellies are filled with every transgression and violation.
One should not look upon them for even a moment, much less endure their coarse and evil speech for long.
Women must at all times guard against all faults, transgressions, and suspicion;

if they fail in even a single practice, they are despised by the multitude. They wound public morality and ruin social customs, and are abandoned by all people—whether in childhood, middle age, or even in old age past a hundred years.
Both internal and external clans are all honorable and noble; in every movement and stillness, they must always be guarded by others.
A maiden lives at home under her parents; upon reaching marriageable age, she follows her husband.
When the husband dies, she follows her son, guarding against suspicion. For this reason, she is always said to lack self-mastery.
Having left the home life to renounce desire and cultivate tranquility, yet the mind dwells on the realm of women, one is no longer a noble or wise person.
Like a saffron flower stained upon a soiled garment, such a person who has abandoned the good is constantly ridiculed by the wise.
Like a prisoner released from confinement who longs to return inside, or like a madman who recovers and wishes to relapse into his madness.
One who has already been cured of leprosy yet dwells on the time of being ill, Or one who abandons a woman yet dwells on her faults—
these are worse than a dragon dwelling in clear, still water, Or like a fierce beast residing in a golden cave.
Though one cultivates precepts and meditative concentration, if one dwells on women, The wise who observe this will see it is likewise so.
A wise person would rather swallow hot iron than allow the sight of a woman’s form to disturb their mind;
for it becomes a universal enemy to the categories of ethical discipline, concentration, and wisdom, causing one to abandon all the requisites for tranquility.
A woman does not regard noble lineage, nor auspiciousness, merit, wealth, wisdom, or renown.
Seeking only sensual desires with no other intent— how could such a person be associated with the wise?
Even one who dwells in the various dhyānas and possesses majestic power, if he teaches those of valorous strength or royal seers,
yet at times his mind becomes stained by female beauty, he will fall away from all the virtues of self-mastery.
They engage in strife amidst elephants, horses, and military arrays; they sacrifice their lives to cross the sea and gather precious treasures;
noble families become beggars and slaves—all such practices contrary to the True Dharma stem from women.
The moods of joy and anger in women are difficult to perceive; their defiled minds and perverse schemes are boundless.
Among those renowned as wise men in the world, there is none who can know the heart of a woman.
Even the celestial lords and seers possessing the five supernormal powers may calculate the exact volume of the waters of the great ocean throughout their entire lives,
yet they cannot know the individual, distinct intentions of each woman.
Deceitful words deceive the ears, as sweet as honey; their hearts are like sharp swords that harm others.
Their speech and meaning are so clever they steal the hearts of men; harboring evil and devising schemes, they spread all manner of poison.
Whether women are exquisitely adorned or unadorned, they harbor suspicion and jealousy in every movement—walking, standing, sitting, or reclining.
Gazing with lustful eyes upon women, whether foolish or wise, even looking at painted images of women increases their malice.
The foolish child delights in climbing the branches of a poisonous tree; the deluded one wishes to dwell in the lair of a venomous snake;
the madman grasps at glowing red-hot iron. To draw near to the form of woman is a transgression even greater than these.
The mind is clouded and intoxicated by attachment to female beauty; When it opposes one's will, it brings the poison of anger that harms the body.
Fearing those women who delight in resentment, how could a wise person dwell in their company?
Their evil natures fill their hearts; how are they any different from deep waters where crocodiles dwell?
She takes no account of valor, strength, appearance, or lineage; Indulging her desires as she pleases, she knows neither right nor wrong.
A woman’s mind is as unstable as a swift wind, And like a fleeting cloud or a flash of lightning.
Even if one serves her for a hundred years and provides all she desires, She will never harbor even the slightest thought of gratitude toward the man.
Disrespecting those with virtue and slighting those without it, Hating the poor and delighting in the wealthy, pursuing greed for beautiful words,
And increasing arrogance through honor and sustenance— When resources and wealth fail, one has no heart to look back;
Like a venomous snake upon a parched desert, or a *vatsanābha* flower, To dwell with such as these is to carry a burden that harms this life.
Brief intimacy with women surpasses that [of others], yet it forever destroys the body of future merit.
Women are sly and artful, constantly engaging in slander; they create estrangement between the six types of relatives and friends.
They conceal their own faults while broadcasting the failings of others; all manner of calamities and afflictions arise from women.
The female mind is unstable like a monkey; it constantly dwells on minor transgressions while forgetting great kindness.

When a fool serves her with the reverence due to a teacher or a lord, his devotion is never satisfied, for the nature of women is like a river that overflows its banks, sweeping away all excellent qualities and destroying many lives.
Like a torrential current rushing down a steep slope, it causes both banks to collapse; the harm women inflict upon the wholesome exceeds even this.

The net of a woman’s desire is exceedingly firm and dense; she looks about and walks slowly with an air of shamelessness, her laughter and speech full of joy and contention, yet harboring a fundamentally alien heart.
She ensnares all who are wealthy and noble as if they were intoxicated by darkness.
A woman’s passion arises from delusion; like a tree without roots, when desire is exhausted, the lamp of her beauty fades.
In a mere moment, all affection ceases. A woman’s love and lust last but an instant;
her defiled mind and deceitful speech are difficult to rely upon.
At times he is valued more highly than pearls; at other times he is cast aside with loathing like a blade of straw.
With the power of an elephant king who uproots trees with ease, his color is like a great white cloud floating in the sky.
Yet, because a female elephant has intoxicated his mind, he follows all others as they tame him.
A bodhisattva may gather women for the sake of the Dharma, Constantly instructing them while remaining detached in mind;
Yet when they become excessively intimate, They are like a bird with broken wings that cannot fly.
The inclinations of women are always base and low, Like a riverbank that crumbles and collapses.
Those who dwell [with them] cause their wholesome dharmas to decline; the destruction of lineages and the extinction of clans all stem from these women.
They can spread the net of craving and desire, ensnaring and capturing all foolish men.
Sentient beings in the world who are stained by lust are like fish that swallow the hook and become their prey.
The wise observe and know that it is fundamentally impure; from the nine orifices, fluids flow constantly day and night.
Thus one should cultivate weary detachment toward the female body. Why then give rise to craving for it?
The female body is as illusory as a bubble on the water, a locus for the sufferings of old age, sickness, and death.
The accumulation of impurities is like a mountain; how can one give rise to craving for this?
All sorrows and terrors are born from the form of women.
If one can contemplate this without craving, one will be liberated, free from sorrow and fear.
Therefore, the wise do not gaze upon women; if they should observe them at times, they do so with a mind of loving-kindness, regarding them as a mother, a daughter, or a sister.
They should teach them the Dharma of non-attachment according to their needs, so that they may understand how the various impurities arise within and without a woman’s body.
How can the movement of objects toward the senses kindle the fire of desire, Scorching all roots of goodness accumulated over countless eons?
Furthermore, the *Sūtra of the Questions of King Ambarīṣa* says:
"Lustful desire is foul and impure; its source is not clean. Once it has passed, the karmic suffering it increases is ever more profound."
The wise Dharma Master rebukes the defilement of desire; even one's parents would be of no benefit [in that state].
It is like a vast pit of impurity, filled with excrement and soil, reeking with foul stench;
it is also like a bloated corpse amidst the graves—such is the person of lustful desire.

Furthermore, like flies and insects gnawing at a festering sore, or like donkeys and horses wallowing in dung and filth, or like pigs and dogs devouring putrid fish—so too is the obsession with women.
It destroys one’s good reputation as well as virtuous conduct; it is a constant practice of violating prohibitions, devoid of all shame.
One will not be reborn in the heavenly realms but will fall into the Avīci hell;
therefore, the Dharma Master censures sensual desire as if a person had mistakenly drunk a potent poison.
Bewildered and frantic, with pain throughout the entire body, one does not realize they have been struck by the poison of impermanence; those who indulge in lust are just like this.
Delighting in fine flavors and exquisite delicacies, Craving the sound of song and attached to sights, sounds, and worldly affairs;
Lacking reflection and prone to forgetfulness, One performs only the karma that causes the suffering of saṃsāra.
Greedy for and praising lustful desires, One fails to understand this deluded body, which is but a sack of excrement.
Day and night they constantly practice base deeds; Lacking merit, they sink into the evil realms.
They praise lustful conduct and unwholesome acts; Abounding in anger, they increase their ignorance.
Like treading upon a towering and perilous precipice, They fail to realize that in an instant they may lose their lives.
Having departed from the human world of Jambudvīpa, one falls into the boundless ocean of karma;
surrounded by five peaks amidst iron mountains, the light of the sun, moon, and lamps is entirely unseen.
Like a wind-driven madman devoid of understanding, one wanders back and forth, traversing in all directions, having lost the path.
Thus, through successive births, they dwell eternally here; nothing in all the worlds is held in high esteem by them.

They do not give rise to various kinds of wholesome karma; even if there are sons or daughters, they lack filial piety and respect, abandoning their honored parents to commit the five heinous acts. They are devoted to their wives and daughters with redoubled diligence.
They cast wide nets of sin without reflection, falling into the midst of greed, delusion, and sensual pleasure;
they distance themselves from their parents without gratitude or reciprocity, failing to consider the hardships of their upbringing.
Indulging in negligence, lust, and frivolity, their mutual afflictions increase manifold.
They destroy their practice and harbor various doubts; failing to meet noble sages, they fail to create wholesome causes.
They delight in practicing evil deeds and undergo extreme suffering. Disregarding punishments, they are beset by shame and humiliation;
through strife, plunder, and deception, they bring about injury and death. They squander wealth and property and alienate themselves from virtuous friends.
Failing to be born in the heavenly realms or among humans, one dies and enters the Avīci Hell,
where iron forests are dark blue with bristling blades; a city of fierce flames and hot embers,
with sword-trees and knife-mountains covering the ground, where molten copper and glowing iron serve as drink and food.
Such great suffering arises from lust, which obscures the root of bodhi-wisdom.
You should feel terror toward women; do not allow them to draw near and give rise to clinging.
If you remain in accord with the wholesome paths of humans and devas, you will soon attain bodhi for yourself.
We have been shrouded by ignorance and failed to recognize the sinful causes of craving. Now that we have encountered this site of enlightenment, we have finally awakened to this truth.
We take refuge in the Tathāgata Vairocana and the ocean-like assembly of all worthy sages. We burn incense and scatter flowers.
I openly confess and repent all karmic offenses and retributions arising from the delusion of craving, not daring to conceal them.
By virtue of these causes and conditions, may the craving, delusion, karma, and afflictions of myself and the ocean of sentient beings within the Dharma-realm attain purification.
Next, the mudrā and mantra for repentance to extinguish transgressions: Oṃ sarvapāpam me kṣayaṃ kuru svāhā.
(Recite three times.)
Sins accumulated over a hundred kalpas are entirely swept away in a single thought; like fire consuming dry grass, they are extinguished without remainder.
All the evil karma I have created in the past arose solely from beginningless greed, anger, and delusion.
I now repent of everything produced by my body, speech, and mind.
Having repented, I take refuge with a sincere heart and pay homage to the Honored One, Vairocana Buddha.

Gathering and then dispersing again, like those assembled at a theater; not abiding for even a single thought-moment, like a thunderclap in the sky;

like the great golden-winged bird devouring the dragons.

A hundred trillion clouds of celestial banners; raining down a hundred trillion clouds of celestial crowns; raining down a hundred trillion clouds of celestial ornaments;
raining down a hundred trillion clouds of celestial jewel garlands; raining down a hundred trillion clouds of celestial jewel necklaces;
raining down a hundred trillion clouds of celestial sandalwood incense; raining down a hundred trillion clouds of celestial aloeswood incense; [a hundred trillion...]
With voices of pleasing resonance, they praised and made offerings; with a hundred trillion vast sounds, they praised and served;
with a hundred trillion profound sounds, they praised their practice; with a hundred trillion exquisite sounds, they extolled the fruits of the Buddha’s deeds;
with a hundred trillion subtle sounds, they extolled the principle of reality as it is; and with a hundred trillion unobstructed, true sounds, they extolled the Buddha’s past conduct.
A hundred trillion sounds of purity praised the offerings made to the Buddhas of the past;
a hundred trillion sounds of Dharma-gates praised the Buddha’s supreme fearlessness; a hundred trillion immeasurable sounds praised the inexhaustible merits of the Bodhisattvas;
and a hundred trillion sounds of the Bodhisattva stages praised the revelation of all practices corresponding to the Bodhisattva stages.
There were a hundred trillion sounds of uninterrupted continuity, extolling the Buddha’s virtues without end;
a hundred trillion sounds of conformity, praising and extolling the conduct of seeing the Buddha;
a hundred trillion sounds of the profound Dharma, extolling the principles corresponding to all unimpeded wisdom; and a hundred trillion vast sounds, whose resonance filled all buddha-fields.
There were a hundred trillion sounds of unimpeded purity that caused all beings to rejoice according to their inclinations;
a hundred trillion sounds of non-abiding in the three realms that caused those who heard them to penetrate deeply into the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*);

a hundred trillion sounds of joy that caused those who heard them to be free from mental obstructions, developing deep faith and reverence; and a hundred trillion sounds of the Buddha-realm, which issued forth in accordance with [the needs of beings].

Their voices were able to reveal the meaning of all dharmas; with the sounds of a hundred trillion *dhāraṇīs*, they skillfully proclaimed the distinctions among all dharma-phrases and definitively resolved the secret treasury of the Tathāgata. With such various articles of offering as these...

Throughout all lands of atoms, they universally display their supernormal powers. The Buddhas, according to the minds of sentient beings, Universally appear before them.

The Sons of the Buddha, according to their wisdom, Are able to enter and observe it, And they speak directly in praise of the Buddha.
The mind, intellect, and consciousness of the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, are all unapprehendable.
One should know the mind of the Tathāgata solely by virtue of his immeasurable wisdom. The wisdom of the Tathāgata is the basis for all mundane and supramundane wisdom;
yet the wisdom of the Tathāgata has no basis of its own. It constantly gives rise to all varieties of mundane and supramundane wisdom, and...
The wisdom of the Tathāgata neither increases nor decreases; it is like the great ocean. Its waters flow secretly through the lands of the four continents and the eighty billion minor islands.
Wherever one digs, there is no place where water cannot be found, yet that great ocean makes no discrimination, thinking, "I am producing this water.
The ocean-water of the Buddha’s wisdom is also like this; it flows into all sentient beings.
Within the mind of birth, if sentient beings observe their objects and cultivate the dharma-gates of wisdom, they will attain the purity of wisdom.
When this wisdom is pure and lucid, the Tathāgata’s wisdom is equal and non-dual, devoid of discrimination;
yet, because the mental activities of sentient beings differ, the wisdom they attain is each distinct.

Next, the Repentance of the Twelve Links of Dependent Origination:
I only pray that the Buddha, Dharma, and Sangha Treasures, Vairocana Tathāgata, Samantabhadra, and Mañjuśrī—like the infinite net of Indra—will [bear witness].

I pray that for myself and the ocean of all sentient beings, from the beginningless past until this very moment, though the ocean of karma is inexhaustible and the Indra-net of causes is layered upon layer, we may understand the twelve links of dependent origination and the delusions of karma.
Regarding the retribution for offenses, one must confess and repent them openly.

As for the twelve links of dependent origination (*dvādaśāṅga-pratītyasamutpāda*), they are all expounded in the teachings of the Two Vehicles, the Three Vehicles, and the Distinct Teaching of the One Vehicle.
Now, according to the Distinct and Perfect Teachings, the twelvefold dependent origination is universally pervasive and mutually inclusive. As the Sūtra says: "The world undergoes birth..."
All this arises from attachment to a self. If one is free from this attachment, there is no place for birth. Furthermore, he reflects: "Ordinary people lack wisdom;
they cling to a self and constantly seek existence or non-existence. Through improper reflection, they give rise to deluded conduct and walk upon false paths."
Through the accumulation and increase of unwholesome, wholesome, and imperturbable formations (*saṃskāra*), the seed of the mind is planted within these formations.

Being with outflows (*sāsrava*) and grasping (*upādāna*), it gives rise again to future birth, aging, and death. That is to say: karma is the field, consciousness (*vijñāna*) is the seed, it is covered by the darkness of ignorance (*avidyā*), moistened by the water of craving (*tṛṣṇā*), and irrigated by the sprinkling of self-conceit (*asmimāna*).
As the net of views (*dṛṣṭi-jāla*) increases, the sprout of name-and-form (*nāmarūpa*) is produced. This is called [the process].
The increase of form gives rise to the five sense faculties (*indriya*). The mutual interaction of the faculties gives rise to contact (*sparśa*). Contact gives rise to feeling (*vedanā*).

Following feeling, there arises craving (*tṛṣṇā*) characterized by the longing for existence. The increase of craving gives rise to grasping (*upādāna*). The increase of grasping gives rise to becoming (*bhava*).

Once becoming has arisen, the manifestation of the five aggregates (*skandha*) as a body within the various realms of existence is called birth (*jāti*). Once born, the process of decay and transformation is aging (*jarā*), and the final passing away is death (*maraṇa*). At the time of aging and death, [the cycle] begins again with birth.
All these afflictions of feverish distress—because of this feverish distress, sorrow, lamentation, and all manner of suffering accumulate. These arise through such causes and conditions;
there is no one who accumulates them, yet they perish spontaneously. There is likewise no one who extinguishes them, for they fail to recognize dependent origination. I now repent of all of this.
1. Contemplation on the Continuity of the Links of Existence. O Son of the Buddha, this Bodhisattva Mahāsattva further reflects:

"Because one does not understand the ultimate truth (paramārtha-satya), it is called ignorance (avidyā). The karma produced is the basis for volitional formations (saṃskāra). The initial moment of consciousness is 'consciousness' (vijñāna);

together with consciousness, the four grasping aggregates arise as 'name-and-form' (nāmarūpa). The growth of name-and-form constitutes the six sense bases (ṣaḍāyatana). [The meeting of] the faculties and their objects..."
The conjunction of the three factors is contact (*sparśa*). Co-arising with contact is sensation (*vedanā*). Attachment to sensation is craving (*tṛṣṇā*).

The intensification of craving is grasping (*upādāna*). The tainted karma produced by grasping becomes existence (*bhava*) in the future. The arising of the aggregates (*skandha*) from that karma is birth (*jāti*).

The maturation of the aggregates is aging (*jarā*). The disintegration of the aggregates is death (*maraṇa*). At the time of death, the separation accompanied by delusion and attachment, and the distress within the heart and mind, is sorrow (*śoka*).

Weeping and sobbing, one utters sighs of lamentation. In the context of the five sense faculties, this is suffering (*duḥkha*); in the mental faculty (*manobhūmi*), it is grief (*daurmanasya*). When grief and suffering increase further, they become affliction (*upāyāsa*).
In this way, there is only the growth of the tree of suffering, which is without self, without what belongs to a self, without an agent, and without an experiencer.
Again, he reflects: "If there is an agent, then there is an action; if there is no agent, then there is no action.
Within the ultimate truth (*paramārtha*), neither can be found. Not understanding dependent origination (*pratītyasamutpāda*), I now repent for all of it."
Second, the contemplation that subsumes [all things] into the single mind. This Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva further reflects:
"The entirety of the triple world is, by nature, the single mind. It is upon this single mind that the Tathāgata has analytically expounded the twelve links of existence."
It is established in this manner. Why? Because craving for objects arises simultaneously with the mind. The mind is consciousness (*vijñāna*); the object is volitional formations (*saṃskāra*).
Delusion regarding these formations is ignorance (*avidyā*). That which arises simultaneously with ignorance and the mind is name-and-form (*nāmarūpa*).

The growth of name-and-form is the six sense bases (*ṣaḍāyatana*). The union of the three factors of the six bases is contact (*sparśa*). That which arises simultaneously with contact is feeling (*vedanā*). Feeling is insatiable.
Craving is the foot [of existence]. Clinging, which grasps and does not let go, is *upādāna*. The arising of those various links of existence is *bhava*.

That which arises from *bhava* is called birth (*jāti*). The maturation of birth is aging (*jarā*). The decay of aging is death (*maraṇa*). Not understanding dependent origination—now I repent for all of this.
Third is the contemplation on the differentiation of one's own karma. O Son of the Buddha, herein ignorance has two kinds of karma:

first, it causes sentient beings to become deluded regarding their objects of perception; second, it acts as the cause for the arising of volitional formations (*saṃskāra*). Volitional formations also have two kinds of karma: first, they are able to produce future retribution;
second, they act as the cause for the arising of consciousness (*vijñāna*). Consciousness also has two kinds of karma: first, it [causes] all states of existence...

[The consciousness] continues. Second, it acts as the cause for the arising of name-and-form (*nāmarūpa*). Name-and-form also has two kinds of functions: first, they mutually assist and accomplish one another;

second, they act as the cause for the arising of the six sense bases (*ṣaḍāyatana*). The six sense bases also have two kinds of functions: first, each individually perceives its own respective object;
second, they act as the cause for the arising of contact (*sparśa*). Contact also has two kinds of functions: first, it is able to touch the object...

Conditioning factors (*pratyaya*). Second, they act as the cause for the arising of feeling (*vedanā*). Feeling also has two kinds of functions: first, it is able to experience objects such as the pleasant and the unpleasant;
second, it acts as the cause for the arising of craving (*tṛṣṇā*). Craving also has two kinds of functions: first, it is stained by and attached to desirable objects;
second, it acts as the cause for the arising of grasping (*upādāna*). Grasping also has two kinds of functions: first, it causes all afflictions (*kleśa*) to manifest...
Continued: Second, [existence] acts as the productive cause for birth. Existence (*bhava*) also has two kinds of functions: first, it can cause one to be born in other realms of existence;
second, it acts as the productive cause for birth (*jāti*). Birth (*jāti*) also has two kinds of functions: first, it can give rise to the aggregates (*skandha*).
Second, it acts as the generative cause for old age. Old age also has two kinds of functions: first, it causes the faculties to undergo transformation;
second, it acts as the generative cause for death. Death also has two kinds of functions: first, it is able to destroy all conditioned formations (*saṃskāra*);
second, because of a lack of awareness, the continuity of existence is not severed, and one fails to recognize dependent origination (*pratītyasamutpāda*). I now repent of all these.

Fourth is the contemplation of non-separation. O Son of the Buddha, herein, from "ignorance conditions volitional formations" up to "birth conditions aging and death," it is because ignorance through birth act as conditions that they cause volitional formations through aging and death to be uninterrupted and to be assisted in their formation.
"When ignorance ceases, volitional formations cease; and so on, until: when birth ceases, aging and death cease.

This means that by virtue of ignorance through to birth no longer acting as conditions, all volitional formations through to aging and death are brought to cessation and extinction, as they are no longer assisted or brought into being.
Not having understood dependent origination, I now repent of it all.

Fifth, the contemplation on the non-interruption of the three paths. Son of the Buddha, herein, the non-interruption of ignorance, craving, and grasping constitutes the path of afflictions (*kleśa-mārga*);

the non-interruption of formative forces (*saṃskāra*) and existence (*bhava*) constitutes the path of karma (*karma-mārga*); and the non-interruption of the remaining factors constitutes the path of suffering (*duḥkha-mārga*).

By discerning the cessation of these three paths at their prior and posterior limits, one cuts off these three paths. Being free from "I" and "mine," there is only arising and ceasing, like a bundle of reeds. It is not...
The arising of consciousness—now I repent all of this.

Sixth, the contemplation of the past, present, and future: furthermore, regarding "ignorance conditions volitional formations," this refers to contemplating consciousness through to feeling in the past;
this refers to contemplating craving through to becoming in the present; this refers to contemplating [the factors] from that point onward in the future.

Regarding the cessation of formations through the cessation of the continuous succession of ignorance: this is the abandonment through dependent observation. I now repent for all instances of failing to understand dependent origination.
Seventh, the contemplation on the accumulation of the three types of suffering: furthermore, the twelve links of existence are called the three sufferings; herein, ignorance...

From volitional formations up to the six sense bases are the suffering of conditioned existence (*saṃskāra-duḥkha*). Contact and sensation are the suffering of pain (*duḥkha-duḥkha*). The remainder is the suffering of change (*vipariṇāma-duḥkha*).

The cessation of ignorance leading to the cessation of volitional formations is the severance of these three types of suffering. Not having understood dependent origination, I now repent for all of it.

The eighth is the contemplation on the arising and ceasing through dependent origination. Furthermore, regarding "ignorance conditions volitional formations": with ignorance as a causal condition, the various formations are able to arise.
Regarding "with the cessation of ignorance, formations cease": because ignorance is absent, the various formations are likewise absent. The same applies to the remaining links.
Failing to understand this dependent origination, I now repent for all of it.
Ninth is the contemplation on the bondage of arising and ceasing: furthermore, that "conditioned by ignorance, volitional formations arise" is the bondage of arising;

that "with the cessation of ignorance, volitional formations cease" is the bondage of cessation. It is the same for the remaining links. I now repent of all failure to understand dependent origination.
The tenth is the contemplation of the exhaustion of non-existence. Furthermore, "conditioned by ignorance, volitional formations arise" is the contemplation that accords with non-existence;
"with the cessation of ignorance, volitional formations cease" is the contemplation that accords with exhaustion and cessation. The remaining [links] are likewise so.
Thus, through these ten types of contemplations in both reverse and forward order, one contemplates dependent origination. Not having understood dependent origination, I now repent for all of it.

We were shrouded by ignorance and did not recognize the twelve links of dependent origination (*dvādaśāṅga-pratītyasamutpāda*). We transmigrated through saṃsāra, unable to contemplate or cultivate it.

Now that we have encountered this site of enlightenment (*bodhimaṇḍa*), we have finally awakened to its realization. We take refuge in the Tathāgata Vairocana and the ocean-like assembly of all worthy and holy ones.
Burning incense and scattering flowers, we confess and repent for our failure to contemplate and cultivate the karmic retributions arising from dependent origination.
I dare not conceal anything. By this cause and condition, may I and the ocean of sentient beings within the Dharma-realm awaken to the twelve links of dependent origination;
may all our sinful karmas be entirely purified.

Homage to the Fire Deity, Lord Who Radiates the Light of Wisdom; homage to the Wind Deity, Lord Whose Crown is Made of Mani Jewels;

homage to the Deity Who Presides Over Space, who adorns the entire dharma-realm and all voids;
homage to the Deity Who Presides Over the Ocean, who universally delivers sentient beings across the sea of existence.
Homage to the Mountain-Ruling Deity, who constantly and diligently accumulates the roots of goodness that assist the path toward omniscience, towering as high as a mountain;
homage to the City-Ruling Deity, who constantly and diligently protects the bodhicitta of all sentient beings.
Homage to the great nāga kings who constantly and diligently guard the unsurpassed dharma-city of the knowledge of all-knowledge.
Homage to the yakṣa kings who constantly and diligently guard all sentient beings.
Homage to the gandharva kings who always cause the joy of sentient beings to increase.
Homage to the Kumbhāṇḍa King Constantly Diligent in Eliminating the Suffering of All Pretas.
Homage to the Garuḍa King Ever-Vowing to Rescue All Beings from the Ocean of Existence.
Homage to the Asura King Vowing to Attain the Body of All Tathāgatas and Transcend the World.
Homage to the Mahoraga King Joyful upon Seeing the Buddha, who bows his body in reverence;
homage to the Great Heavenly Kings who are ever weary of birth and death and constantly delight in seeing the Buddha;
homage to the Great Brahma Kings who honor the Buddha, praising and making offerings to him.
Homage to Mañjuśrī and the hosts of all such divine kings throughout the ten directions;
we take refuge in them all. May our transgressions be extinguished and our pure faith increase; may we be born in the Flower Treasury Ocean and the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss.
The *First Assembly of Six Thousand Bhikṣus: The Scripture on Manifesting the Return from the Small Vehicle toward the Great Vehicle* states:

Homage to the Bhikṣu Samudrabuddhi. Homage to the Bhikṣu Sujāta.

Homage to the Bhikṣu Brahmajaya! Homage to the Bhikṣu Śāntamati!
Homage to these and all others, a multitude of six thousand bhikṣus; throughout the ten directions, we take refuge in them all.
May our transgressions be extinguished and our pure faith increase, and may we be born in the Flower Treasury Ocean.

Stūpa Temple:

together with its ten million billion nayutas of all attendant sūtras.
Homage to the ten thousand nāgas who, upon hearing this Dharma-realm sutra, attained non-retrogression; homage to the immeasurable hundreds of thousands of nāga kings and all the hosts of the oceans.
Homage to all such as these, and furthermore to the unspeakably many, immeasurable, boundless, incomparable, and innumerable ones.

The multitudes of the ocean, throughout the ten directions, take refuge; Their sins are extinguished and their pure faith increases; May they be born within the Flower Treasury Ocean, in the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss.
