Tiantai’s Practice of Teaching and Contemplation: The Monk Zhengzhi’s Stabilization of Mind, Part Twenty-Nine;
Following this, the fifth assembly of the ten good spiritual friends within the stage of the Ten Abidings.
With all reverence, pay homage to the inexhaustible Triple Gem.
All members of this assembly kneel with their right knees on the ground, solemnly holding incense and flowers to make offerings according to the Dharma.

May this ocean-like cloud of offerings pervade the worlds of the ten directions. They present various supreme and wondrous banners and flags, with poles made of myriad jewels and streamers of precious silk.
The banners were adorned with various multicolored silks. Precious nets hung down and covered them, their radiant colors filling all space.

As precious bells swayed gently, their sounds blended in harmony. Extraordinary and wondrous jewels, shaped like half-moons, and Jāmbūnada gold, whose brilliance surpassed the bright sun, were all placed atop the banners.
These served as adornments, manifesting according to the karmic fruits of the various worlds as diverse and marvelous objects.

Adorned with such countless thousands of myriads of koṭis of nayutas of exquisite banners and streamers, their shadows meeting and their splendors connecting, they shine forth in alternating succession.
Their light is pure and majestic, pervading the entire earth and filling all lands throughout the ten directions, the void, and the Dharma-realm.
With such various offerings, he constantly performs worship in a manner as infinitely layered as Indra’s net for all Buddhas.
The assembly of Bodhisattvas, noble and holy as the ocean, receives these clouds of offerings and makes them into a terrace of radiance,
vast as boundless realms, immeasurable and inexhaustible, vowing to perform the work of a Buddha.
Having made these offerings, with all due reverence,
they next present a vast ocean of the nature of precious jewels and gems, along with the most excellent seven-jeweled mountains and so forth.
I bring forth such clouds of offerings as these and present them to all the Buddhas. Oṃ sarva-tathāgata-arcanābhiṣeka-samaya-rakṣa māṃ hūṃ.
The *Ratnakūṭa-sūtra* states: There is a dhāraṇī called the "Spell of Immeasurable Varieties," which can accomplish all things and possesses great efficacy.
The dhāraṇī is as follows: Oṃ sīmala sīmala maimada sigara mahāliṅga hūṃ.
Next is the mantra of the Amoghamani Mudrā: Oṃ a ma ā bhuñja me pade mama cittaṃ dṛḍhīkuru svāhā amoghasiddhe hūṃ.
With a Brahma-voice, he praises the Tathāgata’s great wisdom, which universally purifies all worlds. Once the worlds have been brought to an end, he reveals all Buddha-dharmas.
Should there be anyone who wishes to see Buddhas as numerous as the count of sentient beings—
Nothing fails to respond to their mind, yet in truth there is no place from which it comes.

By focusing their thoughts unceasingly upon the realm of the Buddha, these people shall behold him; their number is equal to the extent of their own minds as they speak words of direct praise for the Buddha.
The Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, by the power of mastery over the mind, turns the wheel of Dharma without arising or turning.

Because he knows that all phenomena are eternally without arising, and so forth, throughout all places where the Tathāgata turns the Dharma, he universally enters into all sentient beings, all phenomena, all karmas, and all retributions, yet abides nowhere. All sentient beings...
All various languages do not depart from the Dharma-wheel of the Tathāgata, for the true reality (*dharmatā*) of speech and sound is itself the Dharma-wheel.
The Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, possesses a samādhi called "Ultimate Unobstructed Fearlessness.
Having entered this samādhi, from each and every body and each and every mouth of his perfectly awakened state, he emits as many words as there are sentient beings.

Regarding sounds: within each and every sound, all manner of sounds are fully contained, each distinct and different, as they turn the wheel of Dharma and cause all sentient beings to give rise to joy.
One who can understand the turning of the wheel of Dharma in this way should be known as one who accords with all Buddha-dharmas;
if one does not understand it thus, then one does not accord with them.
Homage to the Vairocana Buddha, the Original Honored One of Unobstructed Ten Bodies in the Flower Treasury World-Ocean of the Great Vaipulya Buddhāvataṃsaka Sūtra.
Homage to Śākyamuni Buddha,
who with great kindness and compassion made five hundred vows to rescue sentient beings from suffering in the five turbidities.

Homage to the Buddha Bhaisajyaguru-vaidūryaprabha-rāja, King of Medicine, Lapis Lazuli Light, who possesses twelve supreme vows to save those suffering in the five turbidities in the Pūrṇacandra World of the East.
Homage to the Buddha Amitābha, who possesses forty-eight vows to save those suffering in the five turbidities in the Sukhāvatī World of the West.
Homage to the Perfect Teaching of the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha*, throughout all lands as numerous as atoms within the entirety of space across the ten directions and three periods of time.
Homage to the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra, who presides over the truth of the Vows and Practices within the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha*.
Homage to the Mahāsattva Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva Mahāsattva, who presides over faith, understanding, and realized wisdom within the Great Vaipulya Buddha Avataṃsaka Sūtra.
Homage to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, the Thousand Hands and Thousand Eyes, who possesses great kindness and great compassion, rescues from suffering in the five turbidities.

Homage to him whose great vows are profound and vast, who rescues from suffering in the five turbidities, appears in worlds where no Buddha dwells, and eternally abides to comfort the hearts of sentient beings.
Homage to the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Kṣitigarbha-Rāja in the realm of Yama;

and to the Bodhisattvas of the ten stages of faith, the ten abodes, the ten practices, the ten dedications, the ten grounds, and Equal Enlightenment throughout all the lands as numerous as atoms within the entirety of space across the ten directions and the three periods of time.
Homage to the assembly of all oceans of Bodhisattvas, as numerous as the atoms within the oceans of lands pervading the entire Dharma-realm;
and homage to the fifty-five holy ones who realized and manifested the five sites during the final assembly of the Great Vaipulya Buddhāvataṃsaka Sūtra.

Homage to the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Sudhana, who, as a vessel of perfect capacity and superior faculties within the final assembly of the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra*, sought the Dharma through a hundred cities;
who, within a single lifetime, perfected the practices of a Bodhisattva, and who serves as the paradigm for cultivation and realization for the sudden gate of the Dharma in the Final Age.

Homage to all Buddha-activities within the Dharma-body, form-bodies, physical relics, precious stupas, temples, and monasteries throughout the dust-mote lands of the ten directions and three periods of time across the entirety of empty space;
and to the ocean-like assemblies of Bodhisattvas, worthies, and sages at the repositories of the Dharma and the places where the Dharma is preached.
Namo to the Great Vow, Donning the Armor to Seek Birth in the Pure Land, Protector of the True Dharma during the Final Dregs of the Summer Kingdom,
State-Protecting Dharma Master. With a sincere heart, I take refuge and pay homage to the World-Ocean of the Flower Treasury within the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra*, the Honored One.

To Vairocana Buddha, throughout the ten directions, we take refuge; May our sins be extinguished and our pure faith increase; We vow to be born within the ocean of the Flower Treasury and the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss.
The *Sutra on the Dharma-door of Liberation Entitled "The Ocean-bannered Bhikṣu’s Universally Adorned Pure Gate"* states:
At that time, the youth Sudhana [arrived at] the Pure Radiance [gate] and, taking his leave, departed.
May I, together with all sentient beings, be reborn in the Flower Treasury Ocean within the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss.
Homage to the Bhikṣu Samudrareṇu, who attained the pure light of the universal practice of the Prajñāpāramitā realm in the country of Mālikāra on the southern border of Jambudvīpa,
and who attained the ocean of gates of universal adornment and purity.
Homage to the countless hundreds of thousands of billions of elders, householders, and brahmins who emerged from beneath the feet of the bhikṣu Sāgaradhvaja.
Homage to the countless hundreds of thousands of billions of kṣatriyas who emerged from the two knees of the bhikṣu Sāgaradhvaja.
Homage to the assembly of all Brahmins;
homage to the assembly of immeasurable sages, as numerous as all living beings, who emerged from the waist of the bhikṣu Sāgaradhvaja.
Homage to all the inconceivable nāgas and inconceivable nāga maidens who emerged from the two flanks of the bhikṣu Sāgaradhvaja,
and to the immeasurable hundreds of thousands [of deities] who emerged from the auspicious svastika on the chest of the bhikṣu Sāgaradhvaja.
Homage to the assembly of all the billions of asura kings;
homage to the assembly of the countless hundreds of thousands of millions of śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas who emerged from the back of the bhikṣu Sāgaradhvaja.
Homage to the countless hundreds of thousands of billions of all the yakṣa and rākṣasa kings who emerged from the two shoulders of the bhikṣu Sāgaradhvaja.
Homage to the countless hundreds of thousands of billions of kinnara kings who emerged from the belly of the bhikṣu Sāgaradhvaja.

Each was surrounded before and behind by countless kinnarīs; furthermore, there emerged from [the mouth] countless billions of gandharva kings, each surrounded before and behind by countless gandharvīs.
All these multitudes paid homage to the bhikṣu Sāgaradhvaja, as they issued forth in hundreds of thousands of billions from the face of that bhikṣu. All these turned toward him.
Homage from the entire assembly to the Holy King;
homage from the entire assembly to the countless hundreds of thousands of billions of sun-discs of light issuing from the two eyes of the bhikṣu Sāgaradhvaja.
Homage to the immeasurable hundreds of thousands of billions of Śakras and all their retinues who emerged from the white tuft of hair between the eyebrows of the bhikṣu Sāgaradhvaja.
Homage to the countless hundreds of thousands of billions of Brahmā kings who emerged from the forehead of the bhikṣu Sāgaradhvaja.
Homage to the entire assembly of all bodhisattvas, as numerous as the atoms in immeasurable buddha-fields, who emerged from atop the head of the bhikṣu Sāgaradhvaja.
Homage to the entire assembly.
Homage to the immeasurable hundreds of thousands of billions of Tathāgata bodies emerging from the crown of the head of the Bhikṣu Sāgaradhvaja;
may all beings throughout the ten directions take refuge in them. May their sins be extinguished and their pure faith increase, and may they vow to be born in the Flower Treasury Ocean.
The *Sukhāvatīvyūha-saptama-śreṣṭhī-vaśyā-upāsikā-viśoka-praśāntaketu-vimokṣa-dharmaparyāya-sūtra* states: "At that time,
the youth Sudhana (having reached [the place of] the upāsikā Śreṣṭhī Vaśyā Viśokapraśāntaketu) and having formed this thought, took his leave and departed."
May I, together with all sentient beings, be reborn in the Flower Treasury Ocean, within the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss.
Next, the laywoman Śuddhā heard the Dharma and practiced the pure conduct (*brahmacarya*).
Homage to all Buddhas of the ten directions! Homage to the Buddha Dīpaṃkara!
Homage to the Buddha Vimala. Homage to the Buddha Suvicitracchattra.
Homage to the Buddha Jayasumeru. Homage to the Buddha Padmagarbhaśrī.
Homage to the Buddha Vairocana. Homage to the Buddha Samantacakṣus.
Homage to the Buddha Brahmāyus. Homage to the Buddha Vajranābhi.
Homage to the Buddha Varuṇadeva.
Next, the upāsikā Viśākha.
Homage to the laywoman Śrīśa, who dwells in the ocean-tide abode within the universally adorned grove and has attained the liberation door of the banner of peace;
all in the ten directions take refuge in her. May our sins be extinguished, may our pure faith increase, and may we be born in the Flower Treasury Ocean.
The *Sūtra on the Dharma Gate of Liberation of the Immortal Vimalacandra (Vimukta-Indra) of the Eighth [Stage] in the Pure Land of Sukhāvatī* states:
"At that time, the youth Sudhana... [having arrived] gazed upon him with earnest devotion and took his leave to travel south."
May I, together with all sentient beings, be reborn in the Flower Treasury Ocean within the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss.
Next, Vimalakṣa [Vimukta] causes Sudhana to behold the various Buddhas.
Homage to the ocean-like assemblies at the sites of enlightenment and the realms of all the Buddhas beheld by Sudhana.
Next, to the south of the rishi Vimalaghoṣa,
within the realm of the ocean-tide Nara in the southern direction, is the rishi Vimalaghoṣa, who attained the bodhisattva liberation door of the "Invincible Banner."
All in the ten directions take refuge; Sins are extinguished and pure faith increases. May they be born within the Flower Treasury Ocean, In the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss.
The Ninth: The Dharma Gate of the Liberation of the Inexhaustible Wheel of the Fierce Brahmin.
The Sūtra says: "At that time, the youth Sudhana (until) circumambulated him countless times and took his leave to depart.
May I, together with all sentient beings, be reborn in the Flower Treasury Ocean, in the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss.
Homage to the Brahmin Śroṇakoṭīviṃśa, who attained the liberation of the Inexhaustible Wheel while dwelling in the village of Īśāna in the south.
Homage to the Youth Sudhana, who, through the supreme conditions of his exhortation, dwells in mid-air amidst ten thousand assemblies of all the Brahmās of the first dhyāna in the realm of form.
Homage to the noble youth Sudhana, to the ten thousand evil Māras who exhorted him through superior conditions as he dwelt in mid-air,
to the ten thousand Śakra-devānām-indras, the ten thousand Suyāma-devas, the ten thousand Tuṣita-devas,
the ten thousand Trāyastriṃśa-devas, and to all the sons of gods, daughters of gods, and their entire retinues.
Homage to the Youth Sudhana, who, through the inspiration of his excellent conditions, dwells in mid-air; to the ten thousand dragon kings,
the ten thousand yakṣa kings, the ten thousand gandharva kings, the ten thousand asura kings, the ten thousand garuḍa kings,
the ten thousand kiṃnara kings, and the immeasurable dragon maidens and others.
Homage to the Youth Sudhana! Encouraged by these supreme conditions, you abide in the midst of the infinite devas of the desire realm throughout the ten directions;
all take refuge in you. May our sins be extinguished, our pure faith increase, and may we be born in the Flower Treasury Ocean.

The Sūtra says: At that time, the youth Sudhana (up to) paid his respects with longing and veneration, took his leave, and departed.

May I, together with all sentient beings, be reborn in the Flower Treasury Ocean within the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss, and [visit] each of the majestic palaces of Compassionate Conduct and all the Buddhas therein.
Homage to all Tathāgatas within the Dharma-realm in each and every wall of the Vairocana-garbha-alaṃkāra Palace;
homage to all [Tathāgatas] within the Dharma-realm in each and every pillar of the Vairocana-garbha-alaṃkāra Palace.
Homage to the Tathāgatas within every single mirror of the Adorned Palace of Vairocana’s Treasury, throughout the entire Dharma-realm.
Homage to all Tathāgatas within the Dharma-realm, in each and every characteristic within the Adorned Palace of the Vairocana-treasury;
homage to all [Tathāgatas] within the Dharma-realm, in each and every form within the Adorned Palace of the Vairocana-treasury.
Homage to the Tathāgatas within every single maṇi-jewel in the Adorned Palace of Vairocana’s Treasury, throughout the entire Dharma-realm.
Homage to all Tathāgatas within the Dharma-realm, contained within each and every ornamental feature inside the Vairocana-garbha-alaṃkāra-maṇḍala-palace.
Homage to [all Tathāgatas] within the Dharma-realm, contained within each and every golden bell inside the Vairocana-garbha-alaṃkāra-maṇḍala-palace.
Homage to all Tathāgatas within every single jewel tree in the Adorned Palace of Vairocana’s Treasury, throughout the entire Dharma-realm.
Homage to all Tathāgatas within the Dharma-realm, within each and every precious image inside the Adorned Palace of Vairocana’s Treasury;
homage to [all Tathāgatas] within the Dharma-realm, within each and every precious necklace inside the Adorned Palace of Vairocana’s Treasury.
Next, all Tathāgatas attained the place of the dharma-gate from the maiden Maitrīcaryā;
I pay homage to the Buddha Maitrīcaryā, who attended thirty-six Ganges-sands of Buddhas.
Next, I pay homage to the maiden Maitrīcaryā in the city of Siṃhavikrīḍita in the south, who has attained the liberation door of being able to universally adorn the perfection of wisdom.
Homage to the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Sudhana, the supreme vessel of the highest capacity who sought the Dharma through a hundred cities;
within a single lifetime, he perfected the bodhisattva practices and serves as the model for cultivation and realization for the sudden teaching of the final age.
To all in the ten directions, I take refuge in him. May my transgressions be extinguished, may my pure faith increase, and may I be reborn in the Flower Treasury Ocean.
In the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss, I next repent for the ten unwholesome karmas.
I take refuge in the inexhaustible Jewels of the Buddha, Dharma, and Sangha, as vast as a celestial net; in Vairocana Tathāgata; and in Samantabhadra and Mañjuśrī.

Assembly of noble ones gathered like the ocean, and world-transcending deities: by virtue of your compassionate original vows, may you emit great radiance to illuminate this Dharma assembly, bearing witness and providing protective mindfulness, and out of pity, graciously receive us.

I and the ocean of all sentient beings, from beginningless time until this very moment, have accumulated inexhaustible oceans of karma, layered like a celestial net of Indra. We now openly confess and repent for these ten unwholesome karmas.

Now, as for the ten unwholesome karmic actions, they are all clearly expounded by the heterodox teachings, the orthodox teachings, and the provisional, small, sudden, gradual, universal, and perfect teachings.

Herein, the ten wholesome actions are explained according to the Perfect Teaching (Yuanjiao), which also subsumes the others. As the Sūtra says: "By their very nature, Bodhisattvas distance themselves from all killing;
they do not keep weapons or staves, harbor no resentment, possess a sense of shame and dread of blame, and are fully endowed with benevolence and forbearance."
Toward all sentient beings who possess life, I have constantly given rise to a mind of compassion that seeks their benefit.
This Bodhisattva does not even harbor ill will or cause distress to sentient beings, much less give rise to the perception of them as sentient beings and intentionally commit acts of killing.
Failing to realize this Dharma, I now repent for all such actions.

By nature, they do not steal. Regarding their own resources, Bodhisattvas always know contentment; toward others, they are compassionate and forgiving, having no desire to encroach upon or damage them.
If an object belongs to another, they perceive it as belonging to another and never give rise to a thieving mind regarding it.
They would not take even a blade of grass if it were not given, let alone other means of subsistence. Failing to realize this Dharma, [those who act otherwise] now all...
I repent. By nature, I do not engage in sexual misconduct. A bodhisattva is content with his own wife and does not seek the wives of others.

Toward the wives and concubines of others, daughters protected by their kin, those betrothed through family mediation, and those protected by the Dharma, he does not give rise to even a single thought of lustful attachment; how much less so [in other cases]?
How much less so for those engaged in worldly affairs, and how much less so for those who follow unwholesome paths? Failing to awaken to this Dharma, we now repent it all.
By nature, I do not speak falsely; a Bodhisattva always utters truthful speech, words of reality, and timely words.

Even in dreams, I cannot bear to utter words of concealment, nor do I have the intention to do so—how much less would I intentionally commit such an offense? Failing to awaken to this Dharma, we now [repent] it all.
I repent. By nature, I do not engage in double-tongued speech. A bodhisattva harbors no mind of division toward sentient beings, nor any mind of malice or harm.
One does not repeat these words to others for the sake of breaking up their relations, nor does one repeat those words to this person for the sake of breaking up their relations with him.
This is what is said: "I shall not cause that which is unbroken to break, nor shall I increase that which has already broken. I do not delight in causing division;
I do not take pleasure in causing division. I do not engage in divisive speech, nor do I utter divisive words—whether they be true or untrue.
I have failed to realize this Dharma; I now repent for all of it."
By nature, he does not engage in harsh speech. That is to say: poisonous and harmful words; coarse and rugged words; words that cause suffering to others; words that incite hatred in others;
words spoken in their presence; words spoken in their absence; vulgar and evil words; common and base words; words unpleasant to hear; words that bring no joy to the listener;
words of anger and resentment; words that burn the heart like fire; words of enmity and bondage; words of feverish affliction; and words that are unlovely.
He completely abandons speech that is unpleasant, speech that can destroy his own body or the bodies of others, and all such forms of speech.
He always utters speech that is moistening, gentle, pleasing to the mind, delightful to hear, and brings joy to those who hear it.

I have failed to realize these teachings: speech that skillfully enters the hearts of others; speech that is elegant and refined in its principles; speech that is beloved by many; speech that brings joy to many;
and speech that causes both body and mind to leap with rapture. I now repent for all of this.

By nature, I did not engage in frivolous speech. A bodhisattva always delights in speech that is well-considered, timely, truthful, meaningful, in accordance with the Dharma, logical, skillfully subduing, and decisive after due deliberation according to the occasion. This bodhisattva, even in jest, constantly reflects and deliberates;
how much more so would they refrain from intentionally uttering distracted words? Failing to realize this Dharma, I now repent for all such acts.
I repent.
By nature I am free from greed and desire; as a bodhisattva, I have not given rise to covetous thoughts toward the wealth or resources of others, nor have I wished for or sought them.
Failing to realize this Dharma, I now repent it all.

By nature, one is free from anger and malice. A bodhisattva constantly gives rise toward all sentient beings to a mind of loving-kindness, a mind of benefit, a mind of compassion, a mind of joy, a mind of harmonious moisture, and a mind of gathering and sustaining.

Having forever abandoned hatred, resentment, enmity, harm, and the feverish affliction of distress, they always contemplate acting in accordance with these qualities, showing benevolence and providing aid. Failing to realize this Dharma, I now repent for it all.
Furthermore, having abandoned wrong views, the Bodhisattva abides in the Right Path; he does not practice divination, nor does he adopt evil precepts.

His mind and vision are upright, free from deception and flattery, and he gives rise to resolute faith in the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Sangha. Having failed to awaken to this Dharma, I now repent of it all.
O Son of the Buddha, when a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva thus maintains the ten paths of wholesome action without interruption, they further reflect:
"All sentient beings who fall into the evil destinies do so without exception because of the ten unwholesome actions.
Therefore, I shall personally cultivate right practice and also exhort others to cultivate right practice. Why is this? If [I myself]..."
It is impossible for one who cannot practice right conduct themselves to cause others to practice it; such a thing cannot exist, O Son of the Buddha.
Furthermore, this Bodhisattva Mahāsattva reflects as follows: "The ten unwholesome paths of action are the causes for rebirth in the realms of hell, animals, and hungry ghosts.
The ten wholesome paths of action are the causes for rebirth among humans and gods, up to the Peak of Existence (*bhavāgra*). Moreover, these [unwholesome paths] are of the highest grade..."
The ten paths of wholesome action, when practiced with wisdom yet with a narrow and inferior mind, out of fear of the three realms, and due to a lack of great compassion—
understanding them only through hearing the voice of another— constitute the Śrāvaka vehicle. Furthermore, these same superior ten paths of wholesome action,
when cultivated to purity but without following the instruction of another and without self-awakening, and lacking the skillful means of great compassion, [constitute the Pratyekabuddha vehicle].
Therefore, by awakening to and understanding the profound law of dependent origination, one accomplishes the Pratyekabuddha vehicle.

Furthermore, these superior ten paths of wholesome action are purified through cultivation because the mind is vast and immeasurable, because it is endowed with compassion, and because it is embraced by skillful means.
Because they give rise to great vows; because they do not abandon sentient beings; because they seek the great wisdom of all Buddhas;

because they purify and cultivate the various stages (*bhūmi*) of a bodhisattva; because they purely cultivate all the perfections (*pāramitā*); because they accomplish the vast conduct of a bodhisattva;

and because these progressively higher paths of the ten wholesome actions are pure in every respect, even unto the realization of the ten powers (*daśabala*) and the four fearlessnesses (*caturvaiśāradya*).
All Buddha-dharmas will be fully accomplished. Therefore, I shall now practice the ten wholesome paths of action equally, so as to cause all beings to be endowed with complete purity.
A bodhisattva should train in such skillful means. Son of the Buddha, this bodhisattva-mahāsattva further reflects:
"The ten unwholesome paths of action—the superior ones are the cause for rebirth in hell; the middling ones are the cause for rebirth as an animal; the inferior..."
This is the cause for rebirth as a hungry ghost (*preta*). Among these, the sin of killing can cause sentient beings to fall into the realms of hell, animals, or hungry ghosts.
If they are born among humans, they receive two kinds of retributive fruits: first, a short lifespan; second, much illness. This is the repentance for the retribution of such sins.
The sin of stealing also causes sentient beings to fall into the three evil realms. If they are born among humans, they receive two kinds of retribution:
first, poverty; second, being unable to exercise mastery over shared wealth. One must repent for this karmic retribution of sin.
The sin of sexual misconduct also causes sentient beings to fall into the three evil realms. If they are born among humans, they receive two kinds of retributive fruits:
first, their spouse is not chaste and virtuous; second, they do not obtain a retinue according to their wishes. This is the expiation for the retribution of that sin.
The sin of false speech also causes sentient beings to fall into the three evil realms. If they are born among humans, they will receive two kinds of retribution:
first, they will frequently be subjected to slander; second, they will be deceived by others. One must repent for this karmic retribution of sin.
The sin of divisive speech also causes sentient beings to fall into the three evil realms. If they are born among humans, they receive two kinds of retributive fruits:
first, their retinue will be estranged; second, their kinsmen will be wicked. One must repent for this retributive sin.
The sin of harsh speech also causes sentient beings to fall into the three evil realms. If they are born among humans, they receive two kinds of retributive fruits:
first, they constantly hear unpleasant sounds; second, their speech is full of contention and litigation. One must repent for this karmic retribution.
The transgression of frivolous speech also causes sentient beings to fall into the three evil realms. If they are born among humans, they receive two kinds of retributive fruits:
first, their words are not accepted by others; second, their speech is not clear or intelligible. One must repent for this karmic retribution.
The transgression of greed also causes sentient beings to fall into the three evil realms. If they are born among humans, they receive two kinds of retributive fruits:
first, their minds know no contentment; second, they have much desire and are never satisfied. One must repent for these karmic retributions of sin.
The sin of anger also causes sentient beings to fall into the three evil realms. If they are born among humans, they will receive two kinds of retributive fruits:
first, they are constantly sought out by others for their faults; second, they are perpetually tormented and harmed by others.
One must repent for these karmic retributions.
The sin of wrong views also causes sentient beings to fall into the three evil realms. If they are born among humans, they will receive two kinds of retribution:
first, being born into a family of wrong views; second, having a mind that is deceitful and crooked. One must repent for these karmic retributions.
O Son of the Buddha, these ten unwholesome paths of action can give rise to such immeasurable and boundless masses of great suffering.
Therefore, the bodhisattva forms this thought: "I shall distance myself from the ten unwholesome paths and take the ten wholesome paths as my Dharma garden;
I shall delight in dwelling there and abide therein myself, and I shall also exhort others to dwell therein."

Furthermore, they form this thought: "All sentient beings differentiate between self and other, mutually destroying one another; their strife, contention, and resentment burn fiercely without ceasing.
I now repent for these karmic retributions."
All sentient beings greedily grasp at things without satiety, seeking only wealth and profit, sustaining themselves through wrong livelihoods. We repent for these karmic retributions.

All sentient beings constantly follow the three poisons; because of various afflictions, they burn intensely, yet they do not understand how to resolve their will to seek the expedient means of the essential path. We repent for these karmic retributions.

All sentient beings, being shrouded by the heavy darkness of ignorance and the thick film of false views, enter the dense forest of the aggregates (*skandha*), lose the light of wisdom, and wander upon the perilous paths of the wilderness, giving rise to various evil views. [I now] repent of these karmic retributions of sin.
All sentient beings, dwelling within the perilous paths of birth and death, are on the verge of falling into the realms of hell, hungry ghosts, and animals;
they have entered the net of evil views and are bewildered by the dense forest of ignorance, following false paths and practicing perverted conduct.

It is like a blind person who has no guide; mistaking what is not the path of deliverance for the path of deliverance, they enter the realm of Māra, are seized by evil bandits, follow the mind of Māra, and distance themselves from the intent of the Buddha. This is the repentance for the retribution of such offenses.
All sentient beings are submerged by the waves of the great torrential river; they enter the flow of desire, the flow of existence, the flow of ignorance, and the flow of views.
They swirl within the eddies of birth and death, drifting and turning upon the river of craving. Rushing and surging with violent force, they have no leisure for reflection.
They are pursued and never abandoned by thoughts of desire, thoughts of malice, and thoughts of harm. Within this, the rākṣasa of the view of self seizes them and carries them away forever.
Entering the dense forest of craving and desire, they develop deep attachment toward what they covet; dwelling upon the high ground of self-conceit, they settle in the village of the six sense bases.
Having no one to provide virtuous rescue and no one capable of delivering them, they repent for their sinful retributions.
All sentient beings dwell in the prison of the world, beset by manifold sufferings and afflictions; they constantly harbor love and hatred, giving rise to anxiety and fear of their own accord.
Bound by the heavy shackles of craving and desire, and shrouded by the dense forest of ignorance, they remain within the triple realm.
They are unable to emerge from it themselves. Regarding the repentance for the retribution of their offenses:
all sentient beings are attached to a self; within the cave-dwellings of the aggregates (*skandha*), they do not seek liberation.

Relying upon the empty village of the six sense bases (*āyatana*), they give rise to the conduct of the four inversions (*viparyāsa*). They are afflicted by the poisonous snakes of the four great elements (*mahābhūta*) and beset by the enemy bandits of the five aggregates.
They are subjected to slaughter and endure immeasurable suffering. One must repent for these karmic retributions.
All sentient beings have minds that are narrow and inferior; they do not practice the path of supreme universal wisdom (*sarvajñatā*). Although they desire liberation, [they lack the means].
We merely delighted in the vehicles of the Śrāvakas and Pratyekabuddhas; we repented for our karmic retributions.
Enshrouded by ignorance, we did not recognize the ten paths of unwholesome action, nor the distinctions between the four categories.

We failed to understand their shallow or deep natures, nor could we discern the five most subtle dharmas. Only now, having encountered this place of practice, are we able to awaken to them. We take refuge in the Vipaśyin Buddha.
To Vairocana Tathāgata and the ocean-like assembly of all worthy and holy ones, I burn incense and scatter flowers.

I openly confess and repent for the ten unwholesome karmas; I dare not conceal them. By virtue of these causes and conditions, may the ten unwholesome karmas and all sinful obstructions of myself and the ocean of sentient beings within the Dharma-realm be entirely purified.
Next, the mudrā and mantra for repentance to extinguish transgressions: Oṃ sarvapāpam me kṣayaṃ kuru svāhā.
(Recite three times.)
Sins accumulated over a hundred eons are entirely swept away in a single thought; like fire consuming dry grass, they are extinguished without remainder.
All the evil karmas I have created in the past arose from beginningless greed, hatred, and delusion.
I now repent of everything produced by my body, speech, and mind.
Having repented, I take refuge with a sincere heart and pay homage to the Honored One, Vairocana Buddha.
○ (Recitation: May the assembly listen to these verses on impermanence from the Sūtra:
Constantly seeking the realm of desires, One does not practice wholesome deeds. How can one preserve the physical life When death comes to invade?
When the life-faculty and vital breath are about to end, The limbs and joints are all separated.
Amidst manifold sufferings, one dies together with them; at this time, there is nothing but sighs and regrets.
As the two eyes roll upward, the force of death follows one’s karma. The mind should be filled with alarm; unable to save one another, one approaches the abode of Yama.
According to one’s karma, retribution is received; through superior causes, one is born in the good realms.

The Ritual for Constant and Universal Prostration and Repentance Based on the Tenfold Vows and Practices of the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra: The Ocean-Seal Dharma-Avenue*, Volume Twenty-Nine: On Falling into the Evil Realms of Hell due to Malignant Karma.
The Ritual for the Constant and Universal Liturgy of the Tenfold Vows and Practices at the Sea-Seal Bodhimanda from the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha’s Great Vaipulya*,

Supplemented by the Śramaṇa Pūrui of Cāngshān Zàiguāng Temple during the Song Dynasty;
verified by the Buddhist disciple Mùzēng, Provincial Commissioner of Sichuan, who was loyal and devoted to the state during the Ming Dynasty;

The Tiantai Practice of Teaching and Contemplation for the Śramaṇa: The Correct Cessation and Stabilization, Session Thirty;
followed by the Assembly on the Ten Spiritual Friends within the Stage of the Ten Practices.
With all reverence, we pay homage to the inexhaustible Triple Gem.
All members of this assembly kneel with their right knees on the ground, solemnly holding incense and flowers to make offerings according to the Dharma.
May this ocean-like cloud of offerings pervade the worlds of the ten directions: hundreds of billions of golden nets, hundreds of billions of flower canopies, and hundreds of billions of jewels.
Canopies: hundreds of billions of garland-canopies and hundreds of billions of incense-canopies were spread and displayed above it; flower garlands hung down, and fragrances wafted everywhere.
Hundreds of billions of flower-parasols, hundreds of billions of garland-parasols, and hundreds of billions of jewel-parasols were held by the devas, arranged in rows on all four sides.
Hundreds of billions of precious robes were spread upon it, and there were hundreds of billions of multi-storied pavilions.

Resplendent and magnificent, it was covered above by hundreds of billions of mani-jewel nets, hundreds of billions of precious jewel nets, and hundreds of billions of precious necklace nets hanging down from all four sides.

There were hundreds of billions of nets of ornaments, hundreds of billions of parasol nets, and hundreds of billions of garment nets; hundreds of billions of precious canopies further overspread the top. Hundreds of billions...
A net of precious lotuses, blooming with radiant glory; a hundred trillion nets of precious incense, their fragrance exquisite and pleasing to the hearts of all;
a hundred trillion canopies of precious bells, which, when stirred slightly, produce harmonious and elegant sounds;

a hundred trillion canopies of *candana* sandalwood, their fragrance wafting everywhere; a hundred trillion canopies of precious flowers, their blossoms in full and glorious bloom; a hundred trillion...
Canopies of various exquisite colored cloths, rare in the world; canopies of a hundred trillion bodhisattvas; canopies of a hundred trillion variegated colors;
canopies of a hundred trillion pure gold; canopies of a hundred trillion lapis lazuli; and canopies of a hundred trillion diverse jewels.
All were spread above it: a hundred trillion canopies of every kind of jewel; a hundred trillion mani-jewels serving as adornments;
a hundred trillion exquisite jewel-flowers, brilliantly embellishing the perimeter; a hundred trillion *bimbara* canopies, interspersed with extraordinary beauty;
a hundred trillion fragrant garlands hanging down on all four sides; and a hundred trillion celestial, solid fragrances, whose scent—

Pervasively perfumed were a hundred trillion celestial ornaments and necklaces, a hundred trillion jewel-flower necklaces, a hundred trillion supreme-treasury jewel necklaces, a hundred trillion maṇi-jewel necklaces, and a hundred trillion ocean-maṇi jewel necklaces, which adorned the bodies of the thrones.
There were a hundred trillion exquisite jewel silks used as hanging ribbons. A hundred million...
With billions of Indra-vajra jewels, hundreds of billions of sovereign maṇi jewels,
and hundreds of billions of robes of exquisite-colored pure gold serving as interspersed ornaments— using such various articles of offering, they constantly perform worship.
Through these infinitely layered Indra-nets, the ocean-like assemblies of Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and holy sages receive these clouds of offerings, which become their radiance.
The platform is as vast as the boundless realm, immeasurable and inexhaustible; may it perform the work of a Buddha.
Having made this offering, all pay homage with reverence.
Next, the mantra for the offering of the jeweled lattice is recited.
From the ocean-like nature of precious jewels, the most excellent Seven Treasures Mountains and so forth arise;
may such clouds of offerings be presented by me to all the Buddhas and others. Oṃ sarva-tathāgata-arcana-pratimā-samantārambaṇe svāhā.
*Phraṇada-samayaṃ hūṃ*. The *Ratnakūṭa Sūtra* states:
"There is a dhāraṇī called 'The Mantra of Immeasurable Varieties,' which can accomplish all things and possesses great efficacy. The dhāraṇī says:
Oṃ simara simara mīmadā sigrāmaha liṅga hūṃ. Next is the mantra for the Seal of Bestowing Great Wisdom: Oṃ damakṣarim tathāgatāvalokite samaya.
(raṃ raṃ raṃ hūṃ) In the Sanskrit language,
I praise the Buddha:
The Buddha-body is eternally manifest, Pervading the entirety of the dharma-realm, Constantly emitting a vast and sublime sound.
Universally shaking the lands of the ten directions, In accordance with the minds of the Buddha and sentient beings,
He raises great clouds of Dharma through various gates of skillful means, Revealing and awakening them to bring them under discipline.
In all worlds, one sees the Buddha seated at the site of enlightenment, Surrounded by a great assembly, Illuminating the lands of the ten directions.
Directly praising the Tathāgata’s profound realm, whose measure is equal to empty space—
wherein all sentient beings enter yet in reality there is nothing entered— is the Tathāgata’s profound realm; such is its supreme and wondrous cause.
Even if one were to proclaim it for billions of eons, one could never exhaust it.
According to their minds and wisdom, they guide and encourage all so that they may all benefit; thus do they deliver sentient beings.
The realm of all Buddhas and all the lands in the world—all these they enter accordingly; their body of wisdom has no form.
This is not something they can perceive; it is the sovereign wisdom of all Buddhas.
Unimpeded throughout the three times, such is the realm of wisdom— Equal like space, the realm of phenomena and the realm of sentient beings Are ultimately without distinction.
Knowing this one thing, they know all; This is the domain of the Tathāgata.
All sounds that exist within all worlds, The Buddha’s wisdom comprehends them all accordingly, Without any conceptual discrimination.
They cannot be known by consciousness, Nor are they the domain of the mind;
Their nature is fundamentally pure. He reveals this to all living beings: It is neither karma nor affliction.
Without substance and without a place of dwelling, without illumination and without a sphere of action,

he practices with equanimity within the minds of all sentient beings in the world; universally present throughout the three periods of time, the Tathāgata fully and clearly realizes everything in a single thought-moment.
Homage to the Buddha Vairocana, the Original Honored One of Unobstructed Ten Bodies in the Flower Treasury Ocean of Worlds within the Great Vaipulya Buddhāvataṃsaka Sūtra.
Homage to Śākyamuni Buddha, who with great kindness and compassion made five hundred vows to rescue beings from suffering in the five turbidities.

Homage to the Buddha Bhaisajyaguru-vaidūryaprabha-rāja, King of Medicine with Lapis Lazuli Light, who possesses the twelve supreme vows and rescues from suffering amidst the five turbidities in the Full Moon World in the East.
Homage to the Buddha Amitābha, who possesses the forty-eight vows and rescues from suffering amidst the five turbidities in the Land of Ultimate Bliss in the West.

Homage to the Perfect Teaching of the Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Great Vaipulya within the Buddha-fields as numerous as the atoms in all the worlds throughout the entirety of space across the ten directions and three periods of time.
Homage to the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra, who presides over the truth of the Vows and Conduct within the Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Great Vaipulya.
Homage to the Mahāsattva Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva Mahāsattva, who presides over faith, understanding, and realized wisdom within the Great Vaipulya Buddhāvataṃsaka Sūtra.
Homage to the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, the Thousand Hands and Thousand Eyes, who possesses great kindness and great compassion, rescues from suffering in the five turbidities.

Homage to him whose great vows are profound and vast, who rescues from suffering in the five turbidities, appears in worlds where no Buddha dwells, and constantly abides to comfort the hearts of sentient beings.
Homage to the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Kṣitigarbha-Rāja in the realm of Yama;

and to the Bodhisattvas of the ten levels of faith, the ten abodes, the ten practices, the ten transferences, the ten stages, and the stage of Equal Enlightenment within all the lands as numerous as atoms throughout the entirety of space in the ten directions and three periods of time.
Homage to the assembly of all oceans of Bodhisattvas, as numerous as the atoms within the oceans of lands throughout the entire Dharma-realm;
and to the fifty-five holy ones who cultivated and realized the five sites during the final assembly of the Great Vaipulya Buddhāvataṃsaka Sūtra.

Homage to the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Sudhana, who, as a vessel of perfect capacity and superior faculties within the final assembly of the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra*, sought the Dharma through a hundred cities;
who, within a single lifetime, perfected the conduct of a bodhisattva, and who serves as a model for practice and realization for the sudden teaching of the final age.

Homage to all Buddha-activities within the Dharma-body, the physical body, the bodily forms, the śarīra-relics, the precious stūpas, and the monasteries throughout the dust-mote lands of the ten directions and three periods of time,
as far as the limits of empty space; and further, to the entire ocean-like assembly of Bodhisattvas, worthies, and sages within the Dharma-treasury and at the places where the Dharma is preached.
Homage to the Great Vow, Clad in Armor, Seeking Rebirth in the Pure Land, Protector of the True Dharma during the Final Dregs of the Summer Kingdom,
State-Protecting Dharma Master. With a sincere heart, I take refuge in and pay homage to the World-Ocean of the Flower Treasury within the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra*, the Honored One.

To Vairocana Buddha, throughout the ten directions, I take refuge; May my sins be extinguished and my pure faith increase; May I be reborn within the Flower Treasury Ocean, the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss.
The *Sūtra on the Dharma Gate of the Lamp of Liberation Followed by the Bhikṣu Sudarśana* states:
"At that time, the youth Sudhana [proceeded]... gazing up with earnest devotion, he took his leave and departed."
May I, together with all sentient beings, be reborn in the Flower Treasury Ocean within the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss.
Next is the place where the Bhikṣu Sudarśana practiced his cultivation.
Homage to all Buddhas, as numerous as the sands of thirty-eight Ganges Rivers.
Next, the bhikṣu Sudarśana paid homage to the Bodhisattva Anugatalocanapradīpa-vimokṣadharmamukha-prāpta from the southern land of Tryakṣa, who was surrounded before and behind by immeasurable devas,
nāgas, and the eight classes of divine beings. The bhikṣu Sudarśana [prostrated].
All in the ten directions take refuge; Sins are extinguished and pure faith increases. May they be born within the Flower Treasury Ocean, in the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss.
The Second Sovereign Lord, the Artisan Deity Wisdom-Light, Liberation Dharma Gate.
The Sūtra says: "At that time, the youth Sudhana (until) respectfully gazed up at him, took his leave, and departed.
May I, together with all sentient beings, be reborn in the Flower Treasury Ocean, within the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss.
Homage to the Light of All Artistic Skills and Great Supernatural Powers Obtained on the Riverbank in the Southern Country of Renown.
Ten thousand youths of the gates of liberation all surround the youth Īśvarapati;
throughout the ten directions they take refuge, extinguishing their sins and increasing their pure faith. May they be born in the ocean of the Flower Treasury and the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss.
The *Sūtra on the Dharma Gate of Liberation of the Upāsikā Triratnadattā’s Inexhaustible Treasury of Merit* states:
"At that time, the youth Sudhana [arrived]... and gazing upon her without weariness, he took his leave and departed."
May I, together with all sentient beings, be reborn in the Flower Treasury Ocean, in the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss—

namo to the Upāsikā who dwells in the City Abiding on the Southern Sea, who is surrounded by ten thousand young maidens, and who has fully perfected the liberation gate of the Bodhisattva’s Inexhaustible Treasury of Merit.
All in the ten directions take refuge; Sins are extinguished and pure faith increases. May they be born within the Flower Treasury Ocean, In the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss.
The Fourth: The Dharma Gate of the Liberation of the Treasury of Merit Spontaneously Arising According to One’s Wishes, by the Layman of Clear Wisdom.
The Sūtra says: "At that time, the youth Sudhana (up to) reverently gazed upon him and took his leave to depart.
May I, together with all sentient beings, be reborn in the Flower Treasury Ocean within the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss.
Homage to the Southern City of Great Prosperity, where one attains the liberation door of the treasury of merit that arises according to one’s wishes. 10.
Surrounded before and behind by a thousand retinues, the wise householder is taken refuge in by all the ten directions;
may his sins be extinguished, his pure faith increased, and may he be reborn within the Flower Treasury Ocean in the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss.
The *Sūtra on the Dharma Gate of Liberation through the Treasure-Treasury of Immeasurable Merit of the Fifth, Elder Ratnaśikhin*, states:
At that time, the youth Sudhana (until) reverently gazed upon him and took his leave.
May I, together with all sentient beings, be reborn in the Flower Treasury Ocean within the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss.
Next, at the place where the Elder Ratashikhi attained the Dharma:
Homage to the Buddha King of Universal Adornment of the Boundless Radiance of the Dharma Realm in the World Perfectly Adorned.
Next, the Elder Ratnaśikhin,
who had attained the liberation door of the "Inexhaustible Jewel-Treasury of Bodhisattva Merit" within the city of Siṃhacakra in the southern direction, paid homage.
Homage to the assembly of all ocean-like multitudes of Bodhisattvas of the fifth stage who proclaim all dharmas atop the fifth tier of the Eight-Faceted Jewel Canopy of Precious Crest;
homage to those who manifest within the Samantavyūha-maṇḍala atop the sixth tier of the Eight-Faceted Jewel Canopy of Precious Crest.
Homage to the ocean-like assembly of all Bodhisattvas who manifest Prajñā;
homage to the ocean-like assembly of all Bodhisattvas on the seventh tier above the eight-faceted precious canopy of Ratnaśikhin, who have attained the patience like an echo.
Homage to the infinite ocean-like assembly of Bodhisattvas who have attained the stage of non-retrogression through the eighth tier above the Eight-Sided Jewel Canopy of Precious Topknots.
Homage to all the Bodhisattvas in their final birth (ekajātipratibaddha) on the ninth tier above the Eight-Sided Jewel Canopy of Precious Topknots.

The Ocean Assembly pays homage to the Tathāgatas of All Buddhas who purify Buddha-lands and turn the wheel of the true Dharma from atop the tenth tier of the eight-faceted precious canopy of the Jewel-Crested One.
All in the ten directions take refuge; Sins are extinguished and pure faith increases. May they be born within the Flower Treasury Ocean in the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss.
[This is] the sixth [chapter], "The Universal Eye Householder Causes All Sentient Beings Universally to See All Buddhas with Joyful Understanding."
The *Dharmamukha-vimokṣa Sūtra* states: "At that time, the youth Sudhana (until) gazed upon him with earnest devotion, took his leave, and departed.
May I, together with all sentient beings, be reborn in the Flower Treasury Ocean within the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss."

Homage to the Elder Universal Eye of the Southern Land of Vīraṇa, in the City of Samantamukha, who has attained the liberation door of causing all sentient beings to universally behold all Buddhas with joy;
to him throughout the ten directions we pay full prostration. May our sins be extinguished, may our pure faith increase, and may we be born in the Flower Treasury Ocean.
In the *Sūtra on the Dharma Gate of the Illusion-like Liberation of King Anantaprabha, the Seventh [Patriarch] in the Pure Land of Sukhāvatī*,
it is said: "At that time, the youth Sudhana (having arrived) circumambulated him countless times and then took his leave and departed."
May I, together with all sentient beings, be reborn in the Flower Treasury Ocean within the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss;
specifically, may we go to the Southern City of the Many-Treasured Banner, where we shall take refuge in King Anantamati,
who is surrounded before and behind by ten billion maidens who have attained the gate of illusory liberation, ten thousand ministers, and one hundred thousand fierce warriors.
Homage to Sudhana Kumārabhūta, who visited King Anala and manifested various evil forms to arouse doubt within him;
may the devas and humans of the ten directions all take refuge, extinguish their sins, increase their pure faith, and vow to be born in the Flower Treasury Ocean.
The Dharma Gate of the Samādhi of Liberation Entitled "The Great King of the Eighth Radiance, Chiefly Compassionate, Accordant with the World," within the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss.
The Sūtra says: "At that time, the youth Sudhana... [he] gazed up at him with earnest devotion and took his leave to depart.
May I, together with all sentient beings, be reborn in the Flower Treasury Ocean within the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss.
Next is the Buddha of the Abode of King Great Radiance.
Homage to the Buddhas of immeasurable hundreds of thousands of billions of eons as previously asked,
headed by King Mahāprabha;
homage to those who have attained the bodhisattvas in the city of Sudarśana in the southern quarter, whose great compassion is foremost and who are able to accord with the world.
To the Great Radiant King of the Samādhi Dharma-gate of the Intervals,
throughout the ten directions, I take refuge; may my transgressions be extinguished and my pure faith increase, and may I be born within the Flower Treasury Ocean in the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss.
The *Ninth: The Liberation Dharma-Gate of the Invincible Wisdom-Treasury of the Immovable Upāsikā* states:
At that time, the youth Sudhana [proceeded] until he gazed upon her with earnest devotion and took his leave to depart.
May I, together with all sentient beings, be reborn in the Flower Treasury Ocean within the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss.
Next, at the place where the Upāsikā Acalā resolved her mind:
Homage to the Buddha Dīrghabāhu of the Vimala Kalpa, and to the entire ocean-like assembly at his site of enlightenment.
Next, the laywoman Acalā pays homage to the Bodhisattvas within the Southern Palace of King Anuruddha, such as Durjayamati-garbha and others who have attained the gates of liberation;
she pays homage to the laywoman Acalā.

Homage to the Bodhisattva Palace-Deity, the Self-Acting Karma-Witnessing Spirit, who provides excellent conditions for the youth Sudhana in mid-air, constantly following him and exhorting him to remain ever vigilant.
Homage to the Spirit Who Gathers Beings in as many worlds as there are atoms in unspeakably many Buddha-fields, and so forth.

May all the messengers from the ten directions take refuge; may their sins be extinguished and their pure faith increase, and may they vow to be born within the Flower Treasury Ocean in the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss.
The tenth [chapter], the *Sarvatraga-tīrthika-samantāvalokana-loka-vimukti-dharmaparyāya-sūtra*, says:
"At that time, the youth Sudhana (having arrived) gazed upon him with earnest devotion, took his leave, and departed."
May I, together with all sentient beings, be reborn in the Flower Treasury Ocean within the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss.
Homage to the Bodhisattva Anzhuzi (Anvaya) dwelling in the city of Aparimitāyus in the south, who has attained the liberation gate of universally observing the world;
surrounded by ten thousand Brahmās and followed by the Bahulaka heretics.
Homage to the Bodhisattva Sudhana, who for those of superior faculties sought the Dharma through a hundred cities; who, within a single lifetime, perfected the practices of a Bodhisattva;
who serves as the model for cultivation and realization for the sudden gate of the final age;
and to whom all throughout the ten directions pay homage. May my transgressions be extinguished and my pure faith increase; May I be reborn in the Sea of Flower Treasury.
In the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss, I next repent for the destruction of the Buddha-dharma;
I only pray that the infinite Jewels of the Buddha, Dharma, and Sangha, like a celestial net, shall remain unending. To Vairocana Tathāgata, Samantabhadra, and Mañjuśrī.

The assembly of noble ones gathered like the ocean, and the world-transcending and worldly deities, by virtue of your compassionate original vows, radiate great light that illuminates this Dharma assembly.
May you bear witness, protect, and mind us; may you compassionately accept and sustain us.
We—bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, śikṣamāṇās, śrāmaṇeras, and śrāmaṇerīs—having cultivated slight merit in the past, have now obtained human bodies during the final dharma age of Śākyamuni Tathāgata.
In the interim, I left the household life to study the Way, yet I was unable to cause the Sun of the Buddha to shine brightly, nor did I benefit myself or others.
I never practiced meditative concentration or wisdom, yet I received offerings from the faithful in vain. Possessing neither precepts nor virtue, I was arrogant and conceited;
I frequently violated and transgressed the rules of liberation and the Vinaya. I now openly confess and repent of such sinful karmas.
The *Sūtra of the Lotus Face* states: The Buddha told Ānanda, "I shall now speak of a time in the future when there will be certain bhikṣus who violate the precepts.
Though they wear the saṃghāṭī robe, they will wander through cities and towns and travel between villages, dwelling in the homes of their relatives.
They are neither bhikṣus nor laymen; they keep wives and concubines and give birth to sons and daughters. Furthermore, there will be bhikṣus who dwell..."
There was a house of courtesans. Furthermore, there were bhikṣus who violated bhikṣuṇīs. There were bhikṣus who hoarded gold and silver and engaged in worldly business to sustain their lives.
There were bhikṣus who served as messengers for postal relays to sustain their lives.
There were bhikṣus who specialized in the practice of medicine to sustain their lives. There were bhikṣus who played go and the game of six-sided dice...
Furthermore, there are bhikṣus who sustain their lives by performing divination for others.
Furthermore, there are bhikṣus who sustain their lives by casting spells to raise the dead in order to have them kill enemies.

Furthermore, there are bhikṣus who sustain their lives by reciting mantras to exorcise ghosts and spirits for others, taking many goods in exchange. Furthermore, there are bhikṣus who are exclusively...

They commit acts of killing to sustain their own lives. Furthermore, there are bhikṣus who reside in monasteries and privately misappropriate the property of the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Saṅgha to sustain their own lives.
Furthermore, there are bhikṣus who, while inwardly actually violating the precepts, outwardly pretend to uphold them and receive the faithful offerings of others.
Furthermore, there are bhikṣus who, though they do not break the precepts, harbor stinginess regarding clothing, food, drink, and so forth.
There are those who, out of stinginess, do not give property belonging to the Sangha to visiting monks.
Furthermore, there are bhikṣus who, though they have not broken the precepts, are miserly regarding the dwellings, beds, and seats of the Sangha and do not give them to visiting monks.

Moreover, there are bhikṣus who, though they have not broken the precepts, receive great wealth and profit from the offerings and prostrations of various donors, yet their hearts do not wish for other bhikṣus to receive such things.

There are those who accept the faithful offerings of others solely for their own enjoyment. Furthermore, there are bhikṣus who, though they are not actually arhats, constantly falsely claim to have attained the fruit of arhatship, desiring to make others know that they are arhats. Moreover, there are bhikṣus who receive many of the four types of offerings from donors;
yet within they possess no true virtue, but only increase their greed, acting merely to sustain their lives and not for the sake of cultivating the Path. Furthermore...
There was a bhikṣu who supported himself by engaging in trade for profit. There was another bhikṣu who supported himself exclusively by practicing theft.
There was another bhikṣu who supported himself by keeping elephants, horses, camels, donkeys, cattle, and sheep, even to the point of buying and selling them.
There was another bhikṣu who supported himself by trafficking in slaves. There was another bhikṣu who [supported himself] as a butcher...

There were bhikṣus who slaughtered oxen and sheep to sustain themselves. There were also bhikṣus who accepted enlistment to enter battle and wage war, killing many people in their pursuit of military honors and rewards.
Furthermore, there were bhikṣus who breached walls and broke through enclosures to steal the property of others for their livelihood.
Still other bhikṣus specialized in robbery and plunder, attacking and destroying cities, towns, and villages.
Furthermore, there were bhikṣus who destroyed Buddhist stūpas and took their precious treasures to sustain their own lives.
Due to such immeasurable causes and conditions for rebirth in hell, after they passed away, they all fell into the hells. We now repent of them all.
Ānanda, it is like a lion whose life has ended and whose body has died—whether in the air, on the earth, in the water, or on land—no sentient beings dare to eat the flesh of that lion’s body.
Only various worms born from the lion’s own body will consume the lion’s flesh.
Ānanda, my Buddha-dharma cannot be destroyed by others; it is within my own dharma...
These wicked bhikṣus are like poisonous thorns; they destroy the Buddha-dharma accumulated through my three asaṃkhyeya kalpas of diligent and arduous practice.

Ānanda, it is as if a person were to enter the great ocean, reach a treasure island, take many precious objects, place them upon a ship, and then sink in the midst of crossing the great ocean. The True Dharma of the Buddha is like those treasures.
A Ship. In the future, there will be many evil bhikṣus who violate the precepts and take great pleasure in committing various kinds of evil deeds.
They shall destroy my Buddha-dharma, causing it to sink and disappear. Ānanda, not long after the Tathāgata’s parinirvāṇa, the True Dharma shall fall into disorder.
Once the True Dharma has fallen into disorder, there will again appear in the world various kinds of evil bhikṣus who do not believe that the Tathāgata has attained [enlightenment].
Having realized the untainted, tranquil nirvana, how much more so would they believe that there are other people in the world who have attained arhatship and entered nirvana?
Ānanda, all the True Dharma of the Tathāgata consists of names, phrases, sentences, and meanings, namely the sūtras.
The twelve divisions of the scriptures— *geya*, *vyākaraṇa*, *gāthā*, *udāna*,
*nidāna*, *avadāna*, *itivṛttaka*, *jātaka*, *vaipulya*, *adbhutadharma*, and *upadeśa*—
will be destroyed by wicked bhikṣus. Those people will delight in composing literary works and ornate rhetoric.
They adorn their speech with flowery words; there will be many such evil bhikṣus who destroy my Buddha-dharma.
At that time, Ānanda addressed the Buddha, saying: "World-Honored One, in the future, will such evil bhikṣus who break the precepts come into existence?"

The Buddha said: "So it is, so it is. There will appear in the world certain evil bhikṣus who, though they don the Dharma robes and shave their hair and beards, will destroy my Buddha-dharma; now, all such as these must repent."
The *Buddhapiṭaka Sūtra* states: "Śāriputra, I now tell you: suppose there is a person who in a single day kills hundreds of thousands of millions of sentient beings;
who in a single day steals hundreds of thousands of millions of kinds of gold, silver, and precious objects; who practices sexual misconduct day and night without ceasing;
who constantly deceives others with false speech, such that his verbal karma is impure and he has not a single word of truth; and who engages in divisive speech..."
They constantly disrupt harmony and assist those who do so. Those of harsh speech always speak with malice and opposition, never uttering even a single word of gentleness.
Those of frivolous speech have no foundation; when people hear such matters, they further confound them with immeasurable other words.
Those who are covetous and envious harbor thoughts of non-belonging toward the property of others. Those who are wrathful act perversely without any cause or condition.
They give rise to anger and harbor resentment that fills their hearts. As for those with wrong views, they delight in practicing unwholesome paths. Śāriputra, what do you think?

If a person were to commit these ten unwholesome offenses for a hundred years, would the transgression of a precept-breaking bhikṣu who accepts offerings from others for a single day and night be greater than that? Now, all such [transgressions] are repented.
Furthermore, the *Bhaiṣajyaguru Sūtra* states: "To transgress what has been learned regarding the three refuges; or to violate the five precepts, the eight precepts, or the ten precepts;
the four hundred precepts of a bodhisattva—the ten grave and forty-eight light offenses; the four root and forty-six minor infractions;
the two hundred and fifty precepts of a bhikṣu; the five hundred precepts of a bhikṣuṇī; the three thousand rules of decorum; or the eighty thousand [precepts]."
Subtle conduct, Mañjuśrī: there are sentient beings who, although they have received the various precepts from the Tathāgata, violate their ethical discipline (*śīla*);

some, while not violating their ethical discipline, violate the rules of conduct (*ācāra*); some, while remaining unimpaired in both ethical discipline and rules of conduct, destroy right view (*samyagdṛṣṭi*);
and some, while not destroying right view, abandon extensive learning (*bahuśruta*) regarding what has been taught by the Buddha.
They cannot comprehend the profound meaning of the sūtras. Though they may possess great learning, they harbor overweening pride (*adhimāna*).
Because their minds are shrouded by this overweening pride, they affirm themselves and disparage others, slandering the true Dharma and becoming partisans of Māra. Such are these foolish people.
I have personally practiced wrong views and further caused immeasurable koṭis of sentient beings to fall into great perilous pits.
These sentient beings would otherwise have wandered endlessly through the realms of hell, animals, and hungry ghosts; now I repent for all of this.

Furthermore, the *Dharmasamāpti-sūtra* states: When the Tathāgata was about to enter parinirvāṇa after three months had passed, he was visited by an immeasurable multitude of bhikṣus and bodhisattvas who came to where the Buddha was.
Prostrating themselves upon the ground, they were surrounded by their retinue, thirsting for and yearning to hear the Dharma.
Yet the World-Honored One remained in silent tranquility, saying nothing, and his radiance did not manifest. The Venerable Ānanda then paid homage.
He addressed the Buddha, saying, "World-Honored One, in the past and present, when you preached the Dharma, your majestic radiance was uniquely manifest.
Now, in this great assembly, that light no longer appears. What is the reason for this? There must be a cause; we pray to hear its meaning. The Buddha remained silent and did not respond.
This was repeated three times. Then the Buddha told Ānanda, "After my parinirvāṇa, when the Dharma is about to perish, in an age of the five rebellious evils, the path of Māra will flourish."
At that time, Māra shall take the form of a śramaṇa to corrupt and disrupt my Way.

Clad in worldly garments, he will delight in the five-colored robes of the *kāṣāya*, drinking wine, eating meat, killing living beings, and craving flavors; he will lack a heart of compassion and instead harbor mutual hatred and jealousy.

Meanwhile, there will be bodhisattvas, pratyekabuddhas, and arhats who cultivate virtue through diligent effort; they will be honored and served by all, held in high esteem by the people, and will bring peace through their teaching and transformation.

...and so forth. Compassionate toward the poor and mindful of the elderly, they rescue and nurture those in distress. They constantly provide people with scriptures and images to honor and serve, performing various meritorious deeds.
Their disposition is inclined toward goodness; they do not harm others. Sacrificing their own bodies to save sentient beings, they do not begrudge themselves.
Patient, humble, and harmonious—should there be such a person, even the bhikṣus who are Māras will all together envy them, slandering and spreading evil reports, and banishing or expelling them.

They were driven away so that they could not remain. Thereafter, they themselves did not cultivate the Way or its virtue. The temples fell into ruin and desolation, no longer being repaired; they gradually went to destruction.
They merely coveted wealth and goods, accumulating them without dispersing them, and failed to perform meritorious deeds.
They trafficked in slaves, plowed fields and planted crops, burned down mountain forests, and harmed sentient beings without a heart of compassion. Slaves became their peers.
"Kūṭadanta, there are female slaves who become bhikṣuṇīs; they possess no virtue or morality, being lustful, depraved, and confused, making no distinction between men and women.
They cause the Way to become thin and insipid, all because of such as these. Or there are those who, seeking to escape the local authorities, rely upon my Way to become śramaṇas;
yet they do not cultivate the precepts and rules. Though they recite the precepts at the end of each half-month, they are weary, indolent, and unwilling to listen, merely abbreviating them."

From beginning to end, they are unwilling to speak fully. They do not recite or study the sutras; even if there are those who read them, they do not understand the characters or phrases, yet they insist on speaking as if they do.
They do not consult with the wise, but are arrogant and seek fame. They feign elegant deportment to create a hollow reputation for glory, hoping for offerings from others.
These bhikṣus of the Māras, after their lives end, shall have their spirits fall into the Avīci Hell, [the retribution for] the five heinous crimes.

Among the various states of suffering, there is none they have not experienced—whether as hungry ghosts or animals—for kalpas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges. Only when their retribution is exhausted do they emerge;

yet they are born in borderlands where the Three Jewels do not exist. At a time when the Dharma is about to perish, women will be diligent and constantly perform meritorious deeds, while men will be indolent and arrogant, disregarding the words of the Dharma.
Even when seeing śramaṇas with their own eyes, they will regard them as mere dung and soil, lacking any faith in the Dharma that is about to vanish.

They shall be utterly destroyed. At that time, the various devas will weep; floods and droughts will be不调 (irregular), the five grains will not ripen, pestilence will spread, and those who die will be many.
The people will suffer hardship, and officials will inflict punishments unrighteously.
All will long for chaos, and evil people will become as numerous as the sands of the ocean, while those who are good will be extremely few—perhaps only one or two. The kalpa is about to end.
At the end of all things, the sun and moon grow ever more fleeting, and the human lifespan grows ever shorter.

When men reach forty and their hair turns white, they may succumb to debauchery and lose their lives through the exhaustion of their vital essence (*śukra*). Some live to sixty; for men, life is short, while for women it is longer.
Reaching seventy, eighty, or even a hundred years, a great flood may suddenly arise without warning. Yet people do not believe this, and thus they regard themselves as beings subject to permanence.
A diverse multitude, without distinction of noble or base, were submerged, adrift, or devoured by fish and turtles.

At that time, there were Bodhisattvas, Pratyekabuddhas, and Arhats whom the various Māras drove away, preventing them from joining the assembly. These followers of the Three Vehicles entered the mountainous lands of merit, maintaining themselves in tranquil seclusion with joyful contentment.
Their lifespans were prolonged, and they were protected by various kings. When Candraprabha appeared in the world, they attained the marks [of a Buddha].
Having encountered [this time], we shall together promote my Way. At fifty-two years of age, the *Śūraṅgama-sūtra* and the *Pratyutpanna-samādhi-sūtra* will first pass into extinction;

twelve years later, the twelve divisions of the scriptures (*dvādaśāṅga-pravacana*) will follow into extinction. After the Holy King has departed, the saffron robes of the śramaṇas will naturally turn white.
When my Dharma is about to perish, it will be like an oil lamp on the verge of going out, whose light becomes even more intense. This is the True Dharma.
At the time of cessation, it is also like the extinguishing of a lamp; from this point forward, it would be difficult to describe in detail. We now repent all of this.

Enshrouded by ignorance, we have transgressed the laws and precepts, failing to recognize the causes of our offenses. Now that we have encountered this site of practice (*bodhimaṇḍa*), we are finally able to awaken.
We take refuge in the Tathāgata Vairocana and the ocean-like assembly of all worthy sages. [I] burn incense.
I scatter flowers. Having transgressed the laws and precepts, I now openly confess and repent, not daring to conceal anything.
By these causes and conditions, may all heavy offenses committed by myself and the ocean of sentient beings within the Dharma-realm that violate the laws and precepts be entirely purified.
Next is the mudrā and mantra for repentance to extinguish transgressions: Oṃ sṛ māpa bha me si pu danna ha danna mi tra ya svāhā.
(Recite three times.)
Sins accumulated over a hundred kalpas are completely swept away in a single thought; like fire consuming dry grass, they are extinguished without remainder.
All the evil karmas I have created in the past arose entirely from beginningless greed, anger, and ignorance.
Whatever has arisen from my body, speech, and mind—all this I now confess.
Having confessed, I take refuge with a sincere heart and pay homage to the Honored One, Vairocana Buddha.
○ (Proclamation: May the assembly listen to these verses on impermanence from the Sūtra:
Constantly seeking the realm of desires, One does not practice wholesome deeds. How can one preserve the physical life Without realizing that death is encroaching?
When the life-faculty and vital breath are about to end, The limbs and joints shall all be severed.
Amidst manifold sufferings and death, these people do nothing but lament and resent.

They lament the affairs of their lives, failing to understand that they should have practiced the True Dharma early on. They indulge only in fame and profit, extensively committing all manner of evil deeds.
What is wrought by karma is more skilled than a master painter; the artisan of karma is exceedingly clever.
It can produce various forms and various colors; though they appear and may be perceived, the mind’s karma spreads out these myriad shapes in numbers beyond calculation.
Only at the moment of death does one begin to regret what has passed, yet it cannot be pursued again. Therefore, I exhort all my followers: on the final journey, you must change your course.
