The thirty-first session follows with the assembly of the ten spiritual friends within the stage of the ten dedications,
wherein one pays all-respectful homage to the inexhaustible Triple Gem.
All these people knelt with their right knees on the ground and, holding incense and flowers, made offerings according to the Dharma, making this vow:
"May these clouds of incense and flowers fill the worlds of the ten directions. May a hundred trillion walls of various jewels surround them on all sides.
May all the jewel trees stand in rows as a magnificent adornment. May all the jewel-flower trees rain down myriad exquisite blossoms, scattering them across the ground. All...
The precious incense trees emit a swirling fragrance that universally perfumes the ten directions. All the precious flower-garland trees rain down great garlands, which hang down everywhere.
All the precious kingly *maṇi* jewel trees rain down great *maṇi* jewels, which are distributed and fill all places.
All the jewel-clothing trees rain down garments of various colors, spreading them everywhere according to what is appropriate.
All the musical-instrument trees produce sounds when stirred by the wind; these sounds are exquisite and surpass even celestial music.
All the ornamentation trees each rain down rare and wonderful treasures, distributed throughout every place. There are millions of pavilions made of Jāmbūnada gold.
Gold covers its upper surface, adorned with the interlacing patterns of a million palaces made of Vairocana-maṇi jewels.
Within these palaces, there are further immeasurable jewel lotus thrones arranged in rows all around.
With such various articles of offering, they constantly perform worship. Like the layered Indra-nets, the oceans of Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and the assembly of worthies and sages [are present].
Receiving these clouds of offerings, they form a terrace of light, vast as boundless realms, immeasurable and inexhaustible;
may they perform the work of Buddhas.
Having made these offerings, all pay homage with reverence.
Next, I offer clouds of supreme offerings such as these:
vast oceans of the nature of jewels and precious gems, and most excellent mountains of the seven treasures;
I present them to all the Buddhas and their assemblies.
Oṃ sarvamaṇidhāraṇī-prabhāsvara-samantarakṣita-samayā hūṃ. The *Ratnakūṭa Sūtra* states:
"There is a dhāraṇī named 'The Incantation of Immeasurable Varieties,' which can accomplish all things and possesses great power."
It can. The dhāraṇī is: Oṃ sīmala sīmala mīmada sigrāmaha liṅga hūṃ.
Next, perform the mantra of the Amoghamani mudrā.
Oṃ amoghapāśa mahāvidyārāja tathāgatamaitrīkaraṇa sarvasattvān rakṣa rakṣa hūṃ.
(Praise of the Buddha in Sanskrit)
The Buddha’s body is inconceivable; all lands are contained within it.
In every such place, he guides the world and proclaims the true Dharma. From his perfect voice, the Buddha elucidates the nature of reality;
according to the differences in beings' understandings, he manifests inexhaustible gateways to the Dharma throughout all buddha-fields.
Seeing the Buddha seated at the site of enlightenment, the Buddha’s body appears like a reflected image; arising and ceasing cannot be apprehended.
Directly praising the Buddhas of the three periods of time, the Śrāvakas and great disciples are all unable to know the Buddha.
Regarding the matter of lifting and lowering the feet throughout the past, future, and present ages—
this even all the Pratyekabuddhas do not know of the Tathāgata’s lifting and lowering of his feet; how much less could ordinary people,
bound by the fetters of afflictions and with their consciousnesses shrouded by ignorance, ever know the Guide?
The Perfectly Awakened One’s unimpeded wisdom transcends the path of language; its measure is unfathomable, and who is able to know or see it?
Just as the light of the bright moon makes it impossible to fathom its limits, so too are the Buddha’s supernormal powers;
one cannot perceive their end or limit. Such is each and every skillful means.
The manifestations produced in every thought-moment, continuing until the end of immeasurable eons—
To contemplate the omniscience that cannot be fully grasped through thought, And the inconceivable Dharma,
wherein the limits of each and every gateway of skillful means cannot be found; If there be one who, regarding this Dharma, Arouses a vast and great vow.
For such a person, knowledge and vision regarding this realm are not difficult to attain.
By valiantly and diligently practicing mindfulness and contemplating the ocean-like Dharma, their mind becomes free from obstacles.
Having entered this gateway of skillful means with a disciplined mind and vast aspirations, they shall surely attain Great Enlightenment.
Homage to the Buddha Vairocana,
the Original Honored One of Unobstructed Ten Bodies in the Flower Treasury World-Ocean within the Great Vaipulya Buddha Avataṃsaka Sūtra, the Supreme Realm.
Homage to Śākyamuni Buddha, the Greatly Compassionate One who made five hundred vows to save sentient beings from suffering in the five turbidities.

Homage to Bhaisajyaguru Vaidūryaprabha-rāja Buddha, the King of Lapis Lazuli Light, who made twelve supreme vows to save sentient beings from suffering in the five turbidities in the Pūrṇacandra World of the East.
Homage to Amitābha Buddha of the Western World of Ultimate Bliss, who, through his forty-eight vows, rescues those suffering amidst the five turbidities.

Homage to the ocean of the perfect teaching of the Mahāvaipulya Buddhāvataṃsaka Sūtra within all the lands as numerous as motes of dust throughout the space of the ten directions and the three periods of time.
Homage to the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Samantabhadra, who presides over the truth of vows and conduct within the Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Great Vaipulya;
homage to Mañjuśrī, who presides over the wisdom of faith, understanding, and realization within the Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Great Vaipulya.

Homage to the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva of Great Kindness and Great Compassion, the Thousand-Handed and Thousand-Eyed Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva, who rescues from suffering amidst the five turbidities.

Homage to the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Kṣitigarbha-Rāja, whose great vows are vast and profound; who rescues sentient beings from suffering in the five turbidities and appears in worlds devoid of Buddhas;
who comforts the hearts of people and dwells eternally within the realm of Yama.
Homage to the ten [stages of] faith Bodhisattvas throughout the ten directions and three periods of time, within all lands as numerous as atoms filling the entirety of space.
Homage to the Bodhisattvas dwelling in the ten practices, the ten dedications, and the ten stages; to the Bodhisattva of Equal Enlightenment;

and to the ocean-like assembly of all Bodhisattvas as numerous as the atoms within the oceans of lands throughout the entire Dharma-realm—namo to the fifty-five sections on the Places of Cultivation and Realization from the final assembly of the Great Vaipulya Buddha Avataṃsaka Sūtra.
The Noble Sudhana,
a vessel of perfect capacity and superior faculties from the final assembly of the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra*,

who sought the Dharma through a hundred cities and perfected the Bodhisattva practices within a single lifetime, serves as the model for cultivation and realization for those of the sudden teaching in the Final Age.
Homage to the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas,

and to all Buddha-activities— whether in the form of the Dharma-body, the form-body, physical relics, jeweled stupas, or monasteries— within all the lands as numerous as the atoms of the entirety of space throughout the ten directions and the three periods of time;
as well as to the treasuries of the Dharma and the places where the Dharma is preached.
Homage to the assembly of all noble and saintly Bodhisattvas, the ocean-like multitude;

to those who have donned the armor of great vows to seek birth in the Pure Land; to those who protect the True Dharma during the final dregs of the summer-like age; to the Dharma-teachers who protect the nation.
With a sincere heart, I take refuge and pay homage to the World-Honored One Vairocana, the Honored One of the Flower Treasury Ocean World-System in the Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Great Vaipulya.
To all those throughout the ten directions who take refuge, may their sins be extinguished, their pure faith increase, and may they be born in the Flower Treasury Ocean.
In the *Sūtra on the Dharma-Gate of the Liberation of Knowing All Fragrances of the Foremost Incense-Seller in the Land of Ultimate Bliss*,
it is said: "At that time, the youth Sudhana (until) gazed upon him with earnest devotion and took his leave."
May I, together with all sentient beings, be reborn in the Ocean of Flower Treasury and the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss.
In the Southern Land of Vast Extent, I take refuge in the Elder Dhūpa-upāli,
who has attained the liberation door of skillfully discerning all fragrances and mastering the methods for blending incense.
All in the ten directions take refuge; Sins are extinguished and pure faith increases. May they be born in the Flower Treasury Ocean and the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss.
The Second: The Dharma Gate of Liberation through the Practice and Understanding of the Great Compassion Banner, the Shipmaster Vasira.
The Sūtra says: "At that time, the youth Sudhana (until) his heart was never weary of seeking, he took his leave and departed.

May I, together with all sentient beings, be reborn in the Flower Treasury Ocean within the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss, and take refuge in the Bodhisattva Bhaisajyarāja, who attained the liberation door of the Practice of the Great Compassion Banner within the Great City of the Southern Pavilion.
O Master of the Ship,

throughout the ten directions we take refuge; may our transgressions be extinguished and our pure faith increase, and may we be born within the Flower Treasury Ocean in the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss.
The *Sūtra on the Dharma-Gate of the Third Unsurpassed and Supreme Householder Reaching All Places* states:
"At that time, the youth Sudhana (having arrived... gazed upon him with earnest reverence, took his leave, and departed."
May I, together with all sentient beings, be reborn in the Flower Treasury Ocean within the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss;
in the City of Delight in the South, may I reach all places and attain the liberation door of practicing the bodhisattva path—
the Unsurpassed Victorious Elder.

The Fourth: The Liberation Method for the Bhikṣuṇī Siṃhavijṛmbhitā Entitled "All Take Refuge Throughout the Ten Directions, Eradicating Sins and Increasing Pure Faith, Vowing to Be Born within the Flower Treasury Ocean and the Land of Ultimate Bliss, and Accomplishing All-Knowledge. Throughout the ten directions, all take refuge; Sins are extinguished and pure faith increases.
May they vow to be born within the Flower Treasury Ocean and the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss, And accomplish the liberation method of all-knowledge.
The Sūtra says: At that time, the youth Sudhana (until) reverently gazed up at him and took his leave to depart.
May I, together with all sentient beings, be reborn in the Flower Treasury Ocean within the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss.
Namo to the Southern Country of Śūrpāraka, in the city of Kalingavana, where he attained the Gate of Liberation of All-Knowledge.
The Bhikṣuṇī Siṃhahanu, to whom all ten directions pay homage,
has extinguished their sins and increased their pure faith; may they be reborn within the Lotus Treasury Ocean in the Pure Land of Sukhāvatī.
The *Pañcama-Vasu-mitrā-strī-virāga-koṭi-vimukti-dharmaparyāya-sūtra* states:
At that time, the youth Sudhana [arrived] and, gazing up at her with earnest devotion, took his leave and departed.
May I, together with all sentient beings, be reborn in the Flower Treasury Ocean within the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss.
Next, at the place where the woman Vasumitrā first resolved her mind,
I take refuge in the Tathāgata Uccagāmin of the City of the King of Sublime Gates in a past age.
Next, the woman Vasumitrā,
from the southern direction, in the city of Ratnavyūha in the land of Atidurgama, attained the liberation door of reaching the limit of freedom from desire. The woman Vasumitrā.
All in the ten directions take refuge; Sins are extinguished and pure faith increases. May they be born within the Flower Treasury Ocean in the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss.
The Sixth: The Dharma Gate of the Liberation of the Layman Vaiśravaṇa Reaching the Limit of Non-Parinirvāṇa.
The Sūtra says: "At that time, the youth Sudhana (up to) reverently gazed upon him, took his leave, and departed.
May I, together with all sentient beings, be reborn in the Ocean of Flower Treasury within the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss.
Next, the Buddha seen by the householder Viśvāmitra while in meditative concentration:
Homage to Kāśyapa Buddha. Homage to Kanakamuni Buddha.
Homage to Krakucchanda Buddha. Homage to Śikhin Buddha.
Homage to Vipaśyin Buddha. Homage to Tiṣya Buddha.
Homage to Buddha Puṣya. Homage to Buddha Anuttarajaya.
Homage to Buddha Anuttarapadma. Homage to all Buddhas such as these.
Homage to the hundred Buddhas. Homage to the thousand Buddhas.
Homage to the hundred thousand buddhas! Homage to the ten million buddhas! Homage to the ten billion buddhas! Homage to the hundred billion buddhas!
Homage to the ten trillion buddhas! Homage to the hundred trillion buddhas! Homage to the ten quadrillion buddhas!
Homage to the nayuta-billions of Buddhas!
Homage to all Buddhas as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably unspeakable worlds!
Homage to Maitreya Buddha! Homage to Vairocana Buddha!
Homage to all Buddhas, śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, and the entire ocean-like assembly of bodhisattvas throughout the ten directions and the three periods of time,
and next to the lay devotee Viśvantara.
Homage to the layman Viśvantara of the city of Sudarśana in the southern direction, who has attained the liberation door of the limit of non-extinction for Bodhisattvas.
May all in the ten directions take refuge; may sins be extinguished and pure faith increase; may we be born in the Flower Treasury Ocean.
In the *Sūtra on the Dharma Gate of the Liberation of the Seventh Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara’s Great Compassionate Practice within the Pure Land of Sukhāvatī*, it says:
"At that time, the youth Sudhana... was able to know and was able to expound those meritorious practices."
May I, together with all sentient beings, be reborn in the Flower Treasury Ocean within the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss.
Homage to the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara of Mount Potalaka in the South, who has attained the Dharma-gate of the Great Compassionate Conduct and Liberation.
All in the ten directions take refuge; Sins are extinguished and pure faith increases. May they be born within the Flower Treasury Ocean, In the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss.
The Eighth: The Bodhisattva Samantagati’s Liberation Method Door of Swift Action through the Universal Gate.
The Sūtra says: "At that time, there was a Bodhisattva from the eastern direction... (until) he gazed up with earnest devotion, took his leave, and departed.
"May I, together with all sentient beings, be reborn in the Flower Treasury Ocean within the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss.
Next, regarding the place where the Bodhisattva Samantagāmin attained the Dharma-gate, the Buddha [spoke].
Homage to the Buddha Universal Victorious Birth within the World of Wondrous Treasury in the Eastern Quarter.
Homage to all Buddhas, as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably unspeakable numbers of Buddha-fields.
Homage to the entire ocean-like assembly at the sites of enlightenment of all such Buddhas.
Next is the Bodhisattva Samantagāmin;

I pay homage to him. From the summit of Mount Cakravāḍa in the eastern world-realm of Sugandhakośa, he came through the air and pressed the earth with his foot, attaining the bodhisattva liberation door of "Swift Movement through Universal Gateways. This is the Bodhisattva Samantagāmin.
All in the ten directions take refuge; Sins are extinguished and pure faith increases. May they be born within the Flower Treasury Ocean and the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss.
The Ninth Great Deity’s Dharma Gate of Liberation through the Cloud-Network.
The Sūtra says: "At that time, the youth Sudhana... (up to) circumambulated him countless times and took his leave to depart.
May I, together with all sentient beings, be reborn in the Flower Treasury Ocean within the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss.
Namo to the Great Divine Spirit in the city of Dvāravatī in the south, who attained the Dharma-gate of the Cloud-Net Liberation.
All in the ten directions take refuge; Sins are extinguished and pure faith increases. May they be born within the Flower Treasury Sea, In the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss.
The Tenth Ground-Dwelling Goddess, Indestructible Treasury of Wisdom, Dharma Gate of Liberation.
The Sūtra says: "At that time, the youth Sudhana [until] respectfully gazed up at him, took his leave, and departed.
May I, together with all sentient beings, be reborn in the Flower Treasury Ocean and within the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss.
Next is the place where the Earth Deity Anantapratisthāna attained the Dharma-door, as taught by the Buddha.
Homage to the Buddha Sublime Eye of the World Moon Banner in the Adorned Eon of the past.
Homage to all the unspeakably many Buddhas of the present Auspicious Eon.
Next, the Earth Deity Anvaya.
Homage to the Earth Deity Anvaya, who dwells in the Bodhimaṇḍa in the kingdom of Magadha within this Jambudvīpa,
having attained the liberation door of the indestructible treasury of bodhisattva wisdom;

homage to her who is like a perfect vessel of superior faculties, who sought the Dharma through a hundred cities, and who perfected the bodhisattva practices within a single lifetime for the sake of future generations.
To the Bodhisattva Sudhana, the exemplar of the sudden gate of practice and realization in this world,
to whom all ten directions pay homage— I prostrate to extinguish my sins and increase my pure faith; may I be reborn in the ocean of the Flower Treasury and the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss.
Next, for the repentance to remedy the bodhisattva’s mind:
I pray that the inexhaustible Triple Gem of the Buddha, Dharma, and Sangha, the Tathāgata Vairocana, the holy assembly of Samantabhadra, Mañjuśrī, and the ocean-like gathering,
and all mundane and supramundane deities, by the power of your compassionate original vows, may emit great radiance to illuminate this dharma assembly.
May you bear witness and protect us with your mindfulness; may you compassionately accept and take us into your care.

I vow that for myself and all the oceans of sentient beings, from beginningless time until this very moment, I now confess and repent for all sinful karma and the repeated destruction of the bodhicitta within the infinite, interlacing net of Indra.
The *Puṣpamālā-sūtra* states: "If there should be someone who, desiring to destroy the bodhicitta of a bodhisattva, creates obstacles for them, how much sin will that person incur?
Why is this? If those who have already corrupted it, or those who intend to corrupt it, hear of this matter, they will immediately repent of their own accord.
The Buddha told Śāriputra: "If a person creates obstacles and destroys the bodhicitta [of a bodhisattva]..."
One incurs immeasurable sin. It is like a person who wishes to destroy a priceless jewel; such a person loses immeasurable wealth and profit.
In the same way, Śāriputra, if a person disrupts or corrupts the mind of a bodhisattva, they destroy immeasurable jewels of the Dharma.
Śāriputra, it is like planting a medicinal tree; if someone cuts it down and does not allow it to grow, that person ruins it.
Regarding the task of healing the illnesses of immeasurable sentient beings, [he brings about] such that many sentient beings are no longer oppressed by disease.

In this way, Śāriputra, if anyone wishes to destroy this bodhisattva’s mind— the mind of great peace and happiness, the mind of great wisdom and joy that eliminates the suffering and afflictions of immeasurable sentient beings—
you should know that such a person causes immeasurable and incalculable sentient beings to be afflicted by various cravings.

Śāriputra, they are afflicted by the diseases of the various afflictions—desire, malice, delusion, pride, stinginess, envy, flattery, crookedness, lack of shame, and lack of remorse—and they likewise cause immeasurable asaṃkhyeya multitudes to lose their dwelling place of peace and security that is nirvāṇa. Śāriputra, [it is thus].
If a person destroys Lake Anavatapta and kills the Great Dragon King,
you should know that such a person has ruined and lost the water of eight virtues for thirsty beings with two or four legs. In the same way, Śāriputra,
if a person disrupts and confuses the mind of a bodhisattva, they have destroyed the Noble Eightfold Path that can eliminate the thirst and craving of immeasurable sentient beings.
Śāriputra, it is like a person who destroys the sun palace; that person would thereby extinguish the light for the sentient beings of the four continents.

In the same way, Śāriputra, if there is a person who disrupts the mind of a bodhisattva, you should know that this person destroys the great Dharma-light of all sentient beings throughout the worlds of the ten directions. Śāriputra!
Just as one who destroys all precious gems should be known as one who destroys the treasures of immeasurable sentient beings,
so too, Śāriputra, if a person disrupts the mind of a bodhisattva, one should know that such a person destroys their share of the Dharma-treasures of immeasurable asaṃkhyeya beings,
and they likewise bring about the destruction of such sūtras as these, preventing others from hearing them.
"See, Śāriputra, how this nature of jewels produces immeasurable treasures to provide for and satisfy sentient beings.
In the same way, Śāriputra, the minds of bodhisattvas are the nature of the Dharma-jewel. From this Dharma-jewel arise the inconceivable supernormal powers, wisdom, and strength of all Buddhas.
Therefore, Śāriputra, you should know that one who destroys the mind of a bodhisattva incurs [this consequence]."
"Śāriputra, there is immeasurable and boundless deep transgression. Śāriputra, it is as if a person with an evil mind were to draw blood from the body of a Buddha;
if there is another person who, having broken the precepts and lacking faith, destroys and abandons this bodhicitta, their transgression is exactly equal. Śāriputra, [it is thus].

Setting aside this case of one with an evil mind who sheds the blood of a Buddha—I say that such a person is fully possessed of the five ānantarya crimes—if there is a person who destroys the bodhicitta, their transgression exceeds even this. Why is this?
Even the commission of the five heinous crimes cannot destroy the Dharma of a single Buddha; yet if a person destroys the bodhicitta, they sever and extinguish all the Buddhadharmas.
Śāriputra, it is like this: for example, if one slaughters an ox, one thereby destroys the milk, curd, butter, and so forth.
In the same way, Śāriputra, if a person destroys the bodhicitta of a bodhisattva, they sever and extinguish all the wisdom of the Buddhas.

Therefore, Śāriputra, you should know that the transgression of a person who breaks the precepts, lacks faith, reviles, scolds, or disparages others, thereby destroying the bodhicitta, is far more grave than that.
Regarding the five heinous crimes: Śāriputra, setting aside the five heinous crimes, suppose the four continents were filled with arhats, and a certain person were to take the lives of them all.
What do you think? Would that person’s transgression not be very great?
Śāriputra said, “It would be very great, World-Honored One. The Buddha said, “I now tell you: if a person slanders and disrupts the bodhi-”

Sā. To cause them to believe and accept [this], and to abandon such a mind, thereby losing the Buddha’s wisdom—compared to the former offense, this does not even approach a hundredth part, a thousandth part, a hundred-thousand-millionth part; it cannot even be reached by analogy. Why is this?
Although one might take the lives of that many arhats, one cannot obstruct the Buddhas’ ten powers or four fearlessnesses.
The fearlessnesses; the four unhindered knowledges; the eighteen unique qualities; great loving-kindness and great compassion; the fact that the Buddha’s actions are never in vain;
not obstructing the Tathāgata’s elephant-king-like backward glance, his lion-like springing forth, or his invisible crown protuberance;

not obstructing the Tathāgata’s chanting of the hundred-thousandfold complete Dharma hymns, nor hindering the turning of the unsurpassed wheel of Dharma; and not obstructing the sovereign mastery of the Holy Lord.

Through his supernormal powers (*ṛddhi*), he is also unimpeded in knowing the sharpness or dullness of the faculties (*indriya*) of sentient beings, their various inclinations and desires, and their diverse wisdoms. Śāriputra,
if a bodhisattva has resolved upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* and attained the adornment of firm vows for the Great Vehicle (*mahāyāna*),
should anyone come to disrupt or disturb this mind, causing them to regress and abandon it— this is [the case].
Such a person obstructs the Buddha’s ten powers, up to and including the knowledge of the various inclinations of sentient beings.
Śāriputra, setting aside the four continents, suppose the great trichiliocosm were filled with arhats, as dense as a thicket of bamboo, reeds, rice, or hemp.
If there were a single person who were to take the lives of them all, what do you think? Would that person’s transgression be great?

"Very much so, World-Honored One. "Śāriputra, if there is another person who harbors anger and contempt, violates the precepts, lacks faith, and destroys, scatters, and distracts this bodhicitta of a bodhisattva, the offense committed by this person can only be known by a Buddha. Why is this?
Because such a person ruins and disturbs the profound mind of a bodhisattva, thereby destroying all the Buddha-dharma and severing the lineage of the Buddhas."
Why is this? If there were no bodhisattvas who have first resolved their minds [on enlightenment], how could such Buddha-wisdom and the sovereign power of a Buddha appear in the world?
Therefore, Śāriputra, this unsurpassed mind, the great mind, the profound mind—the mind of all bodhisattvas—if it exists in a bhikṣu, a bhikṣuṇī, an upāsaka, an upāsikā, or a deva...
Nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, humans, and non-humans—all those in the world should pay homage and respect.
Why is this? One who possesses such a mind should be known as a World-Honored One of the future. This is the repentance for the retribution of transgressions.

Furthermore, a sutra states: "Śāriputra, if there is a person who disparages the arousal of the Mahāyāna mind, you should know that such a person cannot benefit themselves, nor can they benefit others;
this person is not called one who practices the Way. Śāriputra, such a foolish person walks upon a deviant path;
because they have lost their own benefit, they also lose the benefit of others. For these reasons, such a person..."
One shall encounter eight conditions of decline and affliction. What are these eight? They are: the loss of beloved friends, relatives, and family;
the ruin and turmoil of one's country; the daily depletion of wealth and property; being consumed by destructive fires; being oppressed by government officials;

the impairment of the sense faculties; death followed by entry into hell; and being tortured by the wardens of hell. These are called the eight. Furthermore, there are eight great conditions of insecurity. What are they?
There are eight [states of great insecurity]. These are: being born in the hells, as a hungry ghost, or as an animal; these are states of great insecurity.

Even if one obtains a human body, if one is constantly born in a frontier region where one does not know good from evil, and where there is no Buddha, no Dharma, and no Sangha of noble ones, this is also a state of great insecurity.
Even if one obtains a human body and is born in a central land, if one is deaf, blind, mute, or crippled by various ailments, this too is called a state of great insecurity.

The Dharma of Peace. Although one may be born in a central land and possess a complete human body, if one is constantly subject to decline and ruin, harboring a mind of flattery and crookedness, and practicing falsehood, deceit, and guile, this is also called the "Great Dharma of Unease.

If one is born in a central land and possesses a complete human body, yet receives the teachings of external paths, delights in heterodox arguments, false views, and evil conduct, and accomplishes impure actions of body, speech, and mind—[this is the Great Dharma of Unease]. All Buddhas...
Even the noble sages cannot save them; this is also called a state of great instability.

If one is born in a central land with a complete human body, yet at the very night the Buddha attains the Way, one’s life comes to an end and one does not encounter the Buddha-dharma; this too is called a state of great instability.
These are the eight states of instability for those who disparage those seeking the Buddha-way. Śāriputra, you should know this.

If such a person is born in the hells, they will inevitably fall into the Great Avīci Hell, where they assume a massive body and undergo manifold sufferings while continuously committing grave offenses.
If they fall among the animals, they become wicked insects or beasts, constantly tormented by hunger and thirst;

they seize the lives of others and devour their flesh and muscles to sustain themselves, and wherever they are born, they continue to increase their karmic transgressions. If they are born as water-dwellers...
By nature, they become makara fish, śiśumāras, crocodiles, and *udrā* and so forth.

Caught by people with nets and hooks, they are cut alive with knives and endure manifold sufferings, unable even to seek death. If born again on land, they may become camels, donkeys, oxen, sheep, pigs, or dogs.
If they become camels or oxen, their noses are pierced by humans; their bodies are constantly burdened with heavy loads, and further [torments are inflicted].
Pained by the staff, they groan and cry out loudly, yet there is no one to save them. Exhausted along the way, they are unable to move forward;

while their lives have not yet ended, they are torn apart and flayed alive, and their flesh is devoured. Even so, they continue to revile [their tormentors], saying, "You eat too much and love to lie down;
you have caused me great loss! Śāriputra, observe these causes and conditions of karmic retribution. As I know them, if I were to explain them in detail—
Śāriputra, even from eon to eon, one could not exhaust [the consequences of such acts]. To speak briefly:
if a person destroys the bodhicitta of a bodhisattva, it is impossible for them to escape the eight difficulties. Why is this? Because such a person continuously generates various sinful karmas.
You should know that you have escaped these difficulties; this is for your own salvation.

We have been shrouded by ignorance and failed to recognize the causes of the offense of destroying the bodhicitta. Now that we have encountered this site of enlightenment (*bodhimaṇḍa*), we are finally able to awaken.
We take refuge in the Tathāgata Vairocana and the ocean-like assembly of all worthy and holy ones.

Burning incense and scattering flowers, we openly confess and repent, not daring to conceal anything. By virtue of these causes and conditions, may I and all sentient beings within the Dharma-realm...
O Sea! It destroys all sinful karma that obstructs the bodhisattva mind, purifying them all completely.

The sins accumulated over a hundred kalpas Are entirely swept away in a single thought-moment; Like fire consuming dry grass, they are extinguished without remainder.
All the evil karma I have created in the past, Arising from beginningless greed,

○ (Recitation: May the assembly listen to these verses on impermanence from within the Sūtras:
From beginningless kalpas, the number of births and deaths has been as vast as the sands of the Ganges. The bones piled up would form Mount Pulu;
the blood accumulated would be like a great ocean. It is like a tree by the roadside: one rests there for a moment, but does not stay long.
Carriages, horses, wives, and children—none shall remain so for long.
Just as flocks of birds roosting together at night disperse and fly away at dawn, so too when one dies and parts from kin and friends, such is the nature of separation.
Only the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas are the true refuge and support; relying upon the scriptures, I have briefly explained this.

Directly praising the Buddhas:

All Buddhas are perfect, eternal, and all-pervading; Universally illuminating all lands as numerous as atoms, their forms mutually manifesting in infinite ways; Each and every one is perfect, pervading the entire dharma-realm.

From the pores of the Tathāgata’s body, clouds of light emerge—vast, inconceivable, and without limit—which universally illuminate the minds of all sentient beings, completely extinguishing every affliction.

Manifesting transformations throughout the worlds of the ten directions, they preach the practice of the ten perfections according to the minds of sentient beings.
From every cloud-like body, they emanate infinite assemblies of gods of the desire and form realms,
including the Four Great Kings, the eight classes of beings, and various miscellaneous deities, who pervade the ten directions and fill the entire Dharma-realm, appearing before all sentient beings.

To the body that proclaims its own past practices, the body of all bodies, and the clouds of bodies throughout the ten directions—to you I take refuge. May my sins be extinguished and my pure faith increase; may I be reborn within the Flower Treasury Ocean in the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss.

Next, for the repentance of the one million gates of hindrances, I take refuge in the inexhaustible Buddha, Dharma, and Sangha jewels of the Indra-net; Vairocana Tathāgata; the assembly of holy beings of Samantabhadra, Mañjuśrī, and the ocean-like gathering;
and the mundane and supramundane deities. By the power of your compassionate original vows, may you emit great radiance to illuminate this dharma assembly.
May you bear witness and protect us with your mindful compassion; may you take pity on us and graciously accept us.

I pray that I and the ocean of all sentient beings, from beginningless time until this very moment, shall openly confess and repent for our inexhaustible oceans of karma—interwoven like Indra’s net—and for the delusions and karmic actions that constitute the hundreds of thousands of gates of obstruction.

The *Samantabhadra-caryā-praṇidhāna-parivarta* states: "The Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, appear in the world because sentient beings—due to their lack of wisdom, commit evil deeds, conceive of 'self' and 'what belongs to self,' cling to the body, and are possessed by inversions, doubts, false views, and conceptual discriminations—are constantly associated with all fetters and bonds;
thus they follow the stream of birth and death and remain far from the path of the Tathāgata. O Son of the Buddha, I do not see a single..."
This constitutes a grave transgression. For instance, when Bodhisattvas give rise to a mind of anger toward other Bodhisattvas. Why is this?
O Son of the Buddha, if Bodhisattvas give rise to a mind of malice toward other Bodhisattvas, they immediately bring about one million obstacles.
What are these one million obstacles? They are: the obstacle of not seeing Bodhi, the obstacle of not hearing the True Dharma, and so forth.
The obstacle of being born in impure worlds; the obstacle of being born in the various evil destinies; the obstacle of being born in places of hardship; the obstacle of having many illnesses;
the obstacle of being frequently slandered and reviled; the obstacle of being born in realms of dull and obtuse faculties; the obstacle of losing right mindfulness; the obstacle of lacking wisdom;
the obstacles of the eye, the ear, the nose, the tongue, the body, and the mind; the obstacle of evil associates; and the obstacle of evil companions.

The obstacle of sectarianism; the obstacle of delighting in practicing the Hīnayāna; the obstacle of delighting in associating with the vulgar and ordinary; the obstacle of not having faith in or delighting in those of great majesty and virtue;
the obstacle of delighting in dwelling together with those who have abandoned right view; the obstacle of being born into non-Buddhist sects; the obstacle of dwelling within the realm of Māra;

the obstacle of being separated from the Buddha’s true teaching; the obstacle of not seeing virtuous friends; the obstacle of hindrances to the roots of goodness; and the obstacle of increasing unwholesome dharmas. Attainment...
The obstacle of being born in inferior places; the obstacle of being born in borderlands; the obstacle of being born into an evil family; the obstacle of being born among evil deities;

the obstacles of being born among evil nāgas, evil yakṣas, evil gandharvas, evil asuras, evil garuḍas, evil kiṃnaras, evil mahoragas, and evil rākṣasas—these are the ten obstacles to faith. I now repent of them all.

The obstacle of not delighting in the Buddha-dharma; the obstacle of practicing the ways of the ignorant; the obstacle of attachment to and delighting in the Hīnayāna; the obstacle of not delighting in the Mahāyāna; the obstacle of a nature prone to frequent alarm and fear;

the obstacle of a mind constantly afflicted by sorrow and distress; the obstacle of craving and attachment to birth and death; and the obstacle of not being single-mindedly devoted to the Buddha-dharma.
The obstacle of not delighting in seeing or hearing of the Buddha’s sovereign supernormal powers; these are the obstacles of the ten stages (*daśabhūmi*). I now repent of them all.

The obstacle of failing to obtain the various faculties (*indriya*) of a bodhisattva; the obstacle of failing to practice the pure conduct of a bodhisattva; the obstacle of retreating and becoming cowardly regarding the profound mind of a bodhisattva;

the obstacle of failing to give rise to the great vows of a bodhisattva; the obstacle of failing to resolve upon the mind of omniscience (*sarvajñatā-citta*); and the obstacle of being indolent regarding the practices of a bodhisattva.
The obstacle of indolence; the obstacle of being unable to purify various karmic hindrances; the obstacle of being unable to gather great merit;

the obstacle of being unable to make the power of wisdom clear and sharp; the obstacle of severing vast wisdom; and the obstacle of failing to attain the upholding of all bodhisattva practices—these are the ten obstacles to practice. I now repent of them all.

Delighting in slandering the words of the Omniscient One is an obstacle; being distant from the Bodhi of all Buddhas is an obstacle; delighting in dwelling within the realms of the various Māras is an obstacle;
failing to single-mindedly cultivate the realm of the Buddha is an obstacle; and failing to decisively give rise to the bodhisattva’s great vow is an obstacle.
These are the ten obstacles to the *pariṇāmanā* (dedication of merit). I now repent of them all.

The obstacle of not delighting in dwelling together with bodhisattvas; the obstacle of not seeking the roots of goodness of bodhisattvas; the obstacle of a nature characterized by frequent views and doubt; the obstacle of a mind that is constantly dull and dark;
the obstacle of non-renunciation arising from being unable to practice the impartial giving of a bodhisattva;

the obstacle of breaking the precepts arising from being unable to uphold the Tathāgata’s discipline; and the obstacle of delusion and affliction arising from being unable to enter the gate of patience.
There is the obstacle of harmful ill-will (*vyāpāda*). There is the obstacle of the defilement of indolence (*kausīdya-mala*), because one is unable to practice the great diligence of a bodhisattva.

There is the obstacle of distraction (*vikṣepa*), because one is unable to attain the various samādhis. There is the obstacle of corrupted wisdom (*duṣprajñā*), because one does not cultivate the perfection of wisdom (*prajñā-pāramitā*).

There is the obstacle of lack of skill regarding what is possible and impossible (*sthānāsthāna-kauśalya*). And there is the obstacle of lack of skillful means (*upāya*) regarding the deliverance of sentient beings.
They are hindered by being unable to discern within the wisdom of a bodhisattva; they are hindered by being unable to comprehend the dharmas of a bodhisattva’s renunciation.
Because they have not accomplished the ten kinds of vast eyes of a bodhisattva, they are hindered by having eyes like those of one born blind.

Because their ears do not hear the unimpeded Dharma, they are hindered by having mouths like those of a mute sheep. Because they lack the marks and signs of excellence, their faculty of the nose is impaired.

Obstacles: Because they cannot discern the languages of sentient beings, they achieve an obstacle to the tongue faculty (*jihvendriya*). Because they treat sentient beings with contempt, they achieve an obstacle to the body faculty (*kāyendriya*).
Because their minds are frequently deranged and distracted, they achieve an obstacle to the mind faculty (*manendriya*).

Because they do not maintain the three types of restraint (*saṃvara*), they achieve an obstacle to bodily action (*kāyakarman*). Because they constantly give rise to the four kinds of faults, they achieve an obstacle to vocal action (*vākkarman*). Much...
Because of giving rise to greed, hatred, and wrong views, one accomplishes the obstacle of mental karma; the obstacle of seeking the Dharma with a thief’s mind;
the obstacle of severing the sphere of activity of a bodhisattva; the obstacle of conceiving cowardice and retreat within the courageous Dharma of a bodhisattva;
the obstacle of conceiving indolence within the path of renunciation of a bodhisattva; and the obstacle of conceiving cessation within the gateways of the light of a bodhisattva’s wisdom.
Obstacles: the obstacle of generating a weak and inferior mind within the bodhisattva’s power of mindfulness; the obstacle of being unable to uphold the Tathāgata’s teaching;
the obstacle of being unable to draw near to the bodhisattva’s path of transcendence; the obstacle of being unable to cultivate the bodhisattva’s path free from ruin;
the obstacle of conforming to the fixed positions of the two vehicles; and the obstacle of distancing oneself from the enlightenment of the Buddhas of the three periods of time.
The obstacles to the lineage of the Bodhisattvas are the obstacles to the ten stages; I now repent of them all.
O Son of the Buddha, if a Bodhisattva gives rise to even a single thought of anger toward other Bodhisattvas, they will bring about as many as one million such doors of obstacles.
Why is this? O Son of the Buddha, I do not see any single dharma that constitutes a greater fault or evil than these.
I now repent for all instances of harboring anger toward other bodhisattvas.
Enveloped by ignorance, we failed to recognize the causal nature of the offense of hatred. Only now, having encountered this site of enlightenment (bodhimaṇḍa), have we begun to realize it.
We take refuge in the Tathāgata Vairocana and the ocean-like assembly of all worthy and holy ones. We offer burning incense and scatter flowers.

I openly confess and repent for all various afflictions and hindrances, not daring to conceal them. By these causes and conditions, may all the afflictions of myself and the ocean of all sentient beings become entirely purified.
Next, the mudrā and mantra for repentance and the eradication of transgressions: Oṃ sṛmara pabha me sputanadahanadramaye svāhā.
(Recite three times.)
Sins accumulated over a hundred kalpas are entirely swept away in a single thought; like fire consuming dry grass, they are extinguished without remainder.
All the evil karma I have created in the past arose from beginningless greed, hatred, and delusion.
I now repent of everything produced by my body, speech, and mind.
Having repented, I take refuge with a sincere heart and pay homage to the Honored One, Vairocana Buddha.
○ (Proclamation: May the assembly listen to these verses on impermanence from the Sūtra:
Day and night, not for even a moment may one pause; The lifespan of this body is constantly diminishing, And no other person can increase it. How then could I now not return to death?
When I lie upon my sickbed, though surrounded by all my kinsmen,
at the time of casting off my life, I shall experience extreme suffering entirely alone.
At that time, it is only the wholesome Dharma that is essential, yet I have never cultivated it.
Since there is no one to provide rescue or protection for them, what shall I do at that time?

Āṭāṭānagaṇasvāhā. In the Brahma-sound he praises the Buddha:
"The Buddha-body is immeasurable, yet it can manifest a measurable body, appearing to each according to their capacity."
The Guide manifests in this way, yet the Buddha-body has no fixed location;
it fills all places like space, which is without limit. Such is the inconceivable sphere of activity of compassion, wherein the mind does not arise;
within the realm of the Buddhas, there is ultimately neither birth nor cessation.

He spoke directly in praise of the Buddha, the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, the great ocean of wisdom. Within it are four great jewels of wisdom, fully endowed with immeasurable merit and gnosis.
By means of these, they can give rise to all sentient beings, śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, and those in training (śaikṣa).

The stage of those beyond training (*aśaikṣa*), as well as the jewel of wisdom of all bodhisattvas—namely, the great jewel of wisdom consisting of skillful means free from attachment that skillfully discriminates between conditioned and unconditioned phenomena;

the great jewel of wisdom that explains immeasurable dharmas through discrimination without violating the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*); and the great wisdom that knows the timely and the untimely, never erring or failing.

O Jewel of Wisdom! If these four jewels did not exist within the great ocean of the Tathāgatas’ supreme wisdom, there would never be any possibility for even a single sentient being to enter the Mahāyāna.
These four jewels of wisdom cannot be seen by sentient beings of meager merit. Why is this?
Because they reside within the profound and secret treasury of the Tathāgata. These four jewels of wisdom are even, upright, pure, and sublime.
Excellent. It is universally able to benefit the assembly of Bodhisattvas, causing them all to attain the radiance of wisdom.
This is the fourth characteristic of the Tathāgata’s mind.

As for the classes of *nāgas*: there are those who are lords of the five directions; those who are lords of the eight directions and possess great power;
and those who are of the three types—celestial, terrestrial, and human—namely, celestial *nāgas*, terrestrial *nāgas*, and human *nāgas*. There are also five kinds of *nāgas*:

the frog-like, the snake-like, the fish-like, the elephant-like, and the horse-like. Furthermore, according to their physical characteristics, there are five-horned *nāgas*, those with beaks, those with scales and armor, and those with variegated markings.
Regarding the *barkara* (駁) winged nāgas: there are four types that dwell in palaces—mountain nāgas, ocean nāgas, spring nāgas, and pond nāgas.
Furthermore, there are those of the Four Great Kings’ lineage, the ministerial lineage, the Brahmin lineage, and the mixed-lineage.
With the exception of the eight great nāgas and the nāga king of the Anavatapta Lake, all others are subject to various fears of heat from the *garuḍa*, fear of heat, and fear of hot water.
There is the fear of hot sand, the fear of scorching winds, the fear of royal conscription, the fear of being devoured by one another, the fear of foul odors, and the fear of maggots.

There may also be terrestrial spirits with the heads of pigs. Furthermore, among the dragon kings there are three sufferings: first, although there be delicacies of a hundred flavors, once they enter the mouth, they all turn into tadpoles;
second, although the dragon maidens are beautiful, when they engage in sexual union, it is like being united with a snake; third—

Within the scales of these beings, sand and stones grow, causing them to suffer intense pain. Dragons endure five kinds of suffering: at birth, during sleep, during sexual union, during anger, and at death.
For half a day, three times over, their skin and flesh fall to the ground as they are scorched by hot sands. Thus they repent for the retribution of their transgressions.

The Mahāvaipulya Mahāsannipāta Sūtra states: At that time, the Dragon King Sāgara addressed the Buddha, saying, "World-Honored One, by what causes and conditions are we all born among the dragons? The Buddha said, "Dragon King, listen attentively, listen attentively.
I shall now explain to you in detail and distinguish for you the ten kinds of karma by which one is born among the dragons. What are these ten? There are...
All sentient beings practice the six pāramitās, desiring to attain the awakening of anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, and also wishing to be free from evil obstacles;
or they desire to extensively cultivate the perfection of giving, bestowing gifts at the proper time.

Due to the causes and conditions of their vows, they are born among the dragons. Furthermore, O Dragon King, there are sentient beings who, through the causes and conditions of the merit from practicing generosity within the Mahāyāna, vow to be born among the dragons.

Furthermore, O Dragon King, there are sentient beings who practice giving for the sake of *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*; although their karmic reward of merit is great, [they may still be born among the dragons].
Because they are unable to purify the causes and conditions for the fearsome realms of hell, hungry ghosts, and animals, they vow to be born among the nāgas.
Furthermore, O Nāga King, there are sentient beings who, when wishing to practice for the sake of *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, [make this vow].
Due to the causes and conditions of having given rise to a haughty mind and the power of great pride, they vow to be born among the nāgas.
Furthermore, O Nāga King, there are sentient beings who, when they resolve upon bodhicitta and practice for anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, frequently give rise to anger and resentment.

Hating other sentient beings, with a mind of anger and resentment, they create the causes and conditions for rebirth among those in the hells, hungry ghosts, and animals, thereby perpetually giving rise to anger and resentment.
Having died in this manner, they vow to be born among the nāgas. Furthermore, O Nāga King, there are certain sentient beings...
Seeking the Lesser Vehicle (Hīnayāna) and desiring to become a field of merit (puṇyakṣetra), they search among the noble ones (ārya).

Having relinquished the rewards of giving and the merit of making offerings, by such causes and conditions and through the power of their own vows, they are reborn among the nāgas. Furthermore, O Nāga King, there are sentient beings who...
Because of jealousy and pride, through the causal conditions of those karmas, they are born among the nāgas.

Furthermore, O Nāga King, there are sentient beings who frequently give rise to arrogance and are full of talkativeness; by virtue of their own karma, they are born among the nāgas. Furthermore, O Nāga King.
There are sentient beings who do not place faith in the Triple Gem of the Buddha, Dharma, and Sangha;
who fail to provide for their preceptors (*upādhyāya*), teachers (*ācārya*), and other virtuous elders; and who likewise fail to make offerings to their parents.

Due to various forms of anger, malice, hatred, attachment, pride, and the causes and conditions of delusion, they act erroneously toward fields of merit. By virtue of these karmic conditions, they come [to this state].

They are born among the nāgas. Furthermore, O Nāga King, there are sentient beings who possess various forms of delusion and arrogance, whose power of evil karma is great and whose power of merit is small;

because their minds are filled with fear, they vow to be born among the nāgas. Furthermore, O Nāga King, there are sentient beings who engage in false speech, divisive speech, and harsh speech, and who lack compassion;
by reason of these three types of karmic actions, they are born among the nāgas. Thus spoke the Buddha, O Nāga King.

Due to these ten kinds of karmic causes and conditions, they are born among the nāgas. Furthermore, O Nāga King, there are three other types of karmic causes and conditions by which one is born among the nāgas. What are these three? There are sentient beings who possess firm and evil karma;
because that karma of body, speech, and mind has ripened, they are born in the hells. Having spent immeasurable kalpas undergoing extreme suffering, it is difficult for them to find [liberation].
"Though they have attained liberation and escaped from great karma, their minor karma is not yet exhausted, and they are born among the nāgas, or among animals, or among hungry ghosts (preta).
It is due to these causes and conditions of the three evil karmas that they are born here among the nāgas.
At that time, the Nāga King Sāgara again addressed the Buddha, saying: "It is so, World-Honored One. Yet among these nāgas, there are some nāgas who experience the retribution of pleasure."
"Just as among the devas, there are some nāgas who experience pleasure like humans, some like pretas, and some like animals;
yet there are other nāgas who undergo great suffering and hardship like those in the hells.
Having said these words, the son of the great nāga king Sāgara, named Utpala, addressed the Buddha from before him: "World-Honored One, what evil karma and transgressions have I committed?"
Due to these causes and conditions, I was born among the nāgas. My body was large and handsome;

all its forms and textures, as well as my clothing and my place of rest, were experienced by my body at all times as if they were burning with fire. I was constantly without clothes and walked about naked.
Like my father, the king, I enjoyed the most excellent pleasures, and my karmic fruition was no different from that of a *cakravartin* king. Thus spoke the Buddha.
He said: "O Flower-Face, listen attentively, listen attentively! Reflect upon this well. I shall now relate to you a past event.
Thirty-one eons ago, there was a Buddha, a World-Honored One, named Śikhin Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha. At that time, in that world, there was a king named Bimbasāra."

That King Puṣya made offerings to that Buddha, as well as to immeasurable hundreds of thousands of srotāpannas, sakṛdāgāmins, anāgāmins, arhats, and the assembly of great bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, for a period of three months.
He provided them with various kinds of clothing, food, drink, and medicinal requisites, and listened to the Dharma with a sincere heart. Having heard the Dharma, he immediately...

He resolved his mind upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*. After having made offerings in this manner for three months, King Puṣya constructed monasteries for Śikhin Buddha and the rest of the Saṅgha, and bestowed upon them various kinds of clothing.
His food, drink, medicinal decoctions, beds, couches, and bedding were all provided in full abundance. The eldest son of that King Puṣya was named Piyadāsa-kumāra.
Having seen the Buddha and heard the Dharma, this Kumāra Piyadāsa developed a profound sense of dread regarding the cycle of saṃsāra.
He prostrated before his father the king and made a request, desiring to go to the Buddha to seek ordination as a renunciant. The king replied to his son:
He said, "If you wish to go, do as you please; I leave it to you. After he had gone forth [into homelessness], he spoke again to his father, saying, "I wish to stay at my father the king’s monastery.
King Puṣya said, "You may also go to that monastery according to your wish.

At that time, the disciples of the Saṃgha of Śikhin Buddha were staying in that monastery, sitting, lying down, using its facilities, and partaking of food and drink. There, the son of King Puṣya, Peta...
Śāstṛti conceived feelings of jealousy and became resentful toward the community of the Buddha’s disciples who had resided there for a long time; he constantly scolded and reviled them.
When the monks had been thus scolded and reviled, they all departed from the monastery. Seeing that the monks had left, Śāstṛti felt great joy and thought to himself:
"It is well that they have gone; I am now at peace. After the monks had departed... [time]... (Note: The provided source text ends abruptly with "時", which translates to "at that time" or "then".)
Śātī used the clothing and food within the monastery as he pleased; when others came, he would not allow them to stay.
After Śātī had thus committed all these evil karmas, at the end of his life, he was reborn in the great hells.
For immeasurable thousands of millions of nayutas of years, they underwent the torments of being burned by fires in the hells;

having escaped from there, they were born among the hungry ghosts (preta), where for another immeasurable hundreds of thousands of millions of years they suffered hardship and pain. Dying among the hungry ghosts, they fell back again into the hells.
Having escaped from the hells, they were born among the hungry ghosts. In this manner, they passed through thirty-one kalpas. You all—
"Nāga, listen attentively, listen attentively! That Śatadru, who underwent such various sufferings and hardships within the cycle of saṃsāra—Buddha said:
'O Puṣpamukha, was that Śatadru anyone else? It was none other than you yourself.
Due to the causes and conditions of evil karma in the distant past, you were born in the great hells, as hungry ghosts, and as animals, transmigrating and undergoing suffering.'"
Throughout these thirty-one great kalpas, he has endured all manner of suffering;

because he has never for a moment abandoned his remaining residual karma, he has been reborn among the dragons to undergo this evil retribution. When the dragon Huamian heard these words, he wept aloud.
He threw his entire body down, prostrating with his four limbs spread upon the ground, and addressed the Buddha, saying: "I now repent before the Buddha with a sincere heart.
I have been greatly deluded and confused; I am excessively arrogant, ignorant, and dull-witted. I do not understand skillful means, nor can I distinguish between the good and the evil."
Having committed these sinful karmas, he bowed his head and joined his palms, confessing with a sincere heart and not daring to conceal anything.
"O Tathāgata, World-Honored One, I now with utmost sincerity, penetrating to my very marrow, take refuge in the Buddha, take refuge in the Dharma, and take refuge in the Saṅgha of Bhikṣus.
From this moment until the end of my life, during this time, I shall act as an upāsaka. The Buddha said, "Excellent, excellent, good son!"
"Son, since you now take refuge in me with such sincerity, being anxious over the karmic retribution of the hells, hungry ghosts, and evil realms,
you shall exhaust those karmas and repent for your sinful retribution."
Furthermore, the *Jinglü yìxiàng* (Diverse Phenomena of Sūtras and Vinaya) states: The Dragon King addressed the Buddha, saying, "Since the beginning of the kalpa, I have dwelt in the great ocean.
Since the time of Krakucchanda Buddha, those with wives and children in the great ocean were very few; now, the dragon retinues in the ocean are exceedingly numerous.
The Buddha told the Dragon King: "Those who leave the household life within my Dharma but violate the precepts, persist in transgressions without renouncing them, and break the rules of discipline—"
They were mostly reborn among the nāgas; those who directly witnessed [the transgressions] mostly fell into hell, and those of such a kind, after their lives ended, were all reborn among the nāgas.

The Buddha told the Nāga King: "During the time of Krakucchanda Buddha, nine billion eight hundred million householders left the home life but violated the prohibitions and precepts, and they were all reborn among the nāgas. During the time of Kanakamuni Buddha, eight billion householders left the home life..."
Those who, while living as householders or having left the home life, destroy the precepts and indulge their own minds, will all be reborn among the nāgas after the end of their lives.
During the time of Kāśyapa Buddha, six billion four hundred million householders and renunciants violated the precepts and were all reborn among the nāgas.

In my own world, nine hundred and ninety billion householders and renunciants have engaged in strife, slandered others, and violated the precepts; they have fallen into the realm of nāgas upon death, and some have already been born there now. Because of this—
For this reason, within the great ocean there are incalculable numbers of dragon wives, children, and retinues.

After my parinirvāṇa, there will be many evil upāsakas who violate the prohibitions and precepts; they shall be reborn among the dragons or fall into hell. [This is for the sake of] repenting for the retribution of such sins.
Enveloped by ignorance, we did not recognize the causes of transgression within the dragon realm. Now that we have encountered this site of enlightenment, we have finally awakened to this truth.
We take refuge in the Tathāgata Vairocana and the ocean-like assembly of all worthy and holy ones. We burn incense and scatter flowers.
All the dragon kings approach all karmic retributions, confessing and repenting openly without daring to conceal anything.
By this cause and condition, may all my heavy sins and those of the ocean-like assembly of sentient beings within the Dharma-realm be entirely purified.
Next, the mudrā and mantra for repentance to extinguish transgressions: Oṃ sṛmara pāpamayi sphuṭa naṭa maṭa vidrāya svāhā.
(Recite three times.)
Sins accumulated over a hundred kalpas are entirely swept away in a single thought; like fire consuming dry grass, they are extinguished without remainder.
All the evil karmas I have created in the past arose from beginningless greed, anger, and delusion.
I now repent of everything produced by my body, speech, and mind;
having repented, I take refuge with a sincere heart and pay homage to the Honored One, Vairocana Buddha.
○ (Proclamation: May the assembly listen to these verses on impermanence from the Sūtra:

When the messengers of King Yama arrive, terrifying to behold, And the rākṣasa jailers come to seize one, One gives rise to great terror and loses control of one's bowels and bladder, Suffering such extreme agony of fear.
Thus, in the midst of such extreme evil and terror, who can provide me with protection?
When these terrifying signs appear, my eyes turn malicious as I search for a place of refuge in the four directions;
yet, seeing no place of reliance, I am later overcome by the most extreme grief and distress.
Since they have no one to provide rescue or protection, what can I do at such a time?

Session Thirty-Four:
The Fifth and Sixth Assemblies on Good Spiritual Friends within the Ten Stages.
With all reverence, we pay homage to the inexhaustible Triple Gem.
All members of this assembly kneel with their right knees on the ground, solemnly holding incense and flowers to make offerings according to the Dharma.

May this ocean-like cloud of offerings pervade the worlds of the ten directions—subtle and exquisite fragrant flowers, flowers of various colors, and immeasurable, wondrous, and marvelous blossoms that bring joy.
Behold the flowers: delightful flowers, flowers of all seasons, celestial flowers, human flowers, flowers cherished and loved by the world, and most fragrant and pleasing flowers.
With such various articles of offering, one constantly makes offerings.

The Indra-nets of successive layers—the oceans of Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and the assembly of worthy sages—receive these clouds of offerings and take them as luminous pedestals, extending far and wide.
In boundless realms, immeasurable and inexhaustible, may you perform the work of a Buddha.
Having made these offerings, with all reverence,
next present this jeweled net.
With clouds of offerings such as these— vast oceans of the intrinsic nature of precious jewels, the most excellent emergence of the seven-jeweled mountains,
and so forth— I offer them to all the Buddhas and others. Oṃ sarva-tathāgata-arcanopasthāna-samaya.
*Phraṇada samaye hūṃ*. The *Ratnakūṭa Sūtra* states:
"There is a dhāraṇī named 'Infinite Varieties of Spells,' which can accomplish all things and possesses great efficacy. The dhāraṇī says:
Oṃ sīmala sīmala me manasi kara mā ha laṅka hūṃ. Next, the mantra of the Amoghamani Seal: Oṃ amoghapāśa mahāvidyārāja tathāgata-mīlaṅga.
*Kiṃdasa-manta-prasara hūṃ*. In the Sanskrit language, this praises the Buddha Vairocana:
The Buddha Vairocana is able to turn the true Wheel of Dharma throughout all lands of the Dharma-realm.
Like clouds that completely pervade all that exists throughout the ten directions, the Buddhas of the oceans of great worlds,
through their spiritual powers and the force of their vows, turn the wheel of Dharma everywhere. Amidst the vast assemblies of beings in all lands,
their names and titles differ from one another as they expound the wondrous Dharma according to the conditions of those present.
I directly praise the Buddha, the mountain of great wisdom whose merits of perfect enlightenment are vast;
who has universally reached all realms and attained the further shore, equal to all Tathāgatas of the three periods of time. Therefore, I now pay respectful homage.
Having already ascended to the shore of the signless realm, you manifest a body adorned with wondrous marks and emit a thousand stainless rays of light.
You shatter the hosts of Māra’s army until they are utterly exhausted,
causing all worlds throughout the ten directions to tremble without exception.
Never having terrified a single sentient being, the power of the Sugata’s majesty is thus:
the nature of space and the realm of phenomena are equal, and he has already been able to abide in this way.
Abandoning all beings without measure, he has accomplished the path of supreme enlightenment.
With wisdom unimpeded regarding all objects of perception, sharing the same nature as all Buddhas—
Homage to the Vairocana Tathāgata, the Original Honored One of the Ten Unobstructed Bodies in the Flower Treasury World-Ocean of the Great Vaipulya Buddha Avataṃsaka Sūtra.
Homage to Śākyamuni Buddha, the Greatly Compassionate and Greatly Merciful One who, through five hundred vows, rescues those suffering in the five turbidities.

Homage to Bhaisajyaguru-vaiḍūryaprabha-rāja Buddha, the King of Lapis Lazuli Light, who, through twelve supreme vows, rescues those suffering in the five turbidities in the Pūrṇacandra world of the eastern direction.
Homage to Amitābha Buddha of the Western World of Ultimate Bliss, who, through his forty-eight vows, rescues sentient beings from suffering amidst the five turbidities.

Homage to the ocean of the perfect teachings of the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra* of the Great Vaipulya within all the lands as numerous as motes of dust throughout the entirety of space across the ten directions and three periods of time.
Homage to the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Samantabhadra, who presides over the truth of conduct and vows within the Great Vaipulya Buddha Avataṃsaka Sūtra.
Homage to Mañjuśrī, who presides over the wisdom of faith, understanding, and realization within the Great Vaipulya Buddha Avataṃsaka Sūtra.

Homage to the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva of Great Kindness and Great Compassion, the Thousand-Handed and Thousand-Eyed Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva, who rescues from suffering amidst the five turbidities.

Homage to the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Kṣitigarbha-Rāja, whose great vows are vast and profound, who rescues beings from suffering in the five turbidities and appears in worlds where no Buddha dwells, who comforts the hearts of sentient beings and eternally abides in the realm of Yamarāja.
Homage to the ten [stages of] faith Bodhisattvas within all the lands as numerous as atoms in the entirety of space throughout the ten directions and three periods of time.
I pay homage to the Bodhisattvas dwelling in the ten abodes, the ten dedications, the ten stages, and the stage of Equal Enlightenment;
to the Bodhisattvas as numerous as the atoms within the oceans of lands throughout the entire Dharma-realm; and to the assembly of all oceans of beings.
I take refuge in the fifty-five locations for the cultivation and realization of the five aspects found in the final assembly of the Great Vaipulya Buddha Avataṃsaka Sūtra.
The Noble Sudhana, who paid homage to the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra* during its final assembly; a vessel of perfect capacity and superior faculties who sought the Dharma through a hundred cities;
one who perfected the bodhisattva practices within a single lifetime; and the model for cultivation and realization according to the sudden gate for the final age.

The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva pays homage to all Buddha-activities— whether in the form of the Dharma-body, the form-body, physical remains, reliquary stupas, temples, or monasteries— within every atom of the lands throughout the entirety of space across the ten directions and the three periods of time;
as well as to the treasuries of the Dharma and the places where the Dharma is expounded.
Homage to the assembly of all noble and saintly Bodhisattvas, the ocean-like multitude;

to those who have donned the armor of great vows to seek birth in the Pure Land; to those who protect the True Dharma in the land of Xia during this age of corruption; and to the National Preceptors who guard the nation.

With a sincere heart, I take refuge and pay homage. To the World-Ocean of the Flower Treasury within the Great Vaipulya Buddha Avataṃsaka Sūtra, the Honored One Vairocana Buddha of the ten directions, I take refuge in all their entirety.
May my transgressions be extinguished and my pure faith increase; may I be born in the Ocean of the Flower Treasury.

The Dharma Door of the Liberation Entitled "The Vast Adornment of Great Joy Arising from Every Thought," known by the Night-Spirit Sovereign of the Ocean of Silent Sounds, the Fifth [Spirit] within the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss.
The Sūtra says: "At that time, the youth Sudhana (until) reverently gazed up at her and took his leave.
May I, together with all sentient beings, be reborn in the ocean of the Flower Treasury within the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss.
Next is the night goddess Silent Sound Ocean, the place where she attained the Dharma, and the Buddha there.

there are the sites of enlightenment (*bodhimaṇḍa*) of all the oceans of Buddhas,
such as Vairocana Tathāgata, numbering as many as atoms in unspeakably unspeakable numbers of Buddha-fields— to all these Buddhas, I pay homage (*namas*).
