To all throughout the ten directions, I take refuge. May my transgressions be extinguished and my pure faith increase; may I be born in the Sea of Flower Treasury.
In the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss,
next is the repentance for the sin of failing to respect the Triple Gem.
I pray that the infinite Jewels of the Buddha, Dharma, and Sangha, the Tathāgata Vairocana, Samantabhadra, and Mañjuśrī— like an imperial net— may grant their grace.
The assembly of noble ones gathered like the ocean, and the mundane and supramundane deities, by virtue of your compassionate original vows, emit great radiance that illuminates this dharma assembly.
May you bear witness, protect, and sustain us; may you look upon us with pity and grant us your acceptance.

I pray that I and the ocean of all sentient beings, from the beginningless past until this very moment, having failed to place faith in the Buddha, Dharma, and Sangha jewels, and failing to understand the Three Jewels as the ultimate refuge—the Indra-net of reality—[may we now awaken].
Repeatedly, I confess and repent of all sinful karma.

Regarding the Triple Gem, there is the manifest and there is the image; the image represents the True. If one makes offerings at the place of the image, one obtains the merit of making offerings to the manifest Buddha.
Now, in this age of the Final Dharma, the Sangha is the foremost of the gems. If one takes refuge in the Sangha, it constitutes taking refuge in them all.
The merit of taking refuge in the Triple Gem extends even to those monks who have broken the precepts; they too should be revered, let alone those monks who uphold the precepts.
The *Mahāprajñāpāramitā-śāstra* states: "Within the Buddha-dharma, the way of renunciation is the most difficult to practice.
For instance, when the brahmin Jambukhādaka asked Śāriputra, "What is the most difficult thing within the Buddha-dharma? Śāriputra replied, "Renunciation."
It is difficult. Again, it was asked: "What is difficult for one who has gone forth? He replied: "For one who has gone forth, finding delight in the Dharma is difficult.
Once one has found delight in the Dharma, what else is difficult? "Practicing all wholesome dharmas is difficult. For this reason, one should go forth.
Furthermore, when a person goes forth, the Māra King is struck with alarm and doubt, saying: "This person's fetters and latent tendencies are thin; he will surely attain Nirvāṇa."

They are included within the number of the Saṅgha-ratna. Furthermore, among those who have gone forth in the Buddha’s Dharma, even if they break the precepts and fall into transgression, they attain liberation once their transgressions are exhausted, as stated in the *Utpalavarṇā Bhikṣuṇī Jātaka-sūtra*. When the Buddha was in the world...
This bhikṣuṇī was an arhat who had attained the six supernormal powers. She would enter the houses of the nobility and constantly praise the dharma of renunciation, saying to the noblewomen:
"Sisters, you should leave the household life. The noblewomen replied, "We are young and our physical beauty is at its peak;
it is difficult to maintain the precepts, and we might break them. The bhikṣuṇī said, "Simply leave the household life."
"Breaking the precepts is itself a breaking [of the path]. She asked, "If one who breaks the precepts must fall into hell, how can they be broken?
She replied, "Falling into hell is itself a falling. The noble women all laughed at her, saying, "Hell is where one undergoes retribution; how can one 'fall' into it?
The bhikṣuṇī said, "I myself recall my former lives when I was a female entertainer, wearing various kinds of garments..."
He spoke these old words. At times, he would wear the robes of a bhikṣuṇī as a joke. Because of these causes and conditions, during the time of Kāśyapa Buddha, he was born as a bhikṣuṇī.
Relying on his noble lineage and physical beauty, he gave rise to arrogance and violated the prohibitions and precepts.
Due to the sin of breaking the precepts, he fell into hell and underwent various punishments. When his retribution for those sins was finally exhausted, he encountered Śākyamuni.
The nun Nibbāna left the household life and attained the path of an Arhat endowed with the six supernormal powers.

For this reason, it is known that although one who has left the household life and received the precepts may break them, by virtue of the causal conditions of those precepts, they can attain the path of an Arhat.

If one merely commits evil without the causal conditions of the precepts, one cannot attain the Path. In the past, throughout my successive lives, I fell into hell; upon emerging from hell, I became an evildoer.

An evil person who dies will return to hell and gain nothing at all. Now, by this evidence, one should know that although one may break the precepts after leaving home and receiving ordination, through these causes and conditions, one can still attain the fruit of the Path. Furthermore, it was as when the Buddha was at Jetavana.
There was a drunken brāhmaṇa who came to where the Buddha was and requested to become a bhikṣu. The Buddha commanded Ānanda to shave his head and clothe him in the dharma robes.
Once he had sobered from his intoxication, he was startled and amazed to find that he had suddenly become a bhikṣu; he immediately ran away.
The bhikṣus asked: "Why did the Buddha permit this intoxicated brāhmaṇa to become a bhikṣu? The Buddha said:
"This brāhmaṇa, throughout immeasurable kalpas, has never before had the intention to leave the household life. Now, because of his intoxication, he has briefly given rise to a subtle aspiration.

By virtue of these causes and conditions, he shall leave the household life and attain the Way. Such are the various causes and conditions and the merits of the benefits of leaving the household life."
His virtues are immeasurable. For this reason, although a layperson may observe the five precepts, they are not equal to one who has gone forth from the household life.

Furthermore, the *Mahākaruṇā-sūtra* states: "Ānanda, in the future age when the Dharma is about to perish, there will be bhikṣus within my teaching who, having gone forth, will walk about hand-in-hand with their children, going from tavern to tavern."

Within my Dharma, there are those who engage in unchaste conduct. Although they may have done so for the sake of alcohol, all of them shall attain parinirvāṇa during this Bhadrakalpa. For this reason, one must not violate [this precept].
The *Mahāsannipāta Sūtra* states: At that time, all the devas and other deities addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One, whether the Buddha remains in the world or does not remain in the world, we shall set aside our own affairs to protect and uphold this Dharma.
If the fourfold assembly of the Buddha’s disciples can be courageous and diligent in receiving and upholding such sūtras as these, even if they are merely providing for their own sustenance..."
Wives and concubines; accumulated gold, silver, lapis lazuli, and crystal; fields, lands, and cities;

and male and female servants—these eight kinds of impure things—for the sake of this Dharma, I shall protect those who possess them, ensuring that no evil spirits or ghosts cause them affliction or distress.

Furthermore, it is said that even kings, ministers, and others shall not cause affliction or distress to those who have shaved their heads and donned the *kāṣāya*, even if they do not maintain the prohibitive precepts.

"When one slanders and lashes [such a person], how much demerit is incurred? The Buddha said: "If a person were to draw blood from the bodies of ten trillion Buddhas, the demerit would still exceed that.
If there are sentient beings who have gone forth for my sake, shaving off their hair and beards and donning the saffron robes—"
Even if they do not maintain the precepts, they are all already sealed with the seal of nirvāṇa.
Furthermore, if there are those who, being monastics who do not maintain the precepts, cause disturbance through unrighteous means, or who revile, insult, and strike them with their hands or weapons;
If one beats, binds, or mutilates [a practitioner], or if one robs them of their robes and bowl, or robs them of various means of livelihood,
such a person destroys the true reward-body (*vipākakāya*) of the Buddhas of the three periods of time and plucks out the eyes of all gods and humans.
Because such a person seeks to cause the seeds of the True Dharma and the Triple Gem belonging to all Buddhas to sink into shadow, they deprive all gods and humans of benefit.
Because they fall into hell; because they cause the three evil realms to increase and become full. Regarding the repentance for karmic retribution, the *Daśacakra-kṣitigarbha-sūtra* states:
"O Great Brahmā, if there are those who have gone forth in reliance upon me, yet violate the precepts and engage in evil conduct..."
Internally corrupt, like a filthy snail, he is not truly a śramaṇa though he calls himself a śramaṇa;
he does not truly practice the holy life (brahmacarya) though he claims to practice the holy life. Constantly overcome, defeated, ruined, and overturned by various afflictions—such is this bhikṣu.
Although they have violated the prohibitions and committed various evil deeds, they act as spiritual friends to all devas,
nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, humans, and non-humans.

He reveals and guides them toward an immeasurable treasury of merit. Thus, although such a bhikṣu is not a fit vessel for the Dharma, by shaving his beard and hair and donning the saffron robes, his deportment and dignified bearing become identical to those of the noble ones.

Because of seeing him, the various roots of goodness of immeasurable sentient beings all attain growth; furthermore, he is able to reveal and show immeasurable sentient beings the way to be born in the happy realms and the heavens.

This is the true path to Nirvana. Therefore, regarding those who have gone forth under me—whether they uphold the precepts, violate them, or are without precepts—I do not permit even a Wheel-Turning Sage King, nor other kings, ministers, or officials, to use secular laws to whip, flog, or torture their bodies with whips or staves;
nor to imprison them, nor to revile or abuse them, nor to dismember their limbs.

[One might] even take its life, let alone [harm it] by relying on what is contrary to the Dharma. Mahābrahmā, such a bhikṣu who violates the precepts and engages in evil conduct is called a "corpse" within my Dharma and Vinaya;
yet he still possesses the residual power of the virtue of his renunciant precepts. It is like the ox and the musk deer:
although after their lives have ended they are the senseless corpses of animals in the realm of birth and death, the ox has its gall and the musk deer has its scent.
Musk deer possess fragrance and are able to bring great benefit to immeasurable and boundless sentient beings. A bhikṣu who has broken the precepts is also like this:

although within my Dharma and Vinaya he is called a corpse, yet because of the residual power of his renunciant precepts and virtue, he is able to bring great benefit to immeasurable and boundless sentient beings. Mahābrahmā, it is like a merchant...
The guest enters the great ocean and slays a certain class of immeasurable sentient beings.
He plucks out their eyes, mixes them with *madana* fruit, and grinds and sifts the mixture to produce an eye-remedy jewel.

If there are sentient beings who are blind and sightless, even those born blind from the womb, he takes this precious medicine and applies it to their eyes; all their ailments are removed, and they regain their vision.

Śuddhākṣa, it is the same with a bhikṣu who has broken the precepts. Although within my Dharma and Vinaya he is called a corpse, he still possesses the outward appearance and deportment of one who has gone forth.
Even those immeasurable and boundless sentient beings who merely catch a glimpse of him can obtain the pure eye of wisdom and Dharma;
how much more so for those who are able to proclaim the True Dharma for others, O Mahābrahmā!
It is like burning incense: although its substance is consumed, its fragrance remains pervasive, perfuming others with its scent. A bhikṣu who has broken the precepts is just like this;
because he has violated the discipline, he is not a worthy field of merit, and though he is constantly "burned" by the offerings of the faithful day and night, he cannot benefit them.
At the dissolution of the body and the end of life, they fall into the three evil destinies;
yet they bring great benefit to immeasurable and boundless sentient beings, causing them all to hear the fragrance of rebirth in heaven and of nirvāṇa.
Therefore, Great Brahmā, all laypeople should protect, revere, and make offerings to such bhikṣus who break the precepts and engage in evil conduct; I certainly do not permit otherwise.
As for those householders who beat their bodies with whips and staves, or imprison them, or revile them,
or dismember their limbs, or take their lives— I permit only the pure Saṃgha to perform these acts during the time of the Poṣadha.
Or, at the time of the *pravāraṇā* ceremony, they are expelled and driven out. All food, drink, and requisites belonging to the Saṃgha of the four directions are not permitted for their use.
Regarding all matters concerning the *vinaya* of the śramaṇas, they are entirely excluded and may not remain within the community.
Yet I do not permit the inflicting of whips or staves, binding, or the taking of life.
If one violates the prohibitions and precepts, one should not slander the violator, nor even whip them or seize their stored possessions; such transgressions are immeasurable and boundless.
Now, in this age of final dregs and strife, one should personally repent and reproach oneself, confessing the retribution for these sins.

We have been shrouded by ignorance and failed to recognize the karmic causes for slandering the Triple Gem. Now that we have encountered this site of enlightenment, we are finally able to awaken to this truth.
We take refuge in the Tathāgata Vairocana and the ocean-like assembly of all worthy sages.

Burning incense and scattering flowers, we openly confess and repent for the karmic obstructions resulting from our slander of the Triple Gem; we dare not conceal them. By virtue of these causes and conditions...
May all the grave offenses of myself and the ocean of sentient beings within the Dharma-realm, including the slander of the Triple Gem, be entirely purified.
Next, the mudrā and mantra for repentance and the extinction of offenses: Oṃ sarva-pāpa-maitri-praṇāmayāmi svāhā.
(One should recite this three times:
The sins accumulated over a hundred kalpas Are all swept away in a single thought; Like fire consuming dry grass, they are utterly extinguished without remainder.
All the evil karma I have created in the past, Arising from beginningless greed,
hatred, and delusion, Produced through my body, speech, and mind— I now confess it all. Having confessed,
I take refuge with a sincere heart and pay homage to the Honored One, Vairocana Buddha.
○ (Proclamation: Listen, all you members of the assembly, to these verses on impermanence from the Sūtra:
"Even upon a small, steep, and perilous height, one should dwell without negligence;
how much more so when facing a precipice of a thousand yojanas that leads to a long fall!"
It is unreasonable to dwell in peace while harboring the thought that one will not die today;
when my extinction and return to non-existence must inevitably arrive, there should be no doubt.

With all reverence, we pay homage to the inexhaustible Triple Gem.
May these members of the assembly each kneel on their right knees and, holding fragrant flowers, make offerings according to the Dharma.
May this ocean-like cloud of offerings pervade the worlds of the ten directions. Whether it be the offering of food and drink, various superior flavors, or the offering of vehicles; or...
Robes; or offering flower garlands, various incenses and ointments, seats, dwellings, and residences; exquisite lamps and candles;

medicinal decoctions for the treatment of illness; precious vessels and carriages; well-trained elephants and horses—with such various articles of offering, one constantly makes offerings in a manner as infinite as the Indra-nets of the Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and the ocean-like assembly of worthy sages, who receive these.
Clouds of offerings serve as a terrace of light, vast as boundless realms, immeasurable and inexhaustible; may they perform the work of a Buddha.
Having made these offerings, all pay homage with reverence.
Next, I offer clouds of such supreme offerings as vast oceans of the nature of precious jewels and mountain ranges of the seven treasures,
arising from the finest gems, which I present to all the Buddhas and their assemblies.
Oṃ sarvamantradhāraṇīpraveśa-samaya-spharaṇa-samaye hūṃ. The *Ratnakūṭa Sūtra* states:

The Tathāgata has no fixed abode, yet he dwells universally in all lands; He resides in every realm and is seen everywhere by all.
According to the minds of sentient beings, he is universally seen Attaining enlightenment, turning the wheel of Dharma, And entering parinirvāṇa; All phenomena are thus.
The realm of all Buddhas is likewise; there is not even a single dharma [that exists].
As it is said: "Directly praising the Buddha Śākyamuni, the Unsurpassed Honored One, who is endowed with all merits; those who see him find their minds purified."
Dedicated to great wisdom and the great compassion of the Tathāgata,
you have appeared in this world for the sake of all living beings to turn the unsurpassed wheel of Dharma.
Since the Tathāgata has undergone diligent suffering for the sake of sentient beings throughout incalculable eons, how can the worlds ever repay the kindness of the Great Teacher?
Rather than seeking liberation by abandoning the Tathāgata, one would prefer to undergo all the sufferings of the evil realms for immeasurable eons;
rather than seeking peace and happiness by abandoning the Buddha, one would prefer to undergo every kind of suffering on behalf of all sentient beings;
rather than [seeking safety] while remaining in the various evil destinies...
If one constantly hears the name of the Buddha, one would not wish to be born even in the good realms.

If for a moment one does not hear the Buddha, it would be better to be born in the various hells for countless eons after eon, never being separated from the Buddha while seeking escape from the evil destinies.
For what reason would one wish to dwell for long in all the various evil paths?
Because one attains the vision of the Tathāgata, wisdom increases; If one attains the vision of the Buddha, all suffering is extinguished.
One can enter the sphere of the great wisdom of all Tathāgatas;
If one attains the vision of the Buddha, one abandons all obscurations And nurtures inexhaustible merit.
Having accomplished the path to enlightenment, the Tathāgata is able to forever sever the doubts of all sentient beings;
according to what their hearts desire, he causes them all to be fully satisfied.

Next, for the two types of repentance— of principle and phenomena—

I pray that the inexhaustible Jewels of the Buddha, Dharma, and Sangha of the Imperial Net, Vairocana Tathāgata, and the assembly of holy ones of Samantabhadra, Mañjuśrī, and the ocean-like gathering,
along with all mundane and supramundane deities, by virtue of your compassionate original vows, may radiate great light to illuminate this dharma assembly.
May you bear witness, protect, and sustain us with your compassionate mindfulness.

I pray that for myself and the ocean of all sentient beings, from beginningless time until this very moment, throughout the inexhaustible ocean of karma—layered like Indra’s net—we have failed to understand the gate of repentance regarding both principle and phenomena.
Thus, sentient beings have committed transgressions and endured suffering; now we openly confess and repent.
The *Bodhisattva-bhūmi-citta-darśana-sūtra* (Sūtra on the Contemplation of the Mind-ground of Past Lives) says:
"Arising great compassion for all sentient beings, One should receive the Tathāgata’s threefold aggregate of precepts.
If one wishes to receive the precepts in accordance with the Dharma, One should repent of one's transgressions so that they are extinguished."
There are ten conditions that give rise to the causes of transgression: three of the body, four of the mouth, and three of the mind.
Since birth and death have no beginning, offenses are endless. The great ocean of afflictions is deep and bottomless;
the steepness of karmic obstructions is as high as Mount Sumeru. The commission of karma arises from two kinds of causes.

What are called active manifestations and seeds, held within the storehouse consciousness (ālayavijñāna) as the conditions for all types [of phenomena], follow the body like a shadow follows a form and are never separated from it. At all times, they obstruct the Noble Path;
they closely obstruct the sublime fruits of bliss for humans and devas, and remotely obstruct unexcelled Great Bodhi.
Living at home invites the causes of affliction, And leaving home may likewise break the pure precepts;
Yet if one can perform repentance according to the Dharma, All afflictions will be entirely eliminated,
Just as the fire at the end of an eon destroys the world, Consuming Mount Sumeru and the vast oceans.
Repentance can burn the fuel of afflictions; Repentance can lead one along the path to the heavens.
Repentance can attain the bliss of the four dhyānas; Repentance rains down precious maṇi jewels.
Repentance can prolong adamantine life; Repentance can enter the palace of eternal bliss.
Repentance can deliver one from the prison of the triple world; Repentance can cause the flower of Bodhi to bloom.
Through repentance, one beholds the Buddha’s Great Perfect Mirror; Through repentance, one can reach the Precious Abode.
If one is able to repent according to the Dharma, One should practice by relying on two types of contemplative gates.
First, the gate of extinguishing offenses by contemplating phenomena; second, the gate of extinguishing offenses by contemplating principle.
Regarding the extinguishing of offenses by contemplating phenomena, there are three types corresponding to the three grades of superior, middling, and inferior faculties.
If one possesses superior faculties and seeks the pure precepts, they shall arouse a great resolve and a mind of progress without retreat.
Weeping with tears of sorrow and blood, always with sincere devotion, we are moved by such grief that blood appears all over our bodies.
Keeping our mindfulness fixed upon the Triple Gem of the ten directions, as well as all beings of the six realms,
we remain in full-length kneeling posture with palms joined and undisturbed, confessing our faults and washing our hearts to seek repentance.
I pray that the Buddhas of the ten directions and the three periods of time, Out of great compassion, will take pity on me.
Abiding in saṃsāra without any refuge, I have long remained unawakened through the dark night of birth and death.
As an ordinary being possessed by all fetters, My wild mind is inverted and distractedly clings to all objects of perception.
I dwell within the burning house of the three realms, Delusively defiled by the six sense objects, with no one to protect me.
I was born into a poor and lowly family, Lacking self-mastery and constantly suffering.
I was born into a family of parents with false views, Committing transgressions in reliance upon evil kinsmen.
I pray that all Buddhas, the Honored Ones of Great Compassion, Out of pity, protect and keep me in mind as if I were an only son.
Having repented once, I shall never again commit any transgressions; May the Tathāgatas of the three periods of time bear witness to this.
One who thus repents with such vigor Is said to be of the highest grade in seeking the pure precepts.
If there are those of middling capacity who seek the precepts, with single-minded vigor they repent of all their sins;
tears flow profusely as they lose awareness of themselves, their bodies drenched in sweat as they lament to the Buddha,
confessing the karmic deeds of beginningless birth and death, praying that the waters of great compassion may wash away their defilements.
Washing away karmic obstacles and purifying the six sense faculties, I request the Bodhisattva’s Threefold Aggregate Precepts.
I vow to uphold them firmly without regressing, Cultivating diligently to deliver sentient beings from suffering.
Before I have attained liberation myself, I shall first deliver others; Until the end of the future, may this never cease.

Thus, those who are diligent and courageous, seeking Bodhi without sparing their own bodies or lives, can evoke the wondrous and miraculous signs of the Triple Gem; this is called the Middle Grade Great Repentance.
If there are those of inferior faculties who seek pure precepts, they should give rise to the unsurpassed Bodhicitta.
With tears and weeping, my body hair stands on end; deeply ashamed for the sins I have committed against you,
I sincerely confess before the Triple Gem of the ten directions and before all beings of the six realms all the ways I have troubled and disturbed sentient beings since beginningless time.
Arousing the mind of unimpeded great compassion, Not sparing one’s own body or life, one confesses the sins of the three karmas already committed;
Regarding the evils not yet committed, one vows never to create them again.
Thus, these three grades of repentance for all transgressions Are all called the foremost pure precepts.
Wash away the dust of affliction with the water of shame and remorse; let both body and mind become vessels of purity.
Sons of good family, you should know that I have already explained the various repentances of pure contemplation;
while there is no distinction between their principle and phenomena, they differ only according to the faculties and conditions of those who practice them.
If, while practicing the correct principle of contemplation, one remains free from all distractions and attachments,
puts on fresh, clean robes, and sits in the full lotus posture; with a concentrated mind and right mindfulness, remaining detached from all external conditions,
one should constantly contemplate the wondrous Dharma-body of the Buddhas— its essential nature being like space, ungraspable.
The nature of all transgressions is like this: they arise from a deluded mind through the causes and conditions of inversion.
Such characteristics of transgression are originally empty; throughout the three periods of time, nothing can be apprehended.
Neither internal, nor external, nor in between, their nature and characteristics are suchness, entirely unmoving.
The wondrous principle of True Suchness transcends names and words; Only the wisdom of the sages can penetrate it.
It is neither existent nor non-existent, nor both existent and non-existent; Neither non-existent nor non-non-existent, it is free from names and signs.
Pervading the entire Dharma-realm, it is without birth or extinction; All Buddhas are fundamentally of one and the same essence.
I pray that all Buddhas will grant their protective grace, To extinguish all inverted thoughts;
May I swiftly awaken to the source of true nature, And quickly realize the unsurpassed path of the Tathāgata.
If there are sons of noble family with pure faith, Who can contemplate the wondrous principle of emptiness day and night,
All karmic obstacles will naturally be eliminated; this is called the supreme upholding of pure precepts.

If a person contemplates and realizes the emptiness of the true mark, they can extinguish all heavy obstructions, just as a great wind blowing upon a fierce fire can burn away immeasurable grasses and trees.
"O sons of good family, this true contemplation Is called the secret essential gateway of all Buddhas.
If you wish to analyze it extensively for others, Do not proclaim it among those who lack wisdom.
All classes of ordinary, foolish beings Will surely give rise to doubt and lack faith upon hearing it."
If there are those of wisdom who give rise to faith and understanding, Contemplating moment by moment, they awaken to True Suchness (*tathatā*).
The Buddhas of the ten directions all appear before them, And the wondrous fruit of Bodhi is spontaneously realized.
O son of good family, after my parinirvāṇa, Those with pure faith in future ages—
Constantly repent within these two gates of contemplation; one should then receive the Bodhisattva’s Threefold Vow Precepts.
Next is the Repentance for Extinction of Offenses Seal-Mantra: Oṃ sarvapa-pamre-si-put-nadaha-nadama-draya svāhā.
(One should recite this three times:
The sins accumulated over a hundred kalpas Are all swept away in a single thought-moment; Like fire consuming dry grass, they are utterly extinguished without remainder.
All the evil karma I have created in the past, Arising from beginningless greed, hatred, and delusion,
Produced by my body, speech, and mind— I now confess it all. Having confessed,
I take refuge with a sincere heart and pay homage to the Honored One, Vairocana Buddha.
○ (Proclamation: May the assembly listen to these verses on impermanence from the Sūtra:
This body changes moment by moment; Pleasure is impermanent from moment to moment. Those gods and humans who are attached to desire do not see this because they lack the eye of wisdom.
From craving they proceed to its deepest depths, Constantly experiencing the pleasures of conduct.
If death and rebirth arrive, one cannot reach the place of bliss; those who do not understand birth and death perceive birth but feel no fear of it.
When they later face the time of death, they will only then repent for their karma.

Next, within the stage of Equal Enlightenment (*sambodhi*), in order to encompass all virtues and establish the causes [for enlightenment], the assembly of Maitreya Bodhisattva respectfully pays homage with all reverence to the inexhaustible Triple Gem.
Each member of this assembly kneels on their right knee, solemnly holding incense and flowers, making offerings according to the Dharma. May this ocean of offerings...

Clouds filled the worlds of the ten directions. They erected hundreds of billions of jeweled banners, suspended hundreds of billions of jeweled pennants, and hung hundreds of billions of jeweled silk streamers.

They lit hundreds of billions of jeweled incense burners, spread hundreds of billions of jeweled garlands, held hundreds of billions of jeweled fans, and grasped hundreds of billions of jeweled whisks.
They hung hundreds of billions of jeweled nets with bells, which were stirred by a gentle breeze.
It emitted wondrous sounds. A hundred trillion jeweled railings surrounded it on all sides;
a hundred trillion jeweled *tāla* trees were arranged in successive rows; a hundred trillion windows of exquisite jewels were magnificently adorned;
a hundred trillion jeweled trees provided shade all around; a hundred trillion jeweled pavilions extended and were elegantly decorated; [a hundred trillion] jeweled...
At the gates hang pendants and necklaces; a hundred trillion golden bells emit wondrous sounds, and a hundred trillion necklaces of auspicious marks hang down in pure adornment.
With such various articles of offering, they constantly perform worship.
The Indra-net of successive layers causes the ocean-like assembly of Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and holy sages to receive these clouds of offerings, taking them as platforms of radiant light.
May it extensively perform the Buddha-work throughout boundless realms, immeasurable and inexhaustible.
Having made this offering with all reverence,
next recite the mantra for the offering of the jeweled net.
With clouds of offerings such as these— vast oceans of the intrinsic nature of precious jewels, the most excellent emergence of the mountains of the seven treasures,
and so forth— I offer them to all the Buddhas and others. Oṃ sarvam-tathāgatārdra-puñja-megha-samudra-spharaṇa-samaye hūṃ.
*Phraṇatsamaṃ hūṃ*. The *Ratnakūṭa Sūtra* states:
"There is a dhāraṇī named 'The Mantra of Immeasurable Varieties,' which can accomplish all things and possesses great power. The dhāraṇī says:
Oṃ sīmāra sīmāra maimadra sīgara mahalaṅkhaḍa huṃ.
Next, the mantra for the mental offering (to be recited while placing the two hands in the vajra-añjali mudrā at the crown of the head): Oṃ sarvamalida meṅne’at ding saphra he man.
Āḥ āḥ naṃ kaṃ svāhā! Praise in the Brahma-sound:
The Buddha’s Dharma-body is identical to space—unimpeded, without distinction, and its form and appearance like a reflected image.
Various manifold signs appear, yet their reflected images have no location; like space, they lack intrinsic nature.

Those of vast wisdom realize their equality. Able to abide within the Buddhas' bodies—the domain of wisdom—they swiftly enter the stage of the Tathāgata, universally encompassing the entire Dharma-realm.
Speaking directly in praise of the Buddha:
On the Snowy Mountains there is a king of medicines called "Inexhaustible Root," which can produce all trees—roots, trunks, branches, leaves, flowers, and fruits.
The Buddha’s wisdom is likewise; it is born from the lineage of the Tathāgata.
Having already attained awakening, one further gives rise to the conduct of a bodhisattva.
It is like a person holding dry grass and placing it within the conflagration at the end of an eon; even a diamond would burn away completely.
There is no principle by which this—whether the kalpas and lands of the three times, or the sentient beings therein—could fail to be consumed, yet that grass might somehow not burn.
There is nothing this Buddha does not know. There is a wind named "Dissolution" that can destroy the great trichiliocosm;
yet if there were no other wind to stop it, it would destroy immeasurable realms. The wind of Great Wisdom is likewise:
it extinguishes the delusions of all bodhisattvas, and through a distinct wind of skillful means, it causes them to abide in the stage of the Tathāgata.
Suppose there were a great sutra scroll, Equal in measure to the three-thousandfold world system, Contained within a single mote of dust, And so it was with every mote of dust.
There was a person of wisdom With pure eyes who saw them all clearly;
He broke open the dust and brought forth the scrolls, Universally benefiting all sentient beings. The Buddha’s wisdom is also like this.
Pervading the minds of all sentient beings, they are entangled by deluded thoughts; unaware and unknowing, [the Buddhas],
through their great compassion, cause them to eliminate these delusions, thus appearing to provide benefit for all Bodhisattvas.
Homage to the Buddha Vairocana, the Original Honored One of Unimpeded Ten Bodies in the Flower Treasury World-Ocean of the Great Vaipulya Buddhāvatamsaka Sūtra.
Homage to Śākyamuni Buddha,
who with great kindness and compassion made five hundred vows to save sentient beings from suffering in the five turbidities.
Homage to the Buddha Bhaisajyaguru Vaidūryaprabha-rāja, the King of Medicine with Twelve Supreme Vows who Relieves Suffering in the Pūrṇacandra World of the East.
Homage to the Buddha Amitābha, who Relieves Suffering in the Five Turbidities through Forty-eight Vows in the Sukhāvatī World of the West.
Homage to the Perfect Teaching of the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha*, throughout all worlds as numerous as atoms within the entirety of space across the ten directions and three periods of time;
and homage to the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra, who presides over the truth of the Vows and Conduct within the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha*.
Homage to the Mahāsattva Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva Mahāsattva, who presides over faith, understanding, and realized wisdom within the Mahāvaipulya Buddhāvataṃsaka Sūtra.
Homage to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, the Thousand Hands and Thousand Eyes, who possesses great kindness and great compassion, rescuing beings from suffering in the five turbidities.

Homage to him whose great vows are vast and profound, who rescues beings from suffering in the five turbidities, appears in worlds where no Buddha dwells, and remains forever to comfort the hearts of men.
To the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Kṣitigarbharāja in the realm of Yama;

to the Bodhisattvas of the ten stages of faith, the ten abodes, the ten practices, the ten dedications, the ten grounds, and Equal Enlightenment, throughout the dust-mote lands of the entirety of space in the ten directions and three periods of time; Homage! (Namo).
Homage to the assembly of all oceans of Bodhisattvas, as numerous as the atoms in the oceans of lands throughout the entire Dharma-realm;
and homage to the fifty-five holy ones who cultivated and realized the five sites during the final assembly of the Great Vaipulya Buddhāvataṃsaka Sūtra.

Homage to the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Sudhana, who, as a vessel of perfect capacity and superior faculties within the final assembly of the *Mahāvaipulya Buddhāvataṃsaka Sūtra*, sought the Dharma through a hundred cities;
who perfected the bodhisattva practices within a single lifetime, and who serves as the model for cultivation and realization for the sudden gate of the Dharma-ending age.
Homage to all Buddha-works within the Dharma-body, form-bodies, physical relics, precious stupas, and temple edifices throughout the dust-mote lands of the ten directions and three periods of time,
as far as the limits of empty space; and further, to the entire ocean-like assembly of Bodhisattvas, worthies, and sages within the Dharma-treasury and at all places where the Dharma is preached.
Namo to the Great Vow, Clad in Armor, Seeking Rebirth in the Pure Land, Protector of the True Dharma in the Degenerate Age of the Xia Kingdom,
and Guardian of the Nation: With a sincere heart, I take refuge and pay homage to the World-Ocean of the Flower Treasury within the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra*, the Honored One of the Original Vow.

To Vairocana Buddha, throughout the ten directions, I take refuge; May my sins be extinguished and my pure faith increase; I vow to be born within the Flower Treasury Ocean, in the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss.
The *Sūtra on the Dharma Gate of the Liberation of Gathering Virtues as Causes for the Third Assembly* states:
"At that time, the youth Sudhana [proceeded]... [until] he reached that Honored One of Great Merit, praying: 'May you quickly return so that I may behold you.'"
From the *Sūtra on the Remainder of the Causes for Gathering Virtues*, it is said: "At that time, the youth Sudhana...
having completed his studies and accomplished immeasurable merit, vows together with all sentient beings to be reborn in the Flower Treasury Ocean and within the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss."

From the *Sūtra on the Remaining [Section] of the Compendium of Merits for Accomplishing the Causes*, it says: At that time, the youth Sudhana (until) reverently gazed up at him and took his leave to depart.
May I, together with all sentient beings, be reborn in the Flower Treasury Ocean, within the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss.

Homage to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Maitreya in the south, in the country of Pāramitā, within the Great Multi-storied Pavilion of the Vairocana-Adorned Treasury in the Great Garden of Great Adornment,
who has attained the liberation door of the treasury of adornment of the wisdom of non-forgetfulness regarding entry into all realms of the three periods of time.
Homage to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Mañjuśrī, who is born from within Prajñāpāramitā, possesses profound wisdom and vision, realizes the true Dharma as the mother of all Buddhas,
is perfected in skillful means, attains universal liberation, fulfills the practices of Samantabhadra, serves as the teacher of bodhisattvas,
reaches the ultimate stage of the causal path, and illuminates the fundamental mind.
Homage to the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Sudhana, the supreme vessel of the highest faculties who sought the Dharma through a hundred cities;
within a single lifetime, he perfected the bodhisattva practices and serves as the model for cultivation and realization for the sudden gate of the final age.
To all in the ten directions, I take refuge! May my transgressions be extinguished, may my pure faith increase, and may I be reborn in the Flower Treasury Ocean.
In the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss,
next is the repentance for offenses of the six sense faculties:
I only pray that the inexhaustible Buddha, Dharma, and Sangha Treasures of the Indra’s Net, Vairocana Tathāgata, Samantabhadra, and Mañjuśrī—

The assembly of noble ones gathered like an ocean, together with all mundane and supramundane deities: by virtue of your compassionate original vows, may you emit great radiance to illuminate this Dharma assembly;
bear witness to us, protect and sustain us, and out of pity, graciously accept us.

I and the ocean of all sentient beings, from the beginningless past until this very moment, have accumulated an inexhaustible ocean of karma, as vast and layered as Indra’s net. We now openly confess and repent for the karmic offenses committed through the six sense faculties.
The *Sūtra on the Method for Contemplating the Practices of Samantabhadra* states: "You should now, before all the Buddhas, disclose your past transgressions and repent with utmost sincerity.
Due to the causes and conditions of the visual faculty throughout immeasurable lifetimes, you have been greedily attached to various forms.

Because of this attachment to form, you have craved the sensory objects (*viṣaya*). Because of this craving for sensory objects, you have received a female body. In every life and place of birth, you have been deludedly attached to various forms."
It destroys your eyes; as a slave to affection and craving, form causes you to wander through the three realms.

Because of this wretched defilement, you are blind and see nothing. Again, he spoke these words: "I now repent of the grave offense of the eye-faculty, which obscures, defiles, and blinds me so that I see nothing.
I pray that the Buddha, in his great compassion, will take pity and protect me. Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, riding upon the great Dharma-ship, universally..."

Together with all the infinite bodhisattvas of the ten directions, I pray that you, out of compassion, will grant me your hearing and allow me to repent of the unwholesome karmic obstacles of my visual faculty; I openly confess and repent them.
Samantabhadra spoke again: "Throughout many kalpas, due to the conditions of your faculty of hearing, you have followed after external sounds.

When you hear sublime sounds, your mind gives rise to delusion and attachment; when you hear harsh sounds, you give rise to the one hundred and eight kinds of afflictions that act as thieves and bring harm. Such is your evil ear."

You will experience retribution in the form of misfortune and constantly hear evil sounds. Because you have given rise to various conditions through inverted listening, you will frequently fall into the evil realms, borderlands, and places of wrong views where the Dharma is not heard.
You should yourself confess your own faults and evils, and repent for all your transgressions.
From many kalpas ago until my present body, my faculty of hearing has, through its causal conditions, been deluded by and attached to sounds, like glue adhering to grass.
When I hear unpleasant sounds, the poison of afflictions arises; I am deluded and attached everywhere without a moment’s pause, sitting thus within this cavity of sound.
"I have exhausted my spirit and consciousness and fallen into the three miserable realms. Only now do I begin to realize this; I turn toward all the World-Honored Ones to reveal and repent.
Then, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva further explained the method of repentance: "Throughout immeasurable kalpas of your past lives..."
Because of craving for fragrances, the various consciousnesses differentiate and become greedily attached in every place, falling into the cycle of birth and death.
You should now contemplate the cause of the Mahāyāna; the cause of the Mahāyāna is the true reality (*dharmatā*) of all phenomena. Having already performed repentance, you should speak these words:
In immeasurable kalpas of past lives, I was greedy for fragrances, flavors, and tactile sensations, thereby committing various evils.

Due to these causes and conditions, throughout immeasurable lifetimes, I have constantly received the unwholesome bodies of hell-beings, hungry ghosts, animals, those from borderlands, and those with wrong views.
Such evil karma as this is now revealed; I turn toward the Buddhas, the Kings of the True Dharma, to confess my transgressions and repent.
Furthermore, you yourself must speak of the unwholesome and evil karma produced by the faculty of the tongue. This faculty of the tongue manifests the signs of evil karma:
false speech, frivolous talk, harsh words, and double-tongued speech; it slanders the words of the Buddha, praises false views, and speaks that which is useless.
Speech. Thus, these many various evil karmas—quarreling, causing disorder, and preaching what is not Dharma as Dharma—all such transgressions, I now confess in their entirety.
These faults of the tongue are immeasurable and boundless; the thorns of all evil karma emerge from the root of the tongue.
It cuts off the True Wheel of Dharma, arising from this very tongue. Such an evil tongue severs the seeds of merit regarding that which is not the true meaning.
In the midst [of these matters], he employs many pretexts to insistently preach and praise false views. Like adding fuel to a fire, it is like a raging conflagration that harms sentient beings;

it is like one who drinks poison and dies without even a wound. Such retribution for sins—evil, perverse, and unwholesome—will lead to falling into the evil realms for hundreds or thousands of kalpas.
Because of this false speech, one falls into the great hells. I now take refuge in and pay homage to all...
Buddha, I reveal my dark evils and sincerely repent.
Furthermore, you should now repent with both body and mind: as for the body, [abstain from] killing, stealing, and sexual misconduct; as for the mind, cease all unwholesome thoughts.

One commits the ten unwholesome karmas and the five deeds of immediate retribution. Like a monkey, and like sticky resin, one clings greedily everywhere, pervading all six sense faculties (*ṣaḍāyatana*).
These karmas of the six faculties—like branches, twigs, flowers, and leaves—fill all birthplaces within the twenty-five states of existence throughout the triple world.
They are also able to increase the twelve links of suffering, beginning with ignorance (*avidyā*) and ending with old age and death (*jarāmaraṇa*).
I have experienced all eight forms of wrong action and the eight difficult conditions. I now ought to repent of such evil and unwholesome karma.
The Buddhas of the ten directions have taught the method of repentance, which is the practice of Bodhisattvas: to not sever the fetters and yet not dwell within the ocean of those fetters.
Contemplating the mind, one finds no mind; it arises from inverted thoughts. Such a conceptualizing mind arises from delusive thoughts, like wind in the sky that has no place of dependence.
Such is the nature of phenomena (*dharmalakṣaṇa*): neither arising nor ceasing. What is sin? What is merit?
My own mind is itself empty; sin and merit have no master. All phenomena are likewise thus: they abide nowhere.
It is destroyed. Thus one performs repentance: contemplating that the mind is the dharma of no-mind, not abiding within dharmas, all dharmas are liberated, and the truth of cessation is quiescent.
One who conceives such thoughts is said to perform the Great Repentance.
The entire ocean of karmic obstructions arises entirely from deluded thoughts.
If one wishes to repent, sit upright and contemplate the true nature of reality. All transgressions are like frost and dew; the sun of wisdom can dispel them.
Therefore, with a sincere heart, one should diligently repent for the offenses of the six sense faculties.
Furthermore, an ancient master’s verse says:
"That which obscures the merit of the universal eye Is entirely due to the眼界 (visual faculty) from time immemorial;
Because of giving rise to hatred and attachment toward objects of form, I now sincerely repent before the Triple Gem."
Those who have not heard the True Dharma of the Tathāgata do so because of their ear-faculty from beginningless time;
they are thus deluded by and attached to sounds. Now, at this place of the Triple Gem, we sincerely repent.
Those who do not perfume themselves with the fragrances of precepts, concentration, and wisdom do so because of their nose-faculty from beginningless time.
Because of attachment to various fragrances, I now sincerely repent before the Triple Gem;
because of the tongue-element from beginningless time, I was unable to propagate the True Dharma,
and because I craved and tasted all manner of unwholesome flavors, I now sincerely repent before the Triple Gem.

Those who have not realized the merit of the Dharmakāya all do so because of the body-element (*kāyadhātu*) from time immemorial, whereby they have committed various transgressions; now, they must sincerely repent before the Triple Gem.
Those whose eye of the mind has not attained correct view all do so because of the mind-element (*manodhātu*) from time immemorial.
For the sins of having given rise to greed, anger, and false views, I now sincerely repent before the Triple Gem.
Next is the Seal and Mantra for Repenting and Eradicating Sins: Oṃ sarvapa-pāpam viśuddha dharmanidhāya svāhā.
(One should recite this three times:
Sins accumulated over a hundred kalpas Are all swept away in a single thought-moment; Like fire consuming dry grass, they are utterly extinguished without remainder.
All the evil karma I have created in the past, Arising from beginningless greed, hatred, and delusion,
Produced through body, speech, and mind— I now repent it all. Having repented, with a sincere heart,
I take refuge and pay homage to the Honored One, Vairocana Buddha.
○ (Proclamation: May the assembly listen to these verses on impermanence from the Sūtra:
If a person does not contemplate the mind, But constantly indulges in the pleasures of desire, They will sleep for a long night through many ages, And their suffering will never diminish;
Out of delusion, they delight in pleasure, Failing to perceive their own suffering.
When one later encounters decline and suffering, one then realizes what fruit has been obtained. Desire at first seems virtuous and good, yet one does not perceive its extreme evil;

it is the messenger of hell. The blind who practice it exclusively for their own non-benefit believe in this desire, but those with the eye of wisdom remain detached from it, as if from a perilous precipice.
Thus one falls into hell; heedfulness is the foremost friend, while constant indulgence in negligence brings harm.
Negligence is the foremost enemy; therefore, one should draw near to virtuous friends.
It pervades the entire body like a most virulent poison and is the primary path to the evil realms—namely, negligence.

The thirty-ninth session:
Within the Assembly of Equal Enlightenment, in the Assembly of Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva of Non-dual Wisdom-Illumination,
all pay homage with reverence to the inexhaustible Triple Gem.

These members of the assembly each knelt on their right knees. Holding incense and flowers, they made offerings according to the Dharma, wishing that this ocean-like cloud of offerings would pervade the worlds of the ten directions.

There was the peerless fragrance-king *Anupama-gandha-rāja*, the fragrance-king *Vituśalila-gandha-rāja*—the form and appearance of this incense being like a drop of water—and the unsurpassed fragrance-king *Anativara-gandha-rāja*, and the fragrance-king *Vicitrabodhana-gandha-rāja*.
The *Aluṭha-avadhi* fragrance, King of Fragrances: this fragrance is crimson in color, like the blazing sun; it emerges from within the tree and is a resinous incense (*rasa-gandha*).
The *Cittānukūla-niḥsaraṇa* fragrance, King of Fragrances: it is firm and subtle according to the season. The *Candana* fragrance, King of Fragrances:
it appears as a solid image of the *candana* wood. In the Sanskrit language, it is called *ulūka-sāra*; it is solid.

Black aloeswood, the king of fragrances; the fragrance that renders all sense-faculties unmoving, the king of fragrances—within each of these fragrances, immeasurable scents emerge, pervading the assemblies and sites of enlightenment of all Buddhas throughout the entire Dharma-realm of the ten directions, transforming into various kinds of exquisite perfumes:

the fragrance of palaces, the fragrance of walls and enclosures, the fragrance of multi-storied pavilions, the fragrance of railings and balustrades, the fragrance of defensive towers, and the fragrance of canopies.

Fragrance from gates; fragrance from doors and windows; fragrance from half-moons; fragrance from lattices; fragrance from images; fragrance from circular halos; fragrance from ornaments; fragrance from radiance;
fragrance from clouds and rain; fragrance from banners; fragrance from canopies; fragrance from curtains; fragrance from pennants;

fragrance from parasols—pervading and adorning everywhere throughout all the dharma-realms of the ten directions, filling every place as an offering. By means of these roots of goodness from such offerings...
Dedicate [the merit] to three places: first, to be forever free from all poverty and suffering; second, to constantly behold all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas;
and third, to always hear the true Dharma of all Buddhas. With such various articles of offering, one should constantly make offerings.
May the ocean-like assemblies of Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and holy sages—the Indra-nets of ever-increasing layers—accept these clouds of offerings and transform them into light.
The platform is as vast as the boundless realm, immeasurable and inexhaustible. May it perform the work of a Buddha.
Having made this offering, all pay homage with reverence.
Next, the mantra for the offering of the jeweled lattice is recited.
Clouds of offerings such as these— vast oceans of the intrinsic nature of precious jewels, the most excellent Mount Sumeru of the seven treasures,
and so forth— I offer to all the Buddhas and the like. Oṃ sarva-tathāgata-arcana-pratīccha-samaya-hūṃ.
*Phraṇatsamaṃ hūṃ*. The *Ratnakūṭa Sūtra* states:
"There is a dhāraṇī called 'The Mantra of Immeasurable Varieties,' which is capable of accomplishing all things and possesses great efficacy. The dhāraṇī says:
Oṃ smara smara me manaḥ siddharaṃ hūṃ. Next is the mantra of the Amoghamani-mudrā: Oṃ amoghapāśa mahāvidyārāja tathāgata-maitreya.
*Kiṃ-dsa-man-da-bra-sa-ra hūṃ.* In the Brahma-sound, I praise the Buddha:
The Buddha’s body is equal to the atoms of all lands; He universally rains down the rain of Dharma, Which is unborn and without distinction.
Manifesting all worlds and all lands throughout the three periods of time,
he reveals the various distinct names of all the Teachers, causing them all to be seen. Furthermore,
the sublime wheels of Dharma turned by all the Tathāgatas of the past, future, and present are heard by everyone in this assembly.
Speaking directly, I praise the Buddha, the Tathāgata, when he first sat at the site of enlightenment: The entire great earth shook, and all worlds in the ten directions were bathed in light;
All sentient beings within the six realms of existence were freed from suffering.
The Buddha manifests immeasurable and diverse bodies, turning the pure and wondrous wheel of Dharma;
even throughout all kalpas of the three periods of time, its limit cannot be found.
His precious throne is high, broad, and peerless, pervading the infinite realms of the ten directions.
Adorned with various wondrous marks, the Buddha dwells in that inconceivable land;
or in immeasurable worlds, he manifests leaving home, attaining the Way of Buddhahood,
and even his final parinirvāṇa, distributing his body to establish stupas and temples.

Thus, through these various and boundless practices, the Guide has expounded all the great virtues possessed by the World-Honored One while he was in the world; having vowed to cultivate them until they are all exhausted,
when dedicating those roots of goodness, one abides in such skillful means.
Thus practicing the conduct of enlightenment, his mind is ultimately free from weariness or indolence.
Homage to the Buddha Vairocana, the Original Honored One of the Ten Unobstructed Bodies in the Flower Treasury World-Ocean of the Great Vaipulya Buddhāvataṃsaka Sūtra.
Homage to Śākyamuni Buddha, the Greatly Compassionate One who made five hundred vows to save sentient beings from suffering in the five turbidities.
Homage to the Medicine Master Lapis Lazuli Light King Buddha of the Pūrṇacandra World in the East, who made twelve supreme vows to save sentient beings from suffering in the five turbidities.
